To capture such relationship, we propose to use an extension of Hidden Markov Models to multivariate observations. This model introduces a third auxiliary variable designed to accommodate the economic covariates in the time-series data. We detail the unique aspects of operational risk data and describe how model calibration is achieved via the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm. Additionally, we provide the calibration results for the various risk-event types and analyze the relevance of the inclusion of the macroeconomic covariates.

title: A superconvergent hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method for the convective Cahn--Hilliard equation

original_abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method combined with convex-concave splitting for the temporal discretization of the convective Cahn-Hilliard equation. The convection term is discretized explicitly without stabilization, yielding three key advantages: (1) unconditional stability, (2) preservation of the optimal convergence rate for piecewise constant approximations, and (3) a symmetric system after local elimination, enabling efficient solver via minimal residual methods. We establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^2$ norm for both the scalar and flux variables for any polynomial degree $k \geq 0$. To achieve optimal $L^2$-norm estimates, we introduce a specialized HDG elliptic projection operator and analyze its approximation properties. Within the HDG framework, local elimination is employed to reduce the degrees of freedom associated with the globally coupled unknowns, and the scalar variables exhibit superconvergence. Finally, numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Structure-preserving approximation for non-isothermal phase-field models in melt flow

original_abstract: This work presents a conforming finite-element scheme for the non-isothermal Allen-Cahn-Navier-Stokes system, incorporating periodic, closed, and thermal boundary conditions. The system comprises the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations coupled with the non-isothermal Allen-Cahn equation, which includes a non-conserved phase-field equation and a temperature equation. The proposed numerical scheme preserves entropy production exactly and maintains total energy conservation up to a negative numerical dissipation. Convergence tests in both space and time are conducted, and representative examples are provided to demonstrate the scheme's effectiveness.

title: Model theory of class-sized logics

original_abstract: We study compactness and Löwenheim-Skolem properties of fragments of the class-sized logic $\mathcal{L}_{\infty \infty}$ and of class-sized versions of second-order and sort logics. In these fragments, certain combinations of infinitary quantifiers and boolean connectives are banned. While model-theoretic properties fail for unrestricted class logics, this drastically changes in our more restricted setting. We show that model-theoretic properties of class logics characterise a wide array of large cardinals, and that some of them can even be obtained in ZFC. In particular, we give a characterisation of Weak Vopěnka's Principle and Ord is Woodin by downwards Löwenheim-Skolem properties, and a characterisation of Shelah cardinals by a compactness property of class-sized logics. We further strengthen many known results about properties of set-sized logics by studying how they transfer to class-sized extensions.

title: Optimal control of therapies related to an oxytaxis glioblastoma model

original_abstract: We propose and analyze an optimal control problem associated with a Keller-Segel type parabolic system with chemoattraction, modeling the glioblastoma growth in a bi-dimensional bounded domain, influenced by the presence of oxygen where the controls are two different (chemotherapy and antiangiogenic) therapies. The model considers the random diffusion of tumor cells and oxygen, the movement of cells towards the oxygen gradient (oxytaxis), and reaction terms describing the interaction between cells and oxygen. We establish a mathematical framework to analyze the existence and uniqueness of weak-strong solution of the model and subsequently we analyze an optimal control problem considering a cost functional that minimizes both the tumor growth and the oxygen concentration. We prove the existence of a global optimal solution and derive necessary first-order optimality conditions. Finally, we propose a methodology for approximating the optimal therapies. We use the gradient of the reduced cost functional through the adjoint scheme, and minimize the cost functional implementing the Adam gradient optimization method. Some numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: Normal Functions, Even Theta Characteristics and the Theta Divisor

The significance of this work lies in providing an algebro-geometric counterpart to spectral gap conditions for Dirac operators established in prior work, thereby bridging spectral geometry and the classical theory of theta characteristics on algebraic curves.
original_abstract: Let $[C]$ be a general point in the moduli space of curves $M_g$ with $g > 1$. Let $G \subset J(C)$ be a connected compact subgroup of real dimension $1$ of the Jacobian, and let $L$ be an even theta characteristic on $C$. We prove that $\{ζ\in G \mid H^0(C, L \otimes ζ) \neq 0\} = \emptyset$ if and only if $L \otimes ζ_G$ is an even theta characteristic on $C$, where $ζ_G$ is the unique non-trivial point of $G$ of order two.

title: Triangulations and Maximal Cross-Ratio Degrees

The work connects to broader questions involving Laman graph embeddings, scattering amplitudes, and Kapranov degrees.
original_abstract: The cross-ratio degree problem is about counting rational curves with $n$ marked points satisfying $n-3$ cross-ratio conditions. This problem has a tropical analogue which provides the same number, as shown by a correspondence theorem. In general, there are no closed formulas for this counting problem. In the special case of cross-ratio conditions given by triangulations, a formula was found by Silversmith via techniques of algebraic geometry. We study the cross-ratio problem given by triangulations in the tropical world. In addition to computing the cross-ratio degree by tropical means, we provide concrete solutions for the counting problem in arbitrary settings, thus answering the question by Silversmith. We also use the tropical recursive algorithm by Goldner to compute cross-ratio degrees to provide a new computational tool to compute cross-ratio degrees. With this, we can find all possible cross-ratio degrees for $n=9.$ Previously, these numbers were only known up to $n=8.$

title: Optimal transfer operators for nonsymmetric two-grid methods

This paper presents a unified framework for analyzing the convergence of algebraic two-grid methods applied to nonsymmetric and indefinite linear systems, extending the well-established theory for symmetric positive definite (SPD) problems. The framework allows norm-based convergence analysis in any norm defined by a Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrix B.

The authors consider two distinct error propagation operators with arbitrary numbers of pre- and post-smoothing steps. The first operator serves as the natural generalization of the SPD error operator, while the second has a simpler structure using the same matrix for both pre- and post-smoothing. A key methodological element is the concept of B-normal matrices, which generalizes normal matrices to arbitrary B-inner products, combined with B-orthogonal projections. This B-normality assumption, applied to the smoothing matrix, enables convergence analysis for the simpler error operator within a special class of norms defined through diagonalization of the preconditioned system matrix.

The central results include convergence proofs for both error operators, derivation of optimal compatible transfer operators that minimize error norms, and the demonstration that the first operator achieves equivalent convergence results without the additional B-normality assumption required by the second. The authors further show that increasing the number of coarse variables reduces the error norm and extend McCormick's classical V-cycle bound to nonsymmetric indefinite problems.

This work is significant because it provides the first general framework unifying and extending all existing convergence results for both symmetric and nonsymmetric algebraic multigrid methods.
original_abstract: Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) methods have been proven to be effective solvers for large-scale linear algebraic systems $Ax = b$ with Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrix $A$. For such problems the convergence in the $A$-norm is well understood, but for nonsymmetric indefinite systems fewer results exist. Recently, convergence results for more general $B$-norms induced by certain HPD matrices were established. There, orthogonal projections built by compatible transfer operators are used. Here, we present a theoretical framework for the convergence of nonsymmetric algebraic two-grid methods for arbitrary $B$-inner products and induced $B$-norms which naturally includes the HPD case and all recent results for the nonsymmetric case. For this purpose, we consider two different two-grid error operators with the first one being the natural generalization of the error operator in the HPD case. The second operator has been studied before and is simpler, but requires the additional assumption of normality in some inner product of the smoothing step $M^{-1}A$ to achieve convergence. We prove new convergence results, generalize some previous results and explain the differences and similarities of both operators together with the necessity of the normality. Moreover, we establish optimal compatible interpolation and restriction operators for both two-grid methods that minimize the error norm.

title: The KMS and GNS Spectral Gap of Quantum Markov Semigroups
generated_summary:
This paper resolves a conjecture by Fagnola, Poletti, Sasso, and Umanità concerning the relationship between exponential decay rates of quantum Markov semigroups measured with respect to different inner products. The conjecture, originally formulated for Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups, states that exponential decay with respect to the GNS (Gelfand-Naimark-Segal) inner product implies exponential decay with respect to the KMS (Kubo-Martin-Schwinger) inner product, with the KMS decay rate being at least as large as the GNS rate.

The author proves this conjecture in full generality, showing it holds not only for Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups but for all quantum Markov semigroups possessing a faithful normal invariant state. The methodology relies on an interpolation-type result for a family of inner products parametrized by operator monotone functions: if a state-preserving map is contractive for the GNS inner product, it is contractive for all inner products in this family. The proof draws on classical techniques including the operator Jensen inequality, transformer inequalities for operator means, and exact interpolation theory between Hilbert spaces.

As consequences, the author establishes that quantum Markov semigroups with an invariant state extend to strongly continuous contraction semigroups on completions with respect to any operator-monotone-function inner product, and obtains the spectral gap comparison inequality resolving the conjecture. These results illuminate a fundamental structural feature of quantum Markov semigroups and connect to applications in noncommutative harmonic analysis, quantum information theory, and quantum optics.
original_abstract: We establish a relation between the exponential decay rates of quantum Markov semigroups with respect to different inner products. More precisely, it was conjectured by Fagnola, Poletti, Sasso and Umanità that for a Gaussian quantum Markov semigroup, the exponential decay rate with respect to the KMS inner product is bounded below by the exponential decay rate for the GNS inner product. We show that this is indeed the case and not limited to Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups, but holds for quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Additionally, the KMS inner product can be replaced by a whole class of inner products induced by operator monotone functions.

title: The Representation Type of the Descent Algebras
generated_summary:
This paper provides a complete classification of the representation type of Solomon descent algebras for all finite Coxeter groups (except type E₈) over arbitrary fields. The descent algebra, a subalgebra of the group algebra of a Coxeter group, is classified as having finite, tame, or wild representation type depending on the Coxeter type, rank, and the characteristic of the underlying field.

The methodology combines theoretical and computational approaches. For the infinite families of types B and D, the authors exploit surjective algebra homomorphisms between descent algebras of related types, reducing the classification to small-rank cases. For these small cases and the exceptional types (F₄, H₃, H₄, E₆, E₇), the Ext-quivers are computed using Magma, based on explicit constructions of primitive orthogonal idempotents. The representation type is then determined using classical criteria involving separated quivers, Dynkin diagrams, and path algebras.

The key results provide precise conditions for each type. For type A, finite representation type occurs only for small rank relative to the characteristic, with wild type otherwise. Types B and D exhibit similar patterns with additional tame cases. The exceptional types are individually classified, with most being wild except in specific characteristics. Notably, tame representation type occurs only in limited situations, and no algebra in the classification is tame without being explicitly identified.

This work completes a program initiated by Schocker for type A and substantially extends the understanding of descent algebra structure across all Coxeter types.
original_abstract: Schocker classified the representation type of the descent algebra of type $\mathbb{A}$ over any field of characteristic zero. In an earlier paper, the authors extended this classification for type $\mathbb{A}$ to fields of positive characteristic. In this paper, we complete the classification for all other types except for $\mathbb{E}_8$. The proof for type $\mathbb{B}$ is entirely theoretical, while some small cases in type $\mathbb{D}$ and the exceptional types require computer computation to determine their Ext-quivers.

title: On the hamiltonicity problem of bicirculants: a reduction to cyclic Haar graphs
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the hamiltonicity problem for bicirculant graphs, a broad class of vertex-transitive graphs that includes generalized Petersen graphs and other well-studied families. The main contribution is establishing a reduction showing that the problem of determining whether all connected bicirculant graphs are hamiltonian can be reduced to the same question for cyclic Haar graphs, a specific subclass of bicirculants that are Cayley graphs on dihedral groups.

The methodology centers on introducing non-uniform representations of connected bicirculant graphs, complementing uniform representations developed in prior work. These representations enable techniques for joining Hamilton cycles found in connected components of subgraphs—particularly cyclic Haar graph subgraphs—into a Hamilton cycle for the entire graph. The authors systematically classify bicirculants not covered by previous theorems into type I and type II categories and handle each through iterative reduction arguments.

Key results include proving that all connected bicirculant graphs with at least four spokes per vertex are hamiltonian whenever connected cyclic Haar graphs of valence at least four are hamiltonian. Additionally, the authors establish hamiltonicity for several concrete families, including all connected bicirculants of order 2m where m is even and a product of at most four prime powers, and all connected bicirculants of even order less than 18,480.

These results significantly advance progress toward the conjecture that all connected bicirculant graphs (except known exceptions) are hamiltonian, by elegantly reducing this broad problem to the study of a single prominent subclass.
original_abstract: A bicirculant is a regular graph that admits an automorphism having two vertex-orbits of the same size. A bicirculant can be described as follows. Given an integer $m \ge 1$ and sets $R, S, T \subseteq \mathbb Z_m$ such that $R=-R$, $T=-T$, $0 \not\in R \cup T$ and $0 \in S$, the graph $B(m;R,S,T)$ has vertex set $V=\{u_0,\dots,u_{m-1},v_0,\dots,v_m-1\}$ and edge set $E=\{u_iu_{i+j}| \ i \in\mathbb Z_m, j \in R\} \cup \{v_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in\mathbb Z_m, j \in T\} \cup\{u_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in\mathbb Z_m, j \in S\}.$ Bicirculant graphs with $R=T=\emptyset$ are known as cyclic Haar graphs. In 2025 we conjectured that the only non-hamiltonian graphs among regular connected bicirculants of degree more than one are the generalized Petersen graphs $G(m,2)$ with $m \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. Recently we have verified the conjecture for bicirculants with $|S|\le 2$ and for bicirculants with $|R|=|T|$ odd. In this paper we show that the conjecture holds for all bicirculants with $|S| \le 3$ and for all bicirculants with $|S| \ge 4$ and $m/\gcd(m, S)$ even. As a byproduct of our results, we prove that every connected bicirculant graph on $2m$ vertices with $|S| \ge 4$ is hamiltonian for even $m< 9\, 240$, and for odd $m< 3\,465$. Finally, we show that the existence of a hamilton cycle in every connected cyclic Haar graph of valence at least $4$ implies that every connected bicirculant graph of valence at least $4$ is hamiltonian.

title: Positivity-Preserving and Entropy-Stable Oscillation-Eliminating DGSEM for the Compressible Euler Equations on Curvilinear Meshes with Adaptive Mesh Refinement
generated_summary:
This paper extends an entropy-stable, oscillation-eliminating discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM) for the compressible Euler equations from conforming curvilinear meshes to adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) with nonconforming interfaces. The central contribution is the rigorous development of two nonconforming interface treatments—an entropy-stable flux and a classical mortar-based flux—along with a provably positivity-preserving framework on curvilinear AMR meshes.

The authors construct an entropy-stable interface flux that preserves primary conservation and satisfies a semi-discrete entropy inequality but demonstrate that negative entries in nonconforming interpolation operators degrade formal accuracy to at most first order for polynomial degrees greater than or equal to two. To recover high-order accuracy, they propose a mortar-based flux that performs interpolation at the solution level, retaining design-order convergence at the cost of losing provable entropy stability. This reveals a fundamental trade-off between entropy stability and high-order consistency at nonconforming interfaces. Both fluxes are proven to preserve positivity of density and pressure under appropriate CFL conditions via an extension of the Zhang–Shu framework. The complete AMR algorithm includes shock-indicator-based refinement, a conservative and positivity-preserving data transfer procedure, and selective oscillation elimination.

Numerical experiments—including isentropic vortex convergence studies, double Mach reflection, a Mach-2350 astrophysical jet, and supersonic flow past a circular cylinder—confirm the theoretical findings, demonstrating high-order accuracy, robustness under extreme conditions, and the effectiveness of AMR in resolving complex compressible flow features on curvilinear meshes.
original_abstract: We extend the entropy-stable oscillation-eliminating discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (ES-OEDG) on curvilinear meshes to adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) grids with nonconforming interfaces. The formulation targets two-dimensional curvilinear quadrilateral meshes under a 2:1 refinement constraint, allowing a single level of hanging nodes. Elementwise volume discretization and geometric mapping are retained, while oscillation elimination and interface coupling are adapted for nonconforming interfaces. A central contribution is the design and analysis of numerical fluxes for such interfaces. We construct an entropy-stable flux that ensures global conservation and a semi-discrete entropy inequality. However, for polynomial degree N >= 2, negative entries in nonconforming interpolation operators lead to loss of formal high-order consistency. To address this, we propose a mortar-based flux that preserves high-order accuracy by interpolating at the solution level and evaluating standard two-point fluxes on fine-side mortars, at the cost of losing provable entropy stability. We also extend the Zhang--Shu positivity-preserving framework to curvilinear AMR meshes. Under forward Euler time stepping and a suitable CFL condition, the scheme using either flux preserves positivity of cell-average density and pressure. Combined with the Zhang--Shu limiter, this yields a fully discrete scheme maintaining admissibility at all nodal points. We further incorporate shock-indicator-based AMR and a conservative, positivity-preserving data transfer procedure between successive meshes, resulting in a robust and efficient algorithm. Numerical experiments on Cartesian and curvilinear AMR grids confirm high-order accuracy and robustness.

title: Quantization of nilpotent coadjoint $GL_N$-orbit closures in positive characteristics
generated_summary:
This paper classifies Hamiltonian quantizations of nilpotent coadjoint orbit closures for the general linear group GL_N over algebraically closed fields of positive characteristic. The main result establishes a natural bijection between the set of Hamiltonian quantizations of a nilpotent orbit closure (indexed by a partition of N) and the quotient of a vector space of Lie algebra homomorphisms by the dot-action of a relative Weyl group, which is a product of symmetric groups determined by the partition.

The methodology combines several sophisticated techniques specific to positive characteristic. The authors construct a chain of bijections passing through G-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra, primitive ideals associated to small modules of reduced enveloping algebras, one-dimensional representations of finite W-algebras, and the Miura map. A key technical innovation is the introduction of "p-support," which leverages the large p-centre of the enveloping algebra in positive characteristic. The authors also provide a new proof of Katsylo's theorem valid for GL_N in positive characteristic and develop an induction construction using Frobenius twists to build quantizations from reduced symmetric algebras.

The results parallel Losev's classification of quantizations over the complex numbers, confirming expectations of Premet and the second author. As an application beyond type A, the authors establish the existence and uniqueness of a Joseph ideal for minimal nilpotent orbit closures in types B through G, generalizing Joseph's classical result to positive characteristic. The work bridges representation theory in positive characteristic with the geometric theory of symplectic singularities.
original_abstract: Let $G$ be a reductive group over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p$, good for the root system of $G$. The closures of $G$-orbits in the Hilbert nullcone of the coadjoint representation are conical affine Poisson varieties, generically of full rank, known as {\em nilpotent coadjoint orbits}. In this paper, we classify the filtered Hamiltonian quantizations of these orbit closures for $G = GL_N$ and any $p > 0$. Our main new technique is a construction of quantizations from certain primitive quotients of the enveloping algebra, inducing them from the stabiliser in $G$ of the Frobenius twisted $p$-character.

title: Long-time dynamics of stochastic 2D hydrodynamic-type evolution equations driven by multiplicative Lévy noise
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the long-time dynamics of abstract non-autonomous stochastic hydrodynamic-type evolution equations driven by multiplicative Lévy noise, encompassing models such as the 2D Navier-Stokes equations, magnetohydrodynamic equations, and related fluid dynamics systems. The work fills a significant gap in the literature, as no prior studies had addressed the long-term dynamical properties of these equations under nonlinear multiplicative Lévy noise.

The authors employ several key methodological innovations: a truncation argument approximating locally Lipschitz coefficients by globally Lipschitz ones to establish global well-posedness, stopping time techniques combined with pathwise Gronwall inequalities to prove convergence of solution sequences, and a non-standard weight function technique to derive uniform pullback high-regularity estimates.

The paper delivers three principal results. First, global well-posedness is established under local Lipschitz conditions, enabling the construction of a mean random dynamical system and the proof of existence and uniqueness of weak pullback mean random attractors. Second, the existence of invariant measures is demonstrated in the autonomous setting, with analysis of their limiting behavior as noise intensity varies. Third, under additional structural conditions on the bilinear operator and noise coefficients, the existence and uniqueness of pullback measure attractors are established, along with their asymptotic autonomy robustness with respect to time perturbation parameters.

These results significantly advance the understanding of stochastic fluid dynamics by extending attractor and invariant measure theory to the challenging setting of Lévy-driven nonlinear noise, which lies beyond the scope of classical pathwise random attractor approaches.
original_abstract: This paper investigates the long-time dynamics of solutions for an abstract nonlinear stochastic hydrodynamic-type equation driven by multiplicative Lévy noise. The framework encompasses several key hydrodynamical models, including the stochastic 2D Navier-Stokes equations, magnetohydrodynamic equations, the magnetic Bérnard problem, as well as various stochastic shell models of turbulence. Under the assumption that the nonlinear noise coefficients satisfy local Lipschitz and linear growth conditions, we first establish global well-posedness using a truncation technique. Then, by introducing a mean random dynamical system, we prove the existence and uniqueness of weak pullback mean random attractors for the system. Furthermore, when the external force is time-independent, we study the existence of invariant measures for the corresponding autonomous system, as well as the double limiting behavior of invariant measures with respect to the intensities of Gaussian and Lévy noise. Finally, under additional assumptions on the bilinear nonlinear term (e.g., as in the Navier-Stokes equations), we examine the existence and uniqueness of pullback measure attractors, along with the asymptotically autonomous stability of such attractors as the time parameter tends to negative infinity. It is worth noting that the results of this paper are new even for the single stochastic 2D Navier-Stokes equations.

title: Extremal 1-planar graphs without k-cliques
generated_summary:
This paper establishes tight upper bounds on the number of edges in K_k-free 1-planar graphs (graphs drawable in the plane with each edge crossed at most once) for k = 3, 4, and 5, extending classical Turán-type extremal problems to the 1-planar setting. The main results show that for K_3-free 1-planar graphs, the maximum number of edges is 3n − 8 (improving a previous bound of 3n − 6), for K_4-free 1-planar graphs it is (18n − 48)/7 for n ≥ 9, and for K_5-free 1-planar graphs it is 4n − 8 for n = 8 or n ≥ 10. All bounds are shown to be tight for infinitely many values of n.

The methodology centers on a novel edge-counting formula for connected 1-plane graphs expressed in terms of three planarization-based parameters, which explicitly characterizes correction terms relative to the planar bound 3n − 6. For the K_3-free case, the authors introduce crossing skeletons and alternating k-vertices for refined structural analysis. For the K_4-free case, the formula yields a lower bound on crossings combined with the known upper bound of n − 2 crossings in 1-planar drawings. For the K_5-free case, explicit constructions using recursive Q_4-additions establish tightness.

As corollaries, the authors recover known results about bipartite and tripartite 1-planar graphs and provide simple proofs that 1-planar graphs with minimum degree 6 or 7 must contain K_3 or K_4, respectively. The work significantly advances the understanding of extremal problems beyond planarity.
original_abstract: In 2016, Dowden initiated the study of planar Turán-type problems, which has since attracted considerable attention. Recently, Bekos et al. proved that every $K_3$-free $1$-planar graph on $n\ge 4$ vertices has at most $3n-6$ edges. In this paper, we strengthen this bound to $3n - 8$, which is tight for all even $n \ge 8$. Furthermore, we show that every $K_4$-free $1$-planar graph on $n \ge 3$ vertices has at most $\bigl\lfloor \tfrac{7n}{2} \bigr\rfloor - 7$ edges, and this bound is tight for all integers $n \ge 9$. We also prove that every $K_5$-free $1$-planar graph on $n \ge 3$ vertices has at most $4n - 8$ edges, which is tight for $n = 8$ and for all integers $n \ge 10$.

title: Piercing all maximum cliques in hypergraphs
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the problem of piercing maximum cliques in uniform hypergraphs, resolving a conjecture by Jung, Keszegh, Pálvölgyi, and Yuditsky. The conjecture proposed that for every k ≥ 2, there exists a constant c_k < 1 such that if a k-uniform hypergraph has clique number exceeding c_k times the number of vertices, then all maximum cliques can be hit by a single vertex—generalizing a classical result of Hajnal for graphs.

The authors disprove this conjecture in a strong sense, showing that for any k ≥ 3, any integer t ≥ 1, and any constant c < 1, there exists a k-uniform hypergraph whose clique number exceeds c times the vertex count, yet whose maximum cliques cannot be pierced by t vertices. The proof proceeds by induction on k and t, with the base case of 3-uniform hypergraphs and piercing number one established first, then extended to the general setting.

Beyond the counterexample, the authors introduce and study the function f_{k,t}(n), defined as the minimal threshold such that any k-uniform hypergraph with clique number exceeding this threshold has piercing number at most t. They establish both lower and upper bounds for this function, though a gap remains. The paper concludes by proposing promising restricted settings where positive results might still hold, including intersection hypergraphs of convex sets and hypergraphs arising from transitive triples in tournaments, leaving these as open questions for future investigation.
original_abstract: Graphs whose maximum clique size exceeds half of the total number of vertices satisfy a classical property: the family of their maximum sized cliques can be pierced by a single vertex. This result dates back to a 1965 theorem by Hajnal. Motivated by this theorem, Jung, Keszegh, Pálvölgyi, and Yuditsky recently conjectured that an analogous result should hold for hypergraphs of larger uniformity, with an appropriate constant replacing the threshold $1/2$. In this paper we refute this conjecture in a strong form. We show that for any constant $c<1$ and integers $k\ge 3$ and $t\ge 1$, there exist $k$-uniform hypergraphs $G$ whose maximum clique size exceeds $c|V(G)|$, yet the family of maximum size cliques of $G$ cannot be pierced by $t$ vertices. This demonstrates that no universal constant threshold guarantees bounded piercing number for maximum cliques in uniform hypergraphs. We discuss further questions concerning the relationship between clique size and piercing maximum cliques in hypergraphs, and introduce a geometric variant of the problem using Helly's Theorem.

title: Quantum Mixing for Schrödinger eigenfunctions in Benjamini-Schramm limit
generated_summary:
This paper establishes quantum ergodicity and quantum mixing for Schrödinger operators on sequences of compact hyperbolic surfaces converging to the hyperbolic plane in the Benjamini-Schramm sense, extending previous results that were limited to the Laplacian (free motion). The main contribution is proving that eigenfunctions of perturbed operators H = −Δ + V equidistribute in the large genus limit, provided the surfaces satisfy uniform discreteness, a spectral gap condition, and the potentials are bounded with controlled L² norms.

The methodology employs time averages of Heisenberg evolutions using the hyperbolic sine propagator, which satisfies a Duhamel formula allowing the potential to be extracted as a perturbation. The quantum variance decomposes into a free part and an error term; the error is controlled via L² bounds on potentials and Benjamini-Schramm convergence, while the free part is handled using exponential mixing of the geodesic flow. This approach circumvents the tree-based recursive Green's function techniques used in discrete settings, which do not extend to continuous hyperbolic geometry.

The results apply to potentials induced by fixed L^p functions on the hyperbolic plane, sparse point cloud potentials, weak coupling limits, and Hartree-type potentials arising from thermodynamic limits of dilute Bose gases. A probabilistic version holds for Weil-Petersson random surfaces with high probability. These findings advance understanding of quantum chaos beyond free dynamics and provide rigorous delocalization results for Schrödinger eigenfunctions, with implications for many-body quantum systems and Anderson delocalization on hyperbolic surfaces.
original_abstract: Let $-Δ_{\mathbb{H}}+V$ be the Schrödinger operator on $\mathbb{H}$ where $V \in L^p(\mathbb{H}) \cap L^\infty(\mathbb{H})$ for some $p > 0$. If $(X_n)$ is a uniformly discrete sequence of compact hyperbolic surfaces with a uniform spectral gap that Benjamini-Schramm converges to $\mathbb{H}$, we prove quantum mixing for the eigenfunctions of $-Δ_{X_n}+V_n$ in any sufficiently large spectral window $I$, where $V_n$ is the potential on $X_n$ induced by $V$. These apply to large degree lifts of a potential on a base surface such as congruence covers of arithmetic surfaces, with high probability to random hyperbolic surfaces in the Weil-Petersson model of large genus, and to Hartree one-particle operators arising in thermodynamic limit of many-body Bose gas on hyperbolic surfaces. The proof uses the Duhamel formula for the hyperbolic wave equation together with exponential mixing of the geodesic flow on $T^1 X_n$.

title: Infinite Horizon Optimal Control Problems with Discount Factors
generated_summary:
This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of infinite horizon optimal control problems governed by semilinear parabolic equations with two independent discount factors—one for the state tracking term and one for the control cost term in the objective functional. The main contribution lies in extending previous work by allowing a much wider class of nonlinearities (beyond odd-degree polynomials to include exponential functions and general non-decreasing monotone functions) and by investigating the interplay between the two independent discount factors.

The methodology involves a systematic analysis proceeding through several stages: well-posedness of the state equation with weighted function spaces induced by the discount factors, differentiability of the control-to-state mapping, first-order optimality conditions, second-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions, and convergence analysis of finite horizon approximations to the infinite horizon problem.

Key results establish precise threshold conditions on the discount factors. Well-posedness requires the state discount factor to exceed a positive threshold related to the elliptic operator, while necessary optimality conditions demand a larger threshold dependent on the nonlinearity. Second-order sufficient conditions additionally require the control discount factor to be strictly smaller than the state discount factor. Under these conditions, the authors prove convergence rates for finite horizon approximations.

The significance of this work extends to stabilization problems, asymptotic tracking, and applications in economics and mathematical biology, providing rigorous theoretical foundations for practically important infinite horizon formulations and their numerical approximation through receding horizon approaches.
original_abstract: This paper is dedicated to the analysis of infinite horizon optimal control problems subject to semilinear parabolic equations with constraints on the controls and discounted cost functionals. The discount factors on the cost and the state components are allowed to differ from each other. First-order as well as second-order optimality conditions are derived and the importance of allowing different discount factors for the second-order analysis for the class of nonlinearities under consideration is demonstrated. Finally convergence and rate of convergence for the approximation of the infinite horizon problem by a family of finite horizon problems is proven.

title: Tight constructions for reconfigurations of independent transversals
generated_summary:
This paper solves an open problem posed by Buys, Kang, and Ozeki concerning the exact characterization of extremal instances for their theorem on reconfiguration of independent transversals in vertex-partitioned graphs. An independent transversal is an independent set containing exactly one vertex from each block of a vertex partition, and the reconfiguration graph connects two independent transversals when they differ in exactly one block by non-adjacent vertices. Buys, Kang, and Ozeki previously established a sufficient maximum degree condition for this reconfiguration graph to be connected, but left open the precise characterization of tight examples—so-called "bad instances"—where the reconfiguration graph is disconnected.

The author introduces two key ingredients: elementary non-reconfigurable instances, built on disjoint unions of complete bipartite graphs with specific partition structures, and a construction lemma that generates larger non-reconfigurable instances from smaller ones by combining a graph with a disconnected reconfiguration graph with another graph lacking independent transversals. The main result proves that every bad instance arises either as an elementary non-reconfigurable instance or through iterative application of this construction lemma starting from such an instance.

The proof employs detailed combinatorial techniques, building on prior work by Haxell and the author on graphs without independent transversals, while incorporating new ingredients specific to the reconfiguration setting. The characterization further illuminates deep connections between the existence and reconfiguration problems for independent transversals and extends naturally to simplicial complex and topological settings, with potential applications to list coloring and other combinatorial optimization problems.
original_abstract: For a graph $G$ and partition $\mathcal{U}$ of its vertex set, an independent transversal of $(G, \mathcal{U})$ is an independent set of $G$ that contains one vertex from each block of $\mathcal{U}$. Buys, Kang, and Ozeki studied when a reconfiguration graph on independent transversals of $(G,\mathcal{U})$ is connected, meaning any independent transversal can be transformed into any other one through a sequence of one-vertex modifications while always maintaining an independent transversal. Analogous to a theorem of Haxell, they proved that this is the case if $G$ has maximum degree $Δ$ and each block of $\mathcal{U}$ has size at least $2Δ$, except if the union of some $k \ge 1$ blocks of $\mathcal{U}$ induces $k$ disjoint copies of the complete bipartite graph $K_{Δ, Δ}$ in $G$. Solving one of their problems, we exactly characterize the partition structure in the latter exceptional instances of their theorem, showing that there is a rich variety of them but they are generated by a simple constructive procedure.

title: A nonconforming method for a generalized Darcy-Forchheimer model
generated_summary:
This paper presents a general-order dual mixed nonconforming finite element method for a generalized Darcy-Forchheimer problem, which models nonlinear fluid flow in porous media. The work extends the foundational framework of Girault and Wheeler in several significant directions: it accommodates more general (r-2)-type Forchheimer nonlinearities beyond the standard quadratic model, allows inhomogeneous mixed boundary conditions, permits permeability tensors with lower Lebesgue regularity, and introduces arbitrary-order discretization schemes.

The methodology pairs piecewise-polynomial spaces of order k-1 for fluxes with Crouzeix-Raviart nonconforming elements of order k for potentials. The authors establish convergence to the exact solution under minimal regularity assumptions, leveraging novel Sobolev-trace inequalities in broken polynomial spaces whose constants are independent of the polynomial degree. Under additional regularity assumptions, general-order error estimates are also derived. The convergence proof proceeds through a carefully structured sequence of intermediate results, establishing weak and then strong convergence of both flux and potential variables in their natural norms.

Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings across different nonlinearity parameters, polynomial orders, and model parameters. The results demonstrate that while a standard fixed-point solver may fail for large nonlinearity parameters, a relaxed variant achieves convergence with appropriate tuning. The framework establishes essential mathematical foundations for future hp-adaptive strategies, which are particularly well-suited for efficiently resolving singular solution behaviors characteristic of nonlinear porous media flow problems.
original_abstract: We analyze a dual mixed nonconforming discretization of a generalized Darcy-Forchheimer model. Compared to the analogous scheme proposed by Girault and Wheeler, we consider general, i.e., nonquadratic, Forchheimer nonlinearities; we admit mixed, inhomogeneous boundary conditions; we allow for more general, i.e., with lower Lebesgue regularity, permeability tensors; we construct general-order schemes; we prove convergence to the exact solution under low regularity assumptions, based on novel Sobolev-trace inequalities for broken spaces; we derive error estimates of general-order assuming extra regularity of the exact solution and data; we present numerical results assessing the performance of the proposed schemes for different types of nonlinearity and nonlinear solvers.

title: On the largest chromatic number of $F$-free hypergraphs
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the maximum chromatic number achievable by hypergraphs that avoid a fixed forbidden substructure, extending the classical graph-theoretic question to the hypergraph setting. The authors study both strong and weak chromatic numbers, where strong coloring requires every hyperedge to be rainbow and weak coloring forbids monochromatic hyperedges, focusing particularly on Berge-F-free hypergraphs.

The main contribution is a comprehensive characterization of when the strong and weak chromatic numbers of F-free hypergraphs are bounded versus unbounded. For single r-graphs with r ≥ 3, the strong chromatic number is bounded only when F has at most one edge or when r = 3 and F is the expansion of a star. For Berge-F-free hypergraphs where F is a graph, both chromatic numbers are bounded if and only if F contains no cycle.

The authors employ greedy coloring algorithms, depth-first search techniques adapted to hypergraphs, and constructions based on Steiner systems to establish their bounds. Key results include tight bounds for star-free cases, showing the strong chromatic number of Berge-star-free 3-graphs equals n when Steiner systems exist. For Berge-path-free 3-graphs, they prove the strong chromatic number equals k and the weak chromatic number equals ⌈k/2⌉. They also determine exact values for several special tree families including spiders, double stars, and brooms.

These results significantly advance understanding of extremal chromatic problems in hypergraph theory, bridging Turán-type extremal combinatorics with chromatic number theory in a unified framework.
original_abstract: Given a hypergraph $F$, what is the largest chromatic number that an $F$-free hypergraph can have? In the case of graphs, this question is easy to answer: the chromatic number is unbounded if $F$ contains a cycle, and the largest chromatic number of $F$-free graphs is $k-1$ if $F$ is a forest on $k$ vertices. The situation is more complicated for hypergraphs. The strong coloring of a hypergraph is a coloring of the vertices such that every hyperedge is rainbow. The weak coloring of a hypergraph is a coloring of the vertices such that no hyperedge is monochromatic. The strong/weak chromatic number of a hypergraph is the minimum number of colors in a strong/weak coloring of the hypergraph. Our question has been completely answered for the weak chromatic number, similarly to the graph case. We characterize the hypergraphs $F$ such that $F$-free hypergraphs have bounded strong chromatic number. The only remaining case is when $F$ is the 3-uniform expansion $S_k^+$ of a star with $k$ edges. Concerning the strong chromatic number of $S_k^+$-free hypergraphs, we give bounds that are asymptitically sharp as $k\rightarrow\infty$. We also consider the same problem when the Berge copies of a graph $F$ are forbidden. We characterize when the strong/weak chromatic numbers are bounded in this case, and obtain sharp results or bounds for specific trees. In particular, when $F$ is a path, we give a tight bound when $r=3$ and an asymptotically sharp bound when $r=4$.

title: Adaptation and Development of Super Schemes for Unconstrained Optimization Problems
generated_summary:
This paper proposes a class of "super-schemes" (SS1, SS2, and SS3) for solving nonlinear unconstrained optimization problems, achieving local convergence orders of two, four, and six, respectively. These methods address the well-known limitations of gradient-based approaches, particularly the slow linear convergence rate and zigzagging behavior of steepest descent methods near optimal points.

The methodology centers on reformulating the optimization problem as a system of nonlinear gradient equations and developing one-step, two-step, and three-step iterative schemes with two novel step-size parameter selection strategies. Importantly, the methods avoid computing second-order derivative information and rely on component-wise vector operations rather than matrix-by-matrix operations, maintaining a computational complexity of O(n²) per iteration comparable to existing gradient-based methods.

Numerical experiments implemented in MATLAB compare the proposed methods against established approaches including the Barzilai-Borwein and Neculai Andrei methods across multiple test functions. Results demonstrate that SS2 and SS3 achieve faster convergence, requiring fewer iterations than competing methods in most cases. The approximate computational order of convergence confirms the theoretical convergence rates. The paper also shows that preconditioning can significantly reduce iteration counts for ill-conditioned problems.
