original_abstract: In this paper, we propose a class of super-schemes for efficiently solving nonlinear unconstrained optimization problems. The proposed approach introduces two novel choices of step-size parameters, leading to efficient descent directions without requiring second-order information. We develop one-step, two-step, and three-step iterative schemes (denoted by SS1, SS2, and SS3) and establish that these methods achieve higher-order convergence of orders two, four, and six, respectively. Despite their high convergence rates, the computational complexity of the proposed methods remains comparable to existing gradient-based methods, with a cost of $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ per iteration. The proposed methods are simple to implement and do not require complicated line-search procedures. Their effectiveness is demonstrated through extensive numerical experiments on a wide range of problems, including large-scale and ill-conditioned cases. The results show that the proposed methods significantly outperform classical methods, such as the Barzilai-Borwein method and other gradient-based approaches, in terms of iteration count and computational efficiency. Finally, the numerical results are consistent with the theoretical analysis, confirming the stability of the proposed schemes for test optimization problems.

title: Pohozaev identities and bubbling obstruction for Yang-Mills fields in conformal dimension
generated_summary:
This paper establishes Pohozaev-type identities that reveal nontrivial compatibility constraints between weak limit connections and bubbles arising in the blow-up analysis of Yang–Mills connections on four-dimensional manifolds. The main contribution extends previous obstruction results, which required local conformal flatness, to general compact four-manifolds by incorporating the Weyl curvature tensor.

The methodology relies on exploiting the conformal invariance of the Yang–Mills functional in dimension four. By integrating the Yang–Mills equations against suitable solutions of the linearized problem—corresponding to infinitesimal conformal and gauge symmetries—the author derives conservation laws involving the stress-energy tensor. These are carefully evaluated in the neck regions where the weak limit connection and the emerging bubbles interact, yielding precise balancing conditions through asymptotic expansions of the curvature using Rivière's gauge construction.

The key result is that a certain two-tensor involving the stress-energy tensors of the inverted bubble and the limit connection, together with the Weyl tensor of the underlying manifold, must be traceless and symmetric. As a concrete application, the author proves that on CP² with gauge group SU(2), a 1-instanton bubble cannot form on a −1-instanton limit. Furthermore, in general bubble-trees, if all bubbles are (anti-)self-dual with absolute degree one, the bottom bubble determines the self-duality type of the entire branch.

These results provide new structural constraints on bubble-tree compactifications of Yang–Mills moduli spaces beyond the locally conformally flat setting.
original_abstract: We study bubbling for sequences of Yang-Mills connections on closed four-manifolds and we derive a compatibility of Pohozaev type between the weak limit connection and the bubble formed at a concentration point, involving the Weyl tensor of the background metric. This yields obstruCtions to bubbling extending earlier results of Yin beyond the locally conformally flat case. As an application, we rule out certain bubbling configurations on CP2.

title: The similarity of irreducible operators in factors
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the similarity of irreducible operators in von Neumann algebra factors, extending classical results from the algebra of bounded linear operators on Hilbert spaces to the broader setting of separable factors. An operator in a factor is irreducible if the von Neumann algebra it generates is an irreducible subfactor.

The main contribution is a complete characterization of when a normal operator in a separable factor is similar to an irreducible operator. Specifically, the authors prove that for a separable factor with dimension greater than four, a normal operator N is similar to an irreducible operator if and only if two conditions hold: the range projection of N minus any scalar is never equivalent to a projection dominated by its complement, and the set {I, N, N²} is linearly independent over the complex numbers.

The methodology relies on developing new techniques for projections and maximal abelian self-adjoint subalgebras (MASAs) in factors. A key intermediate result, of independent interest, establishes that for suitable MASAs, certain projections can be conjugated into the MASA via unitary operators. The authors also connect their work to Shen's generator invariant G for type II₁ factors and extend results to spectral operators using Dunford's decomposition theory.

The significance of this work lies in unifying and generalizing previous results confined to specific factor types, providing a framework applicable across type I, II, and III factors. The paper also identifies open questions about characterizing operators similar to irreducible operators or generators in general separable factors.
original_abstract: An operator $T$ in a separable factor $\mathcal{M}$ is said to be irreducible in $\mathcal{M}$ if the von Neumann subalgebra $W^*(T)$ generated by $T$ is an irreducible subfactor of $\mathcal{M}$, i.e., $W^*(T)'\cap\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{C}I$. We say that $T$ is a single generator of $\mathcal{M}$ if $W^*(T)=\mathcal{M}$. In this paper, we study generators of separable factors related to maximal abelian self-adjoint subalgebras. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of normal operators in separable factors which are similar to irreducible operators.

title: Spectral radius and edge-disjoint spanning trees of $(k+1)$-edge-connected graphs
generated_summary:
This paper investigates spectral radius conditions that guarantee the existence of k edge-disjoint spanning trees in (k+1)-edge-connected graphs, addressing a problem posed by Zhang and Fan. The work is motivated by two fundamental questions: determining what additional conditions force graphs with prescribed edge connectivity to contain k edge-disjoint spanning trees, and understanding the relationship between spanning tree packing numbers and graph eigenvalues.

The authors establish a tight spectral radius condition for the general case where k ≥ 3. Specifically, they prove that if G is a (k+1)-edge-connected graph of order n ≥ 3k+2 and its spectral radius ρ(G) satisfies a precise inequality involving the spectral radius of an extremal graph F_{n,k}, then G contains k edge-disjoint spanning trees unless G is isomorphic to F_{n,k}. The extremal graph F_{n,k} is explicitly constructed with a specific structure involving two disjoint vertex sets with prescribed edge configurations.

The methodology relies on the classical Nash-Williams–Tutte theorem characterizing graphs with k edge-disjoint spanning trees, properties of the Perron vector, spectral radius bounds for graphs with given minimum degree, and optimization over convex sets. The proof proceeds by analyzing partitions of the vertex set and applying combinatorial and spectral arguments to establish the result.

This work extends a previous result by Zhang and Fan for the case k=2 to all k ≥ 3, representing significant progress on the general problem. The authors also propose a conjecture regarding extremal graphs for the broader case of (k+c)-edge-connected graphs with arbitrary c.
original_abstract: Let $κ'(G)$ and $τ(G)$ denote the edge connectivity and the spanning tree packing number of a graph $G$, respectively. Recently, Zhang and Fan [J. Graph Theory 112 (2) (2026) 128--144] posed the problem of finding a tight spectral radius condition for an $m$-edge-connected graph $G$ to guarantee $τ(G)\ge k$ for $k+1\le m\le 2k-1$, and solved the case $k=2$ and $m=3$. In this paper, we study the general case $m=k+1$ for $k\ge 3$. We obtain a tight spectral radius condition for a $(k+1)$-edge-connected graph to contain $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, and characterize the corresponding extremal graph. More precisely, we prove that if $k\ge 3$ and $G$ is a $(k+1)$-edge-connected graph of order $n\ge 3k+2$, and $ρ(G)\ge ρ(F_{n,k})$, then $τ(G)\ge k$ unless $G\cong F_{n,k}$, where $F_{n,k}$ is the graph with vertex set $U\cup T$, in which $U=\{u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_{n-4}\}$ and $T=\{v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4\}$, such that $F_{n,k}[U]\cong K_{n-4}$, $F_{n,k}[T]\cong K_4-e$ with missing edge $v_1v_2$, and $E_G(T,U)=\{v_i u_j : i \in \{1,2\},\ 1 \le j \le k-1\} \cup \{v_i u_j : i \in \{3,4\},\ 1 \le j \le k-2\}$. We also give a heuristic discussion of the more general case $m=k+c$ with $0\le c\le k-1$ and propose a conjecture on the structure of the corresponding extremal graphs.

title: Bounding the density of spherical polygon packings
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of packing congruent regular spherical polygons (triangles, squares, pentagons) on the unit sphere, developing both computational methods for constructing good packings and optimization-based upper bounds on packing density. The work extends techniques previously applied to spherical cap packings into the more challenging domain of polygonal shapes.

The methodology combines two complementary approaches. For lower bounds, the authors formulate packing as a manifold optimization problem, using smooth Riemannian optimization to find near-optimal configurations. For upper bounds, they extend the Lovász theta number framework to an infinite Cayley graph on the special orthogonal group SO(3), yielding semidefinite programming problems whose variables are positive-semidefinite kernels parameterized via the representation theory of SO(3). Central to both approaches is the concept of "admissible" polygons, which enables clean algebraic characterization of when two polygon copies are interior-disjoint.

Key results include proving maximality of several polygon packings, determining that the kissing number of the icosahedron is 4, and narrowing the octahedron kissing number to 7 or 8. However, the tetrahedron kissing number—the original motivation—remains unresolved, with the upper bound barely improving upon the simple volume bound. The theta prime bound proves sharp only for sphere-tiling configurations.

This work represents a significant advance in computational packing theory, providing the first systematic framework for bounding packing numbers of non-circular shapes on the sphere, while identifying the development of higher-order bounds as a critical future direction.
original_abstract: We determine putative optimal packings of regular spherical polygons via optimization on smooth manifolds. For several cases, we establish maximality by extending the Lovász theta number to Cayley graphs on the special orthogonal group ${\rm SO}(3)$. To this end, we introduce an algebraic criterion characterizing when congruent regular spherical polygons have disjoint interiors, leading to a unified formulation of the packing constraints. Using harmonic analysis on ${\rm SO}(3)$, we reduce the theta number to a trigonometric sum-of-squares problem, which can be solved via semidefinite programming.

title: Mini-Batch Stochastic Halpern Algorithm for Nonexpansive Fixed point Problems
generated_summary:
This paper presents a convergence analysis of the mini-batch stochastic Halpern algorithm for solving nonexpansive fixed point problems. While the deterministic Halpern algorithm finds the closest point in a nonexpansive mapping's fixed point set to an initial point, it becomes computationally impractical when the mapping is defined as the mean of a very large number of nonexpansive mappings. The mini-batch stochastic variant addresses this by replacing the full mapping evaluation with a stochastic approximation computed from a randomly sampled mini-batch of component mappings at each iteration.

The authors prove that the algorithm converges in mean square to the closest fixed point when using a diminishing step size and an increasing batch size, establishing this result through three supporting lemmas. They further derive convergence rate bounds under certain conditions, showing that with a diminishing step size of order 1/(k+1) and increasing batch sizes, the algorithm achieves an O(√K/K) convergence rate, which is comparable to existing deterministic methods.

The increasing batch size requirement parallels similar conditions needed for the mini-batch stochastic Krasnosel'skiĭ–Mann algorithm's almost-sure convergence, though the authors note that practically, finite batch size increases within computable ranges suffice for acceleration. The work identifies extending the analysis to heavy-tailed noise settings as an important future direction, since the current analysis assumes bounded variance of the stochastic mapping.
original_abstract: The Halpern algorithm is a powerful fixed point approximation method for finding the closest point in the fixed point set of a nonexpansive mapping to the initial point. However, in practice, it is not necessarily true that this algorithm can be applied to large-scale fixed point problems, since the computation of the nonexpansive mapping is expensive. In this paper, we present mini-batch stochastic Halpern algorithm to resolve the issue caused by the computational difficulty of the mapping. We preform a convergence analysis demonstrating that the algorithm with diminishing step sizes and increasing batch sizes converges in mean square to the closest point in the fixed point set to the initial point. We also perform a convergence rate analysis demonstrating that convergence speed of the algorithm depends on the settings of the diminishing step sizes.

title: Unveiling universality, encloseness, and orthogonality in dynamics
generated_summary:
This paper advances the understanding of Sarnak's conjecture on Möbius orthogonality by investigating three interconnected dynamical concepts: universal models for characteristic classes, enclosedness (uniform relative ergodicity), and orthogonality properties of bounded sequences with topological systems.

The main contribution is establishing that certain characteristic classes of measure-preserving automorphisms admit universal topological models—single topological systems that realize all automorphisms in the class as invariant measures. Notably, the authors prove that the class of automorphisms whose ergodic components have discrete spectrum admits a universal model, constructed explicitly using group automorphisms on infinite-dimensional tori. This is surprising given Serafin's theorem that the full zero-entropy class has no universal model.

The paper introduces the notion of enclosed (uniformly relatively ergodic) automorphisms, characterized by the separability of ergodic components in Ornstein's d-bar metric, and shows these systems have a common ergodic extension. This property bridges non-ergodic and ergodic dynamics and connects to the orthogonality problem through a key theorem: if a topological system's invariant measures yield enclosed automorphisms belonging to a characteristic class for which orthogonality is known for uniquely ergodic systems, then full orthogonality follows.

Among the applications, the authors prove that zero-entropy topologically URE systems satisfy logarithmic Sarnak's conjecture, provide new criteria for logarithmic Sarnak's conjecture in terms of piecewise Markov URE properties of Pinsker factors of Furstenberg systems, and give a purely ergodic-theoretic proof of Tao's equivalence between vanishing second Gowers-Host-Kra seminorms and local Fourier uniformity.
original_abstract: Motivated by Sarnak's conjecture on Möbius orthogonality, we investigate the general problem of orthogonality for a bounded sequence to topological models of characteristic classes of measure-preserving automorphisms. Our main observation is that whenever a strong form of such orthogonality holds in a system $(X,T)$ then the orthogonality holds for all topological systems in which each ergodic measure yields an automorphism that is measure-theoretically isomorphic to one arising from an ergodic measure in $(X,T)$. This leads us to study two purely dynamical problems: the existence of universal topological models for characteristic classes of measure-preserving automorphisms and the existence of a common ergodic extension for a measurable family of ergodic automorphisms. We show that the class of automorphisms with relative discrete spectrum over the identity factor--as well as several related classes including the weakly mixing case--admit universal models. We also highlight potential applications to the orthogonality phenomena. Moreover, we show that if the set of all measure-theoretic eigenvalues of a zero entropy system $(X,T)$ is countable, then $(X,T)$ satisfies Sarnak's conjecture along a subsequence of full logarithmic density.

title: Existence and uniqueness for singular stochastic differential equations with piecewise well-behaved coefficients
generated_summary:
This paper establishes existence and uniqueness results for one-dimensional stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with singular, distributional drift and potentially degenerate, discontinuous diffusion coefficients. Such equations arise naturally in threshold diffusion models, including the threshold Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (T-CIR) and threshold Chan-Karolyi-Longstaff-Sanders (T-CKLS) processes used in quantitative finance.

The authors develop two complementary approaches. The first is a novel pasting technique that constructs global solutions by combining local solutions from auxiliary SDEs defined on overlapping intervals separated by threshold interfaces. Under natural compatibility conditions on the coefficients across regimes, the authors prove both weak existence with uniqueness in law and, independently, strong existence with pathwise uniqueness. The strong pasting result is new in the literature. The second approach extends classical pathwise uniqueness criteria of Le Gall and Engelbert-Schmidt to the non-uniformly elliptic setting, where the diffusion coefficient may vanish. This yields a new comparison theorem for threshold SDEs.

A key application provides the first complete weak and strong existence and uniqueness results for the T-CKLS model, where coefficients are piecewise constant with possible discontinuities at finitely or countably many thresholds, encompassing the T-CIR process as a special case. The framework also accommodates skew diffusions, sticky interfaces, and reflecting boundaries.

These results significantly extend classical SDE theory by removing the standard requirements of uniform ellipticity and continuity of the diffusion coefficient, offering flexible tools applicable to a broad class of regime-switching and interface models.
original_abstract: We study existence and uniqueness for one-dimensional generalized stochastic differential equations with singular coefficients, including distributional drift and degenerate, possibly discontinuous, diffusion coefficients. Such singularities naturally encode changes in the dynamics at thresholds, including reflecting, skew, or sticky interface behavior. We develop two directions. We provide sufficient conditions for pathwise uniqueness, under weak existence and uniqueness in law, without assuming uniform ellipticity or continuity of the diffusion coefficient. We also investigate a pasting approach for generalized stochastic differential equations that transfers strong existence and pathwise uniqueness, as well as weak existence and uniqueness in law, from local component equations to a global solution. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first explicit pasting theorem yielding pathwise uniqueness in the setting of generalized stochastic differential equations. As an application, we establish the first existence and uniqueness results for a class of skew sticky threshold Cox-Ingersoll-Ross-type diffusions, including the threshold Chan-Karolyi-Longstaff-Sanders process.

title: Nonsmooth Nonconvex-Concave Minimax Optimization: Convergence Criteria and Algorithms
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the convergence guarantees for general nonsmooth nonconvex-concave minimax optimization problems, removing the commonly required weak convexity assumption that limits applicability in settings such as neural networks with ReLU activations and certain statistical learning problems.

The main contribution is the introduction of the *Goldstein saddle stationary point* (GSSP), a new convergence criterion for constrained nonsmooth minimax problems that extends existing Goldstein stationary point concepts from nonsmooth minimization to the minimax setting. The authors also consider convergence with respect to the primal function using *generalized Goldstein stationary points* (GGSPs). Building on these criteria, they propose two stochastic zeroth-order algorithms: a single-loop method called Projected Gradient-Free Descent Ascent (PGFDA) for finding approximate GSSPs of the objective, and a double-loop variant (NL-PGFDA) for finding approximate GGSPs of the primal function. Both methods leverage randomized smoothing techniques and require only Lipschitz continuity of the objective, covering both nonconvex-concave and nonconvex-strongly-concave settings.

The authors establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for both algorithms without relying on weak convexity assumptions, which distinguishes their results from prior work. Numerical experiments on poisoning attack problems across multiple datasets validate the practical effectiveness of the proposed methods. This work broadens the theoretical foundation for nonsmooth minimax optimization, making it applicable to a wider class of real-world machine learning problems.
original_abstract: This paper considers constrained stochastic nonsmooth minimax optimization problem of the form $\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{X}}\max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{Y}}f\left(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\right)=\mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y};\mathbfξ)]$, where the objective $f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ is concave in $\mathbf{y}$ but possibly nonconvex in $\mathbf{x}$, the stochastic component $F(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y};\mathbfξ)$ indexed by random variable $\mathbfξ$ is mean-squared Lipschitz continuous, and the feasible sets $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ are convex and compact. We introduce the notion of $(η_x,η_y,δ,ε)$-Goldstein saddle stationary point (GSSP) to characterize the convergence for solving constrained nonsmooth minimax problems. We then develop projected gradient-free descent ascent methods for finding $(η_x,η_y,δ,ε)$-GSSPs of the objective function $f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ with non-asymptotic convergence rates. We further propose nested-loop projected gradient-free descent ascent methods to establish the non-asymptotic convergence for finding $(η,δ,ε)$-generalized Goldstein stationary points (GGSP) [Liu et al., 2024] of the primal function $Φ(\mathbf{x})\triangleq\max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{Y}}{f}\left(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\right)$. It is worth noting that our algorithm designs and theoretical analyses do not require additional assumptions such as the weak convexity used in prior works on nonsmooth minimax optimization [Lin et al., 2025, Boţ and Böhm, 2023].

title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Optimization with Rademacher Perturbations and Momentum Gradient Tracking
generated_summary:
This paper introduces Zeroth-Order Momentum Gradient Tracking (ZO-MGT), a distributed optimization algorithm designed for non-convex multi-agent problems where gradient information is unavailable and data heterogeneity across agents is severe. The key contribution lies in integrating momentum-based variance reduction with dynamic gradient tracking to eliminate the steady-state bias caused by data heterogeneity while avoiding the variance explosion that plagues standard zeroth-order gradient tracking methods.

The algorithm employs two-point Rademacher perturbation-based gradient estimators, requiring only two function evaluations per iteration, combined with momentum smoothing and gradient tracking across a decentralized peer-to-peer network. The authors establish convergence guarantees through Lyapunov stability analysis, proving an O(1/T) convergence rate for non-convex objectives. Critically, the analysis reveals that the heterogeneity-induced error floor is suppressed at a quadratic rate of (1−β)², where β is the momentum parameter, enabling aggressive bias reduction with large momentum values.

Experiments on non-convex binary classification with extreme non-IID data partitioning demonstrate that ZO-MGT achieves consensus errors approximately two orders of magnitude lower than standard distributed zeroth-order gradient descent, while maintaining superior wall-clock efficiency compared to deterministic full-coordinate methods that require O(d) queries per iteration. The sensitivity analysis confirms the theoretically predicted quadratic suppression scaling. This work provides a practical framework for derivative-free distributed optimization in black-box settings such as large language model fine-tuning and adversarial attacks, with potential for hardware acceleration through discrete bitwise operations.
original_abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization is indispensable for complex non-convex tasks where explicit gradients are computationally prohibitive or strictly inaccessible. For deploying ZO methods over distributed heterogeneous networks, the gradient tracking technique is often employed to eliminate structural data biases. However, the inherent variance of derivative-free estimators is also amplified. To overcome this problem, we propose Zeroth-Order Momentum Gradient Tracking (ZO-MGT), which integrates momentum-based variance reduction with dynamic gradient tracking. Specifically, ZO-MGT that requires exactly two function queries per iteration can avoid costly batch sampling and prevent variance explosion, while eliminating structural biases. Moreover, by utilizing Rademacher perturbations, it preserves optimal query efficiency and enables bitwise hardware acceleration. We theoretically analyze the convergence of ZO-MGT and establish an $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ convergence rate. Furthermore, we prove that a large momentum factor can aggressively suppress the heterogeneity-induced bias floor at a remarkable quadratic rate of $\mathcal{O}((1-β)^2)$. Numerical experiments under extreme data heterogeneity verify that ZO-MGT can effectively overcome traditional tracking failures with accelerated convergence guarantees, while achieving significantly tighter consensus.

title: A chain of $\mathbb{C}^{*}$-flips of the moduli spaces of $\mathcal{O}$-twisted rank 2 constrained framed Hitchin pairs on a smooth curve
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the birational geometry of moduli spaces of constrained framed Hitchin pairs on smooth complex projective curves, establishing a structural relationship between two chains of birational transformations arising from variation of GIT quotients.

The main contribution is the construction of a surjective commutative forgetful diagram connecting the chain of ℂ*-flips of the moduli space of 𝒪_X-twisted rank 2 constrained framed Hitchin pairs to the chain of ℂ*-flips of the moduli space of framed modules. This diagram arises naturally from forgetting the Higgs field component. The methodology relies on establishing equivalences between stability conditions: the authors prove that a constrained 𝒪_X-twisted framed Hitchin pair is δ-semistable (respectively δ-stable, for nonzero framing) if and only if its underlying framed module is δ-semistable (respectively δ-stable). These equivalence results, which hold more generally for smooth complex projective varieties of arbitrary dimension, are the technical foundation enabling the comparison of the two flip chains.

Key results include explicit descriptions of the birational maps in both chains, showing that intermediate spaces are smooth projective varieties related by blow-ups along subvarieties of codimension two. The authors also derive explicit Poincaré polynomial formulas for the moduli spaces involved. The work extends previous results on GIT-theoretic approaches to birational geometry of moduli spaces, providing a unified framework that connects the study of framed modules with that of Hitchin pairs through constrained objects, thereby deepening understanding of how these moduli spaces are related through wall-crossing phenomena.
original_abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective curve. We prove that there exists a surjective commutative forgetful diagram from the chain of $\mathbb{C}^{*}$-flips of the moduli spaces of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$-twisted rank 2 constrained framed Hitchin pairs on $X$ to the chain of $\mathbb{C}^{*}$-flips of the moduli spaces of rank 2 framed modules on $X$.

title: Ribbon graphs and meromorphic functions
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the interplay between ribbon graphs and meromorphic functions on compact Riemann surfaces, establishing a correspondence between immersed graphs in the Riemann sphere and triples consisting of a surface, a meromorphic function, and a ribbon graph. The main contribution is a systematic framework connecting the combinatorics of ribbon graphs to the analytic properties of meromorphic functions, along with an analysis of when immersed graphs in the sphere can be lifted to such triples.

The methodology centers on two complementary constructions: a direct one, where a ribbon graph on a Riemann surface is pushed forward via a meromorphic function to produce an immersed graph in the sphere, and an inverse construction that recovers a surface, meromorphic function, and ribbon graph from an immersion of an abstract multigraph. The paper develops existence results for spanning ribbon graphs with prescribed combinatorial properties on surfaces of given genus.

A key finding is the remarkable flexibility in the relationship between surface topology and graph combinatorics: a surface of genus g admits spanning ribbon graphs whose underlying abstract graphs can have any graph genus at most g, including planar graphs. This demonstrates that surface genus is not rigidly encoded in the graph's combinatorics. Consequently, naive expectations relating self-intersection counts of immersed graphs to surface genus generally fail, necessitating more subtle invariants incorporating both ribbon structure and analytic data.

The significance lies in opening a new direction connecting combinatorial topology with complex analysis, with particular implications for understanding lower bounds on self-intersections and the geometry of meromorphic functions.
original_abstract: Let Y be a compact Riemann surface, phi:Y -> CP^1 a meromorphic function, and Gamma in Y a ribbon graph avoiding the critical points of phi. Then phi(Gamma) is an immersed graph in CP^1. Conversely, given an immersion im:Theta to bCP^1 of an abstract multigraph Theta without vertices of valence 1 or 2, we describe a construction of a compact Riemann surface Y and a meromorphic function phi_{im}:Y in CP^1 such that phi_{im}(Gamma)=im(Theta). We investigate the relation between the topology of Y and the combinatorics of Gamma. In particular, for a surface of genus g we construct spanning ribbon graphs whose underlying abstract graphs have arbitrary prescribed graph genus g' smaller or equal g, including the planar case. As a consequence, the number of self-intersections of φ(Gamma) cannot, in general, be controlled solely by the genus of Y. We establish general lower bounds for the number of self-intersections and formulate several open problems, with emphasis on planar ribbon graphs.

title: Three-dimensional time-periodic problem on the Boltzmann equation with external force
generated_summary:
This paper resolves the open problem of establishing the existence and stability of time-periodic solutions to the three-dimensional Boltzmann equation for hard-sphere gases under time-periodic external forces. Previous results were limited to spatial dimensions five and above, leaving the physically crucial three-dimensional case unresolved.

The methodology combines semi-group theory at low frequencies with refined energy methods at high frequencies, employing macro-micro decomposition around the global Maxwellian equilibrium. The authors work within hybrid homogeneous Besov spaces rather than standard L² spaces for the low-frequency analysis. A key technical challenge arises from velocity-weighted and velocity-derivative terms generated by the external force, which are handled through regularity propagation of microscopic components at high frequencies, with partial regularity of the external force sacrificed at low frequencies. The asymptotic stability analysis employs time-weighted estimates at both low and high frequencies, with higher decay rates first established at high frequencies and then iteratively transferred to lower frequencies.

The main results establish three theorems: global existence of solutions to the Cauchy problem, asymptotic stability with explicit time-decay rates, and existence and stability of time-periodic solutions via Serrin's method. The time-periodic solution is constructed as the limit of a Cauchy sequence using the Banach Completeness Theorem. These results also apply to stationary solutions when the external force is time-independent, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of the dynamical behavior of the Boltzmann equation in physically realistic three-dimensional settings.
original_abstract: The time-periodic problem on the Boltzmann equation with a given time-periodic external force in the three-dimensional whole space has remained open since it was first studied in [13] for only spatial dimensions not less than five. The goal of this paper is to give an affirmative answer to this problem provided that the external force is sufficiently small in the function space $\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{R};\dot{B}^{-3/2}_{2,\infty}\cap\dot{H}^N)$ with $N\geq 4$. The proof is based on Serrin's method through studying the global-in-time stability of the Cauchy problem with time-periodic external forces. As a direct consequence, the result also yields the existence and stability of stationary solutions to the physically realistic three-dimensional Boltzmann equation when the external force is time-independent.

title: Generalized String-Stability Criteria for Consensus Protocols
generated_summary:
This paper develops a unified frequency-domain framework for analyzing string stability in leader-follower multi-agent systems governed by arbitrary-order consensus protocols under r-predecessor directed communication topologies. The work bridges two traditionally separate fields—consensus theory and string-stability analysis—by establishing fundamental connections between communication structure, protocol order, and disturbance propagation.

The methodology centers on deriving a common scalar propagation transfer function that governs how disturbances transmit through the formation. By modeling agents as chains of integrators under first-, second-, and general m-th order consensus protocols with r-predecessor communication, the authors obtain closed-form frequency-domain expressions for the disturbance-propagation coefficient. The shift-invariant Toeplitz structure of the r-predecessor topology enables this exact scalar characterization without requiring explicit eigenvalue decompositions.

original_abstract: This paper presents a unified string-stability framework for leader-follower multi-agent systems governed by first-, second-, and m-th order consensus protocols operating under an r-predecessor directed communication topology. While string stability has been extensively studied for specific vehicle models and individual consensus protocols, existing results remain fragmented across protocol orders and do not identify the fundamental factors governing disturbance amplification or attenuation. This work shows that, for all consensus orders, string stability is dictated solely by the communication richness r, while the protocol order m influences only the mid-frequency transient behavior. In particular, the low-frequency gain of the disturbance propagation coefficient is inversely proportional to r for every m, implying that higher-order consensus cannot overcome the structural limitation imposed by insufficient communication and that, under the adopted H-infinity-based string-stability definition and the present framework, string stability is achievable if and only if r >= 2. This establishes a structural-dynamic separation principle that unifies and generalizes classical platoon results, providing new insight into the interplay between topology and controller design in cooperative driving and multi-agent coordination. The framework is developed under idealized identical-agent and fixed-topology assumptions, providing a baseline for future robust extensions. Numerical simulations corroborate the analysis and illustrate how m and r jointly shape disturbance propagation along the formation.

title: On a Boundary-Initial Value Problem for Fractional Differential Equation with Sequential Caputo derivatives

Theoretical well-posedness is established under the admissible conditions α + β > 1 and α > β, with an explicit eigenfunction-series representation derived using bivariate Mittag-Leffler functions.

original_abstract: In this paper, we investigate a fractional differential equation involving sequential Caputo derivatives, motivated by recent research on fractional models with multiple memory effects. Using techniques inspired by earlier works on sequential fractional operators, we derive the exact analytic solution of the problem in terms of the bivariate Mittag-Leffler function. Additionally, several useful properties of the bivariate Mittag-Leffler function are formulated to support the solution construction. Furthermore, we develop a numerical scheme using a sequential reformulation and the L1-finite element method.

title: Inhomogeneous parabolic equations with Hardy potential and memory on the Heisenberg group

original_abstract: We study a class of inhomogeneous parabolic equations on the Heisenberg group $\mathbbm{H}^N$ with Hardy-type singular potentials, nonlocal memory terms, and a space-time forcing term: \begin{align} \partial_tu-Δ_{H}u=λ\frac{ψu}{\|\cdot\|^{2}_{H}}+\frac{1}{Γ(γ)}\int_0^t(t-τ)^{γ-1}|u(τ)|^{p}dτ+t^αf \text{ in } \,\mathbbm{H}^N\times (0,T). \end{align} Here, $γ\in [0,1),$ $α\in (-1,\infty),$ $p>1,$ $λ>0,$ and $ψ(\cdot)=|\nabla_{H}\|\cdot\|_{H}|^2,$ where $\nabla_H$ is the horizontal gradient associated to $Δ_H.$ Also, $\|\cdot\|_{H}$ and $Δ_{H}$ denote the Korányi norm and sub-Laplacian associated with the sub-Riemannian geometry of $\mathbbm{H}^N,$ respectively. The combination of a singular Hardy potential and a memory kernel introduces significant analytical challenges. Using a Harnack-type inequality adapted to the Heisenberg group setting, we obtain quantitative positivity estimates that enable a detailed blow-up analysis. We identify parameter regimes depending on $p,γ,α$ leading to finite-time blow-up or instantaneous blow-up, and establish local well-posedness in the absence of the Hardy potential. These results reveal an interplay between the spatial singularity, temporal nonlocality and a time-dependent forcing term. Finally, under a suitable lower bound on the forcing term $f,$ we derive an explicit lifespan estimate for local-in-time solutions.

title: Birational Geometry of Quot Schemes on smooth projective curves via Stable Pairs

The methodology centers on exploiting an isomorphism between Quot scheme fibers and moduli spaces of stable pairs at large stability parameter values. By varying the stability parameter through critical values, the authors obtain a sequence of birational models connected by explicit wall-crossing transformations. The key results include complete descriptions of the nef, effective, and movable cones of the Quot scheme fibers, with all edges of nef cones spanned by semiample line bundles. The authors show that the movable cone decomposes into finitely many nef cone chambers corresponding to the various stable pair moduli spaces. When the quotient rank permits, additional small Q-factorial modifications arise from dualizing the quotient construction.

original_abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g \geq 2$ over $\mathbb C$, and let $E^0$ be a vector bundle on $C$. We investigate the birational geometry of the Quot scheme ${\rm Quot}_C(E^0, k, n)$, which parametrizes quotients of $E^0$ of rank $k$ and degree $n$, and its fiber $\mathcal Q_L$ over ${\rm Pic}^n(C)$ for $n \gg 0$. Our main tool is the moduli space of stable pairs, which yields small $\mathbb Q$-factorial modifications (SQMs) of ${\rm Quot}_C(E^0, k, n)$ and $\mathcal Q_L$. We explicitly describe the nef, movable, and effective cones of each SQM. Consequently, we prove that $\mathcal Q_L$ is a Mori dream space and that the determinant morphism ${\rm Quot}_C(E^0, k, n) \to {\rm Pic}^n(C)$ is a Mori dream morphism.

title: On The Ellipticity Of Generalised Monge-Ampère Equations on Vector Bundles
generated_summary:

These equations generalize well-studied line bundle versions and are connected to stability conditions in algebraic geometry.

The authors introduce "Condition E," a tractable criterion related to ellipticity, and establish its relationship to ellipticity through key lemmas: Condition E implies ellipticity, and ellipticity along a continuous path preserves Condition E. Their strategy for constructing counterexamples involves finding continuous paths of metrics that satisfy the relevant equation throughout, where Condition E holds initially (at the trivial solution) but fails at the endpoint, thereby demonstrating that ellipticity must break down along the path.

The main results show that ellipticity is not preserved along continuity paths for the vector bundle Monge-Ampère equation, the σ_k equations (for k ≥ 3), the vector bundle J-equation, and the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills equation when the bundle rank is at least 3 and the manifold dimension is at least 3. In contrast, the σ_2 equation preserves ellipticity along continuity paths, and all equations preserve ellipticity in dimension two.

These findings are significant because ellipticity is essential for applying the method of continuity—a standard technique for solving such equations—and help explain why establishing Donaldson-Uhlenbeck-Yau-type existence theorems for these generalized equations remains challenging beyond the large-volume limit.
original_abstract: In this paper, we study the ellipticity of the vector bundle versions of the Monge-Ampère, $J$, dHYM and $σ_{k}$-equations at a point. These are nonlinear geometric partial differential equations defined on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact Kähler manifold. We show that when both the dimension of the manifold and the rank of the bundle are greater than or equal to three, these equations do not preserve ellipticity along continuity paths. However, the $σ_{2}$-equation does preserve ellipticity along continuity paths.

title: A Convexified Eulerian Framework for Scalable Coordination of Massive DER Populations
generated_summary:

original_abstract: This paper proposes a scalable coordination framework with aggregator-side privacy protection for storage-like distributed energy resources (DERs). The framework adopts a two-layer architecture. At the macroscopic layer, building upon an \emph{Eulerian} modeling perspective, the DER population is represented as a continuum whose density evolution is governed by a partial differential equation (PDE), such that the computational complexity is independent of the population size. To address the bilinear non-convexity in this PDE-constrained optimization problem, we develop a convexification method that combines finite-volume discretization with a flux-lifting technique, reformulating the macroscopic problem into a sparse linear program (LP). The LP solution yields a unified, state-dependent broadcast signal for population coordination. Furthermore, a Wasserstein-based relaxation is introduced to replace rigid cyclic constraints and provide additional operational flexibility for improved economic performance. At the microscopic layer, individual resources autonomously recover local setpoints from the broadcast signal and their local states, while an upstream data-mixing protocol aggregates individual states into a macroscopic density histogram without exposing raw individual states to the aggregator. Numerical studies validate the scalability, feasibility, and economic effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Optimum adaptation of a Steiner network
generated_summary:

The methodology centers on analyzing the cost function representing total network length and its partial derivatives with respect to Steiner point and terminal node positions. By applying implicit differentiation to the first-order optimality conditions, the authors derive an update formula expressing the Steiner point displacement as a product of the inverse Hessian matrix and a mixed partial derivative matrix, applied to the terminal perturbation vector. A central theoretical result is the rigorous proof that the Hessian matrix is always invertible for any valid ESMT, established through careful analysis of its decomposition into non-negative definite summands and demonstration that their nullspace intersection is trivial.

Key results include the first-order approximation theorem and numerical demonstrations showing the method performs well when the tree topology remains unchanged. For larger perturbations, the authors propose an iterative stepwise approach that subdivides the displacement into smaller increments, maintaining accuracy even for substantial shifts.

The significance lies in providing a computationally efficient alternative to full recomputation, with practical applications in dynamic network design. The authors identify extension to soft obstacle scenarios as a primary future direction, where recomputation costs are substantially higher.
original_abstract: The Euclidean Steiner tree problem, normally posed in two dimensions, seeks to connect a set of prescribed terminal nodes by placing additional nodes, known as Steiner points, with edges connecting such nodes either to another Steiner point or a terminal node, and with the placements minimising the sum of all the edge lengths of the associated tree. We consider a problem in which we start with a known solution to a Steiner tree problem, and the terminal positions are then perturbed. A first-order approximation theorem is established for efficiently updating the Steiner point positions to recover a Steiner tree solution after the perturbations to terminal nodes. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of our approach (including a stepwise application for large perturbations) as well as its limitations.

title: Lean-certified four-point HRT results for three lattice points and one off-lattice point

Assuming a nontrivial linear dependence among the four time-frequency shifted copies of a nonzero function f, the authors first invoke the three-point HRT theorem to show the coefficient of the off-lattice shift must be nonzero. They then construct the lattice-cyclic subspace V generated by f and demonstrate it is invariant under the off-lattice shift. Using projective commutation relations, they show V is invariant under a semigroup that, by Kronecker's theorem on dense orbits (exploiting linear independence over the rationals), is dense in the plane. Strong continuity then extends this invariance to all time-frequency shifts, forcing V to equal the entire L² space by irreducibility of the Schrödinger representation. However, the large-covolume condition implies the lattice Gabor system is incomplete, yielding a contradiction.

The significance lies both in the mathematical result advancing understanding of the HRT conjecture and in its formal certification in Lean 4, contributing to the growing body of machine-verified mathematics in harmonic analysis.
original_abstract: We record a Lean-certified theorem package for the four-point Heil--Ramanathan--Topiwala configuration \[ Λ=\{0,a,b,ν\}\subset \R^2, \qquad \Lzero=\Z a+\Z b, \qquad ν=r a+s b, \] with $a$ and $b$ linearly independent. The principal certified theorem states that if $|\symp(a,b)|>1$ and $1,r,s$ are linearly independent over $\Q$, then for every nonzero $f\in L^2(\R)$ the four vectors \[ f,\qquad π(a)f,\qquad π(b)f,\qquad π(ν)f \] are linearly independent. A second certified theorem treats the rational-coordinate case $r,s\in \Q$, where the configuration lies in a finer full-rank lattice and linear independence follows from Linnell's theorem. The paper is written in standard mathematical prose. An appendix records the precise Lean certification ledger and the explicit analytic inputs used by the formal development and a download link is provided.

title: Temporal decay estimates for global solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations with the Coriolis force
generated_summary:

The main contribution is extending the range of exponents for which faster-than-heat-equation decay rates hold, broadening the permissible range of the Lebesgue exponent *p* from a bounded subinterval of [2, 3) to the full range [2, ∞], while also providing decay estimates for spatial derivatives of arbitrary order.

The authors employ direct estimates of the Duhamel integral representation, dispersive estimates for the linearized propagator arising from the Coriolis term, Littlewood-Paley decomposition techniques, and fractional Leibniz rules for nonlinear term estimation. The strategy parallels the author's recent work on viscous β-plane equations.

The key results demonstrate that global solutions are smooth away from the initial time, satisfy the energy equality, and exhibit temporal decay rates of the form *t*^(−3/2(1/2−1/p)−m/2−1/2) for *m*-th order derivatives in *L^p* norms, which are faster than the corresponding heat equation decay by a factor of *t*^(−1/2). This improvement stems from the dispersive effects induced by the Coriolis rotation term, highlighting the regularizing influence of rotation on fluid dynamics and contributing to the broader understanding of dispersive-dissipative systems.
original_abstract: We consider temporal decay estimates for global solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations with the Coriolis force. We show that under several conditions including the smallness of the initial data, the solution decays as fast as the corresponding linearized solutions, and its decay rate is higher than expected from the flow of the heat equation. The estimates are derived for all $L^p$-norms with $p\in[2, \infty].$

title: A Temperature-Coupled Cahn-Hilliard-Stokes-Heat Model for Thermally Driven Phase Separation
generated_summary:

The main contribution is a novel temperature-dependent Landau-type bulk potential that smoothly transitions between a single-well landscape (homogeneous vapor phase) when the local temperature exceeds a saturation threshold and a double-well landscape (phase separation into liquid-rich and vapor-rich regions) when the temperature falls below it. This potential is embedded within a fully coupled diffuse-interface framework incorporating variable-density and variable-viscosity Stokes flow, advective phase-field dynamics, and heat transport.

On the analytical side, the authors establish local-in-time existence of weak solutions in two and three dimensions using a Schauder fixed-point argument, analyzing each component operator—heat, Cahn-Hilliard, and Stokes—individually before composing them. The proof accommodates mixed boundary conditions and the absence of global boundedness for the order parameter under polynomial potentials. For numerical implementation, a semi-implicit finite-element scheme employing Eyre-type convex splitting for the Cahn-Hilliard substep and Taylor-Hood elements for Stokes flow is developed in FreeFEM++.

Numerical experiments demonstrate isothermal phase separation behavior, gravity-driven sedimentation of dense phases, and thermally induced nucleation or suppression of phase-separated domains near heated or cooled boundaries. These results confirm that the model qualitatively reproduces condensation-like phenomena, providing a mathematically rigorous framework for studying moisture-related degradation in electrochemical energy systems.
original_abstract: We study a diffuse-interface model for thermally driven phase separation in viscous incompressible mixtures. The system couples a convective Cahn-Hilliard equation for the order parameter with a Stokes subsystem for the velocity-pressure field and a heat equation for the temperature. Temperature enters the bulk free energy through a Landau-type coefficient, while the phase field feeds back on the flow through concentration-dependent density and viscosity, yielding a phenomenological temperature-coupled Cahn-Hilliard-Stokes-Heat system. We motivate the chemical potential by a temperature-dependent Landau free energy and derive a priori estimates for the regularized subproblems. On the analytical side, we prove local-in-time existence of weak solutions for a regularized coupled system. On the numerical side, we propose a fully discrete finite element scheme combining a convex-splitting time discretization for the Cahn-Hilliard equation with an implicit treatment of viscous and thermal diffusion terms and a an implicit Stokes solve. Under impermeable velocity boundary conditions, the Cahn-Hilliard substep conserves mass, in the purely diffusive isothermal case, the convex-splitting discretization is unconditionally energy-stable for the Cahn-Hilliard free energy. Numerical experiments in two dimensions illustrate thermally driven spinodal decomposition, wall-induced phase separation near cooled walls, and phase separation in narrow channels under imposed thermal gradients. The simulations show the qualitative influence of key nondimensional parameters (such as the mass and thermal Péclet numbers, the Cahn number, the density and viscosity ratios, and the gravitational parameter $G$) on pattern formation, interface motion, and flow structure, and confirm that the proposed framework is a robust tool for studying thermally driven phase separation in confined geometries.

title: Moments and joint nonvanishing of symplectic $L$-functions
generated_summary:
This paper establishes the first asymptotic moment results for the standard (degree five) L-function associated with Siegel cusp forms of genus 2, averaged over a Hecke eigenbasis of weight k. The main result provides an asymptotic formula for a mixed moment involving both the standard L-function D(1/2, F) and the spinor L-function L(1/2, F), weighted by harmonic weights that, via Böcherer's conjecture (now a theorem of Furusawa and Morimoto), correspond to central values of spinor L-functions twisted by a quadratic character.

The methodology centers on Kitaoka's spectral summation formula—the higher-rank analogue of the Petersson formula for Sp(4)—combined with an approximate functional equation for the standard L-function. The authors analyze the diagonal, rank one, and rank two contributions from the formula. The rank two term, involving matrix Kloosterman sums and matrix Bessel functions, constitutes the most technically challenging part, requiring Poisson summation in matrix variables and a detailed analysis of Bessel function oscillation depending on proximity to orthogonal matrices. A key auxiliary result demonstrates square-root cancellation in certain exponential sums.

The asymptotic formula yields several important corollaries: a simultaneous nonvanishing result establishing that for sufficiently large k, there exist non-lift eigenforms where both D(1/2, F) and L(1/2, F) are simultaneously nonzero with D(1/2, F) positive, and a lower bound on the number of such forms. The positivity result is notable as it does not follow unconditionally from known period formulas.
original_abstract: We compute an asymptotic formula for a moment involving the spinor and the standard $L$-functions for holomorphic Siegel cusp forms of degree two and large weight $k$. Applications include simultaneous non-vanishing statements and lower bounds for second moments.

title: 3-Designs from $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$-Invariant Subspaces of $\mathbb F_q[X,Y]_k$
generated_summary:
This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing 3-designs from GL₂(𝔽_q)-invariant subspaces of the homogeneous polynomial space 𝔽_q[X,Y]_k. The central approach associates to each such invariant subspace W a GL₂(𝔽_q)-invariant family of k-subsets of the projective line PG(1,q), leveraging the natural group actions through fractional linear transformations on the projective line and the induced representations on homogeneous polynomial spaces. When k ≤ q, the evaluation map identifies W with a subcode of the projective Reed–Solomon code, and the authors prove that any nonempty invariant block family forms a 3-(q+1, k, λ) design. They further show that supports of minimum-weight codewords in the associated subcodes and supports of fixed-weight codewords in their duals also yield 3-designs. A Cayley transform reformulation on the unit circle expresses block membership conditions as explicit linear relations among elementary symmetric polynomials.

Applying this framework to Lucas subspaces W_k^Luc, the authors derive concrete block set descriptions and establish emptiness/nonemptiness criteria. Notably, for q = pᵉ and k = pᵐ + 1, the construction produces the Steiner system S(3, pᵐ+1, q+1) precisely when m < e. The framework also recovers previously known constructions as special cases and resolves an open problem by determining explicit design parameters left unspecified in prior work on ternary codes, using the weight distribution of the ternary Melas code. This unified approach bridges permutation group theory and coding theory, replacing ad hoc constructions with a coherent algebraic methodology.
original_abstract: We present a uniform framework for constructing \(3\)-designs from \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_q)\)-invariant subspaces of \(\mathbb F_q[X,Y]_k\), the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree \(k\). Given such a subspace \(W\), we associate a \(\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb F_q)\)-invariant family of \(k\)-subsets of \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)\). Whenever this family is nonempty, it forms a \(3\text{-}(q+1,k,λ)\) design. When \(k\le q\), the evaluation map on \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)\) identifies \(W\) with a subcode \(C_W\) of the projective Reed--Solomon code. We also show that the supports of minimum-weight codewords in \(C_W\), as well as the supports of suitable fixed-weight codewords in the dual code \(C_W^\perp\), yield further \(3\)-designs. Via the Cayley transform, the construction is transferred to the unit circle \(U_{q+1}\subseteq \mathbb F_{q^2}^{\times}\), where the block conditions become explicit linear relations among elementary symmetric polynomials. Applying this framework to the Lucas subspaces, we obtain explicit block descriptions, classify the cases in which the defining conditions reduce to a single equation, and establish several emptiness and nonemptiness results. In particular, for \(q=p^e\) and \(k=p^m+1\), we show that the associated block family is nonempty if and only if \(m\mid e\), in which case it yields the Steiner system \(S(3,p^m+1,q+1)\). Finally, in the ternary case \(p=3\) and \(k=7\), we use the weight distribution of the ternary Melas code to determine the design parameters left undetermined by Xu et al. (Designs, Codes and Cryptography: Vol. 92, 2024).

title: Discretization error from regularized Reinforcement Learning to continuous-time stochastic control
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the discretization error that arises when feedback policies learned via regularized reinforcement learning on discrete-time data are applied to continuous-time stochastic control problems governed by stochastic differential equations. The authors decompose this error into two components: the gap between discrete-time and continuous-time regularized Bellman equations due to time discretization, and the gap between regularized and unregularized formulations due to entropy regularization.

The methodology employs a relaxed control formulation, comparing policies through their induced value functions under true continuous-time dynamics rather than through pointwise policy differences. A key technical innovation involves estimating differences in density functions via Fokker-Planck equations rather than tracking individual trajectories, which circumvents challenges posed by the limited regularity of discrete optimal value functions whose gradients scale as O(h⁻¹/²).

The main results establish that the discretization error achieves a nearly linear rate in the time step h, with dependence on the exploration parameter ε. Specifically, the regularized policy approximation contributes an error of order |ε|, while discrete feedback control approximation contributes O(h/εᴺ), where N is the control space dimension. Optimally choosing ε = h^{1/(N+1)} yields an overall error of O(h^{1/(N+1)}). As a byproduct, the authors establish uniform-in-h regularity bounds for entropy-regularized value functions and policies under SDE-induced transition kernels, improving upon existing bounds that diverge as the discretization step vanishes. These results provide the first quantitative discretization error estimates for feedback controls in this setting.
original_abstract: This paper establishes a rigorous connection between regularized discrete-time reinforcement learning (RL) and continuous-time stochastic optimal control. Specifically, classical RL algorithms are typically solving a regularized discrete-time Bellman equation. We study the discretization error, namely, the gap between the optimal policy induced by the regularized discrete-time Bellman equation and the true optimal feedback control of the underlying continuous-time stochastic control problem. By deriving quantitative convergence rates for this gap, we provide a rigorous foundation for understanding the stability and implementation of exploratory RL policies in stochastic continuous-time environments.

title: Revisiting Subgradient Dominance in Robust MDPs: Counterexamples, Hardness, and Sufficient Conditions
generated_summary:
This paper critically reexamines the subgradient dominance property underlying projected subgradient descent (PSD) methods for solving robust Markov decision processes (RMDPs). The authors demonstrate that prior analyses claiming PSD converges to globally optimal policies in general RMDPs are flawed.

The main contribution is threefold. First, the authors construct a simple counterexample—an RMDP with a finite uncertainty set of just two models—showing that the robust total cost admits a strictly suboptimal local minimum where PSD can become trapped, disproving the claimed subgradient dominance property. Second, they establish NP-hardness results showing that finding approximately optimal policies is computationally intractable even when subgradients are efficiently computable, specifically for finite transition uncertainty sets and sa-rectangular finite transition uncertainty sets with finite cost uncertainty sets. These hardness results are proven via reductions from satisfiability problems, ruling out polynomial-time algorithms unless P equals NP.

Despite these negative findings, the authors identify two sufficient conditions that restore PSD's convergence guarantees: when either the worst-case transition kernel or the worst-case action-value function is unique for each policy. These conditions encompass several important special cases, including regularized RMDPs, sa-rectangular and r-rectangular uncertainty sets, cost-robust MDPs, and convex MDPs.

The significance of this work lies in correcting fundamental misunderstandings in the RMDP optimization literature while precisely delineating the boundary between tractable and intractable settings for PSD-based approaches.
original_abstract: Projected subgradient descent (PSD) has gained popularity for solving robust Markov decision processes (RMDPs) because it applies to a broader class of uncertainty sets than traditional dynamic programming. Existing work claims that RMDPs with a general compact uncertainty set satisfy the subgradient dominance property, under which exact PSD converges to an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy in a polynomial number of updates (e.g., Wang et al., 2023). We show that these claims are incorrect. Even when the uncertainty set has cardinality two, the RMDP objective is not subgradient-dominant and can admit suboptimal strict local minima. Moreover, we prove that finding an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy can be NP-hard even in settings where subgradients are efficiently computable: (i) finite transition uncertainty sets and (ii) $sa$-rectangular finite transition uncertainty sets with finite cost uncertainty sets. original_abstract: We extend the concept of a partial group action to non-associative algebras in a variety \(\mathcal{V}(I)\), solve the globalization problem within \(\mathcal{V}(I)\) and examine its universal property. original_abstract: Let $n=hw$, where $h$ and $w$ are integers with $h,w \ge 2$. We determine the set of possible intersection numbers of two $n \times n$ latin squares having the additional `Sudoku' constraint based on a $w \times h$ grid of $h \times w$ boxes.

original_abstract: We consider the long-range random conductance model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ at the critical exponent: the jump rate between sites $x$ and $y$ decays as $\mathbf{a}(x,y) |x-y|^{-(d+2)}$, where $\mathbf{a}(x,y)$ are i.i.d. uniformly elliptic conductances. As a consequence, we deduce quenched convergence of the random walk to Brownian motion under the anomalous $\sqrt{t \log t}$ scaling. original_abstract: We study additively graceful labelings of signed graphs on stars and double stars. original_abstract: The Method of Ellipcenters (ME), introduced in~\cite{ME2025} for strongly convex quadratic minimization, uses two gradient evaluations per iteration: one at the current iterate and one at a companion point on the same level set. We extend ME to the broader class of strongly convex functions with Lipschitz continuous gradient, and prove that ME matches the convergence rate of gradient descent with exact line search on this class. When the two gradient directions are linearly independent, a midpoint argument exploiting the level-set symmetry yields a further per-step improvement, which is global when the angle between the two gradients is uniformly bounded away from zero. title: A goodness-of-fit test for the logistic propensity score model under nonignorable missing data

original_abstract: Logistic regression is widely used to model the propensity score in the analysis of nonignorable missing data. In this paper, we propose a new goodness-of-fit testing procedure for the logistic propensity score model under nonignorable missing data. The proposed test is based on an unweighted sum-of-squared residuals constructed from the marginal missingness mechanism and accommodates the partial observability of the outcome. We establish the asymptotic distribution of the test statistic under both the null hypothesis and general alternatives, and develop a bootstrap procedure with theoretical guarantees to approximate its null distribution. We show that the resulting bootstrap test attains asymptotically correct size and is consistent, with power converging to one under model misspecification. title: A Nearest-Neighbor Hard-Core Model on a Penrose Graph

original_abstract: We prove that the maximal graph-density of an independent set in a Penrose P3 tiling considered as a planar non-directed graph is equal to $(57 - 25 \sqrt{5})/2 \approx 0.54915$ despite the fact that the graph is bipartite. Accordingly, the extreme Gibbs measure of the nearest-neighbor hard core particle model on this graph is unique for sufficiently large values of the particle activity. title: Old and new Schrödinger eigenvalue localisation
generated_summary:

original_abstract: Unconditional guaranteed lower and upper eigenvalue bounds are mandatory for the understanding of the Schrödinger eigenvalue spectrum and its spectral gaps. While upper eigenvalue bounds are naturally induced by conforming discretisations, guaranteed lower eigenvalue bounds (GLB) are less immediate. This paper clarifies the adaptation of nonconforming GLB from the harmonic eigenvalue problem and discusses their comparison for general and piecewise constant potentials. A fine-tuned extra-stabilised scheme is proposed and found superior in numerical comparisons. This new direct calculation of GLB is compatible with adaptive mesh-refinement and successfully circumvents the appearance of maximal mesh-size parameters in former GLB based on post-processing. Computational benchmarks also investigate guaranteed upper eigenvalue bounds (GUB) for two-sided eigenvalue control by conforming test functions associated to the underlying nonconforming computations. title: On the dynamic behavior of the network SIRS epidemic model

Numerical simulations on a five-node network corroborate the theoretical findings and suggest that the region of attraction of the endemic equilibrium encompasses all initial conditions with nonzero infection, motivating conjectures about almost global asymptotic stability for future investigation.
original_abstract: We study the Suscectible-Infected-Recovered-Susceptible (SIRS) epidemic model on deterministic networks. For connected but otherwise general interaction patterns and heterogeneous recovery and loss-of-immunity rates, we identify a fundamental parameter R_0 (the basic reproduction number), which fully characterizes the qualitative dynamic behavior of the system. This parameter is the dominant eigenvalue of a rescaled version of the interaction matrix, whose rows are normalized by the corresponding recovery rates. We prove that a transcritical bifurcation occurs as R_0 crosses the threshold value 1. Specifically, we show that, if R_0 does not exceed 1, then the disease-free equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable, whereas, if R_0 is larger than 1, then the disease-free equilibrium is unstable and there exists a unique endemic equilibrium, which is asymptotically stable. As a byproduct of our analysis, we also identify key monotonicity properties of the dependence of the endemic equilibrium on the model parameters (the interaction matrix as well as the recovery rates and the loss-of-immunity rates) and obtain a distributed iterative algorithm for its computation, with provable convergence guarantees. Our results extend existing ones available in the literature for network SIRS epidemic models with rank-one interaction matrices and homogeneous recovery rates (including the single homogeneous population SIRS epidemic model).

title: Modeling Gaps in Hydropower Cascading System Models: A Systematic Review of Rule-Based Formulations

original_abstract: The coordination of cascading hydropower systems represents a fundamental challenge in modern energy systems engineering, requiring a sophisticated balance between multi-reservoir physics, stringent environmental regulations, and dynamic market participation. As intermittent energy sources increase, the transition to high-fidelity hydropower modeling has become a core requirement for ensuring power system reliability, long-term energy resilience and affordability. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of 131 seminal articles through the exclusive lens of optimization-based approaches, intentionally omitting pure simulation and heuristic methods to focus on rigorous mathematical formulations. A generalized 10-equation mathematical framework is established as a formal baseline, capturing the full physical and hydraulic behavior of cascading systems, including spatiotemporal inflow routing, storage-to-elevation relationships, head-dependent power generation, and prohibited operating zones. Each article is evaluated against every equation of this Standard Model in a systematic census documenting which physical relationships are included, simplified, or omitted, providing an empirical measure of modeling fidelity across the field. Modeling simplifications are evaluated through the lens of grid reliability rather than water management performance alone. The review makes a focused technical case for mixed-integer linear programming with piecewise linear approximations as the optimal balance between physical accuracy and computational tractability, highlighting recent optimal regression techniques that minimize combinatorial overhead. Finally, a bibliometric analysis of solver usage identifies the near-absence of high-performance open-source solvers as a critical reproducibility barrier, and a promising avenue for broader adoption of high-fidelity cascading hydropower models.

title: A Bochner-type integration theory for random normed modules

original_abstract: We develop a measure and integration theory for random normed modules. Given a probability space $({\rm X},Σ,\mathfrak m)$, we introduce and study measures taking values into the space $L^0(\mathfrak m)$ of $\mathfrak m$-measurable functions quotiented up to $\mathfrak m$-a.e. equality. Moreover, we develop a Bochner-type integration theory with respect to an $L^0(\mathfrak m)$-valued measure $μ$, for maps whose target ${\rm M}$ is a complete random normed module with base $({\rm X},Σ,\mathfrak m)$, or equivalently an $L^0(\mathfrak m)$-Banach $L^0(\mathfrak m)$-module. Inter alia, we prove versions of the Radon-Nikodým theorem and of the Riesz-Markov-Kakutani representation theorem for $L^0(\mathfrak m)$-valued measures. We also outline several applications of our integration theory: we introduce a notion of martingale with values in a complete random normed module, we propose a definition of random Radon-Nikodým property and we discuss random sets of finite perimeter.

title: Emergence of Mandelbrot-like and Julia-like Structures in Parameter Slices of Rational Maps

The work poses precise open questions about the rigorous foundations of these observations and invites theoretical development connecting renormalization, parabolic bifurcation theory, and critical orbit interactions in rational families.
original_abstract: We study complex one-dimensional parameter slices in a three-parameter family of rational maps with two free critical points, obtained by imposing the existence of periodic orbits with prescribed multipliers. Using explicit parametrizations, we explore these slices numerically by analyzing the behavior of the critical orbits and approximating the corresponding connectedness loci. The computations reveal rich parameter space structures closely analogous to those arising in cubic polynomial families, including Mandelbrot-like sets. In addition, we observe regions exhibiting Julia-like structures embedded in parameter space, arising from the interaction between bounded and escaping critical orbits. While the appearance of such structures is well established in polynomial dynamics, it remains comparatively less explored in the setting of rational maps. Our results provide numerical evidence that these parameter slices contain subsets closely related to the period-one and period-two slices of cubic polynomial families. More precisely, certain regions appear to exhibit geometric and dynamical features consistent with embedded copies of these classical parameter spaces. These observations highlight how classical structures from polynomial dynamics can emerge naturally within parameter slices of rational maps.

title: Dimension Drop for Harmonic Measure on Ahlfors Regular Boundaries

The methodology centers on establishing uniform decay estimates for density ratios of harmonic measure versus Hausdorff measure across dyadic scales using David-Mattila lattices. The proof proceeds by contradiction: assuming no significant density jump occurs forces comparability between harmonic and Hausdorff measures across scales, enabling application of Tolsa's theorem relating L²-beta numbers to Riesz transforms. The Riesz transform of harmonic measure is expressed through Green function gradients, bounded via capacity density conditions. The geometric non-flatness hypothesis forces linear growth of accumulated beta numbers, eventually contradicting density controls when sufficiently many generations are considered. A careful averaging argument eliminates dependence on the Ahlfors regularity constant in the general-dimensional result.

Two main theorems are established: one for general dimensions under L²-beta number conditions with a threshold independent of the regularity constant, and one for the planar case under an L∞ non-flatness condition exploiting dimension-specific relationships between flatness parameters. These results advance understanding of a fundamental open problem concerning optimal dimension drop bounds for harmonic measure.
original_abstract: We provide quantitative estimates for the dimension drop of harmonic measure. We show that for a domain $Ω= \mathbb{R}^{n+1} \setminus E$ where $E$ is an $s$-Ahlfors regular compact set satisfying a uniform $L^2$-based non-flatness condition $β_2 \ge δ_0$, the dimension of its harmonic measure is strictly less than $s$ for $s \in (n - cδ_0^2, n]$. For planar domains, we establish an analogous quantitative threshold $s_0 = 1 - cδ_0^2$ under Azzam's uniform non-flatness condition $β_\infty + β_{\operatorname{hole}} \ge δ_0$.

title: Modeling and Control for Distributed Measurements of the Earth's Energy Imbalance

title: Graphon Limits of Graph Reaction--Diffusion Equations

original_abstract: A graph reaction--diffusion (RD) equation is a system of differential equations that is defined on the nodes of a graph. Consider a sequence of growing graphs that converges in cut norm to a limiting graphon. We show that the solutions of the sequence of graph RD equations converge in $L^p$ norm, for $p \in [1,\infty]$, to the solution of a limiting nonlocal RD equation, which we call a graphon RD equation. Furthermore, we show a large numbers result for a stochastic particle process that consists of a random walk and a birth-death process on graphs. For a sequence of graphs that converge in cut norm to a limiting graphon, the sequence of stochastic processes converges in probability to the solution of the graphon RD equation.

title: $E_6$-local systems from cubic threefolds

original_abstract: We produce infinitely many local systems on (level covers of) the moduli space of smooth cubic threefolds, with algebraic monodromy group equal to the exceptional group $E_6$. title: Sharp bounds for covering with large cliques and independent sets

original_abstract: Let $n(k_1, k_2)$ be the least integer $n$ such that there exists a graph on $n$ vertices in which every vertex is contained in both a clique of size $k_1$ and an independent set of size $k_2$. original_abstract: We consider minimax (saddle-point) problems of the form max_{c \in C} min_{β\in S} g(c; β), where C and S are compact convex sets, and g is concave-convex.
