title: Topologically protected interface modes in multi-band damped lattice models

original_abstract: Tridiagonal $k$-Toeplitz operators provide a natural framework for modelling one-dimensional $k$-periodic lattice systems. A fundamental connection is obtained between Coburn's lemma for tridiagonal $k$-Toeplitz operators and the existence of edge modes. A complete analysis of tridiagonal interface operators satisfying global inversion symmetry is then presented. These results are applied to finite one-dimensional $k$-periodic chains of damped resonators that satisfy both local and global inversion symmetry. title: A dichotomy for hypergraph Zarankiewicz problems on axis-parallel boxes

original_abstract: We study the Zarankiewicz problem for $r$-partite, $r$-uniform intersection hypergraphs arising from $r$ families of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with prescribed directions $F_1, \dots, F_r \subseteq \{1, \dots, d\}$. title: Rigorous High-Order Hausdorff Dimension Estimation of Limit Sets of Continued Fraction Iterated Function Systems via B-Splines

original_abstract: We develop a method for the rigorous estimation of Hausdorff dimensions of limit sets produced by continued fraction iterated function systems. Our method is based on the approximation of a Perron-Frobenius operator using the finite element method with B-splines as the choice of basis functions. This choice provides key numerical advantages including higher-order convergence and computational flexibility. We prove an analogue of Falk and Nussbaum's result on "hidden positivity" for B-spline quasi-interpolants to give rigorous upper and lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimensions of various limit sets. title: Bulk-Surface Coupled PDE with an Open Boundary

original_abstract: We study a bulk-surface coupled Laplace system involving an embedded open boundary. The problem is reformulated as an integro-differential equation using boundary integral representations, for which we establish existence and uniqueness of the solution. A Wiener-Hopf technique is employed to study the solution regularity and derive asymptotic expressions for the edge singularity. Building on these results, we develop a finite element method that incorporates the singularity structure and provide a rigorous error analysis. title: Magnetic uncertainty in variable geometry

original_abstract: In this paper, we study Hardy-type uncertainty principles and unique continuation properties for linear covariant Schrodinger equations with variable coefficients in the presence of bounded electric and magnetic potentials. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the leading coefficients, we prove that any solution exhibiting super-quadratic exponential decay at two distinct times must vanish identically. Under an additional structural assumption on the coefficient matrix $G$, we further establish a Hardy-type result at the quadratic exponential scale. We also obtain an analogous uniqueness result for the heat equation with variable-coefficient magnetic perturbations. Our results unify and extend previous works in two directions: they recover the constant-coefficient covariant case treated by Barcelo-Fanelli-Gutierrez-Ruiz-Vilela when $G=I$, and the variable-coefficient non-magnetic case considered by Federico-Li-Yu when $A=0$. The proofs combine logarithmic convexity arguments with Carleman estimates adapted to variable-coefficient covariant Schrödinger and parabolic flows. Although our approach follows the general strategy introduced by Escauriaza-Kenig-Ponce-Vega, substantial new difficulties arise from the interaction between the variable metric and the magnetic structure, which requires new weight functions and refined commutator estimates.

title: Computing the Exchange Number in Graphs with respect to Cycle Convexity
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the exchange number parameter under cycle convexity in graphs, where cycle convexity is defined by an interval function that "infects" a vertex if it lies on a cycle within the induced subgraph formed by adding it to an existing set. The exchange number measures the maximum cardinality of an E-independent set, where a set is E-independent if removing some pivot element prevents the remaining set from generating that pivot through the convex hull operation.

The authors establish both hardness results and tractable cases. From a computational complexity perspective, they prove that the decision version of the exchange number problem is NP-complete even for K₅-free graphs, via a reduction from 3-SAT. On the positive side, they derive closed-form expressions for several graph classes: trees, cycles, complete graphs, complete multipartite graphs, graphs with universal vertices, and unicyclic graphs, all yielding polynomial-time computations. For chordal graphs whose blocks form a single chain, they provide a formula expressing the exchange number as a function of the number of blocks. They also characterize n-vertex graphs whose exchange number equals n−1.

For graph products, the authors establish a lower bound for the Cartesian product and determine exact values for products of paths and complete graphs. They provide exact formulas for strong and lexicographic products of nontrivial connected graphs.

These results advance understanding of cycle convexity, a relatively new graph convexity with connections to knot theory and dissemination processes, by systematically mapping the computational landscape of its exchange number parameter across diverse graph families.
original_abstract: Given a graph $G$, a subset $S \subseteq V(G)$ is \textit{cycle convex}, if for any vertex $v \in V(G) \setminus S$, the induced subgraph, $G[S \cup \{v\}]$ cannot form a cycle containing the vertex $v$. The \textit{exchange number} of $G$, denoted by $e_{cc}(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of an $\textit{$E$-independent}$ set of $G$. This paper studies the computational complexity of determining the exchange number of graphs and provides exact values for some graph classes. Given a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, we show that deciding whether $e_{cc}(G) \geq k$ is NP-complete even if $G$ is a $K_5$-free graph. In contrast, we characterize all $n$-vertex graphs $G$ with exchange number $n-1$ and obtain closed formulas for chordal graphs $G$ whose blocks lie in a single chain, which leads to polynomial-time algorithms for computing $e_{cc}(G)$. We also establish a lower bound for the exchange number of the Cartesian product of general graphs and by using the results of Anand et al. \cite{bijo2}, we derive an explicit formula for the exchange number of strong and lexicographic graph products.

title: Twisted Alexander Polynomials, Ribbon Homology Cobordisms, and the Thurston Norm

Key technical ingredients include extending representations of fundamental groups along ribbon cobordisms using the handle structure, and analyzing how zeroth twisted Alexander polynomials behave under the injective and surjective maps on fundamental groups induced by the cobordism. The divisibility relationship between these polynomials, combined with known connections between twisted Alexander polynomials, the Thurston norm, and fiberedness, yields the main results.

As corollaries, the authors recover previously known results: the genus is non-decreasing under ribbon concordance of knots, and fiberedness is preserved. The significance lies in providing purely classical, algebraic proofs of results previously established using more sophisticated Floer-theoretic techniques, suggesting that twisted Alexander polynomials can serve as a complementary tool for studying ribbon homology cobordisms.
original_abstract: Let $Y_-$ and $Y_+$ be two compact 3-manifolds with empty or toroidal boundary. A 4-dimensional ribbon homology cobordism is a homologically trivial cobordism built with 1-handles and 2-handles. In this note, following the work of Friedl and collaborators, we apply twisted Alexander polynomials to show that if there is a ribbon homology cobordism from $Y_-$ to $Y_+$ with $Y_-$ irreducible, then the unit ball of the Thurston norm of $Y_-$ contains that of $Y_+$. Moreover, we show in general that the fibered classes of $Y_+$ correspond to those of $Y_-$.

title: Modularity, Extensions and Connectivity in Infinite Matroids

This paper develops a comprehensive theory of modularity, extensions, and connectivity for infinite matroids, addressing the fundamental challenge that standard finite matroid definitions relying on rank subtraction fail in the infinite setting. The authors introduce the concept of a "mutual basis" — an independent set containing bases for every set in a family — as the foundation for defining modular pairs, modular flats, and skew families in infinite matroids, ensuring these notions specialize correctly to finite cases.

A central contribution is an amended definition of modular cuts for infinite matroids, adding closure under intersections of modular chains. The authors prove that the original finite definition fails for infinite-rank matroids — every such matroid admits a "modular cut" in the finite sense corresponding to no extension — while their revised definition restores the bijective correspondence between modular cuts and single-element extensions. They further show that quotients and projections, equivalent for finite matroids, diverge in the infinite setting, and identify conditions (finitariness plus finite rank difference) under which equivalence is recovered.

The paper introduces nullity as dual rank, establishes a simplified formula for connectivity requiring only one basis choice, and provides a geometric interpretation of multipartite connectivity via iterated guts extensions. Notable structural results include proving all modular matroids are finitary and characterizing modularity through line-hyperplane intersection. All results are formally verified in the Lean4 theorem prover, ensuring machine-checked correctness.
original_abstract: We generalize the well-studied notion of a modular pair of a finite matroid to arbitrary families of sets in infinite matroids, and use it to develop the theory of infinite matroids in several as-yet-unexplored areas. Our results include a complete theory of single-element extensions, a description of the relationship between quotients and projections, a proof that matroids for which every flat is modular must be finitary, and two new perspectives on the infinite matroid connectivity parameter λ. In most cases, existing theory for finite matroids either fails completely or does not extend in obvious ways, and as a result we develop multiple new techniques for reasoning about infinite matroids, including establishing well-behaved infinite analogues of nullity, local connectivity and skewness. We also point to an online repository containing formalized proofs of all our results using the lean4 proof assistant

title: Finite Riesz products and Ornstein non-inequalities on quantum tori
generated_summary:

Ornstein's classical result demonstrates that certain differential operators cannot be bounded by others in the L¹ norm unless they are linearly dependent. The authors extend this phenomenon to the quantum torus setting, where standard commutativity no longer holds.

The methodology relies on two key ingredients. First, the authors leverage finite Riesz product constructions from prior work by Kazaniecki and Wojciechowski on the commutative torus, which produce trigonometric polynomials witnessing the Ornstein non-inequality. Second, they exploit a deep continuity result of Haagerup and Rørdam showing that generators of irrational rotation algebras depend continuously on the rotation parameter θ. By treating the quantum torus as a small perturbation of the commutative case (θ = 0), the authors transfer estimates from the commutative setting to obtain non-commutative analogues.

The main result (Theorem 5.1) demonstrates that specific derivation operators on the quantum torus cannot satisfy L¹-type inequalities, constructing explicit trigonometric polynomials via non-commutative Riesz products that violate such bounds. This result extends to higher-dimensional quantum tori and anisotropic cases (Theorem 7.2).

The significance lies in initiating the study of Ornstein-type phenomena and Riesz products in non-commutative harmonic analysis, bridging classical results with the operator-algebraic framework of quantum tori and opening avenues for further research in non-commutative analysis.
original_abstract: We demonstrate a construction of products on the quantum torus $\mathbb{T}_θ^2$ that generalises the usual construction of finite Riesz products on the commutative torus $\mathbb{T}^2$. We explain why the former constitutes a natural analogue of the latter in the non-commutative setting and, based on this construction, as well as on previous results by K. Kazaniecki and the second author, we prove a non-commutative version of an Ornstein non-inequality.

title: A provably stable numerical method for the anisotropic diffusion equation in confined magnetic fields: Curvilinear coordinates and multi-block domains
generated_summary:
This paper extends a penalty-based numerical method for solving the anisotropic diffusion equation from Cartesian coordinates to curvilinear coordinate systems, addressing heat transport modeling in magnetic confinement fusion plasmas where parallel-to-perpendicular diffusion ratios can reach 10^10. The main contribution is demonstrating that the method remains provably unconditionally stable in curvilinear geometries with multi-block domain decomposition.

The methodology employs summation-by-parts (SBP) finite difference operators combined with a nonlinear penalty term that weakly enforces parallel diffusion along magnetic field lines via field line tracing. Complex geometries are handled by splitting the computational domain into multiple sub-blocks mapped to reference domains, with inter-block coupling achieved through simultaneous approximation terms analogous to discontinuous Galerkin approaches. Variable coefficient SBP operators embed metric information from the curvilinear coordinate transformation into the diffusion coefficient matrix.

Numerical verification through manufactured solutions confirms expected convergence rates for the perpendicular diffusion operator. Self-convergence tests with magnetic island configurations show degraded convergence rates, with errors concentrated at inter-block boundaries rather than at separatrices. The method successfully models solution profiles in highly shaped geometries using magnetic fields from the SPEC MHD equilibrium code, though time step limitations remain challenging.

The significance lies in enabling stable, high-fidelity anisotropic diffusion simulations in realistic fusion geometries featuring magnetic islands and separatrices, which are critical for understanding edge plasma transport and wall heat loading in fusion devices.
original_abstract: We present a robust and accurate numerical method for the anisotropic diffusion equation in curvilinear coordinates. This study extends the recent work [Muir et al., Computer Physics Communications, 2025] for solving the anisotropic diffusion equation in magnetic fields from Cartesian meshes to to curvilinear coordinates and complex geometries. The method uses summation by parts with simultaneous approximation terms for computing the diffusion perpendicular to field lines. The diffusion along field lines is computed using a penalty approach, similar to a simultaneous approximation term, but applied across the volume. To extend the method to complex geometry we use a multi-block approach with piecewise smooth structured meshes. That is, the domain is split into sub-grids, with locally adjacent boundaries coupled weakly using penalties. We prove the semi-discrete stability for the curvilinear implementation by deriving discrete energy estimates. The approach is verified though a number of numerical tests, which demonstrate the convergence properties of the method in multi-domain approach. Finally, we present a qualitative result generated in complex geometry and magnetic field, which is generated by the Stepped Pressure Equilibrium Code.

title: Incremental SVD Compression for Nonlinear Oldroyd Equations with General Memory Kernels
generated_summary:
This paper presents an online incremental singular value decomposition (SVD) compression strategy for efficiently handling the memory history term in mixed finite element discretizations of nonlinear Oldroyd viscoelastic flow equations with general memory kernels. The central challenge is that standard approaches require O(mN) storage and O(mN²) total work, where m is the number of spatial degrees of freedom and N is the number of time steps, due to the nonlocal-in-time integral term requiring access to all previous velocity states.

The proposed method compresses the velocity snapshot history by maintaining and incrementally updating a low-rank SVD representation. Under a numerical rank-r assumption, storage is reduced from O(mN) to O((m+N)r). The approach is kernel-agnostic, applying to both nonsingular and weakly singular memory kernels, and is integrated into a Mini element (P₁b-P₁) spatial discretization with Crank–Nicolson time stepping. For nonsingular kernels, the authors derive a tolerance-dependent perturbation estimate proving that the compressed scheme preserves baseline finite element accuracy when the compression tolerance is sufficiently small.

Numerical experiments on manufactured solutions with nonsingular and weakly singular kernels demonstrate that the compressed and uncompressed schemes produce nearly indistinguishable results while the compressed version achieves substantial reductions in memory and wall-clock time. A planar 4:1 contraction flow benchmark further confirms that compression does not materially alter representative viscoelastic flow patterns. This work offers a practical, kernel-independent approach to alleviating the memory burden in viscoelastic flow simulations, complementing existing kernel-specific acceleration techniques.
original_abstract: We study mixed finite element/Crank--Nicolson discretizations of a nonlinear Oldroyd problem with general nonsingular and weakly singular memory kernels. Direct evaluation of the history term requires storing all previous velocity snapshots, which leads to $\mathcal{O}(mN)$ memory and $\mathcal{O}(mN^2)$ work over $N$ time steps, where $m$ denotes the number of spatial degrees of freedom. To reduce this burden, we compress the velocity history online by an incremental singular value decomposition and use the compressed representation in the discrete memory term. Under an approximate low-rank assumption of numerical rank $r$, the storage decreases to $\mathcal{O}((m+N)r)$, while the total history-evaluation work becomes $\mathcal{O}(mNr+rN^2)$. For nonsingular kernels, we derive a tolerance-dependent perturbation estimate showing that the baseline finite element accuracy is retained when the compression tolerance is sufficiently small. We also extend the approach to tempered weakly singular kernels via convolution quadrature. Numerical tests show near-indistinguishable solutions from the uncompressed scheme for the reported tolerances, together with substantial memory savings and reduced wall-clock time.

title: Universal $2$-parameter $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}_{\infty}$-algebra
generated_summary:
This paper constructs the universal two-parameter N=2 supersymmetric W∞-algebra, denoted Ŵ^{N=2}_∞, which serves as a classifying object for vertex superalgebras of a specific generating type related to N=2 superconformal symmetry. The algebra is freely generated by fields organized into N=2 "diamonds" and is defined over a localized polynomial ring in two parameters.

The authors employ techniques from vertex algebra theory, including nonlinear Lie conformal superalgebras, SUSY W-algebras constructed via BRST cohomology, and the framework of vertex algebras over commutative rings. A key methodological insight is that Ŵ^{N=2}_∞ is a conformal extension of a tensor product of two copies of the previously known universal 2-parameter W∞-algebra, establishing it as a minimal N=2 supersymmetric extension.

The central results include proving that an infinite family of N=2 Y-algebras, defined as affine cosets of hook-type W-(super)algebras, arise as one-parameter quotients of Ŵ^{N=2}_∞ along explicit truncation curves. Using uniqueness of simple quotients determined by truncation curves, the authors establish a triality of isomorphisms among these algebras, confirming conjectures of Procházka and Rapčák. As a special case, this proves the longstanding Ito conjecture on coset realizations of principal W-superalgebras of type sl_{n+1|n}. Additionally, the authors establish strong rationality results for simple quotients of these W-superalgebras at specific levels, generalizing the rationality of N=2 minimal models, and classify their simple modules and fusion rules.
original_abstract: The universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $\mathcal{W}_{\infty}$ of type $\mathcal{W}(2,3,\dots)$ is a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $\mathcal{W}(2,3,\dots,N)$ for some $N$; under mild hypotheses, all such vertex algebras arise as quotients of $\mathcal{W}_{\infty}$. In 2017, Gaiotto and Rapčák introduced a family of such vertex algebras called $Y$-algebras, and conjectured that they fall into groups of three that are mutually isomorphic. This is a common generalization of both Feigin-Frenkel duality and the coset realization of principal $\mathcal{W}$-algebras in type $A$, and was proven in 2021 for the simple $Y$-algebras (i.e., one label is zero) by the first and third authors. In this paper, we extend this entire story to the $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal setting. First, we prove the 2013 conjecture of Gaberdiel and Candu that there exists a universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $\mathcal{W}^{\mathcal{N}=2}_{\infty}$ which is an extension of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal algebra, and has four additional generators in weights $i, i + \frac{1}{2}, i + \frac{1}{2}, i+1$, for each integer $i > 1$. This admits many $1$-parameter quotients which we call $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric $Y$-algebras, and we prove the dualities among these algebras which were conjectured in 2018 by Prochazka and Rapčák. A special case is the coset realization of the principal $\mathcal{W}$-algebra $\mathcal{W}^k(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1|n})$ which was conjectured in 1992 by Ito. As a corollary, we obtain the strong rationality of $\mathcal{W}_k(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1|n})$ for $k = -1 + \frac{1}{n+a+1}$ for all positive integers $n,a$, and we describe its module category. This generalizes Adamović's 1999 result on $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal models, which is the case $n=1$.

title: Global Hopf Bifurcation and Symmetric Periodic Solutions in Multi-Agent Systems with Neutral Distributed Delays
generated_summary:
This paper introduces and analyzes a multi-agent system (MAS) whose closed-loop dynamics incorporate distributed delays of both retarded and neutral type, modeled as neutral functional differential equations (NFDEs). Unlike prior work that predominantly considers discrete delays and retarded-type equations, this framework captures agents' continuous memory of past states and past derivatives, providing a more realistic representation of phenomena such as sensor averaging and network buffering.

The authors employ equivariant twisted Nussbaum-Sadovskii degree theory to study global Hopf bifurcation in the system. This topological approach enables classification of bifurcating solution branches according to their spatio-temporal symmetries without requiring restrictive analyticity assumptions typical of other NFDE methods. The methodology combines rigorous degree-theoretic analysis with symmetry-informed numerical simulations.

The key results establish sufficient conditions for local asymptotic stability of the consensus equilibrium, prove the existence of global connected branches of non-constant periodic solutions bifurcating from consensus when transversality conditions hold, demonstrate that these branches are unbounded under additional conditions, and classify the branches by their isotropy types. An illustrative example modeling coupled asset markets with fundamental and momentum trading strategies demonstrates numerically that bifurcating periodic solutions constitute locally stable periodic multiconsensus.

The significance of this work lies in extending equivariant degree methods to MAS contexts for the first time, bridging distributed neutral-type delay modeling with global symmetric bifurcation analysis, and providing a framework applicable to systems where continuous memory and derivative-dependent delays arise naturally.
original_abstract: We study the emergence of symmetric oscillatory behavior in multi-agent systems where each agent incorporates a continuous memory of its past states and past rates of change, modeled by distributed retarded and neutral delays. The closed-loop dynamics are described by a system of nonlinear neutral functional differential equations (NFDEs) with a high degree of symmetry, arising from a network of homogeneous agents. By reformulating the problem as a fixed point operator equation, we apply equivariant degree theory to establish rigorous conditions for unbounded global Hopf bifurcation from the consensus equilibrium. Our main results provide sufficient conditions for the local asymptotic stability of consensus and for the existence of unbounded global branches of non-constant periodic solutions with prescribed spatio-temporal symmetries. The question of whether such periodic solutions are stable (and therefore constitute periodic multiconsensus) is not resolved by the degree method; we address it in an illustrative example via numerical simulation. The example, which models eight coupled asset markets with momentum traders and fundamentalists, demonstrates how memory-driven instability can generate periodic boom-bust cycles across clusters of assets. The numerical experiments confirm the bifurcation predictions and reveal the stability of the resulting oscillations, illustrating the power of combining symmetric bifurcation theory with targeted numerical analysis.

title: Evaluation of Various Objective Functions for Optimal Reactive Power Flow Including Transformer Tap Changer Optimisation
generated_summary:
This paper presents a novel framework for solving the optimal reactive power flow (ORPF) problem with multiple objectives, addressing the challenge of balancing competing goals such as minimizing power losses, maintaining voltage profiles, and managing reactive power exchanges. The key contribution is an interdependence analysis method that systematically tunes weighting parameters for combining multiple objectives in a specific power grid, enabling informed selection of Pareto optimal solutions.

The methodology formulates the ORPF as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, incorporating transformer tap changer optimization. Objectives are combined quadratically to penalize large deviations and normalized consistent with the per-unit system to improve scalability across different network sizes. The optimization framework reads network data from pandapower, formulates the problem in Pyomo, and solves it using IPOPT, while transformer tap positions are discretized iteratively based on their influence. The approach is demonstrated on a high-voltage benchmark network from SimBench using 1000 historically-based network states.

Results show that the proposed method achieves Pareto optimal solutions with good performance across all considered objectives simultaneously. The evaluation highlights the importance of STATCOM-domain reactive power capability for managing voltage and reactive power in grids with high shares of decentralized renewable energy. This work is particularly significant given the increasing need for reactive power management during Germany's energy transition, as conventional generation providing ancillary services is progressively replaced by distributed renewable sources.
original_abstract: Modern distribution grids with high penetration of renewable generation provide substantial flexibility through distributed reactive power sources and transformer tap changers. This high degree of freedom can be exploited for optimisation. However, choosing an objective function for optimisation is not trivial, e.~g. minimising grid losses may lead to overvoltages and minimising voltage deviations may lead to higher reactive power flows to neighbouring system operators. Thus, this paper deals with the design of an objective function for the centralised optimisation of distributed reactive power sources and transformer tap changers. Different objectives for characteristic network quantities are investigated for the optimisation and optimised in a combined manner and separately. The consequences of optimising conflicting target values are then analysed. For the optimisation, various grid usage cases of a 110 kV benchmark power grid from SimBench are examined. The investigated power grid is characterised by a high proportion of renewable energy plants. The optimisation is carried out in a data-driven, object-oriented manner using the interior point method with open source software. At the end of the paper, a meaningful optimisation function with combined weighted objectives is derived and the results are analysed.

title: Heat Transfer Modeling in Enhanced Geothermal Energy: A Three-Temperature Approach for Solid, Injected, and Residing Fluids
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a three-way local thermal nonequilibrium (LTNE) framework for enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) that distinguishes among three separate temperature fields: injected fluid, resident fluid, and solid rock matrix. Unlike conventional models that assume local thermal equilibrium or use two-temperature LTNE formulations, this approach explicitly tracks the thermal evolution of injected cold fluid as it heats through contact with hot reservoir rock and resident pore fluid, using a concentration field to decompose fluid enthalpy into injected and resident components.

The numerical methodology employs an enriched Galerkin (EG) finite element method for spatial discretization, ensuring local mass conservation while maintaining computational efficiency. A sequential IMPES-type splitting strategy solves pressure implicitly, advances concentration explicitly using strong-stability-preserving Runge–Kutta time integration, and updates temperatures implicitly via BDF2. Flux-corrected transport stabilization prevents spurious oscillations in the advection-dominated concentration equation.

Numerical experiments demonstrate optimal convergence rates, validate that the model reduces to classical LTE and LTNE formulations in appropriate limits, and show that LTE assumptions break down under slow heat exchange and strong advection. A fractured reservoir simulation with 34 high-permeability channels reveals thermal structures along concentration fronts—including temperature jumps and enthalpy redistribution patterns—that remain hidden in averaged-temperature approaches.

This framework offers improved predictive capability for thermal breakthrough and reservoir lifetime estimation in EGS design, providing information inaccessible to conventional two-temperature models.
original_abstract: Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) involve strongly coupled, advection-dominated flow and heat transfer in fractured porous media. Conventional models typically assume local thermal equilibrium with a single effective fluid temperature or, at best, an averaged pore-fluid temperature, so the thermal evolution of injected cold fluid is only inferred indirectly. In this work, we develop a local thermal non-equilibrium (LTNE) model that explicitly resolves the temperature of injected fluid as it moves through the reservoir and exchanges heat with the hot rock and resident fluid. The key ingredient is a concentration variable that tracks the injected fluid and induces a three-way LTNE coupling among rock, resident-fluid, and injected-fluid temperatures. This framework distinguishes, at the continuum scale, how newly injected fluid parcels are heated by conductive and convective exchange, and predicts production-well temperatures without relying on bulk averages. To discretize the resulting nonlinear, advection-dominated system, we employ an enriched Galerkin (EG) finite element method for Darcy flow, temperature, and concentration, providing local mass conservation with relatively few degrees of freedom. We further design a flux-corrected transport (FCT) strategy for the EG concentration and temperature equations to enforce a discrete maximum principle and suppress nonphysical oscillations while preserving local conservation. Time integration uses an IMPES-type splitting combined with a strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta scheme. Numerical experiments for fractured EGS problems show that the proposed LTNE--EG--FCT framework captures injected-fluid heating paths and thermal breakthrough behavior not resolved by standard single-temperature or averaged LTNE models.

title: Lifting Cubic Realizations of Weak Orders in Types A and B
generated_summary:
This paper develops a formal framework for constructing cubic coordinate systems for posets by lifting them through towers of projections. The main contribution is the introduction of two directed graph structures—the pre-Reeb graph and the augmented pre-Reeb graph—associated with cylindrical projections between posets, which govern when cubic realizations and order-embedding cubic realizations, respectively, can be extended by adding a single new coordinate.

The methodology centers on cylindrical projections, defined as maps between posets whose fibers are total orders with additional structural properties. For such a projection from P to Q, the pre-Reeb graph captures vertical adjacency between horizontal equivalence classes, while the augmented version incorporates additional edges reflecting incomparability constraints. The key theoretical results establish that acyclicity of the pre-Reeb graph guarantees liftability of any cubic realization, while acyclicity of the augmented pre-Reeb graph guarantees liftability of order-embedding cubic realizations. For towers of cylindrical projections with acyclic augmented pre-Reeb graphs, this yields an inductive proof that the Dushnik-Miller order dimension equals the rank.

The authors apply this framework to deletion towers in the weak orders of types A and B. Pre-Reeb graphs in type A are shown to be Boolean lattice skeleta, while those in type B are skeleta of certain zonotopes. In both cases, augmented Reeb posets are total orders, establishing combinatorial uniqueness of the compatible order-embedding coordinates. This provides new structural insight into Reading's classical result that weak orders have order dimension equal to rank, while suggesting applications to permutoassociahedra and higher categorical associahedra.
original_abstract: We study cubic realizations of posets compatible with projection maps, meaning that the projection is represented by deletion of the last coordinate. For cylindrical projections, we introduce the pre-Reeb graph and the augmented pre-Reeb graph, which control compatible cubic lifts and compatible order-embedding cubic lifts, respectively. We apply this construction to the deletion towers in weak order of types \(A\) and \(B\). The pre-Reeb graphs are the \(1\)-skeleta of, respectively, cubes and certain zonotopes. In both cases, the augmented pre-Reeb graphs have reachability posets that are total orders, yielding combinatorial uniqueness of the compatible order-embedding cubic coordinates.

title: On $q$-convex hypersurfaces in Riemannian manifolds
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the topology of q-convex hypersurfaces immersed in Riemannian manifolds, where q-convexity means the sum of the smallest q principal curvatures is nonnegative at every point. The main contribution lies in establishing new vanishing and estimation results for Betti numbers of such hypersurfaces under curvature conditions on the ambient manifold, specifically lower bounds on the average of the smallest eigenvalues of the curvature operator.

The authors employ the Bochner technique, relating curvature conditions to the behavior of harmonic forms via the Hodge Laplacian. By combining estimates from the second fundamental form of the immersion with eigenvalue bounds on the ambient curvature operator, they derive differential inequalities that constrain the space of harmonic forms, thereby controlling Betti numbers.

The key results include several theorems showing that when the ambient manifold has sufficiently positive curvature operator and the hypersurface is q-convex, specific Betti numbers vanish or can be explicitly bounded. Notable consequences include "sphere theorems": convex hypersurfaces in manifolds with appropriately nonnegative curvature operators are rational homology spheres with finite fundamental groups, and in dimension three, are diffeomorphic to spherical space forms. When curvature bounds are negative, the authors obtain explicit upper bounds on Betti numbers depending on dimension, curvature, and diameter.

These results significantly generalize previous topological classification results for convex and 2-convex hypersurfaces in space forms to general Riemannian ambient spaces, providing an extrinsic analogue to recent intrinsic Bochner technique results of Petersen and Wink.
original_abstract: We prove that any closed, convex hypersurface in an $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-positive curvature operator is a rational homology sphere with finite fundamental group. The same conclusion holds for any $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-convex hypersurface, provided that the mean curvature satisfies a natural pinching condition. Both results follow from more general vanishing and estimation theorems for the Betti numbers of closed $q$-convex immersed hypersurfaces in $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, under a lower bound on the average of the smallest $(n-p)$ eigenvalues of the curvature operator.

title: CRITERIA: A network decomposition and elementary flux mode translation-based tool for computing equilibria of biochemical systems
generated_summary:
This paper presents CRITERIA (Computing paRametrized posITive EquilibRIA), a MATLAB-based computational tool that significantly enhances the derivation of analytic steady states for biochemical reaction networks, addressing key limitations of its predecessor, COMPILES. The main contribution lies in three methodological improvements: replacing the computationally expensive exhaustive network translation scheme with an efficient elementary flux mode-based approach for constructing weakly reversible, deficiency zero translations; reordering procedural steps to merge translated subnetworks before computing equilibria, thereby eliminating interdependencies in equilibrium expressions; and extending applicability to networks with positive kinetic deficiency.

The methodology combines independent network decomposition, elementary flux mode computation via the Canonical Basis Method, binary linear programming for constructing compatible reaction-to-reaction graphs, and graph traversal algorithms for determining translation complexes. Benchmarking across 26 biochemical models demonstrates that CRITERIA successfully parametrizes equilibria for all models, whereas COMPILES fails on 11, particularly for networks exceeding six reactions. CRITERIA completes most computations in under 7 seconds compared to COMPILES frequently exceeding the 3600-second time limit.

The authors demonstrate CRITERIA's utility by revealing that the EnvZ-OmpR signaling pathway admits exactly two or zero positive equilibria and by discovering absolute concentration robustness of the dCas9 species in the full CRISPRi toggle switch model. These applications illustrate how closed-form equilibrium parametrizations enable parameter-free structural analyses of complex biochemical networks, offering significant advantages over simulation-based approaches for studying multistationarity and robustness.
original_abstract: Understanding how biochemical systems settle into stable states, such as how protein concentrations reach equilibrium, is central to explaining cellular behavior and designing synthetic biological circuits. However, existing analytical tools for computing these equilibria, such as COMPILES, are limited by computational bottlenecks and can only be applied to a restricted class of reaction networks. In this work, we introduce CRITERIA (Computing paRametrized posITive EquilibRIA), a new computational framework that makes equilibrium analysis more efficient and broadly applicable. CRITERIA uses a graph-based approach built on elementary flux modes to streamline key steps in the computation. It also changes how the problem is solved by combining subnetworks into a single system before computing equilibria, which avoids complicated symbolic calculations required in previous methods. We demonstrate the usefulness of CRITERIA by studying biologically important systems, including the EnvZ-OmpR signaling pathway and a synthetic CRISPRi circuit. Our approach enables faster and more scalable analysis, allowing researchers to better understand how complex biochemical networks behave over time.

title: Wall-crossing of Instantons on the Blow-up
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the problem of counting instantons on the blow-up of C², where the Euclidean space-time origin is replaced by a complex projective line (2-sphere). The main contribution is a systematic analysis of how instanton-monopole configurations and their partition functions depend on stability conditions, revealing a rich wall-crossing structure organized through the combinatorics of super-partitions.

The authors employ the ADHM construction to formulate the equivariant volume of the instanton moduli space as a contour integral, using the Jeffrey-Kirwan residue prescription to select physical poles. The choice of poles depends on stability parameters that define different chambers separated by walls. The selected configurations are first represented as oriented bipartite graphs, then more efficiently described using super-partitions—generalizations of integer partitions featuring new "boundary boxes" visualized as triangles in super-Young diagrams.

Key results include explicit characterizations of stable super-partitions in each chamber, demonstrating how configurations reorganize across walls. In the blow-up chamber (the limiting case where stability parameters approach accumulation), only separable super-partitions contribute—those decomposable into pairs of ordinary integer partitions. This decomposition provides an alternative derivation of the celebrated blow-up formula, which bilinearly relates partition functions on the blow-up to those on the original geometry.

The significance of this work extends to multiple areas: it provides new computational tools for non-perturbative gauge theory, connects to integrable systems through Hirota differentials, and suggests generalizations to higher-dimensional blow-ups and theories with defects.
original_abstract: We study the instanton counting in four dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric gauge theories on the blow-up of $\mathbb{C}^2$: we start by formulating the instanton moduli space as a quiver variety, which we regularise by introducing two stability parameters, thus endowing it with a structure of infinitely many chambers separated by walls. Within a given chamber, we formulate the instanton partition function as a contour integral, which can be evaluated using the Jeffrey-Kirwan residue prescription. We characterise the physically relevant contributions in terms of bipartite oriented graphs and show that they can more efficiently be classified in terms of combinatorial objects called super-partitions. Within a given chamber, only certain types of super-partitions contribute and we show that the corresponding selection criteria are equivalent to stability conditions that have previously been proposed in the literature. We use this formalism to compare how the instanton counting changes when moving across walls between neighbouring chambers and provide explicit expressions for the corresponding partition functions. In a limiting chamber and using our approach, we show how to reproduce the Nakajima-Yoshioka blow-up formula.

title: p-adic elliptic polylogarithms and cubic Chabauty
generated_summary:
This paper advances Kim's nonabelian Chabauty programme to depth 3 ("cubic Chabauty") for elliptic curves with the origin removed, providing explicit computations of the depth 3 Chabauty set X(ℤ_p)_3 for elliptic curves of Mordell-Weil ranks 0, 1, and 2. The main contribution is expressing the functions cutting out X(ℤ_p)_3 as polynomials in p-adic elliptic polylogarithms, drawing a striking connection to the Goncharov-Levin elliptic Zagier formulas for the special value L(E,2).

The methodology combines p-adic Hodge theory, nonabelian Galois cohomology, and a linearization procedure that reduces the nonabelian cohomological problem to computations involving abelian Galois cohomology and Coleman integration. The authors develop algorithms for computing p-adic elliptic polylogarithm functions and apply resultant techniques to determine the vanishing locus in the rank 2 case.

Key results include verification of Kim's conjecture in several cases. For a rank 1 curve (37.a1), mock rational points present in the quadratic Chabauty locus are eliminated at depth 3, recovering exactly the integral points. Most notably, for the rank 2 curve 433.a1, the depth 3 locus coincides precisely with the set of integral points — the first verification of Kim's conjecture for a rank 2 elliptic curve. This represents significant progress, as rank 2 curves are beyond the reach of both classical Chabauty-Coleman and quadratic Chabauty methods.
original_abstract: The Chabauty--Coleman--Kim method, under favourable circumstances, describes the set of integral points of a hyperelliptic curve inside the $p$-adic zeroes of certain transcendental functions. For an elliptic curve of Mordell--Weil rank one, the Chabauty--Coleman--Kim set in depth 2 is given by the zeroes of a (finite union of) quadratic polynomial(s) in the $p$-adic logarithm of the elliptic curve and the local $p$-adic height at $p$. Here, we give an explicit formula for a finite set containing the Chabauty--Coleman--Kim set in depth 3 for an elliptic curve of rank at most 2 under an assumption on non-vanishing of a special value of a $p$-adic $L$-function. The finite set is given by the zeroes of a polynomial in $p$-adic elliptic polylogarithms. We use these formulas to verify new instances of Kim's conjecture.

title: On sums of two squares and a basis of order $2$
generated_summary:
This paper establishes that certain sets related to sums of two squares form a basis of order 2, meaning every sufficiently large positive integer can be expressed as a sum of two elements from the set. The main result (Theorem 1) shows that for integers *a* > 0 and *b* with *a* ≠ *b*, and for sufficiently large *N*, there exist two intervals of consecutive positive integers whose union sums to *N*, where for every integer *n* in either interval, at least one of *n* or *an* + *b* fails to be representable as a sum of two coprime squares. This implies that the set of integers *n* for which both *n* and *an* + *b* are representable as sums of two coprime squares forms a basis of order 2.

The methodology builds on and modifies constructions introduced by Ford, Konyagin, Maynard, Pomerance, and Tao for finding large gaps in sieved sets, as well as improvements by Ford and Gabdullin. The approach employs probabilistic methods, sieve theory, and careful analysis of integers composed of primes in specific congruence classes modulo 4. Numerical calculations establish that the key constant satisfies C(1/2) > 1/325565, providing an explicit parameter range.

The significance lies in extending gap results for sums of two squares to the basis problem and demonstrating the versatility of the sieving framework. The technique applies broadly to general sieving situations where classical methods for problems like prime gaps appear difficult to adapt, though for prime gaps specifically, stronger bounds are known through other approaches.
original_abstract: Let $\mathcal{R}$ denote the set of integers $n$ that can be represented as the sum $n = x^2 + y^2$ with $(x,y) = 1$. Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with $a>0$, $a \nmid b$. We show that for sufficiently large positive integer $N$ there are two strings of consecutive positive integers $I_{1}=\{n_1-m,\ldots, n_1+m\}$ and $I_{2}=\{n_2-m, \ldots, n_2+m\}$ such that $m = [(\log N) (\log \log N)^{1/325525}]$, $I_{1}\cup I_{2} \subset [1, N]$, $N = n_1 + n_2$, and for any $n\in I_{1}\cup I_{2}$ at least one of $n$ or $an+b$ does not lie in $\mathcal{R}$. In particular, we have $n(an+b)\notin \mathcal{R}$ for all $n\in I_{1}\cup I_{2}$.

title: Trivial extensions of Koszul Artin-Schelter regular algebras

original_abstract: Let $S$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded Koszul Artin-Schelter regular algebra and let $σ$ be a graded algebra automorphism of $S$. We study the stable category of graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules over the trivial extension algebra $S\ltimes S_σ(-1)$. We show that this category is triangle equivalent to the bounded derived category of finitely generated (ungraded) modules over the Koszul dual algebra of the Zhang twist $S^{σ^{-1}}$. In the connected graded case, we also obtain a criterion for when two such stable categories are triangle equivalent, and show that such an equivalence induces an equivalence between the categories of graded modules over the original algebras.

title: Interacting Multi-Node Conifold Light Sectors

original_abstract: We study finite-node conifold degenerations of Calabi--Yau threefolds from the point of view of interacting light sectors. Although each ordinary double point contributes a rank-one local vanishing sector, the corrected global object need not assemble as a freely independent sum of nodewise pieces. Using the corrected perverse and mixed-Hodge-module degeneration package, the global gluing law for corrected extension classes, and the rigid-flexible atom decomposition on the \(F\)-bundle side, we define an interacting multi-node light-sector package and prove a block-reduced structure theorem. In the block-separated cycle family, the finite-node package separates into two logically distinct layers: relation collapse, controlled by a common relation lattice on the corrected-extension, smoothing, and resolution sides, and residual interaction among the surviving global sectors, controlled by a reduced block interaction matrix on the transport and atom sides. The result isolates the geometric and Hodge-theoretic precursor of coupled conifold light states and provides the mathematical input for a later multi-node reformulation of Strominger's conifold mechanism.

title: Variational Principles for Shock Dynamics in Compressible Euler Flows

The key results reveal a fundamental structural distinction between the two settings. In the barotropic case, the absence of entropy degrees of freedom necessitates an additional interface contribution, yielding a modified energy balance. The significance of this work lies in embedding shock dynamics within classical Lagrangian mechanics, providing a geometric foundation for structure-preserving numerical discretizations, variational approximations of discontinuous solutions, and connections with thermodynamic admissibility criteria for compressible flows.
original_abstract: Hamilton's principle plays a central role in fluid mechanics as a fundamental tool for deriving governing equations, analyzing conservation laws, and designing structure-preserving numerical schemes. However, its classical formulation is restricted to smooth solutions and does not directly accommodate shock discontinuities. Addressing this limitation within a variational framework has long been a challenging issue. In this paper, we develop a variational framework that extends Hamilton's principle to shock solutions in compressible fluid dynamics. For the barotropic Euler equations, we introduce a modified action principle that incorporates additional contributions localized at discontinuities. This allows the Rankine--Hugoniot conditions for mass and momentum to emerge directly from unrestricted variations, without imposing continuity across shocks. The additional term admits a natural interpretation as a dissipation potential, linking the variational structure to energy loss at shocks. We then extend the approach to the full compressible Euler equations. Using a variational formulation of nonequilibrium thermodynamics together with suitable variational and phenomenological constraints, we recover the Rankine--Hugoniot relations for mass, momentum, and energy. This yields a unified variational description of shock dynamics in compressible fluids and highlights a fundamental distinction between barotropic and full compressible models in the treatment of energy and entropy at discontinuities.

title: Distributional Statistical Models: Weak Moments, Cumulants, and a Central Limit Theorem

They address the weak moment problem, proving uniqueness at three levels depending on kernel properties, including a Gaussian kernel uniqueness theorem extended to multiple dimensions via Hermite functions. They prove a weak central limit theorem with a quantitative Berry–Esseen type refinement, and demonstrate that in the density case, the weak CLT implies classical convergence in distribution of kernel-weighted measures to the standard normal. A statistical application shows that a single weak moment suffices to construct a consistent estimator for the Cauchy location parameter, where no classical moment-based estimator exists.

Key examples spanning Cauchy, stable, and normal inverse Gaussian distributions illustrate three regimes: complete moment failure, partial failure, and improved numerical stability. The framework represents a paradigm shift by extending moment-based and cumulant-based statistical methods to models previously inaccessible to such techniques, while recovering classical results as special cases.
original_abstract: Many important statistical models fall outside classical moment-based methods due to the non-existence of moments or moment generating functions. We propose a generalised probabilistic framework in which densities are replaced by pairs $(T,\varphi)$, where $T \in \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R})$ is a tempered distribution and $\varphi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ is a Schwartz kernel. Expectations are defined via the action of distributions on regularised test functions, yielding well-defined weak moments, weak characteristic functions, and weak cumulants of all orders. These extend classical quantities and retain key algebraic properties such as additivity under independence and natural affine transformation rules. The main results are: (i) a systematic algebra of weak cumulants; (ii) a weak moment problem where existence of all moments holds unconditionally and uniqueness depends on the kernel, with uniqueness results under Gaussian kernels (via Hermite completeness), positive Schwartz kernels with square-integrable densities (via a Carleman-type criterion), and kernels with exponential decay (via Denjoy-Carleman quasi-analyticity); and (iii) a weak central limit theorem formulated as convergence of weak characteristic functions to a Gaussian limit, covering cases where the classical theorem fails. The framework is illustrated with Student's $t$, stable, and hyperbolic distributions. As a statistical consequence, the weak first moment yields a consistent estimator of the location parameter in the Cauchy model, where no classical moment-based estimator exists. A full statistical treatment is given in a companion paper.

title: A weighted angle distance on strings

The authors establish that the construction yields a genuine metric for all ρ > 0, prove explicit Lipschitz-type bounds for elementary edits and stutter operations, and fully characterize its isometry group as symbol permutations optionally composed with string reversal. For ρ ∈ (0,1), they identify the metric completion as a disjoint union of finite strings and shift-invariant probability measures on infinite strings, connecting the framework to symbolic dynamics. Computationally, they present a generalized suffix-tree algorithm achieving O(|S|+|T|) time complexity.

Empirical evaluation using DBSCAN clustering on three sequence benchmarks demonstrates that the weighted angle distance substantially outperforms edit distances and fixed-scale k-gram baselines on datasets driven by tandem-repeat statistics, while remaining competitive on conventional corpora. Performance is reasonably stable across a broad range of ρ values. The work offers a principled, efficiently computable alternative to edit distances when repetition scale is a nuisance factor rather than a meaningful signal.
original_abstract: We define a multi-scale metric $d_ρ$ on strings by aggregating angle distances between all $n$-gram count vectors with exponential weights $ρ^n$. We benchmark $d_ρ$ in DBSCAN clustering against edit and $n$-gram baselines, give a linear-time suffix-tree algorithm for evaluation, prove metric and stability properties (including robustness under tandem-repeat stutters), and characterize isometries.

title: Rates of forgetting for the sequentially Markov coalescent
generated_summary:
This paper establishes rigorous bounds on the rates of forgetting—how quickly the process loses dependence on its initial condition—for the sequentially Markov coalescent (SMC) and its refined variant SMC', two widely used Markov approximations to the ancestral recombination graph for pairs of recombining chromosomes.

The authors analyze both the embedded jump chains (indexed by recombination events) and the continuous processes (indexed by genetic distance along the chromosome). For the jump chains, they prove geometric ergodicity in total variation using a coupling-based approach combined with Lipschitz continuity bounds on transition densities, obtaining explicit exponential decay rates. Specifically, the SMC jump chain achieves total variation distance decaying as (5/2)(1/2)^n, and the SMC' chain as 2(1/2)^n.

In stark contrast, for the continuous processes, the authors demonstrate that total variation distance from stationarity decays only as Θ(1/ρ), where ρ is genetic distance. This polynomial rate is proven sharp for both SMC and SMC'. A key technical contribution for the SMC' process is showing it can be obtained as a random time change of the SMC process via Poisson subordination, enabling transfer of ergodicity results between the two models. The authors further show via data processing inequalities that this 1/ρ lower bound extends to genealogies on more than two samples.

These results have practical implications for methods that treat genealogies at distant loci as approximately independent, demonstrating that such independence emerges slowly along the genome, while sampling by tree distance rather than genetic distance may achieve faster decorrelation.
original_abstract: The sequentially Markov coalescent (SMC) is a Markov jump process which models correlations in local genealogies across a chromosome. It has been used as a theoretical tool for studying linkage disequilibrium and identity-by-descent, and it also forms the basis of a class of statistical procedures for estimating population history and inferring ancestry. In this paper, we study the rate at which SMC forgets its initial condition in the pairwise setting. For the embedded jump chain, we prove geometric ergodicity in total variation, with explicit constants. For the continuous process, by contrast, the total variation distance from stationarity decays as $\asymp 1/\ell$ in genetic distance $\ell$. We obtain analogous results for the closely related SMC' process using a novel time-change argument. One application of these results is to justify heuristic approximations used in the literature that treat distant loci as evolving independently.

title: A note on the cardinality of Lagrangian packings
generated_summary:

For the smooth case, the authors provide two proofs. The first uses the second countability of the space of Hamiltonian functions under the C²-metric, combined with the observation that C²-close Hamiltonians produce intersecting Lagrangians. The second, more conceptual proof employs the Lagrangian flux homomorphism, showing that disjoint Lagrangians in a Weinstein neighborhood must represent distinct cohomology classes, whose possible values are constrained by the countable image of an evaluation map on homology.

The central result, Theorem 1.5, extends countability to C⁰ Lagrangian packings—where Lagrangians are related by Hamiltonian homeomorphisms—under a mild discreteness condition on the topological flux group. The proof constructs closed cycles from concatenations of cylinders arising from Lagrangian isotopies, homotopies, and Hamiltonian isotopies, then analyzes their symplectic areas using properties of flux and Floer homology.

The paper further characterizes when half-dimensional submanifolds admit uncountable smooth packings: precisely when they are non-Lagrangian with a nowhere vanishing normal section. These results clarify fundamental constraints on Lagrangian packings and connect packing problems to C⁰ symplectic rigidity and flux geometry.
original_abstract: Given a symplectic manifold, can one pack uncountably many Lagrangian submanifolds in a given Hamiltonian isotopy class of this symplectic manifold? We address $C^\infty$ and $C^0$ versions of this question.

title: Too Sharp, Too Sure: When Calibration Follows Curvature
generated_summary:

original_abstract: Modern neural networks can achieve high accuracy while remaining poorly calibrated, producing confidence estimates that do not match empirical correctness. Yet calibration is often treated as a post-hoc attribute. We take a different perspective: we study calibration as a training-time phenomenon on small vision tasks, and ask whether calibrated solutions can be obtained reliably by intervening on the training procedure. We identify a tight coupling between calibration, curvature, and margins during training of deep networks under multiple gradient-based methods. Empirically, Expected Calibration Error (ECE) closely tracks curvature-based sharpness throughout optimization. Mathematically, we show that both ECE and Gauss--Newton curvature are controlled, up to problem-specific constants, by the same margin-dependent exponential tail functional along the trajectory. Guided by this mechanism, we introduce a margin-aware training objective that explicitly targets robust-margin tails and local smoothness, yielding improved out-of-sample calibration across optimizers without sacrificing accuracy.

title: E-values and sequential power-one tests for monotonicity and unimodality
generated_summary:

The methodology employs a "mixture of witness" approach to build e-processes for discrete monotonicity (distributions on nonnegative integers with non-increasing probability mass functions) and discrete unimodality with a fixed mode. These e-processes grow to infinity exponentially fast under any alternative distribution, ensuring power-one testing. The authors also leverage convex duality to fully characterize the set of all valid e-values for these null hypotheses given a single observation, establishing information-theoretic optimality criteria. For unimodality with an unknown mode, the results yield power-one sequential tests and finite-length confidence sets for the mode from a single observation, as well as almost surely eventually correct set-valued mode estimators from i.i.d. sequences. The framework partially extends to continuous distributions, connecting with the shape-constrained inference literature.

The significance lies in addressing a nonparametric testing problem—mode testing—not previously covered in the sequential testing literature, while providing a comprehensive characterization of valid tests and optimal procedures for monotonicity and unimodality.
original_abstract: We develop e-values and e-processes testing the null hypothesis that a distribution over nonnegative integers is monotone, and that a distribution over integers is unimodal given a certain mode. Our e-processes lead to tests of power one under any non-null distribution with a sequence of i.i.d. observations, and consistent set-valued mode estimators that eventually equal the true set of modes. Additionally, we characterize the set of all e-values, and therefore the set of all valid tests, with one monotone and unimodal observation, as well as the most powerful e-value for a fixed alternative. We then show that many of our results can be generalized to continuous random variables, relating them to the existing results in the shape-constrained inference literature.

title: Admissible Lax-Wendroff Flux Reconstruction Method with Automatic Differentiation on Adaptive Curved Meshes for Relativistic Hydrodynamics

AMR achieves substantial computational speedups—up to 14× for the isentropic vortex test—while producing results in excellent agreement with fine uniform mesh simulations.

The significance lies in providing a robust, efficient framework for RHD simulations that maintains physical admissibility while substantially reducing computational costs through adaptive refinement.
original_abstract: The relativistic hydrodynamics (RHD) equations can give rise to solutions which have shocks, contact discontinuities, and other sharp structures, which interact and evolve over time. Capturing these sharp waves effectively requires a mesh with high resolution, making the scheme computationally expensive. In this work, adaptive mesh refinement is used with the high-order Lax-Wendroff flux reconstruction (LWFR) method to solve the system of RHD equations, which is closed with general equations of state. To make the scheme Jacobian-free, the idea of automatic differentiation is incorporated for computing the temporal derivatives in the time average flux approximations. The high-order method is blended with an admissible low-order method at the subcell level to control the Gibbs oscillations and maintain the physical admissibility of the solution. Finally, several test cases involving high Lorentz factors, low densities, low pressures, strong shock waves, and other discontinuities are used to demonstrate the robustness, accuracy, and effectiveness of the proposed method. These simulations are performed with AMR using various linear and curved meshes to show the scheme's efficiency and ability to handle complex geometries.

title: Enumeration of skew morphisms of cyclic $2$-groups
generated_summary:
This paper completes the enumeration of skew morphisms of cyclic p-groups by resolving the remaining case of cyclic 2-groups. A skew morphism of a finite group B is a permutation fixing the identity such that its action on products satisfies a twisted homomorphism property governed by a power function. Skew morphisms generalize automorphisms and arise naturally in the study of regular Cayley maps and group factorizations with cyclic core-free complements.

The main result provides a closed-form formula for Skew(2^e), the number of skew morphisms of the cyclic group Z_{2^e}. For e ≥ 4, the count satisfies the recurrence Skew(2^e) = 4·Skew(2^{e-1}) − 4, yielding an explicit formula. The proof strategy, inspired by a computational observation of Conder and Kovács, demonstrates that for all but two skew morphisms φ' of Z_{2^{e-1}}, exactly four skew morphisms of Z_{2^e} reduce to φ' modulo 2^{e-1}, while the two exceptions (the identity and the inversion automorphism) each lift to exactly two. The methodology employs properties of derived skew morphisms, kernel structures, and power functions specific to cyclic 2-groups, splitting the argument into establishing an upper bound and then proving tightness.

This result, combined with the previously known enumeration for odd prime powers and the multiplicativity of skew morphism counts under φ-coprimality, settles the enumeration problem for all cyclic p-groups. The remaining open challenge is determining Skew(nm) when n and m are coprime but not φ-coprime, which would complete the enumeration for all finite cyclic groups.
original_abstract: A skew morphism of a finite group $B$ is a permutation of $B$ fixing the identity and satisfying $\varphi(xy) = \varphi(x)\varphi^{i_x}(y)$ for some integers $i_x$ indexed by $x \in B$. The enumeration of skew morphisms of finite cyclic groups remains an open problem. The most substantial progress to date concerns cyclic $p$-groups with $p$ odd, for which a full classification and enumeration was obtained by Kovács and Nedela. In this paper we treat the remaining case $p = 2$, giving a complete classification and enumeration of skew morphisms of finite cyclic $2$-groups. Writing $\mathrm{Skew}(n)$ for the number of skew morphisms of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, we prove that $\mathrm{Skew}(2^e) = 4\,\mathrm{Skew}(2^{e-1}) - 4$ for each $e \geq 4$, and that $\mathrm{Skew}(2^e) = (7 \cdot 4^{e-2} + 8)/6$ for each $e \geq 3$. This completes the enumeration of skew morphisms for all cyclic $p$-groups.

title: The Mihail-Vazirani conjecture and strong edge-expansion in random $0/1$ polytopes

The Mihail-Vazirani conjecture, which posits that every 0/1 polytope has edge-expansion at least 1, has significant algorithmic implications for sampling and approximate counting but remains open in general.

The authors study the random 0/1 polytope P^d_p, formed by retaining each vertex of the d-dimensional hypercube independently with probability p. Their first main result shows that for any p bounded away from 1, the edge-expansion grows linearly in d — a factor of d stronger than the conjecture requires — and this bound is tight up to constants when p > 1/2. Their second result reveals a striking phase transition at p = 1/2: when p is bounded away from 1/2 from below, expansion is linear in d, but when p < 1/2, it grows super-polynomially in d.

The key methodological innovation is a coupling between long edges of the random polytope and mixed vertex-edge percolation on hypercubes, where vertices and edges are retained independently. The authors embed many lower-dimensional cubes within distance-k graphs of the hypercube, prove local expansion estimates for the mixed percolation model, and then bootstrap these via renormalization into global expansion bounds. These results have direct implications for bounding the mixing time of random walks on random 0/1 polytopes.
original_abstract: We study the edge-expansion of the graph of a random $0/1$ polytope $P^d_p$, defined as the convex hull of a random subset of the points in $\{0,1\}^d$ where every point is retained independently and with probability $p$. This problem was introduced more than twenty years ago in a work of Gillmann and Kaibel, and has been extensively studied ever since. We prove that, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and every $p\in(0,1-\varepsilon]$, with high probability the graph of $P^d_p$ has edge-expansion $Θ(d)$. This improves the previously best known bound due to Ferber, Krivelevich, Sales and Samotij, and verifies, in a strong form, the celebrated Mihail-Vazirani conjecture for random $0/1$ polytopes. Although the expansion factor $Θ(d)$ is typically best possible for $p\ge 1/2+\varepsilon$, we also show that the behaviour changes drastically at $p=1/2$. Namely, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and every integer $k\ge 2$, if $p\le 1/2-\varepsilon$, then with high probability the graph of $P^d_p$ has edge-expansion $Ω(d^k)$. Thus, random $0/1$ polytopes exhibit an interesting phase transition at $p=1/2$.

title: Beyond Bass Collapse: New Irregular Edge-Space Invariants in Ihara Theory
generated_summary:
This paper investigates what structural information exists in the directed-edge state space of the Ihara zeta function beyond what is captured by the classical Bass determinant formula, which reduces edge-space data to vertex-space adjacency information. The main contribution is identifying a canonical sector decomposition of the Hashimoto non-backtracking operator using the edge-reversal involution as a Z₂-symmetry, revealing that the symmetric sector recovers the ordinary line graph while the antisymmetric sector yields the antisymmetric line graph, with an explicit mixed transport block coupling the two.

The methodology centers on resolving this symmetry through a Schur-complement factorization of the Ihara determinant into a line-graph factor and a correction factor, then constructing gauge-invariant "mixed shadows" from the coupling block to obtain well-defined graph invariants. The paper localizes trivial Ihara roots onto canonical edge subspaces and establishes a resolution principle showing that for line-graph-cospectral pairs, all remaining Ihara separation must reside in the correction sector.

Key results include a concrete pair of non-isomorphic graphs that are simultaneously adjacency-cospectral and line-graph-cospectral yet have distinct Ihara zeta functions, with divergence forced entirely into the correction sector. Crucially, one example demonstrates mixed-shadow separation even when the scalar Ihara determinant fails to distinguish the graphs. In the regular regime, these mixed shadows collapse to adjacency data, explaining why new invariants emerge specifically in the irregular setting. The work thus establishes a genuinely new hierarchy of irregular edge-space invariants in Ihara theory.
original_abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph and let \(T\) be its Hashimoto operator on the directed-edge space. We show that edge reversal induces a canonical symmetric/antisymmetric splitting under which \(T\) acquires an explicit \(2\times 2\) block form. The diagonal blocks are \(\tfrac12 L(G)\) and \(-\tfrac12 A(G)\), where \(L(G)\) is the line-graph adjacency and \(A(G)\) is the antisymmetric line-graph adjacency, while the off-diagonal block is the mixed incidence product \(M=|D|^\top D\). This identifies the ordinary and antisymmetric line-graph sectors as the two canonical diagonal sectors of Hashimoto theory and isolates a mixed sector linking them. A Schur-complement argument then gives a factorization \[ \det(I-wT)=\det\!\bigl(I-\tfrac w2 L(G)\bigr)\,C_G(w), \] where \(C_G(w)\) is an explicit correction determinant built from the antisymmetric and mixed sectors. We show that the trivial roots \(w=\pm1\) localize on canonical edge subspaces, and that for line-graph-cospectral pairs all remaining Ihara separation is forced into the correction sector. Although the raw mixed block \(M\) depends on edge orientation, its natural gauge-invariant shadows, including \(MM^\top\), \(M^\top M\), and \(M^\top L^kM\), define a canonical matrix package attached to the graph. In the regular case these collapse to adjacency-side data, but in the irregular case they need not. As an application, we exhibit irregular non-isomorphic graphs that are adjacency-cospectral and line-graph-cospectral yet are separated by the correction sector, and we find further examples where the gauge-invariant mixed shadows separate even when the scalar Ihara polynomial does not. This isolates new irregular edge-space invariants in Hashimoto--Ihara theory.

title: Blow-up phenomena for the constant Q/R-curvature equation
generated_summary:
This paper investigates blow-up phenomena for the constant Q/R-curvature equation, a new Yamabe-type problem involving the quotient of Q-curvature and scalar curvature on compact Riemannian manifolds. The main contribution is proving non-compactness of the solution set in dimensions n ≥ 25 by constructing one-bubble blow-up sequences on the sphere S^n, extending the understanding of compactness failure beyond the classical Yamabe and Q-curvature settings.

The methodology employs a Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction scheme transferred to Euclidean space via stereographic projection. The authors construct a carefully designed local model metric using a trace-free perturbation encoding Weyl tensor structure, then build approximate solutions and reduce the problem to a finite-dimensional variational system. A critical technical innovation addresses the borderline dimension n = 25: while a quartic polynomial test function suffices for dimensions n ≥ 26, it fails to produce the necessary sign structure at n = 25, necessitating the introduction of a fractional-order function of degree 3.5. This result, combined with known compactness results in dimensions 5–24 for related problems, highlights a sharp dimensional dichotomy in the behavior of solutions to conformally invariant geometric equations and underscores the critical interplay between dimension, operator order, and solution compactness.
original_abstract: Let $n\ge 25$ be an integer. In this paper, we construct a smooth metric $g_{0}$ on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with the property that the set of metrics in the conformal class of $g_{0}$ having positive scalar curvature and positive constant quotient $Q/R$ is non-compact. Equivalently, we construct families of solutions exhibiting blow-up behavior for the following equation \begin{align*} P _{g_{0}}u- \frac{ (n+2 )(n-4 )}{4} u^{ \frac{2}{n-4}} L_{g_{0}}u^{ \frac{n-2}{n-4}} =0, \quad u>0\quad\text{on} \ \mathbb{S}^{n}, \end{align*} where $P _{g_{0}}$ is the Paneitz operator and $ L_{g_{0}}=-Δ_{g_{0}} +\frac{n-2}{4(n-1 )}R_{g_{0}} $ is the conformal Laplacian of $ g_{0}$.

title: Submetry onto one-dimensional space
generated_summary:

A submetry is a map between metric spaces that sends balls surjectively onto balls of the same radius, generalizing Riemannian submersions to settings where fibers may have varying dimensions or lower regularity.

The author constructs explicit families of C^{1,1} curves that serve as the middle fibers of these decompositions. In Euclidean space, the curve γ_{a,h} is built by joining concentric half-circles centered at two points in opposite half-planes with orthogonal line segments, parameterized by positive reals a and h. For the sphere, the base space is always a segment of length π/k, with the submetry being either a quotient of an isometric circle action (k=1) or a signed distance function to an explicit curve Γ_s (k>1).

original_abstract: We provide the full classification of equidistant decomposition of a two-dimensional Euclidean plane and a two-dimensional sphere.

title: Periodic homogenization of convolution type operators with irregular Lévy type tails
generated_summary:
This paper advances the homogenization theory for convolution-type nonlocal operators with rapidly oscillating periodic coefficients, where the kernel functions possess irregular Lévy-type tails.
