The methodology employs the corrector method combined with a novel ε-cubes decomposition technique to handle the analytical challenges arising from the absence of pointwise kernel bounds. This decomposition, inspired by work on stochastic homogenization with L¹ convolution potentials, leverages local L¹-boundedness of rescaled kernels to establish required convergence properties. Careful treatment of boundary contributions from cubes intersecting domain boundaries is also necessary.

The key results establish homogenization in the resolvent sense for nonlocal operators with both periodic and locally periodic coefficients, proving that solutions converge to those of an effective nonlocal equation. Existence and uniqueness of solutions to both the original and limiting equations are demonstrated using spectral theory and variational methods, respectively. original_abstract: We establish the homogenization results for a class of nonlocal operators of convolution type with integrable jumping kernel $p$ multiplied by rapidly oscillating periodic or locally periodic coefficients. The associated measure $p(z)dz$ is assumed to belong to the domain of attraction of a symmetric $α$-stable law. We also assume that $p$ satisfies a pointwise Lévy type lower bound and an averaged annular upper bound for points bounded away from the origin, and that the local $L^1$ oscillation of $p$ decays faster at infinity than its local $L^1$-norm. Under these assumptions, we prove the resolvent convergence of the nonlocal operators and explicitly determine the corresponding homogenized nonlocal operator, which is shown to be comparable to the fractional Laplacian. The proof relies on compactness arguments and a refined analysis based on the annular integral upper bound and an $\varepsilon$-cube decomposition.

title: The Tentacles Landscape
generated_summary:
This paper provides rigorous mathematical proofs for the "octopus-like" basin geometry previously observed only numerically in high-dimensional Kuramoto oscillator networks on ring graphs. From winding-number conservation, the author rigorously establishes four geometric properties: (i) basin volumes follow Gaussian scaling in the winding number (e^{−kq²}); (ii) the master distribution of distances between states and their attractors concentrates at π√(2/3), explaining a numerically observed constant of 1.81; (iii) almost every ray from a twisted state is equidistributed on the torus, visiting each basin with frequency proportional to its volume—formalizing the "tentacle" structure; and (iv) tight bounds on the size of each basin's "head" near the attractor. Additionally, the expanded coupling class yields a wider stability range for twisted states compared to the standard Kuramoto model.

The significance extends beyond oscillator networks, as the underlying energy landscape structure connects to spin glasses, jammed packings, and transformer self-attention dynamics, suggesting these geometric features may be universal in high-dimensional multistable systems.
original_abstract: Zhang and Strogatz [Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 194101 (2021)] used high-dimensional simulations to argue that basins of attraction in the Kuramoto ring are octopus-like: their volume scales as $e^{-kq^2}$ in the winding number $q$, nearly all of it concentrated in filamentary tentacles rather than near the attractor. They conjecture this geometry to be common in high dimensions but note that high-dimensional simulations are unreliable. We prove every feature of the octopus picture rigorously for identical oscillators on a ring coupled by any smooth odd function strictly increasing on $(-π,π)$.

title: Construction of Laguerre pseudospectral differentiation matrices
generated_summary:
This paper addresses a long-standing numerical instability in constructing Laguerre pseudospectral differentiation matrices, which are essential for spectral collocation methods on semi-infinite domains. The rapid growth of high-degree Laguerre polynomials and the extreme magnitudes of intermediate quantities cause overflow, underflow, and catastrophic cancellation in standard floating-point implementations, limiting practical computations to roughly 125 collocation points.

The authors propose a reformulation of the differentiation matrix entries that circumvents these difficulties. For off-diagonal entries, they introduce a scaled representation based on derivatives of Laguerre functions, computed simultaneously with collocation nodes using the Glaser–Liu–Rokhlin algorithm, thereby avoiding the separate evaluation of exponentially large or small quantities. For diagonal entries, they advocate direct closed-form expressions rather than the conventional "negative sum trick," which amplifies round-off errors in the weighted interpolation setting. The approach extends to second-order differentiation matrices through a recursive procedure combined with improved first-order matrices.

Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method maintains near machine-precision accuracy for substantially larger numbers of collocation points than the widely used DMSUITE package, which breaks down around n = 125. Two application problems—a second-order boundary value problem and eigenvalue computation for the Schrödinger equation with a Woods–Saxon potential—confirm that the stable construction enables solutions requiring over 200 collocation points, a regime previously inaccessible with standard implementations. The methodology is publicly available as open-source software.
original_abstract: In this paper, we present a stable and efficient approach for constructing Laguerre pseudospectral differentiation matrices. The proposed method reformulates the off-diagonal entries and computes all required quantities simultaneously using an existing fast algorithm that also generates the collocation nodes. For the diagonal entries, a closed-form expression is employed to improve numerical accuracy. This construction avoids the catastrophic cancellation present in classical formulations and yields an all-in-one procedure for generating differentiation matrices. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved robustness and sustained high accuracy for significantly larger numbers of collocation points compared to standard implementations.

title: Intersecting families with bounded intersections
generated_summary:
This paper investigates intersecting set families where pairwise intersection sizes are bounded, establishing improved upper bounds that significantly strengthen classical results from extremal set theory. The main contribution is an analog of the Ray-Chaudhuri-Wilson theorem for the special case where every pair of distinct sets intersects in at least one but at most k elements, along with a generalization of the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem under similar bounded intersection constraints.

The methodology employs a case-based approach depending on the structure of common elements across the family. Three cases are analyzed: when a single element belongs to all sets, when two elements cover all sets, and when no such pair exists. A key technical tool is a lemma showing that when no two elements cover the entire family, a collection of at most s³ triples can be found such that every family member contains at least one triple. This structural result enables counting arguments based on the distinctness of small subsets within family members.

The first main result shows that for an s-uniform intersecting family with pairwise intersections between 1 and k, the family size is at most the binomial coefficient (n-1 choose k-1), provided n ≥ s⁵/2. The second result extends this to non-uniform families where set sizes range from k to s, recovering the Erdős-Ko-Rado bound for sufficiently large n. These results substantially improve previous bounds for large n and, as a corollary, imply Snevily's theorem under mild additional conditions.
original_abstract: Let $\mathcal F\subset 2^{[n]}$ be an $s$-uniform family such that every two distinct sets have a nonempty intersection but intersect in at most $k$ elements. By the well-known Ray-Chaudhuri--Wilson theorem, since the intersections can take at most $k$ different values, we have $|\mathcal F|\leq \binom{n}{k}$. We give a stronger upper bound under our assumptions above, when $n$ is large enough compared to $s$ (and $k+1<s$): $|\mathcal F|\leq \frac{\binom{n-1}{k}}{\binom{s-1}{k}}$. Furthermore, we prove a generalization of the Erd\H os--Ko--Rado theorem for non-uniform families. Let $\mathcal F\subset \binom{[n]}{k}\cup\binom{[n]}{k+1}\cup\dots\cup\binom{[n]}{s}$, $3\leq k\leq s$, be a family such that for every two distinct sets the size of the intersection is between 1 and $k-1$ and $n$ is large enough then $|\mathcal F|\leq {n-1 \choose k-1}$.

title: Non-vanishing of the $p$-adic constant for mock modular forms associated to a newform with real Fourier coefficients
generated_summary:
This paper establishes the non-vanishing of the p-adic constant αg associated with mock modular forms linked to normalized newforms with real Fourier coefficients. The work answers a question posed by Bringmann, Guerzhoy, and Kane regarding whether the p-adic constant βg can ever vanish in certain settings, proving it cannot when the newform has real Fourier coefficients.

The methodology employs a cohomological approach using the relative de Rham cohomology of universal generalized elliptic curves. The author works with the g-isotypical component of parabolic cohomology and defines a pairing inspired by Bruinier and Funke's work. The key technical argument shows that the cohomology class corresponding to the (k-1)-th derivative of a good lift F⁺ and the newform g are linearly independent in the de Rham cohomology space. This linear independence is established through the Stokes' theorem, connecting the pairing to the Petersson inner product, which is known to be non-zero by the definition of a good lift.

The main theorem states that αg ≠ 0 when g is a normalized newform with real Fourier coefficients, p ∤ 6N, N ≥ 5, and {g, V(g)} forms a basis of the relevant cohomological space. As a corollary, βg ≠ 0 when g additionally has complex multiplication by an imaginary quadratic field with p inert. This result extends previous work, which was limited to weight 2 and relied on formal group theory of elliptic curves, to the higher weight case through cohomological methods.

title: Bounding Transient Instability in Sensor Data Injected Nonlinear Stochastic Flight Dynamics
generated_summary:
This paper develops a logarithmic-norm-based framework for analyzing finite-time transient stability in nonlinear Itô stochastic differential equations, addressing a critical gap in safety-critical aerospace applications where failure arises from finite-time excursions rather than asymptotic divergence. The methodology extends classical matrix measures to nonlinear mappings in a Lipschitz sense, characterizing instantaneous perturbation growth without requiring Lyapunov function construction, local linearization, or weak derivative assumptions on the Wiener process.

The framework yields explicit bounds on the mean and variance of logarithmic perturbation growth, decomposed into a mean contraction component and a diffusion-induced variability component. A key theoretical result demonstrates that stability in expectation does not guarantee pathwise finite-time safety, and that stochastic diffusion induces a strictly nonzero probability of transient growth over arbitrarily small time intervals—establishing a fundamental structural limitation. The analysis extends to data-constrained and projected stochastic dynamics, revealing an inherent trade-off between estimation consistency and transient robustness introduced by continuous data injection in navigation systems.

Demonstration on flight-like lunar lander descent telemetry shows that the proposed transient stability indicators distinguish between successful and failed trajectories that exhibit similar mean behavior, with failure correlating to accumulated transient instability during the terminal descent phase. These results motivate a paradigm shift from asymptotic stability analysis toward probabilistic finite-time stability metrics for certifying safety-critical autonomous systems.
original_abstract: Transient instability in nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems is a fundamental limitation in safety-critical aerospace applications, particularly during powered descent and landing where failure is driven by finite-time excursions rather than asymptotic divergence. Classical notions of mean-square or asymptotic stability are therefore insufficient for certification and design. This paper develops a logarithmic-norm-based framework for finite-time transient stability analysis of nonlinear Ito stochastic differential equations. The approach extends matrix measures to nonlinear mappings in a Lipschitz sense, enabling efficient characterization of instantaneous perturbation growth without local linearization. Using Ito calculus, bounds on the mean and variance of transient growth are derived, providing conditions for non-positive finite-time mean growth and probabilistic bounds on instability events. The analysis highlights a key distinction between mean and sample-path behavior, showing that stability in expectation does not guarantee pathwise finite-time safety, and that almost-sure transient stability cannot generally be ensured under stochastic diffusion. The framework is extended to data-constrained stochastic dynamics in navigation and estimation, revealing a trade-off between estimation consistency and transient robustness due to continuous data injection. Demonstrations with flight-like lunar lander telemetry show that similar mean trajectories can exhibit significantly different transient stability behaviour, and that mission failure correlates with accumulation of transient instability over short critical intervals. These results motivate probabilistic finite-time stability metrics for safety-critical autonomous systems.

title: Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs
generated_summary:
This paper establishes the existence of macroscopic loops in the random loop model with crosses and bars on several classes of sparse random graphs, significantly generalizing prior work that was restricted to interchange-type models on random regular graphs. The main contribution is twofold: extending results from the interchange process to the full random loop model (which includes a richer split-merge-rewire mechanism), and broadening the applicable graph ensembles through an abstract sparsity-based framework.

The methodology centers on a deterministic drift argument that operates on arbitrary finite graphs, requiring only two graph-theoretic inputs: a small-set sparsity condition (small vertex sets span at most linearly many internal edges) and a lower bound on edge density. The authors derive differential identities capturing the split-versus-twist mechanism specific to the crosses-and-bars model, then convert these into drift inequalities yielding positive lower bounds on macroscopic loop probabilities. For integer loop weights, log-convexity of the partition function enables strengthening averaged bounds to pointwise-in-time statements.

The authors verify their abstract criterion for three canonical sparse random graph ensembles: random regular graphs, sparse Erdős–Rényi graphs, and simple bounded-degree configuration models, proving macroscopic loops emerge above explicit thresholds in all cases. This work demonstrates that the drift philosophy is robust enough to handle the richer local geometry of general loop models and isolates a flexible graph-theoretic sparsity principle applicable across diverse sparse random structures, unifying probabilistic ideas from interchange processes, random loop models, and quantum spin systems.
original_abstract: We study the random loop model with crosses and bars on sparse random graphs. Our main objective is to prove the existence of macroscopic loops, in the sense that a loop visits a positive proportion of the vertices. We develop a deterministic drift method on arbitrary finite graphs based on three ingredients: a local split--merge--rewire analysis for the loop number, an exact differential identity for the partition function, and a slice estimate reducing the relevant same-loop insertion volume to induced edge counts of small vertex sets. This yields a general criterion in terms of a small-set sparsity condition on the underlying graph. We then verify this condition for random regular graphs, sparse Erdős--Rényi graphs, and simple bounded-degree configuration models, obtaining averaged lower bounds on the probability of a macroscopic loop whenever the edge density exceeds an explicit threshold depending on the loop weight \(θ\) and the cross parameter \(u\). For integer values of \(θ\), a trace representation of the partition function implies log-convexity, which upgrades the averaged bounds to pointwise-in-time results away from the threshold time.

title: Constrained Optimal Polynomials for Quantum Linear System Solvers
generated_summary:
This paper develops three classes of quantum linear system solvers inspired by classical Krylov subspace methods, designed to improve practical performance under realistic noise conditions. The authors introduce quantum Chebyshev-type iterations (QCheb), Constrained Uniform Polynomial (CUP) solvers that optimize polynomial approximations over a given spectral interval, and Constrained Adaptive Polynomial (CAP) solvers that adapt to the problem's actual spectral distribution using moments extracted from quantum measurements via a maximum entropy ansatz. These solvers can be further enhanced through structural transformations of the block encoding domain when a matrix square root is available.

The methodology centers on optimizing the tradeoff between polynomial approximation accuracy and block encoding normalization constraints, keeping polynomial degree low to minimize circuit depth and noise accumulation. Benchmarks are conducted using parameterized noise models simulating Pauli flips during block encoding applications, with both uniform and clustered eigenvalue distributions tested across varying noise levels and sampling budgets.

Key results show that CUP and CAP solvers reduce noise-induced error by nearly an order of magnitude compared to the standard QSVT solver. CUP performs best on uniform spectra while CAP excels on clustered spectra, though CAP is more sensitive to noise amplification beyond optimal polynomial degree. Hardware experiments on IBM quantum hardware demonstrate that CAP achieves 1.5% relative error compared to 18.3% for the standard QSVT solver on an elliptic PDE benchmark. These improvements are significant for both near-term noisy devices and fault-tolerant computation, where circuit depth remains a critical resource.
original_abstract: Quantum linear system solvers typically realize the inverse map as a polynomial transformation of the spectrum, so their practical cost hinges on implementing this transformation at a low polynomial degree. We introduce constrained optimal polynomials as a framework for this task, drawing on classical Krylov subspace theory. Within this framework, we develop three classes of polynomial solvers. Baseline quantum Chebyshev-type iterations provide general-purpose polynomials based on spectral bounds. Constrained Uniform Polynomial (CUP) solvers optimize the tradeoff between approximation accuracy and block encoding normalization under a uniform spectral model consistent with the available bounds. Constrained Adaptive Polynomial (CAP) solvers retain this structure but replace the uniform model with a probability measure reconstructed from spectral moments via a maximum entropy ansatz, where the moments are extracted from QSVT measurements. Numerical experiments under hardware and stochastic noise show that these methods achieve lower error than standard QSVT-based inversion at a comparable polynomial degree, up to an order of magnitude in noise-limited regimes. CUP offers robust performance under generic spectra, while CAP provides further improvement when the spectral structure can be exploited.

title: Approximate Simulation-based Hierarchical Control of Nonlinear Systems
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the open problem of approximate simulation-based hierarchical control (ASHC) for general nonlinear systems. In the ASHC framework, a complex "concrete" system is controlled indirectly by first designing a controller for a simpler "abstract" system, then translating control inputs back to the concrete system via an interface function, with guaranteed bounds on output error. While previous ASHC solutions existed only for linear systems and special nonlinear cases such as differentially flat or Lur'e-type systems, this work provides the first constructive methods applicable to general nonlinear systems, with particular focus on input-affine systems.

The methodology addresses two fundamental ASHC requirements: bounded output discrepancy and the generalized "m-relation." Under assumptions of asymptotic stabilisability of the concrete system and Lipschitz continuity of its output mapping, the authors characterize the bounded output discrepancy condition through a partial differential equation (PDE). The m-relation requirement, which ensures preservation of input-output controllability properties, is similarly characterized through another PDE. Combining these PDE-based characterizations yields overall solvability conditions, with a complete design procedure summarized in a flow chart.

The approach is demonstrated on a DC-to-DC Ćuk converter, illustrating the step-by-step design process. The significance of this work extends beyond hierarchical control, as it can alternatively be viewed as a novel model order reduction technique for controlling nonlinear systems, bridging connections between ASHC and moment-matching-based reduction methods.
original_abstract: Controlling complex dynamical systems to satisfy sophisticated specifications remains a significant challenge in modern engineering. A promising approach to this problem is the approximate simulation-based hierarchical control (ASHC) technique. In this method, a simplified representation of the complex system, called the abstract system, is first designed and controlled. An interface function is then designed to translate the control law into the input of the complex system, thereby achieving approximate control synthesis. However, most existing results in ASHC are only for linear systems. This paper proposes a constructive method for solving the ASHC problem for nonlinear systems. To this end, we propose invariance equation-based methods to achieve the two classical requirements of the ASHC technique, namely the bounded output discrepancy and the $m$-relation. We then study the solvability conditions of the problem and summarise the overall design procedures. We illustrate the results with a practical example, providing step-by-step solutions to the ASHC problem of a DC-to-DC Ćuk converter.

title: A unified framework for inexact adaptive stepsizes in the gradient methods, the conjugate gradient methods and the quasi-Newton methods for strictly convex quadratic optimization
generated_summary:
This paper proposes a unified framework for inexact adaptive stepsizes applicable to gradient methods, conjugate gradient methods, and quasi-Newton methods for strictly convex quadratic optimization problems. The main contribution is the introduction of the "approximately optimal stepsize," which provides a common inexact stepsize strategy across these three major optimization method families — addressing a gap in the literature where inexact adaptive stepsizes had been studied primarily for gradient methods but not systematically for conjugate gradient and quasi-Newton methods.

The methodology centers on developing the approximately optimal stepsize as a unified alternative to exact stepsizes, which are theoretically appealing but computationally expensive. The authors establish global convergence and convergence rate guarantees for the gradient method with this stepsize by exploiting connections to the well-known Barzilai-Borwein stepsizes. The framework leverages the fact that exact stepsizes across all three method families share a common structure.

Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach. The conjugate gradient method with approximately optimal stepsize (CG_AOS) outperforms both the BB method and the HDL method across multiple test problems, particularly for larger dimensions. The BFGS method with approximately optimal stepsize (BFGS_AOS) successfully solves more problems than the standard BFGS with unit stepsize and shows superior robustness across different initial matrix choices.

The significance lies in unifying stepsize selection across three fundamental optimization method families, offering both theoretical convergence guarantees and practical computational advantages for quadratic optimization.
original_abstract: The inexact adaptive stepsizes for the conjugate gradient method and the quasi-Newton method are very rare. The exact stepsizes in the gradient method, the conjugate gradient method and the quasi-Newton method for strictly convex quadratic optimization have a unified framework, while the unified framework for inexact adaptive stepsizes in the gradient method, the conjugate gradient method and the quasi-Newton method for strictly convex quadratic optimization still remains unknown. Based on the above observations, we propose a unified framework for inexact adaptive stepsizes in the gradient method, the conjugate gradient method and the quasi-Newton method for strictly convex quadratic optimization, which is called approximately optimal stepsize. The global convergence and the convergence rate of the gradient method with the approximately optimal stepsize are established by exploring the relation between the approximately optimal stepsize and the famous Barzilai-Borwein (BB) stepsizes. Some numerical results are presented, which confirm the remarkable numerical advantage of the gradient method, the conjugate gradient method and the quasi-Newton method with the unified framework for inexact adaptive stepsizes. Some open problems about the gradient method, the conjugate gradient method and the quasi-Newton method with approximately optimal stepsize are raised.

title: An unusual example of a universal automorphism group
generated_summary:
This paper addresses a question about the relationship between universality and group-extensibility of automorphism groups of countably infinite ultrahomogeneous structures (Fraïssé limits). In all previously known examples, universality of an automorphism group was established through group-extensibility—meaning every structure in the age admits a group-extensive embedding into the Fraïssé limit, where the embedding structurally witnesses the group embedding. The central question, posed by Kwiatkowska, Bartoš, Kubiś, and Vaccaro, asks whether universality necessarily implies group-extensibility.

The authors provide a negative answer by constructing a Fraïssé limit D in a finite relational language that is transitive and has strong amalgamation, whose automorphism group is universal but not group-extensible. This demonstrates that abstract group embeddings into the automorphism group need not always be "structurally witnessed" by embeddings of the underlying structures.

The methodology introduces a novel approach to proving universality that departs from the standard tower construction used in all prior work. Rather than building group-extensive embeddings directly, the authors construct, for each structure A in the age of D, an auxiliary structure M embeddable in D on which the automorphism group of A acts faithfully by automorphisms, thereby producing the required group embedding into the automorphism group of D.

This result is significant because it reveals a fundamental distinction between universality and group-extensibility that was previously unobserved, and introduces a new technique for establishing universality that the authors conjecture may be applicable to other structures.
original_abstract: Let $M$ be a Fraïssé structure (a countably infinite ultrahomogeneous structure). We refer to the class of structures embeddable in $M$ as the $ω$-age of $M$. We consider the following two properties of $M$: we say that $M$ has a universal automorphism group if, for each $A$ in the $ω$-age of $M$, there is an embedding $\textrm{Aut}(A) \to \textrm{Aut}(M)$, and we say that $M$ has group-extensible $ω$-age if, for each $A$ in the $ω$-age of $M$, there is an embedding $A \to M$ such that each automorphism of the image extends to an automorphism of $M$ and the extension map preserves group composition. It is immediate that if $M$ has group-extensible $ω$-age, then $M$ has a universal automorphism group. We give an example of a Fraïssé structure with a universal automorphism group whose $ω$-age is not group-extensible, showing that the above two properties are not equivalent.

title: A topological decoupling of modified nodal analysis including controlled sources
generated_summary:
This paper presents a significant generalization of the topological decoupling method for modified nodal analysis (MNA) — the foundational circuit formulation used in SPICE-like simulators — by extending it to circuits containing controlled sources such as those modeling transistors, operational amplifiers, and switches. Previous work established a topological decoupling of MNA into a semi-explicit index-one differential-algebraic equation (DAE), but only for circuits without controlled sources, limiting its practical applicability.

The authors derive topological conditions under which circuits with controlled sources can be similarly decoupled, building upon earlier index characterizations by Estévez Schwarz and Tischendorf. The methodology relies on analyzing subgraph topologies of the circuit to construct basis matrices that split system variables into differential, algebraic, and output components. The decoupling preserves key structural properties of MNA, including sparsity and positive-definiteness.

Through detailed examples — including a buck converter, a MOSFET model, an idealized operational amplifier, and a complete switched-mode power supply — the authors demonstrate that the required assumptions are satisfied by most common circuit elements, with only minor modifications needed in some cases. A software implementation is also provided.

The significance of this work is substantial: the semi-explicit DAE structure enables efficient model order reduction, machine learning approaches, computation of consistent initial conditions, and potentially faster time-domain simulations. By accommodating controlled sources, the decoupling becomes applicable to industry-relevant circuits, removing a major barrier to practical adoption.
original_abstract: We derive a topological decoupling of the equations of modified nodal analysis (MNA) to a semi-explicit index one differential-algebraic equation. The decoupling explicitly allows for controlled sources, which play a crucial role in engineering design workflows. Furthermore, the proof is constructive and provides a graph-based algorithmic framework for the computation of the decoupling, enabling its application to a variety of industry problems. These include the generation of consistent initial conditions, model order reduction, (scientific) machine learning, as well as speeding up conventional circuit simulation. In addition, the decoupling preserves the structure of MNA, i.e. the resulting systems remain sparse and key parts remain positive definite. We illustrate the decoupling using multiple examples, including some of the most common subcircuits containing controlled sources. Lastly, we also provide a first software implementation of the decoupling.

title: Indirect Prey-taxis VS a Shortwave External Signal in Multiple Dimensions
generated_summary:
This study develops a full asymptotic expansion for predator-prey systems with indirect Keller-Segel prey-taxis subject to a short-wave external signal in multiple spatial dimensions. The work substantially extends prior one-dimensional results by accommodating general spatial dimensions, general inter/intraspecific reaction kinetics, and complete asymptotic expansions rather than just leading-order terms.

The methodology employs homogenization and multiple-scale expansion techniques, separating fast and slow variables to derive an effective slow system governing the amplitude modulation of short-wave solution packages. The authors then perform linear stability analysis of quasi-equilibria of this slow system, drawing analogies with Kapitza's inverted pendulum theory to study signal-induced stability or instability.

Key results reveal two principal effects of the short-wave external signal: a drift of predators and modification of system kinetics. The drift vanishes for stationary signals with constant driver intensity, while the kinetic modification disappears for "p-linear" kinetics common in population dynamics. A transport tensor characterizing anisotropic predator sensitivity emerges, showing that generic stationary signals suppress taxical transport sensitivity, with exponential decay possible as signal intensity grows. Conversely, unsteady wave-like signals can enhance sensitivity in certain directions, leading to destabilization. Notably, the stability of individual modes depends substantially on wave vector direction.

These findings are significant for understanding how environmental heterogeneity influences pattern formation in predator-prey systems, demonstrating that external signals can either stabilize or destabilize coexistence equilibria depending on their spatiotemporal structure.
original_abstract: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak--Keller--Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modelling the predator--prey community with the prey-taxis that means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a driving signal produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the driving signal is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent from the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter/intraspecific reactions. Further, we apply the short wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza' theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal or, oppositely, blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium. These results contribute to filling the gap in the literature, since the theory and techniques for the asymptotic integration of systems described above represent a weakly charted area.

title: Forward--Inverse Interplay in FEM-Based EEG Source Imaging: Distributional Signatures of Advanced Source Models and Inverse Solvers

original_abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) source imaging aims to infer brain activity from electrical potentials measured on the scalp. This is a difficult problem because many different source patterns can explain the same measurements. The result depends strongly on two things: the forward model and the inverse method. In this work, we study how these two parts work together. We focus not only on where the activity is located, but also on how the reconstructed activity is distributed in space. We suggest that different source models create different signatures in the reconstructed activity. We use realistic head models and compute forward solutions with the finite element method using Zeffiro Interface and DUNEuro. We test different source models, including 2 implementations of a divergence-conforming model, and one implementation of Local subtraction approach. For inverse methods, we use advanced methods such as standardized hierarchical adaptive L1 regression (sHAL1R), standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), and classical dipole scanning. To understand the complex interplay between the forward and inverse approaches, we analyze the inverse source localization results using distributional quantitative measures, including Earth Mover's Distance and depth bias scatter plot, and qualitatively assess the amplitude distribution and focality. The results show that there is a strong dependence between the choice of source model and the success rate of a given inverse method: a source model that corresponds well with a single point-like source is a good match with an inverse method that presupposes such a source.

title: Stochastic Extinction with Relaxed Boundedness Conditions

original_abstract: We study stochastic extinction for a class of Markov processes motivated by models in ecology and epidemiology. Extinction is often characterized by a boundedness condition and a condition on boundary Lyapunov exponents (invasion rates). While the latter is typically sharp, the former is often restrictive and can be improved. Building on the ideas initiated in \cite{benaim2018stochastic}, we develop a streamlined approach that relaxes this boundedness condition and yields concise and accessible criteria for extinction. In particular, we establish extinction criteria in two settings: with and without a linearly bounded quadratic variation condition. In the first case, our result is comparable to, and slightly improves upon, the main results in \cite{foldes2024stochastic}. In the second case, where the quadratic variation is not linearly bounded, we obtain new extinction results that fall outside the scope of existing frameworks. title: A discrete-time overdetermined problem for the heat equation
generated_summary:

The paper presents three main theorems. Theorems 1 and 2 address the two accumulation regimes respectively, while Theorem 3 extends the result to overdetermination on an interior surface, concluding that both the domain and subdomain must be concentric balls. original_abstract: In this paper, we consider a parabolic counterpart of Serrin's overdetermined problem, in which the overdetermined condition (constant flux condition) is imposed only on a discrete infinite set of time values. We show that, under suitable regularity assumptions on the domain, such a discrete-time overdetermined problem admits a solution if and only if the domain is a ball. Remarkably, depending on the temporal scale, the same overdetermined condition captures either geometric or spectral information, yet both mechanisms lead to the same rigidity conclusion. We study both the case in which the constant flux condition is imposed on the boundary and the case in which the constant flux condition is imposed on an interior surface. We remark that the methods employed in our analysis do not depend on the location of the overdetermined surface but only on whether the sequence of time instants accumulates away from zero. Finally, we will show how this problem generalizes to complete Riemannian manifolds.

title: On G-birational rigidity of projective spaces

The methodology combines equivariant birational geometry, toric symmetry analysis of P^n, and detailed classification of primitive finite subgroups in low dimensions. For P^4, the authors prove that the group PSp(4,3) of order 25920 (related to the Burkhardt quartic) makes P^4 G-birationally superrigid (Theorem C). Over the real numbers, they prove an analogous primitivity requirement (Theorem D) and show that P^n over ℝ is never G-birationally rigid for n ∈ {4,5,6} (Theorem E), leading them to conjecture this holds for all n ≥ 4. original_abstract: In this paper, we study finite subgroups $G\subset\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^n)$ such that $\mathbb{P}^n$ is $G$-birationally rigid. For each $n\geqslant 3$, we prove that $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^n)$ contains at most finitely many such subgroups up to conjugation. For $n=4$, we prove that $\mathbb{P}^4$ is $G$-birationally superrigid if $G\simeq\mathrm{PSp}_{4}(\mathbf{F}_3)$.

title: Likelihood-based inference for birth-death processes with composite birth mechanisms
generated_summary:

The authors address two key challenges: the mixture of latent birth mechanisms observable only through aggregate state changes ("event-space deconvolution"), and survival selection bias arising from an absorbing extinction state, since only non-extinct trajectories are typically observed. They employ the Doob h-transform to construct the Q-process—an ergodic surrogate that captures the dynamics of the original process conditioned on long survival. This enables derivation of a conditional likelihood, from which both a conditional maximum likelihood estimator and a quasi-maximum likelihood estimator are developed.

The main theoretical results establish that both conditional estimators are consistent and asymptotically normal under the Q-process law, while the naive unconditional estimator exhibits persistent survival bias. original_abstract: We develop a likelihood-based inference for finite-state birth-death processes with composite birth rates, in which multiple distinct mechanisms contribute additively to the total birth intensity. Our main motivating example is an SIS epidemic model with pairwise and higher-order transmission. The process is observed through a single aggregate trajectory, and in the main setting of interest, birth events are unmarked. This creates a deconvolution problem in event space: the state is one-dimensional, but the mechanism underlying each birth is latent. We formulate the inference under a Doob $h$-transformed $Q$-process, which is time-homogeneous and ergodic and which provides a time-homogeneous asymptotic surrogate for the law of the original process conditioned on long survival. We derive the corresponding conditional likelihood and study both the conditional maximum likelihood estimator and a quasi-maximum likelihood estimator which is based on a simplified working score. Under the Doob-transform law, we prove consistency and asymptotic normality for both estimators, with asymptotic covariance determined by the inverse Fisher and inverse Godambe information matrices, respectively. We also showcase a practical one-dimensional test for the presence of a specific higher-order birth mechanism.

title: Fast and Provably Accurate Sequential Designs using Hilbert Space Gaussian Processes

original_abstract: Gaussian processes are widely used for accurate emulation of unknown surfaces in sequential design of expensive simulation experiments. Integrated mean squared error (IMSE) is an effective acquisition function for sequential designs based on Gaussian processes. However, existing approaches struggle with its implementation because the required integrals often lack closed-form expressions for most kernel functions. We propose a novel and computationally efficient Hilbert space Gaussian process approximation for the IMSE acquisition function, where a truncated eigenbasis representation of the integral enables closed-form evaluation. We establish sharp global non-asymptotic bounds for both the approximation error of isotropic kernels and the resulting error in the acquisition function. In a series of numerical experiments with $γ$-stabilizing, the proposed method achieves substantially lower prediction error and reduced computation time compared to existing benchmarks. These results demonstrate that the proposed Hilbert space Gaussian process framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient approach for Gaussian process based sequential design.

title: On the Hyperbolic Fractional Sum of the Divisor Function
generated_summary:

The paper establishes two main theorems: one providing the improved asymptotic formula for the hyperbolic fractional sum with error term O(x^{131/229+ε}), and another giving new upper bounds for the generalized three-dimensional exponential sums S(H,M,N) with constant perturbation. The significance lies in unconditionally improving the error term without relying on the classical conjecture Δ(x) ≪ x^{1/4+ε}, while also advancing the broader theory of exponential sum estimation that has applications throughout analytic number theory.
original_abstract: Let $τ(n)$ denote the classical divisor function. In this paper, we consider the hyperbolic fractional sum of the divisor function defined by $$ T(x) = \sum_{n_1 n_2 \leqslant x} τ\left( \left[ \frac{x}{n_1 n_2} \right] \right) = \sum_{n \leqslant x} τ\left( \left[ \frac{x}{n} \right] \right) τ(n), $$ where $[t]$ denotes the integral part of the real number $t$. By establishing new estimates for a class of three-dimensional exponential sums with constant perturbation, we obtain an improved asymptotic formula for $T(x)$. In particular, we show that for any $\varepsilon > 0$, the error term in the asymptotic expansion of $T(x)$ is bounded by $O(x^{17/30+\varepsilon})$. This result breaks the $4/7$-barrier which corresponds to the application of the classical divisor problem conjecture $1/4+\varepsilon$.

title: A Loewner-Nirenberg phenomena for Ricci flow on compact manifolds with boundary.II

original_abstract: This is a continuation of the research in [16]. Let $(\overline{M},g_{-1})$ be a closed geodesic $r_0$-ball in the hyperbolic space $(\mathbb{H}^n,g_{-1})$. title: A Loewner-Nirenberg phenomena for Ricci flow on compact manifolds with boundary

original_abstract: In this paper, we show that starting from a geodesic ball $\overline{B_{r_0}}(0)$ in $\mathbb{H}^n$, for $n\geq3$, with prescribed non-decreasing rotationally symmetric mean curvature and the fixed conformal class $[g_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}]$ on the boundary, the solution $g(t)$ to the normalized Ricci flow $(1.2)$ which is continuous up to the boundary, exists for all $t>0$ and converges locally uniformly in $B_{r_0}(0)$ to a complete hyperbolic metric as $t\to\infty$(see Theorem 1.2 for details). title: Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Nonlinear Control

The authors prove both a converse (lower) bound showing that the rate-cost function cannot fall below the minimum directed information F_n(D), and an achievability (upper) bound showing it is at most F_n(D) plus a logarithmic term. The key technical innovation in the achievability proof is the novel application of the strong functional representation lemma (SFRL) in a sequential, controlled setting—the first such use. The construction employs a stagewise application of SFRL combined with a time-sharing argument using Carathéodory's theorem to ensure causality.

The logarithmic gap becomes negligible in high-rate regimes, yielding first-order tightness. original_abstract: We study the rate-cost tradeoff in rate-limited control of general stochastic control systems, including nonlinear systems, over a finite horizon. At each time step, an encoder observes the state and transmits a description to a controller, which then selects the control action. For an average control-cost threshold $D$, we characterize the minimum achievable communication rate $R_n(D)$ via a nonasymptotic bound: $R_n(D)$ lies within an additive logarithmic gap of the optimal value of a directed-information minimization $F_n(D)$, namely, we show that $F_n(D) \le R_n(D) \le F_n(D)+\log \bigl(F_n(D)+3.4\bigr)+2+\frac{1}{n}$, in bits. This establishes directed information as the operationally relevant quantity governing rate-limited control, thereby broadening its utility beyond its previously established roles in causal source coding and linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control to general nonlinear control systems. We prove the upper bound constructively by building an encoding-and-control policy using the strong functional representation lemma at each time step. As special cases of our setting, our framework yields nonasymptotic bounds for sequential (causal) rate-distortion and LQG control.

title: Smith Form Equivalence for Several Classes of Multivariate Polynomial Matrices

For matrices whose determinants take the form of a product of a linear factor and a univariate polynomial, they derive criteria based on whether the reduced minors of all orders generate the unit ideal. A key methodological innovation is the construction of a ring isomorphism that maps multivariate polynomial rings to themselves, enabling the extension of results to a new class of matrices whose determinants involve products of linearly independent linear polynomials with univariate polynomials. The approach also handles non-square and rank-deficient cases.

The established criteria are computationally verifiable through reduced Gröbner bases of ideals generated by the reduced minors. These results significantly advance the understanding of the long-standing open problem of Smith form equivalence for multivariate polynomial matrices, with direct implications for controllability and stability analysis of multidimensional systems in signal processing and dynamic control.
original_abstract: This paper investigates the equivalence reduction for several classes of multivariate polynomial matrices and their Smith forms, establishing some criteria for such reduction. In particular, we employ algebra isomorphisms as a key tool to study this equivalence problem. We then leverage the Quillen-Suslin and Lin-Bose theorems to extend these results to non-square and rank-deficient matrices. Moreover, the verification of our criteria is achievable algorithmically via existing Gröbner basis methods.

title: On the convergence of an adaptive denoiser driven iterative regularization with early stopping

The methodology combines an averaged denoiser with adaptive step sizes and dynamically weighted parameters in an iterative scheme. The algorithm features an automatic switching mechanism: when the denoiser reaches a fixed point, the iteration transitions to an adaptive gradient descent step. The discrepancy principle terminates iterations when the residual norm becomes comparable to the noise level, preventing overfitting. This addresses an open question regarding adaptive parameter selection in denoiser-based regularization methods.

The authors establish three key theoretical results: finite termination of the algorithm, stability of the iterates with respect to data perturbations, and strong convergence to the true solution as the noise level approaches zero. Numerical experiments on image deblurring and phase retrieval computed tomography problems demonstrate that DDIR achieves high reconstruction quality while overcoming limitations of existing Regularization by Denoising (RED) and Plug-and-Play (PnP) approaches.

The significance lies in placing denoiser-based reconstruction methods on solid theoretical ground within modern regularization theory, bridging the gap between practical denoising-based algorithms and rigorous convergence guarantees for nonlinear inverse problems.
original_abstract: Solving inverse problems requires appropriate regularization techniques to ensure well-posedness and stability. In recent years, denoiser-driven methods have emerged as effective regularization strategies, achieving state-of-the-art performance in various imaging applications. However, their stability and convergence within iterative regularization frameworks remain largely unexplored. In this work, we extend the framework of Regularization by Denoising (RED) by introducing a novel denoiser-driven iterative regularization scheme, referred to as \texttt{DDIR}, that incorporates a new regularization functional based on averaged denoisers. The proposed approach employs an adaptive step-size strategy together with an \emph{a posteriori} stopping rule to ensure stability while alleviating oscillatory behavior and semi-convergence effects induced by noise. As our main theoretical contribution, we prove that the resulting reconstruction method constitutes a stable and convergent regularization scheme in the classical sense. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous justification of \texttt{DDIR} within the framework of regularization theory. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the proposed method through numerical experiments on image deblurring and phase retrieval Computed Tomography (CT) using three denoisers, namely median, TNRD, and TV proximal. The results highlight the effectiveness of the method in terms of reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: New inequalities for eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on the hyperbolic space

The key innovation lies in the construction of new test functions, which yield sharper estimates than those previously available. The authors utilize the Rayleigh-Ritz inequality framework combined with these carefully chosen test functions to derive their bounds.

The main result (Theorem 1.2) provides an improved universal inequality that strengthens a recent result by Luo and Zheng by replacing the coefficient (n² − 2n − 4) with the larger quantity (n−1)², thereby tightening the bound. As corollaries, the authors verify Cheng's conjecture up to a lower-order correction term of (n−1)²/4 for two special classes of bounded domains satisfying certain geometric conditions. Additionally, by choosing alternative test functions, Theorem 1.3 establishes the conjecture with the same lower-order loss for another family of domains under different geometric assumptions.

These results represent meaningful progress on a challenging open problem in spectral geometry, narrowing the gap between known estimates and the conjectured sharp inequality for hyperbolic space.
original_abstract: In this paper, motivated by study on universal inequalities for eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian, we prove some new inequalities for eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on the hyperbolic space. In particular, we verify Cheng's conjecture (Adv. Lect. Math. 37, 2017) up to loss of $ε$ for two special kinds of bounded domains in the hyperbolic space.

title: Comparison principles and long time behavior for a diffusive Energy Balance Model with vertical resolution

This paper presents a rigorous mathematical analysis of a two-layer Energy Balance Model (2LEBM) with degenerate diffusion, describing the coupled evolution of surface and atmospheric temperatures as functions of time and latitude. The model extends classical one-dimensional EBMs by incorporating vertical structure through two interacting layers, enabling a more refined treatment of the greenhouse effect and vertical energy transfer.

The authors employ techniques from degenerate parabolic equation theory combined with qualitative analysis of cooperative dynamical systems. They develop novel comparison principles adapted to the degenerate, strongly coupled PDE setting, construct explicit super- and sub-solutions using the spatially homogeneous ODE system, and establish maximum principles to ensure positivity and boundedness of solutions.

The key results demonstrate that when the atmospheric absorptivity parameter satisfies αa ≤ 2, the system admits unique, globally bounded classical solutions, possesses invariant regions, and has a global attractor with distinguished warmest and coldest stationary solutions. The findings carry important physical implications: the persistence of global attractors for αa ≤ 2 suggests that even strongly opaque atmospheric conditions remain compatible with stable radiative balance, while the blow-up threshold provides a mathematical characterization of climate tipping points associated with extreme greenhouse forcing.
original_abstract: We study a two-layer one-dimensional energy balance model, which allows for vertical energy exchanges between a surface layer and the atmosphere, as well as meridional energy transport across latitudes via a diffusion law. The evolution equations of the surface temperature and the atmospheric temperature are coupled by exchange of infrared radiation as well as other non-radiative energy exchanges. The energy enters the system as solar radiation, which is partially absorbed and partially reflected by the two layers. The system is then composed of two degenerate parabolic equations coupled by nonlinear terms, the growth of these terms being crucial for the choice of the functional setting. An essential parameter is the absorptivity of the atmosphere, denoted $\varepsilon _a$, whose value depends critically on greenhouse gases. We prove that blow up in finite time occurs if $\varepsilon _a >2$, while global existence of solutions and the existence of a global attractor hold when $\varepsilon _a \in (0,2)$. Proofs are based on comparison principles that derive from the cooperative structure of the problem, and that provide invariant rectangles for smooth initial conditions, and on regularity properties.

title: Composition operators and Rational Inner Functions on the bidisc: A geometric approach

The methodology centers on analyzing the level-set geometry of RIFs on the distinguished boundary of the bidisc. The authors systematically identify geometric configurations that force unboundedness: when level sets share a common exceptional line, contain a common arc of an analytic curve, or intersect tangentially at smooth or singular points. original_abstract: We develop an operator-theoretic framework for the Convergent Born Series (CBS) method applied to the Lippmann--Schwinger equation for high-frequency Helmholtz problems. In contrast to the Fourier-based analysis of Osnabrugge et al., our approach expresses the preconditioned Lippmann--Schwinger iteration entirely in terms of the resolvent of a self-adjoint background operator. This leads to a unitary Cayley-transform representation of the CBS iteration operator, from which we derive basis-independent bounds on its numerical range and a general convergence criterion valid on arbitrary bounded domains and for complex-valued wave numbers. Because the analysis does not rely on an explicit Green's function in the Fourier domain, the Cayley-transform framework extends naturally to a broader class of frequency-domain wave and diffusion equations whose fundamental solutions are not available in closed form. We further incorporate smoothly tapered complex-wavenumber absorbing layers that preserve the self-adjoint structure of the reference operator and enhance the contractivity of the iteration without modifying the differential operator. In addition to this theoretical generalization, we present a detailed numerical validation in which CBS solutions are benchmarked against PML-based finite-difference wavefield simulations. original_abstract: We study the existence of asymptotically $Z$-stable (a.Z stable) bundles over polycyclic surfaces. In particular, this leads to new examples of strictly a.Z-stable bundles over $\mathbb{P}^2$, the product $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^1$, and the blow-up $\mathrm{Bl}_q\mathbb{P}^2$. original_abstract: The identity map of an Einstein manifold is a critical point of both the classical energy functional and the conformal-bienergy functional. In this paper, we investigate the conformal-biharmonic stability of the identity map of compact Einstein manifolds of dimension at least four and with nonnegative scalar curvature, and we compare it with the harmonic stability, when the identity map is considered as a harmonic map. Somewhat surprisingly, we show that the conformal-biharmonic index coincides with the harmonic index, with a single notable exception: the four-dimensional Euclidean sphere. In this case, the identity map is unstable with respect to the energy functional, as shown independently by Mazet and Smith, whereas it is stable with respect to the conformal-bienergy functional.

title: Geometric Layer-wise Approximation Rates for Deep Networks

original_abstract: Depth is widely viewed as a central contributor to the success of deep neural networks, whereas standard neural network approximation theory typically provides guarantees only for the final output and leaves the role of intermediate layers largely unclear. We address this gap by developing a quantitative framework in which depth admits a precise scale-dependent interpretation. Specifically, we design a single shared mixed-activation architecture of fixed width $2dN+d+2$ and any prescribed finite depth such that each intermediate readout $Φ_\ell$ is itself an approximant to the target function $f$. For $f\in L^p([0,1]^d)$ with $p\in [1,\infty)$, the approximation error of $Φ_\ell$ is controlled by $(2d+1)$ times the $L^p$ modulus of continuity at the geometric scale $N^{-\ell}$ for all $\ell$. Our network design is inspired by multigrade deep learning, where depth serves as a progressive refinement mechanism: each new correction targets residual information at a finer scale while the earlier correction terms remain part of the later readouts, yielding a nested architecture that supports adaptive refinement without redesigning the preceding network.

title: Stochastic Barrier Certificates in the Presence of Dynamic Obstacles

original_abstract: Safety of stochastic dynamic systems in environments with dynamic obstacles is studied in this paper through the lens of stochastic barrier functions. We introduce both time-invariant and time-varying barrier certificates for discrete-time, continuous-space systems subject to uncertainty, which provide certified lower bounds on the probability of remaining within a safe set over a finite horizon. These certificates explicitly account for time-varying unsafe regions induced by obstacle dynamics. By leveraging Bellman's optimality perspective, the time-varying formulation directly captures temporal structure and yields less conservative bounds than state-of-the-art approaches. By restricting certificates to polynomial functions, we show that time-varying barrier synthesis can be formulated as a convex sum-of-squares program, enabling tractable optimization. title: Structure-Aware Variational Learning of a Class of Generalized Diffusions

original_abstract: Learning the underlying potential energy of stochastic gradient systems from partial and noisy observations is a fundamental problem arising in physics, chemistry, and data-driven modeling. Classical approaches often rely on direct regression of governing equations or velocity fields, which can be sensitive to noise and external perturbations and may fail when observations are incomplete. Starting from the energy-dissipation law associated with the Fokker-Planck equation, we construct loss functions based on the De Giorgi dissipation functional, which consistently couple the free energy and the dissipation mechanism of the system. This formulation avoids explicit enforcement of the governing partial differential equation and preserves the underlying variational structure of the dynamics. Through numerical experiments in one, two, and three dimensions, we demonstrate that the proposed energy-based loss exhibits enhanced robustness with respect to observation time, noise level, and the diversity and amount of available training data. original_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of quantitatively reconstructing initial acoustic sources from time-dependent wave measurements. These indicators are foundational for both proving the uniqueness of source reconstruction and developing a quantitative direct sampling scheme. Our comprehensive numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness, accuracy, and computational efficiency of these methods, highlighting their potential for practical acoustic imaging applications.

original_abstract: We study quadratic monomial algebras \(Λ\) and the structure of their graded module categories, with particular emphasis on finitely presented and finitely copresented modules over the Koszul dual algebra \(Λ^{!}\). We prove that, for a finite-dimensional quadratic monomial algebra, the Koszul dual \(Λ^{!}\) is both left coherent and left co-coherent, and that the categories of perfect and coperfect modules coincide with the categories of finitely presented and finitely copresented graded modules, respectively. We further show that quadratic monomial algebras are absolutely Koszul and have global linearity defect at most one. As a consequence, every finitely presented \(Λ\)-module has a rational Poincaré series, and the associated tails and cotails categories are abelian and hereditary. We also establish that the class of finitely presented (resp.\ finitely copresented) modules coincides with the class of modules admitting a linear (resp.\ colinear) truncation. Building on these structural results, we refine the graded derived and singular Koszul dualities for quadratic monomial algebras. In particular, we obtain triangulated equivalences \[ \mathsf{D}^b(Λ^{!}\textup{-Fcp}^{\mathbb{Z}}) \;\simeq\; \mathsf{D}^b(Λ\textup{-gmod}) \;\simeq\; \mathsf{D}^b(Λ^{!}\textup{-Fp}^{\mathbb{Z}}), \qquad \mathsf{D}^b(Λ^{!}\textup{-Fcp}^{\mathbb{Z}}/Λ^{!}\textup{-gmod}) \;\simeq\; \mathsf{D}_{\mathrm{sg}}(Λ\textup{-gmod}). \] Moreover, we show that these equivalences induce natural \(t\)-structures on the bounded derived and singularity categories, whose hearts admit explicit descriptions in terms of linear complexes and shifts of linear modules. Finally, we refine the corresponding ungraded derived and singular Koszul dualities and obtain an ungraded BGG correspondence for quadratic monomial algebras.

title: Cover meets Robbins while Betting on Bounded Data: $\ln n$ Regret and Almost Sure $\ln\ln n$ Regret

original_abstract: Consider betting against a sequence of data in $[0,1]$, where one is allowed to make any bet that is fair if the data have a conditional mean $m_0 \in (0,1)$. Cover's universal portfolio algorithm delivers a worst-case regret of $O(\ln n)$ compared to the best constant bet in hindsight, and this bound is unimprovable against adversarially generated data. In this work, we present a novel mixture betting strategy that combines insights from Robbins and Cover, and exhibits a different behavior: it eventually produces a regret of $O(\ln \ln n)$ on \emph{almost} all paths (a measure-one set of paths if each conditional mean equals $m_0$ and intrinsic variance increases to $\infty$), but has an $O(\log n)$ regret on the complement (a measure zero set of paths). Our paper appears to be the first to point out the value in hedging two very different strategies to achieve a best-of-both-worlds adaptivity to stochastic data and protection against adversarial data. We contrast our results to those in~\cite{agrawal2025regret} for a sub-Gaussian mixture on unbounded data: their worst-case regret has to be unbounded, but a similar hedging delivers both an optimal betting growth-rate and an almost sure $\ln\ln n$ regret on stochastic data. title: Robust Out-of-Distribution Stochastic Optimization

original_abstract: Data-driven decision-making under uncertainty typically presumes the collection of historical data from an unknown target probability distribution. However, one may have no access to any data from the target distribution prior to decision-making. We then incorporate this set into a min-max stochastic program to derive robust decisions. Notably, under randomness of distribution generation, we establish rigorous out-of-distribution generalization guarantees for the uncertainty set as well as the solution. To ease problem-solving in RKHS, an approximate parametrization with a provably bounded suboptimality and a row generation strategy are presented. Extensive numerical experiments on multi-item newsvendor and portfolio optimization demonstrate the superior out-of-distribution performance of our decision-making framework under unseen data distribution, even when only a small or moderate number of relevant sources are available.

title: Fractal transference principle for continued fractions of Laurent series

original_abstract: We establish a fractal transference principle for continued fraction expansions over the field of Laurent series. Let $S$ be an infinite subset of the set of all polynomials over a finite field of $q$ elements of positive degree with growth density exponent $α\ge 1$, and let $U \subset S$ be a subset of positive relative upper density. We prove that there exists a subset $E_{S,U}$ of the set of points whose continued fraction digits are pairwise distinct and belong to $S$ such that \[\dim_{\rm H} E_{S,U}=\frac{1}{2α}.\] Moreover, the set of digits appearing in the continued fraction expansions of points in $E_{S,U}$ recovers the relative upper density of $U$ in $S$. We also show that the same construction preserves the relative upper density of the corresponding degree sets in $\mathbb N$. As a consequence, combinatorial statements for subsets of $\mathbb N$ of positive upper density can be transferred to degree sets arising from continued fraction expansions of Laurent series on sets of optimal Hausdorff dimension.

title: From Finite-Node Conifold Geometry to BPS Structures II: Functorial Incidence and Quiver Assembly

original_abstract: In previous work, we extracted the intrinsic finite algebraic state data of a finite-node conifold degeneration in the form $A_Σ:= (V_Σ,E_Σ,c_Σ)$, where $V_Σ$ is the finite node-indexed vertex set, $E_Σ$ is the nodewise coupling space, and $c_Σ$ is the coefficient vector of the corrected global extension class. This yields the interaction and incidence layer required for later graded interaction, stability, BPS, and wall-crossing structures.

title: Learning to Solve the Quadratic Assignment Problem with Warm-Started MCMC Finetuning
generated_summary:

The methodology centers on an energy-based model (EBM) with an additive structure enabling constant-time evaluation of 2-swap proposals within a Metropolis-Hastings sampler. A cross-graph attention network captures the coupled two-graph structure of QAP instances without constructing expensive association graphs, maintaining scalability. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across synthetic and real-world benchmarks. PLMA achieves a near-zero (0.06%) average optimality gap on QAPLIB while being faster than competing heuristics, and exhibits remarkable robustness on challenging Taixxeyy instances with a 2.56% average gap, vastly outperforming robust tabu search (81.01%) and breakout memetic algorithm.
