These operators provide a realization of the Kontsevich-Soibelman Lie algebra, demonstrating that the identification of Stokes constants with generalized DT invariants is exactly what ensures the consistency of the Stokes automorphism under moduli variations—specifically, that it remains invariant when active rays in the Borel plane do not cross.

The methodology combines formal resurgent analysis with extensive numerical computation. The authors dramatically improve computational algorithms for multi-instanton amplitudes, enabling identification of subleading singularities in the Borel plane. They study local P² and the quintic Calabi-Yau, identifying bound states of D4-branes in the Borel plane and matching their Stokes constants with DT invariants encoded in Poincaré polynomials of Hilbert schemes of points. They also numerically verify the Borel plane structure of instanton amplitudes and observe the manifestation of a D2-brane decay across a wall of marginal stability.

The significance of this work lies in providing a concrete framework linking the asymptotic divergence of perturbative topological string amplitudes to the enumerative geometry of Calabi-Yau threefolds, with wall-crossing phenomena emerging naturally from the resurgent structure.
original_abstract: We study the resurgence structure of the topological string partition function, with an emphasis on the Borel analysis of the instanton amplitudes. To this end, we introduce a differential operator that implements the pointed alien derivative when acting on the topological string partition function and its iterated alien derivatives. We show that the algebra of alien derivatives is isomorphic to the Kontsevich-Soibelman Lie algebra, thus establishing a direct link between the resurgence of the topological string and wall-crossing of generalized Donaldson-Thomas invariants. Numerically, we continue the exploration of the Borel plane of the quintic and local $\mathbb{P}^2$. For the latter, we identify Borel singularities due to bound states involving D4-branes, and match the associated Stokes constants to the appropriate Donaldson-Thomas invariants. Finally, we identify the manifestation of a D2-brane decay in the Borel plane, and match to theoretical predictions.

title: On Scott's odd induced subgraph conjecture and a related problem
generated_summary:
This paper advances the study of Scott's conjecture, which posits that every graph G without isolated vertices contains an odd induced subgraph of order at least half its vertices divided by its chromatic number. The main contribution is a proof that Scott's conjecture holds for claw-free graphs (graphs with no induced K₁,₃), strengthening a prior result by Wang and Wu that confirmed the conjecture for line graphs, since every line graph is claw-free. Crucially, the authors demonstrate this is optimal with respect to star-forbidding conditions: for every r ≥ 4, there exist arbitrarily large K₁,r-free graphs violating the conjecture, establishing K₁,₃-freeness as the precise threshold.

The paper also addresses an open problem of Wang and Wu asking whether the line graph of every connected regular graph G of order n ≥ 3 satisfies f₀(L(G)) ≥ n/2. The authors identify C₅ as the smallest counterexample and prove a positive result: every connected k-regular C₅-free graph with k ≥ 2 satisfies this bound. The proof leverages classical factor theorems of Petersen and Kano.

Additionally, the authors reduce the problem of bounding odd induced subgraphs in girth-5 planar graphs to the bipartite planar case using Grötzsch's theorem, and conjecture that Scott's conjecture holds for all 3-chromatic graphs. These results clarify the structural boundaries governing the existence of large odd induced subgraphs across important graph families.
original_abstract: For a graph $G$, let $f_o(G)$ denote the maximum order of an induced subgraph of $G$ all of whose vertices have odd degree, and let $χ(G)$ denote the chromatic number of $G$. Scott (CPC, 1992) proved that $f_o(G) \ge |V(G)|/(2χ(G))$ for every graph without isolated vertices, and conjectured that the factor $2$ can be removed. Wang and Wu (JGT, 2024) showed that this conjecture fails for bipartite graphs, but holds for line graphs. In this article, we confirm Scott's conjecture for claw-free graphs without isolated vertices, thereby strengthening the result of Wang and Wu. We also construct $K_{1,r}$-free graphs of arbitrarily large order to show that the conjecture fails for this broader class, for every integer $r \ge 4$. Wang and Wu also asked whether $f_o(L(G)) \ge n/2$ holds for every connected regular graph $G$ of order $n \ge 3$. We show that $C_5$ is the smallest counterexample to this problem. On the positive side, we prove that if $G$ is a connected $k$-regular $C_5$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $k \ge 2$, then $f_o(L(G)) \ge n/2$.

title: Fast computation and theoretical guarantees for the NPMLE in exponential family mixtures
generated_summary:
This paper advances the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) for exponential family mixtures through two complementary contributions: a computationally efficient approximation scheme and a unified theoretical framework for marginal density estimation.

The computational contribution centers on a data-compression strategy using Gaussian quadrature. Rather than evaluating the log-likelihood over all n observations—which costs at least O(n) per iteration—the method replaces the empirical distribution with a discrete measure supported on only J_n points that matches the first 2J_n − 1 moments. The authors prove that polylogarithmic growth of J_n in n suffices to ensure the approximate NPMLE achieves a likelihood gap of O(n^{−α}) for any desired α, yielding substantial computational savings. In practice, J_n values of 20–30 suffice even for sample sizes of 100,000, delivering speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude over existing methods.

The theoretical contribution establishes nearly parametric convergence rates for the approximate NPMLE in squared Hellinger distance across two broad scenarios: compact mixing support with general base densities, and unbounded mixing support with sub-Gaussian base densities satisfying tail regularity conditions. Both results achieve rates of order (log n)^c/n, up to logarithmic factors, unifying previously model-specific analyses for Gaussian location mixtures, Poisson mixtures, and scaled chi-square mixtures.

The key insight underlying both contributions is the analytic smoothness of the likelihood ratio function, exploited through classical Bernstein approximation theorems from complex analysis. This unified framework extends naturally to multivariate settings and provides principled statistical support for the proposed computational procedure.
original_abstract: This work makes two advances in the study of the (approximate) nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) for exponential family mixture models. First, we develop a data-compression strategy that reduces the cost of repeated likelihood evaluations in NPMLE computation to logarithmic order in the sample size. Second, we show that, for a broad class of approximate NPMLEs, the resulting marginal density estimator attains an almost parametric rate of convergence.

title: Juniper Green and the Gallai-Edmonds Decomposition
generated_summary:
This paper establishes a precise structural characterization of winning first moves in Juniper Green, a combinatorial number game played on the set {1, 2, ..., n} where players alternately select factors or multiples of the previously chosen number. While Julien Lemoine previously proved that the first player has a winning strategy for all n ≥ 120, the question of which specific opening moves constitute winning moves remained open.

The authors connect the game to the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition of the divisibility graph G_n, where vertices represent integers in {1, ..., n} and edges connect pairs related by divisibility. The Gallai-Edmonds decomposition partitions vertices into three sets: D(G) (inessential vertices not covered by every maximum matching), A(G) (essential vertices with inessential neighbors), and C(G) (remaining essential vertices). The main result proves that the winning first moves for player one are precisely the vertices in D(G_n), derived as a consequence of Berge's Theorem from matching theory.

Computational analysis using the blossom algorithm reveals intriguing structural patterns: |A(G_n)| remains consistently small, while |C(G_n)| and |D(G_n)| alternate dramatically in relative size, with transitions occurring near values of n having many small prime factors. The paper identifies several empirical observations about the decomposition's behavior but notes the difficulty of proving these patterns rigorously, effectively transforming Stewart's original question about game strategy into a new open problem about the number-theoretic structure of divisibility graphs.
original_abstract: Juniper Green is a simple combinatorial game invented by Rob Porteous and popularized by Ian Stewart. It was originally designed to familiarize school children with the concepts of multiplication and division. We analyze this elementary game through a completely different lens and show that it recovers the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition of the divisibility graph on the vertex set $V= \left\{1,2,\dots, n\right\}$. This characterizes the winning moves of the game; as a byproduct, we show that this decomposition seems to have many interesting and curious patterns that are currently unexplained.

title: The integral Chow ring of $\mathscr{M}_{0}(\mathbb{P}^r, 2)$
generated_summary:
This paper computes the integral Chow ring of the moduli stack $\mathscr{M}_0(\mathbb{P}^r, 2)$, which parameterizes degree-two stable maps from rational curves to projective space $\mathbb{P}^r$, for all positive integers $r$. The main result presents this Chow ring as a quotient of a polynomial ring in three variables, with relations generated by at most seven elements, five of which can be efficiently encoded as homogeneous coefficients of two explicit rational generating functions.

The methodology relies on presenting $\mathscr{M}_0(\mathbb{P}^r, 2)$ as a global quotient stack by the special group $\mathrm{GL}_3$. Since the degree is even, the standard $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ quotient presentation cannot be directly lifted to a special group action; instead, the authors employ a "$\mathrm{GL}_3$ counterpart" construction that reinterprets the source curve as a smooth conic in $\mathbb{P}^2$. The Chow ring is then computed via $\mathrm{GL}_3$-equivariant intersection theory: the stack is realized as an open subset of a projective bundle, and an equivariant envelope for the complement is constructed with two manageable components—a projective bundle over the universal conic and a product of projective spaces. Atiyah-Bott localization yields the relations in closed form.

The key finding is a complete, explicit presentation valid for all $r$ simultaneously, with relations arising naturally from the geometry of conics and their degenerations. This work represents the second step in a broader program to compute integral Chow rings of spaces $\mathscr{M}_0(\mathbb{P}^r, d)$ for all degrees, and the exceptional simplicity of the $d=2$ case—compared to higher even degrees where Hilbert schemes of points become involved—makes it a natural self-contained contribution.
original_abstract: We compute a presentation for the integral Chow rings of the moduli stacks of degree $2$ maps from smooth rational curves to projective space $\mathbb{P}^r$, as a quotient of a three-variable polynomial ring. The relations as $r$ varies have rich combinatorial structure: all non-trivial relations are encoded by two generating functions which are rational functions.

title: Ultrametric OGP - parametric RDT \emph{symmetric} binary perceptron connection
generated_summary:

The authors introduce s-level ultrametric OGPs for SBPs and develop an analytical framework combining union-bounding methodology with convex programming for the combinatorial component and nested integration for the probabilistic component, enabling rigorous upper bounds on the critical constraint densities at which ultrametric OGP emerges.

For the canonical margin κ=1, numerical evaluations yield bounds of approximately 1.738 and 1.682 for the first and second ultrametric levels, respectively. These values align remarkably well with the constraint density estimates of approximately 1.737 and 1.679 obtained at the 3rd and 4th lifting levels of parametric RDT. Beyond matching density values, the authors observe excellent agreement in overlap values and relative sizes of ultrametric clusters between the two frameworks.

Based on these observations, the authors conjecture that in the limit of large ultrametricity and lifting levels, ult-OGP and parametric RDT constraint densities converge to the algorithmic threshold, with possible finite-level equality. Since parametric RDT has already been linked to local entropy predictions, this work suggests a triangular correspondence among ult-OGP, parametric RDT, and local entropy—three distinct approaches that may all accurately characterize algorithmic thresholds. The authors propose this connection extends beyond SBPs to other optimization problems.
original_abstract: In [97,99,100], an fl-RDT framework is introduced to characterize \emph{statistical computational gaps} (SCGs). Studying \emph{symmetric binary perceptrons} (SBPs), [100] obtained an \emph{algorithmic} threshold estimate $α_a\approx α_c^{(7)}\approx 1.6093$ at the 7th lifting level (for $κ=1$ margin), closely approaching $1.58$ local entropy (LE) prediction [18]. In this paper, we further connect parametric RDT to overlap gap properties (OGPs), another key geometric feature of the solution space. Specifically, for any positive integer $s$, we consider $s$-level ultrametric OGPs ($ult_s$-OGPs) and rigorously upper-bound the associated constraint densities $α_{ult_s}$. To achieve this, we develop an analytical union-bounding program consisting of combinatorial and probabilistic components. By casting the combinatorial part as a convex problem and the probabilistic part as a nested integration, we conduct numerical evaluations and obtain that the tightest bounds at the first two levels, $\barα_{ult_1} \approx 1.6578$ and $\barα_{ult_2} \approx 1.6219$, closely approach the 3rd and 4th lifting level parametric RDT estimates, $α_c^{(3)} \approx 1.6576$ and $α_c^{(4)} \approx 1.6218$. We also observe excellent agreement across other key parameters, including overlap values and the relative sizes of ultrametric clusters. Based on these observations, we propose several conjectures linking $ult$-OGP and parametric RDT. Specifically, we conjecture that algorithmic threshold $α_a=\lim_{s\rightarrow\infty} α_{ult_s} = \lim_{s\rightarrow\infty} \barα{ult_s} = \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty} α_{c}^{(r)}$, and $α_{ult_s} \leq α_{c}^{(s+2)}$ (with possible equality for some (maybe even all) $s$). Finally, we discuss the potential existence of a full isomorphism connecting all key parameters of $ult$-OGP and parametric RDT.

title: Proximal Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Variational Inequalities
generated_summary:
This paper introduces and analyzes proximal discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods for variational inequalities, specifically the unilateral Poisson obstacle problem. The authors extend the proximal Galerkin framework, previously developed primarily for conforming finite element discretizations, to nonconforming settings encompassing four DG-type methods: symmetric interior penalty DG (IPDG), enriched Galerkin (EG), hybridizable interior penalty (H-IP), and hybrid high-order (HHO) methods. These are unified within a common abstract framework.

The methodology combines the Bregman proximal point algorithm with broken finite element spaces, yielding iterative schemes that simultaneously handle the nonlinear inequality constraints and spatial discretization. The authors establish well-posedness of each nonlinear subproblem, monotone energy dissipation, and best-approximation-type error estimates under minimal regularity assumptions. A key theoretical result demonstrates that the optimization error is decoupled from the spatial discretization error, preserving the mesh-independent convergence behavior characteristic of proximal Galerkin methods.

A particularly notable achievement is the first rigorous higher-order convergence result for any proximal Galerkin method: the proximal HHO method with piecewise constant cell unknowns and piecewise linear facet unknowns achieves an energy error of order h^{3/2-ε}. Numerical experiments on a benchmark obstacle problem confirm optimal convergence rates across all methods, with HHO providing the best accuracy due to its higher-order reconstruction operator. This work significantly broadens the applicability of the proximal Galerkin framework to a wide class of nonconforming discretizations.
original_abstract: We introduce a family of proximal discontinuous Galerkin methods for variational inequalities, focusing on the obstacle problem as a didactic example. Each member of this family is born from applying a different well-known nonconforming finite element discretization to the Bregman proximal point method. We explicitly treat four examples: the symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin, the enriched Galerkin, the hybridizable interior penalty and the hybrid high-order methods. We formulate a unified analysis framework for this family of methods and prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions, energy dissipation, and error estimates for both the primal and dual variables. Remarkably, the proximal hybrid high-order method with piecewise constant cell unknowns and piecewise affine facet unknowns leads to the first higher-order convergence result for any proximal Galerkin method.

title: Minimal time for null controllability of the parabolic spherical Baouendi-Grushin equation
generated_summary:
This paper determines the exact minimal time for null controllability of the parabolic equation associated with the spherical Baouendi-Grushin operator on the two-dimensional sphere, resolving an open question from prior work. The operator, arising from the canonical almost-Riemannian structure on S², is hypoelliptic and degenerates along the equator. The main result establishes that for a one-sided spherical crown control region with lower boundary at latitude angle a from the equator, the minimal null controllability time is precisely π/(2a), matching the previously known lower bound.

The proof strategy combines two complementary approaches. First, when the control region contains the equator in its interior, Carleman estimates uniform in the Fourier index are established, with a Hardy-Poincaré inequality handling pole singularities, yielding null controllability in arbitrarily small time. Second, for control regions away from the equator, a moment method using mode-dependent controls and explicit lower bounds on associated Legendre functions achieves controllability for times exceeding the critical threshold. A cut-off argument then extends results from boundary-touching strips to general one-sided crowns.

The key findings are that null controllability holds for all times exceeding π/(2a) and fails below this threshold, while crowns containing the equator require no positive minimal time. These results provide a complete characterization of the threshold phenomenon for spherical crowns and highlight how degeneracy geometry governs controllability in non-uniformly parabolic settings, with implications for broader classes of almost-Riemannian manifolds.
original_abstract: We study null controllability for the parabolic equation on $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ endowed with its canonical almost-Riemannian structure. For a spherical crown $ω=\{α<x_3<β\}$, where $0\le α<β\le1$, we prove the sharp minimal time formula $T_{\min}(ω)=\ln(1/\sqrt{1-α^{2}})$ for null controllability in $ω$. We also prove that, whenever the control region contains the equator, null controllability holds in every positive time. The proof combines two complementary tools. First, after Fourier decomposition with respect to the periodic variable, we establish observability estimates for a family of one-dimensional singular parabolic equations, with constants uniform with respect to the Fourier mode; the singularities at the poles are handled via a Hardy-Poincaré inequality. Second, for crowns away from the equator, we use the moment method to construct controls on the pole-touching crown $α<x_3< 1$ from sharp weighted lower bounds on associated Legendre functions, and then pass to a general crown $α<x_3<β$ by a cut-off argument on the full domain combined with the arbitrary-time controllability of crowns containing the equator. The result closes the large-time gap left in earlier work and gives the exact null-controllability threshold for the canonical almost-Riemannian heat equation on $\mathbb S^2$.

title: On two ways to use determinantal point processes for Monte Carlo integration
generated_summary:
This paper investigates two approaches for using determinantal point processes (DPPs) in Monte Carlo integration: the Bardenet-Hardy (BH) estimator and the Ermakov-Zolotukhin (EZ) estimator. The main contribution is providing a modern, simplified proof of the EZ estimator's properties using the generalized Cauchy-Binet formula, while also establishing that the EZ estimator can be interpreted as a quadrature rule with weights summing to one when one kernel eigenfunction is constant.

The methodology centers on multivariate Jacobi ensembles as the underlying DPP, with exact sampling achieved via tridiagonal matrix models in one dimension and chain rule-based rejection sampling in higher dimensions. The authors carefully analyze rejection bounds, noting how they grow with dimension and depend on the base measure parameters. Both estimators are systematically compared across diverse test functions including smooth bumps, sums of eigenfunctions, absolute values, Heaviside functions, cosines, and mixtures thereof.

Key results show that BH exhibits the expected variance decay of order 1/N^(1+1/d) and satisfies a central limit theorem, while EZ can achieve dramatically lower variance for functions well-approximated by kernel eigenfunctions but may produce outliers that compromise Gaussianity. Notably, EZ does not necessarily preserve the sign of the integrand, and its weights need not be nonnegative.

The findings clarify the complementary strengths of both DPP-based integration approaches, offering practitioners guidance on when each estimator is preferable depending on the smoothness and spectral properties of the integrand.
original_abstract: The standard Monte Carlo estimator $\widehat{I}_N^{\mathrm{MC}}$ of $\int fdω$ relies on independent samples from $ω$ and has variance of order $1/N$. Replacing the samples with a determinantal point process (DPP), a repulsive distribution, makes the estimator consistent, with variance rates that depend on how the DPP is adapted to $f$ and $ω$. We examine two existing DPP-based estimators: one by Bardenet & Hardy (2020) with a rate of $\mathcal{O}(N^{-(1+1/d)})$ for smooth $f$, but relying on a fixed DPP. The other, by Ermakov & Zolotukhin (1960), is unbiased with rate of order $1/N$, like Monte Carlo, but its DPP is tailored to $f$. We revisit these estimators, generalize them to continuous settings, and provide sampling algorithms.

title: Explicit counting of ideals in number fields of arbitrary degree
generated_summary:
This paper presents explicit bounds on the error term in the ideal counting function for number fields of arbitrary degree, improving upon previous work by Debaene in terms of dependence on the field degree. The ideal counting function estimates the number of ideals in the ring of integers of a number field whose norm is bounded by a parameter *t*, a quantity closely connected to the Dedekind zeta function and important for applications such as the Chebotarev density theorem.

The authors employ geometry of numbers techniques, introducing a lattice point counting method based on the covering radius rather than successive minima, which avoids the factor of roughly *n*^(*n*²) appearing in prior work. Key methodological innovations include exploiting freedom in choosing fundamental domains for the unit lattice action and generalizing Schmidt's partition trick to decompose the counting domain into more tractable pieces. The authors also derive bounds on the covering radius of the relevant lattices and establish Lipschitz properties of the domains involved.

The main result provides two explicit estimates whose error terms grow roughly as *n*^(2.5*n*) and 2^(4.1*n*) in the degree *n*, substantially improving Debaene's *n*^(10*n*²) dependence while maintaining the same dependence on the regulator and class number. The bounds hold for sufficiently large *t*. Through a concrete example using the cyclotomic field ℚ(ζ₁₁), the authors demonstrate that their estimates can outperform Lee's explicit version of Landau's estimate for moderate values of *t*, despite Landau's estimate being asymptotically superior.
original_abstract: We implement methods from the geometry of numbers to give explicit estimates for the number of integral ideals in a number field. We pay particular attention to minimising the effect of the degree $n$ of the number field on the error term and avoid terms on the order of $n^{n^2}$. We do this by studying fundamental domains for the action of multiplying with units of infinite order in Minkowski space. With some lattice theory we show that one can make different choices for such a fundamental domain, which yield a smaller error, especially when the degree of the field extension is large. We also adapt Schmidt's partition trick to this generalised setting.

title: Improving the Even-Size Threshold in Spectral Extrema for $H(4,3)$-Free Graphs
generated_summary:
This paper improves the even-size threshold in the spectral extremal problem for graphs forbidding H(4,3), the graph formed by identifying a vertex of a 4-cycle with a vertex of a triangle. The main contribution is lowering the threshold from m ≥ 38, established by Zheng and Zhang, to m ≥ 24. Specifically, the authors prove that for any H(4,3)-free graph G of even size m ≥ 24 without isolated vertices, the spectral radius ρ(G) is bounded above by σ(m), the largest real root of a specific quartic polynomial, with equality characterizing a unique extremal graph.

The methodology refines a single branch of the Zheng–Zhang proof rather than replacing it entirely. The authors introduce a local independence lemma for vertices in a specific neighborhood partition set W adjacent to a maximum Perron-vector vertex. This lemma enables exact analysis of the cases e(W) = 0 and e(W) = 1, while sharpened numerical inequalities handle e(W) = 2 and e(W) = 3. The case e(W) = 2 proves to be the genuine bottleneck determining the threshold 24.

The authors also identify an explicit obstruction family showing that no theorem of the same form can hold below m = 18, thereby confining the exact threshold to the interval [18, 24]. Computational evidence supports the conjecture that the sharp threshold is precisely 18. This work narrows a meaningful numerical gap between neighboring results in fixed-size spectral extremal graph theory.
original_abstract: For the fixed-size Brualdi--Hoffman--Turan problem forbidding the fish graph $H(4,3)$, Zheng and Zhang proved that every $H(4,3)$-free graph of even size $m \ge 38$ without isolated vertices satisfies $ρ(G) \le ρ'(m)$, where $ρ'(m)$ is the largest root of $x^4-mx^2-(m-2)x+\frac{m}{2}-1=0$, with equality only for $S^{-}_{\frac{m+4}{2},2}$. We revisit their branch analysis and show that the published threshold is carried entirely by one local configuration, namely the branch in which the Perron-neighborhood core $A^{+}$ induces $K_4$. By refining that branch, we lower the unconditional threshold from $38$ to $24$. The cases $e(W)=0$ and $e(W)=1$ are resolved exactly, while the case $e(W)=2$ remains the bottleneck and yields the final hand-proved bound. We also exhibit an explicit obstruction family showing that no theorem of the same form can hold below $18$, and we record computational evidence that the exact threshold is likely $18$.

title: Pseudometrics and preorders on sets of integer sequences induced by arithmetic functions functions
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the construction of pseudometrics and preorders on sets of integer sequences using arithmetic functions as generating mechanisms. The main contribution is a systematic framework that connects arithmetic functions—particularly additive and multiplicative ones central to number theory—to distance measures and ordering relations on integer sequences, revealing structural equivalences among the resulting preorders.

The methodology begins by establishing centered pseudometrics on general spaces using non-negative generating functions and their supplements, then extends these constructions to higher-dimensional spaces of m-tuples of integers. The authors employ the three Pythagorean means (arithmetic, geometric, and harmonic) to create moving averages along sequences of consecutive integers, which serve as the basis for defining pseudometrics and preorders on these sequence spaces. Admissible arithmetic functions are projected onto residue class representatives to enable this framework.

A key result is that function triples related through exponential-like and linear transformations induce equivalent preorders, establishing preorder-preserving isomorphisms between sets of generating and supplementary functions. For admissible arithmetic functions, the combination of three functions and three types of means produces nine preorders, but structural equivalences reduce these to at most five generally distinct preorders on the space of integer sequences.

The significance of this work lies in providing a unified algebraic and metric-theoretic perspective on comparing integer sequences through the lens of divisibility properties, connecting classical number-theoretic functions to modern concepts in pseudometric spaces and order theory.
original_abstract: Starting from pseudometrics and preorders on sets of integers, we extend the focus to sets of finite sequences of integers, in particular sequences of consecutive integers. We outline existing concepts for deriving centred pseudometrics and preorders in a given pseudometric space and their application to $\mathbb{Z}$ and develop approaches to generalize the ideas to $\mathbb{Z}^m$. Sequences of consecutive integers represent a special case here and are examined in more detail. Another main topic is the use of arithmetic functions in this context. The types of pseudometrics and preorders examined in this paper can be induced by suitable arithmetic functions. We derive fundamental conclusions about relationships between functions and preorders, as well as about equivalent and potentially distinct types of preorders.

title: Regulation Zero 2: A Flow-Centric Sequential Regulation Planning Framework to Counter Regulation Cascading in Pre-tactical Air Traffic Flow Management
generated_summary:
This paper introduces Regulation Zero v2 (RZ), a flow-centric framework for pre-tactical air traffic flow management that addresses "Regulation Cascading"—the phenomenon where independently designed flow regulations interact unpredictably, creating secondary hotspots and undermining network performance. The key contribution is framing sequential regulation planning as a Markov Decision Process and solving it using hierarchical Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), enabling the system to anticipate how each regulation reshapes demand before proposing subsequent ones.

The framework comprises three components: an MCTS-based search over regulation sequences, a regulation proposal engine that extracts candidate flows through community detection on flight-similarity graphs and evaluates them using novel heuristics (Nominal Relief and Induced Overload), and a First-Planned-First-Served slot allocator that preserves operational fairness. This architecture is designed to integrate with existing ATFM workflows without requiring fundamental operational changes.

Experiments on seven full days of pan-European traffic (22,000–25,000 flights each) demonstrate that RZ achieves 30–40% higher objective improvements than Simulated Annealing and NSGA-II baselines while affecting approximately 25% fewer flights. Ablation studies confirm that MCTS contributes critically, with its removal causing roughly 50% performance degradation, quantifying the cost of regulation cascading. RZ excels particularly in high-exceedance, large-scale regimes, while flight-centric methods show superior delay efficiency, suggesting the approaches are complementary rather than competitive.
original_abstract: Air Traffic Flow Management (ATFM) traffic regulations are being increasingly used as rising demand meets persistent workforce shortages. This operational strain has amplified a critical phenomenon that we call \emph{regulation cascading}: the compounding, non-linear interactions that occur when multiple regulations influence one another in unpredictable ways. As the number and complexity of regulations grow, cascading effects become more pronounced, undermining the network operator's ability to protect sectors reliably. To address this challenge, we introduce Regulation Zero 2, an updated sequential planning framework that natively operates in the regulation space, optimizing over ordered sequences of flow-level regulations that remain compatible as much as possible with existing slot-allocation systems such as CASA and RBS++. We equipped Regulation Zero 2 with new heuristics to render flow finding more efficient. At its core, the method employs a hierarchical Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) that first samples congestion hotspots and then selects candidate regulations synthesized by a local proposal engine. Each proposal is evaluated by a fast First-Planned-First-Served (FPFS) allocator to estimate its reward, with these feedbacks guiding the subsequent MCTS exploration. Experiments on many pan-European summer-peak traffic days that Regulation Zero delivers promising and consistent performance. Compared to a flight-centric simulated-annealing and NSGA-II baselines, it achieves markedly higher objective improvements, while maintaining a tighter scope of impact on the network. Ablation studies also found that Regulation Cascading could reduce up to 50\% of potential effectiveness. RZ also preserves FPFS fairness and supports expert knowledge injection, offering a pragmatic and low-disruption pathway toward automation in operations.

title: An upper bound on the growth of minimal graphs
generated_summary:
This paper establishes a sharp upper bound on the growth rate of positive solutions to the minimal surface equation on unbounded simply connected plane domains with zero boundary values, confirming a previously stated conjecture. The main result (Theorem 1) proves that for such solutions, the maximum function M(r,u) — defined as the maximum of u over the circle of radius r intersected with the domain — satisfies M(r,u) ≤ Cr for sufficiently large r, where C is a constant depending on the solution.

The methodology employs techniques from the theory of univalent harmonic mappings and conformal representation. The authors work with the Weierstrass representation of the minimal surface, mapping the problem to the upper half-plane and analyzing the associated holomorphic functions. A key lemma establishes growth properties of the mapping function using the representation of positive harmonic functions. The proof proceeds through an iterative expansion process: starting from an arc in a sector, the authors repeatedly expand outward, tracking how the solution values grow relative to the radial distance. Estimates on the conjugate function, bounded by a constant, play a crucial role in controlling the solution on extended arcs reaching the domain boundary.

Combined with the previously established lower bound of logarithmic growth (Theorem A), this result provides a complete picture of the possible growth rates for minimal graphs over unbounded domains. The upper bound is shown to be sharp, as demonstrated by the upper half of the horizontal catenoid, and generalizes earlier results that required the domain to be contained in a half-plane.
original_abstract: Graphs of solutions to the minimal surface equation over simply connected domains with boundary values 0 can have at most exponential growth.

title: The filter of singularities in global anisotropic microlocal analysis
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a novel concept for analyzing singularities of tempered distributions in the context of global anisotropic microlocal analysis: the **filter of anisotropic Gabor singularities**. Unlike traditional wave front sets, which are closed conic subsets of phase space, this new notion is formulated as a filter—a non-empty collection of subsets of phase space closed under enlargement and finite intersection. The key methodological innovation involves relaxing the conic invariance requirement imposed on regular subsets in the definition of anisotropic Gabor wave front sets, thereby capturing more refined microlocal information.

The authors develop this framework for positive rational anisotropy parameters, constructing the necessary microlocal excision symbols and establishing fundamental properties of the filter. A central result characterizes the filter of singularities through the short-time Fourier transform. The paper demonstrates that the classical anisotropic Gabor wave front set can be recovered from the filter by intersecting all filter sets that are closed and appropriately invariant, confirming that the filter carries strictly more information.

The main applications concern propagation of singularities for linear evolution equations with anisotropic Hamiltonian Weyl symbols. The filter framework yields generalized propagation results that relax conditions on the Hamiltonian's power, and enables a new supercritical propagation result in dimension one. This work extends earlier approaches using dyadic filters and frequency-variable filters to full phase space, offering a more flexible and informative tool for studying singularity propagation in equations involving anharmonic oscillators and related operators.
original_abstract: We define a filter of time-frequency anisotropic global singularities of phase space for tempered distributions. The filter contains information from the corresponding anisotropic Gabor wave front set and admits propagation results for the Cauchy problem for certain linear evolution equations of Schrödinger type that generalize the harmonic oscillator.

title: On Weighted Star--Convex Graphs
generated_summary:
This paper introduces the concept of weighted star-convex graphs, establishing a graph-theoretic framework that bridges geometric star-convexity, convex function theory, and discrete mathematics. A weighted graph is defined as star-convex if there exists a vertex from which weighted-monotone paths extend to every leaf vertex, with the collection of such vertices forming the graph's "core"—analogous to the center of a star-convex set in geometry.

The authors develop several structural properties of these graphs. They demonstrate that the union of two star-convex graphs remains star-convex when their cores intersect, while their intersection may fail to preserve star-convexity—a result that notably contradicts the typical behavior observed in algebraic and geometric structures. For star-convex trees, they prove that extremal weights are attained at leaf vertices or core vertices. A central result establishes that a weighted graph is star-convex if and only if a star-convex tree containing all its leaf vertices can be extracted from it, effectively reducing the structural analysis of star-convex graphs to trees.

As a key contribution connecting convex sequences to spider graphs, the authors prove that convex sequences satisfying certain boundary conditions can be embedded as vertex weights into regular spider graphs to produce star-convex graphs. This result reinterprets weight allocation as a transportation problem. The framework offers potential applications in chemical graph theory, network science, and algorithm design, particularly for core detection in weighted networks.
original_abstract: The primary objective of this paper is to investigate the notions of geometric and sequential convexity within a graph-theoretic framework, with the aim of examining various structural properties and exploring the connection between these two branches of mathematics. A simple connected vertex-weighted graph $G(V,E)$ with a non-empty set of leaf vertices is said to be star-convex if there exists at least one node $u\in V(G)$ such that, for every chosen leaf vertex $v$, there is a monotone path (either increasing or decreasing) connecting $v$ to $u$. One of the main results states that a graph $G$ is star-convex if and only if there exists a tree $T\subseteq G$ that contains all leaf vertices and is itself star-convex. On the other hand, a sequence $\big(u_n\big)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ is said to be convex if it satisfies the following inequality $$ 2u_{i}\leq u_{i-1}+u_{i+1}\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad i\in \mathbb{N}. $$ We demonstrate that, under minimal assumptions, a class of convex sequences can be embedded into a spider graph so as to make it star-convex.

title: Quadrature-Enhanced Monte Carlo fPINN Method for High-Dimensional Fractional PDEs
generated_summary:
This paper presents a quadrature-enhanced Monte Carlo fractional physics-informed neural network (QE-MC-fPINN) method for solving high-dimensional fractional partial differential equations involving the fractional Laplacian on bounded domains. The main contribution is a geometry-adaptive discretization that addresses key challenges of hypersingular nonlocal operators, exterior Dirichlet constraints, reduced boundary regularity, and high dimensionality simultaneously.

The methodology introduces a spatially varying splitting radius based on the distance from each evaluation point to the domain boundary, decomposing the fractional Laplacian into three components: a singular near-field term, a regular interior far-field term, and an exterior far-field term. Gauss-Jacobi quadrature handles the singular radial integral, standard Gauss quadrature addresses the regular interior radial integral, and Monte Carlo sampling manages the angular variables to maintain scalability in high dimensions. The discretization is embedded within a feature-enhanced PINN trial space incorporating explicit boundary factors to improve approximation of low-regularity solutions near boundaries.

Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing MC-fPINN and improved MC-fPINN approaches in accuracy and convergence, with advantages particularly pronounced for problems with strong boundary singularities and larger fractional orders. The method scales effectively to very high dimensions, with experiments reported up to 10,000 dimensions for the fractional Poisson equation. This work provides an accurate, robust, and scalable mesh-free framework for bounded-domain fractional Laplacian problems, significantly advancing the computational tractability of high-dimensional nonlocal PDEs.
original_abstract: Fractional PDEs involving the fractional Laplacian on bounded domains are challenging because of hypersingular nonlocal kernels, exterior Dirichlet constraints, reduced boundary regularity, and the high computational cost in high dimensions. To address these issues, we first adopt a spatially varying radius with directional distance-to-boundary information, which yields a geometry-adaptive three-part decomposition of the fractional Laplacian: singular near-field, regular interior far-field, and analytical exterior far-field contributions. Then we employ Gauss-Jacobi quadrature for the singular radial integral, Gauss quadrature for the regular interior radial integral, and Monte Carlo sampling for the angular variables. A feature-enhanced physics-informed neural network trial space is finally used to tackle the low-regularity behavior near the boundary. Through the above steps, we obtain a quadrature-enhanced Monte Carlo fractional physics-informed neural network (QE-MC-fPINN) method. Numerical experiments on fractional Poisson equations and time-dependent fractional PDEs show that, on the tested benchmarks, the proposed method outperforms two representative MC-fPINN discretizations in accuracy and convergence, especially for solutions with strong boundary singularities.

title: Quantum $f$-divergences via Nussbaum-Szkoła Distributions in Semifinite von Neumann Algebras
generated_summary:
This paper extends the concept of Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions from the von Neumann algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space to general semifinite von Neumann algebras. The main contribution is proving that the quantum f-divergence between any two normal states on a semifinite von Neumann algebra equals the classical f-divergence between corresponding classical probability distributions, called Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions.

The methodology relies on a formula for the relative modular operator in semifinite von Neumann algebras, previously discovered by Łuczak, Podsędkowska, and Wieczorek, combined with the multiplicative form of the Spectral Theorem for strongly commuting normal operators. This approach creates a bridge between non-commutative and commutative L₂-spaces, enabling the construction of a σ-finite measure space and measurable functions that define the classical Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions associated with the quantum states.

The key result demonstrates that quantum f-divergences—encompassing important special cases such as relative entropy, χ²-divergence, and total variation distance—can be computed via their classical counterparts. As applications, the authors show how classical f-divergence inequalities between probability distributions automatically transfer to quantum f-divergence inequalities between normal states on semifinite von Neumann algebras.

The significance of this work is both mathematical and physical. It substantially generalizes previous results limited to finite-dimensional or B(H) settings, and it connects to physical contexts where Type II von Neumann algebras arise, including quantum field theory, black hole physics, and random matrix models. The authors identify extending the result to general (non-semifinite) von Neumann algebras as the main open problem.
original_abstract: In this article, we prove that the quantum $f$-divergence between two normal states on a semifinite von~Neumann algebra is equal to the classical $f$-divergence between two corresponding classical states, which are called Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions. This result has been proved by the second named author and T.C.~John for normal states on the von~Neumann algebra $\mathbb{B}(\mathscr{H})$ of all bounded operators on a Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$. We extend their result for normal states on any semifinite von~Neumann algebra, not only $\mathbb{B}(\mathscr{H})$.

title: Minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy functional with the Flory-Huggins potential under strong anchoring conditions
generated_summary:
This paper resolves an open problem concerning the minimizers of the Cahn-Hilliard energy functional equipped with the physically relevant Flory-Huggins (logarithmic) potential under homogeneous Dirichlet (strong anchoring) boundary conditions. The logarithmic singularity of this potential, which enforces the physical constraint that the order parameter remains within admissible concentration bounds, requires substantially different analytical techniques compared to previously studied quartic and trigonometric potentials.

The authors employ a methodology centered on the Nehari manifold to study the existence and properties of minimizers, alongside careful approximations and modifications of the Flory-Huggins potential to handle its singular behavior. The main theoretical result establishes a bifurcation phenomenon governed by the interplay between the transition layer thickness parameter, the rescaled temperature parameter, and the smallest eigenvalue of the negative Laplacian. Specifically, when the product of the squared transition layer thickness and the smallest eigenvalue exceeds a critical threshold determined by the temperature, the unique minimizer is the trivial solution. Below this threshold, two nontrivial symmetric minimizers emerge, bounded by the potential's minimizers. Notably, the temperature enters as an additional bifurcation parameter absent in prior quartic or trigonometric settings, yielding a richer bifurcation structure.

Numerical simulations using the Allen-Cahn equation with forward Euler time-stepping corroborate the theoretical predictions. The results extend the understanding of phase separation models under rigid boundary constraints and open pathways to analyzing other boundary conditions with singular potentials.
original_abstract: In this paper, we theoretically and numerically study the minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy with the Flory-Huggins potential under the strong anchoring condition, i.e., the Dirichlet boundary condition. We reveal bifurcation phenomena mediated by the boundary condition, the transition layer thickness, and the temperature of the system. Numerical simulations are also presented to approximate the minimizers of this energy by solving a gradient-flow equation, namely the Allen-Cahn equation constrained with strong anchoring conditions and random initial data. The effects of varying the transition layer thickness and temperature are presented to confirm the theoretical analysis.

title: The right invariant metric on the analytic automorphism group of the unit open disk induced by maximal modulus
generated_summary:
This paper introduces and studies a right invariant metric on the analytic automorphism group Aut(D) of the unit open disk D, defined using the maximal modulus (H∞-norm). The metric, denoted d_H∞, measures the distance between two automorphisms by taking the supremum of the quasi-hyperbolic metric applied to their compositions over the disk. Each automorphism of D can be parameterized by a rotation angle θ and a point u in D, providing a natural local coordinate system for the group manifold.

The authors derive an explicit distance formula for d_H∞ between any two elements of Aut(D), expressed in terms of the parameters of the automorphisms. The formula involves two cases depending on a geometric condition relating the parameters. They further analyze the induced geometric structure, showing it constitutes a non-Riemannian reversible almost regular Finsler structure on Aut(D), providing its explicit expression. The almost regularity means the Finsler metric is smooth except along certain directions. Notably, despite being reversible, this structure remains non-Riemannian—a phenomenon possible for almost regular Randers metrics but impossible for standard Randers metrics by Deicke's theorem. The authors also prove that the resulting metric space is not a geodesic space.

This work connects complex analysis, group theory, and Finsler geometry, contributing to the understanding of invariant metrics on transformation groups with applications in hyperbolic geometry, conformal field theory, and computer graphics.
original_abstract: In this paper, we study the right invariant metric $d_{H^{\infty}}$ on the analytic automorphism group $\rm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$ of the unit open disk $\mathbb{D}$ induced by maximal modulus, that is, $d_{H^{\infty}}(\varphi, ψ)=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}|\varphi(z)-ψ(z)|$ for any $\varphi, ψ\in \rm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$. We give the explicit formula of the right invariant metric $d_{H^{\infty}}$ and characterize the almost regular Finsler geometric structure of $(\rm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}), d_{H^{\infty}})$.

title: Fractionally Calabi-Yau algebras and cluster tilting

original_abstract: We show that the class of twisted fractionally Calabi-Yau algebras of finite global dimension coincides with the stable endomorphism algebras of $d$-cluster tilting modules over $d$-representation-finite algebras. This is an application of our main result stating that an algebra $A$ of finite global dimension is twisted fractionally Calabi-Yau if and only if there exists $i$ such that the replicated algebra $A^{(i)}$ is a higher Auslander algebra if and only if there exist infinitely many $i$ such that $A^{(i)}$ is a higher Auslander algebra. This gives a new connection between the study of higher Auslander-Reiten theory and twisted fractionally Calabi-Yau algebras, and provides a new construction of large classes of higher Auslander algebras and higher representation-finite algebras. We give several applications such as an explicit characterisation of twisted $\frac{n}{2}$-Calabi-Yau algebras, and a triangle equivalence between the bounded derived category of a twisted fractionally Calabi-Yau algebra of finite global dimension and the $\mathbb{Z}$-graded stable module category of an associated higher preprojective algebra.

title: Regularity Analysis and Tensor Neural Network Methods for Quasiperiodic Elliptic Equations

original_abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel machine learning method based on an adaptive tensor neural network subspace for solving quasiperiodic elliptic problems. To this end, we first provide a theoretical analysis of the associated quasiperiodic and periodic function spaces and establish regularity estimates for the quasiperiodic elliptic problems. In particular, under the Diophantine condition, we derive a suitable condition on the source term to guarantee the regularity of the solution, which provides a theoretical basis for the design of numerical schemes. An efficient numerical method is then designed by combining the projection method with tensor neural networks. Leveraging the special structure of tensor neural networks, high-dimensional integration can be performed directly and with high accuracy, without relying on Monte Carlo methods. title: The Lefschetz type theorem for fundamental group schemes
generated_summary:

The methodology centers on a systematic study of restriction functors from a variety to an ample divisor within the language of Tannakian categories. The main results establish Lefschetz-type isomorphisms in three settings: characteristic zero (for smooth projective varieties of dimension at least three), positive characteristic (under ampleness and global generation conditions), and varieties liftable to the Witt vectors W₂(k). These results generalize Langer's earlier work from algebraically closed fields to perfect fields. The framework clarifies the categorical mechanisms underlying geometric Lefschetz-type phenomena and provides a template applicable to future fundamental group schemes defined via Tannakian categories.
original_abstract: Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a connected scheme proper over $k$, $D\subsetneq X$ an ample effective connected divisor, $x\in D(k)$. For Tannakian categories $\mathcal{C}_X$ and $\mathcal{C}_D$ whose objects consist of vector bundles on $X$ and $D$ respectively, we establish general Tannakian criteria for the natural homomorphism \(π(\mathcal{C}_D,x)\longrightarrow π(\mathcal{C}_X,x)\) to be faithfully flat, a closed immersion, or an isomorphism. As applications, under Langer type positivity assumptions, we prove that \(π^{\ast}(D,x)\longrightarrow π^{\ast}(X,x)\) is an isomorphism for $\ast\in\{S,N,EN,F, EF,Loc,ELoc,\acute{e}t,E\acute{e}t,uni\}$ over perfect fields.

title: Existence of small semi-vortex solutions for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger system with Rashba type Spin-Orbit coupling on $\mathbb{R}^2$
generated_summary:

The authors employ a variational approach, minimizing the energy functional under a mass constraint to obtain solutions of specific semi-vortex form. The key innovation involves comparing nonlinear and linear energies using Bessel functions of the first kind, which arise as resonance functions from the essential spectrum. Lieb's compactness theorem and the Brezis-Lieb lemma are applied to handle the lack of radial symmetry, which prevents standard compactness embeddings.

The main results establish the existence of countably many small non-scattering global solutions (indexed by vortex number), demonstrating that small data scattering fails for this system. The authors also prove the existence of small stable energy ground states and, in the special case of equal nonlinearity coefficients, construct mixed-mode solutions combining two semi-vortices. Global existence criteria and orbital stability of ground states are additionally established.

These results are significant because, unlike standard cubic NLS equations where ground states have fixed mass and small solutions scatter, the spin-orbit coupling fundamentally alters the solution landscape by enabling arbitrarily small non-scattering solutions through bifurcation from the essential spectrum.
original_abstract: We consider the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger system with Rashba type Spin-Orbit coupling (SOC) on $\mathbb{R}^2$, which is also called the Gross--Pitaevskii equation with SOC. The system describes SO-coupled spinor BEC in physics. In the literature of physics, the existence of small semi-vortex solutions and small ground state is known. In the present paper, we give their mathematical proofs by finding minimizers of the energy under small mass constraint.

title: Hypergraph Mining via Proximity Matrix
generated_summary:
This paper proposes a proximity matrix P for hypergraph representation that addresses limitations of the traditional binary incidence matrix M in capturing the heterogeneous strengths of node-hyperedge relationships. The key insight is that nodes belonging to small hyperedges have tighter connections than those in large hyperedges, a distinction the incidence matrix cannot encode.

The proximity matrix is constructed through a resource allocation process on hypergraphs, transforming the binary membership information in M into continuous-valued proximity scores that account for the heterogeneity of node degrees and hyperedge orders. Based on this matrix, the authors develop three simple algorithms—HRA@LP, HRA@CD, and HRA@VNI—for link prediction, community detection, and vital nodes identification, respectively. For link prediction, a similarity matrix derived from P scores candidate hyperedges; for community detection, a spectral method using a normalized Laplacian built from P is employed; for vital nodes identification, a centrality measure based on products of proximity values quantifies spreading influence.

Extensive experiments on 18 real-world hypergraphs demonstrate that these proximity matrix-based algorithms consistently outperform state-of-the-art benchmarks across all three tasks. Notably, direct comparison between P-based and M-based algorithms confirms the superiority of continuous-valued proximity information over binary membership encoding. The authors argue that the proximity matrix can serve as a foundational tool for hypergraph analysis broadly, with potential applications extending to curvature computation, optimal transport, and weighted dynamical processes on hypergraphs.
original_abstract: Hypergraphs serve as an effective tool widely adopted to characterize higher-order interactions in complex systems. The most intuitive and commonly used mathematical instrument for representing a hypergraph is the incidence matrix, in which each entry is binary, indicating whether the corresponding node belongs to the corresponding hyperedge. Although the incidence matrix has become a foundational tool for hypergraph analysis and mining, we argue that its binary nature is insufficient to accurately capture the complexity of node-hyperedge relationships arising from the fact that different hyperedges can contain vastly different numbers of nodes. Accordingly, based on the resource allocation process on hypergraphs, we propose a continuous-valued matrix to quantify the proximity between nodes and hyperedges. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed proximity matrix, we investigate three important tasks in hypergraph mining: link prediction, vital nodes identification, and community detection. Experimental results on numerous real-world hypergraphs show that simply designed algorithms centered on the proximity matrix significantly outperform benchmark algorithms across these three tasks.

title: Singularities in phase separation models: a spectral element approach for the nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equation
generated_summary:

They rigorously demonstrate the strict separation property, showing solutions remain uniformly bounded away from pure phases.

Methodologically, the authors introduce a novel spectral element method based on a "multishape" decomposition technique to approximate convolutions against singular kernels. This approach partitions the domain around each collocation point, isolating the singularity into a small neighborhood where piecewise-constant approximation is applied, while standard pseudospectral methods handle the remainder. A differential algebraic equation solver enforces Neumann boundary conditions. Analytical error bounds are established and computationally verified.

Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness across different parameter regimes, kernel scalings, and domain geometries, revealing rich phase-separation dynamics including pattern formation and convergence to nontrivial stationary states. The method achieves high-resolution solutions with limited computational resources, and all code is provided as open source. This work opens pathways for solving coupled systems involving nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equations in applications such as tumor growth modeling.
original_abstract: The nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equation provides a natural extension of the classical model for phase separation by incorporating long-range interactions through a singular convolution kernel. While this formulation admits a rich existence and regularity theory, its numerical approximation remains challenging: discretisation of the nonlocal term leads to dense operators, and the singularity of the kernel requires special treatment in collocation-based schemes. In this work, we develop an efficient and error-controlled numerical framework for the nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard system with constant mobility, logarithmic potential, Newtonian interaction kernel, and no-flux boundary conditions. Our approach is based on a pseudospectral multishape method that accurately approximates the action of singular convolution operators. We present high-resolution numerical solutions for this nonlocal system of equations that can be achieved with limited computational resources.

title: Cyclic Equalizability Characterized by Parikh Vectors
generated_summary:
This paper completely characterizes cyclic equalizability for two words over arbitrary finite alphabets, resolving open problems posed by Shinagawa and Nuida in the context of card-based cryptography. Cyclic equalizability captures whether two words can be transformed into cyclic shifts of one another by inserting identical letters at identical positions in both words. This notion arises naturally in card-based cryptographic protocols, where inserting letters corresponds to adding cards to face-down sequences, and random cuts make cyclically shifted sequences indistinguishable.

The main result establishes that two words over a finite alphabet are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Parikh vector—that is, if and only if they contain the same number of occurrences of each letter. This equivalence connects cyclic equalizability precisely to the well-studied notion of Abelian equivalence in combinatorics on words. The proof employs techniques from combinatorics on words, utilizing structural analysis of cyclic shifts, simultaneous insertions, and readings with specific step sizes to construct the required transformations.

This characterization strictly generalizes the previously known binary case, where the condition reduces to equal Hamming weight, and resolves the ternary alphabet case as a special instance. For card-based cryptography, the result demonstrates that the indistinguishability of two card encodings under insertions and random cuts is entirely determined by the multiset of cards present, providing a simple and complete criterion for protocol analysis.
original_abstract: Cyclic equalizability is a notion introduced by Shinagawa and Nuida in 2025, in the study of card-based cryptography. Informally, a collection of words is cyclically equalizable if, by inserting the same letters at the same positions in all words, they can be transformed into words that are cyclic shifts of one another. Shinagawa and Nuida showed that two binary words of equal length are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Hamming weight. They also posed the problem of characterizing cyclic equalizability over larger alphabets. In this paper, we completely characterize cyclic equalizability for two words over an arbitrary finite alphabet by proving that two words are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Parikh vector.

title: Scalable Multigrid Solver for the Helmholtz Equation: Real-Shifted Coarse Grid Correction
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a real-shifted coarse grid correction (RS-CGC) method for solving the high-frequency Helmholtz equation using multigrid, addressing the longstanding challenge of achieving wavenumber-independent convergence without expensive complex shifts. The key innovation is interweaving a real shift into the Galerkin coarsening process combined with high-order discretization and intergrid transfer operators, which corrects numerical dispersion between grid levels without requiring re-discretization or optimization of finite difference weights.

The authors develop a specialized grid-to-grid dispersion analysis that quantifies the misalignment between fine and coarse grid operators, enabling theoretical optimization of the real shift parameters and estimation of maximum achievable grid sizes. The method employs a three-level W-cycle with simple damped Jacobi smoothing using only one pre- and one post-relaxation.

Numerical experiments demonstrate that RS-CGC achieves nearly constant iteration counts (6–8 iterations) for 12 grid points per wavelength across grids up to 1024² cells in 2D, outperforming the classical complex-shifted Laplacian preconditioner by factors of 2.6 to 15.2. For 3D problems on the heterogeneous Overthrust model, the method maintains a constant iteration count of 10 with linear time scalability. The approach works effectively for both homogeneous and heterogeneous media, including realistic geophysical models like Marmousi, representing a significant advance toward practical, scalable Helmholtz solvers for wave propagation problems.
original_abstract: We present a convergent and scalable multigrid solver for high-frequency Helmholtz equations. Standard multigrid methods do not converge for high-frequency Helmholtz problems, and a common cure is adding a complex shift and using the shifted operator as a preconditioner. Nevertheless, the complex shift prevents scalability. In this work we present a new method that achieves scalable convergence of a 3-level cycle without a complex shift. Our key idea is real-shifting the coarsest grid Galerkin operator, to correct the numerical dispersion between the grids. We show that this real-shifted coarse grid correction leads to a scalable 3-level method, for problems with 12 grid points per wavelength on the fine grid, and a convergent cycle with very few iterations for 11 grid points per wavelength, using standard point-smoothers. For problems with 10 grid points per wavelength, our method combined with a modest complex shift outperforms the standard complex shifted Laplacian method by an order of magnitude. We demonstrate wavenumber independent convergence for heterogeneous geophysical media in 2D and 3D.

title: Verma Bases and Kashiwara-Nakashima Tableaux of $\mathfrak{sp}_4$

The Verma basis is a monomial basis for highest weight modules expressed in terms of negative simple root vectors, depending on a reduced expression of the longest Weyl group element. While Verma bases were originally computed for several Lie algebra types by Li, Moody, Nicolescu, and Patera in 1986, rigorous proofs of linear independence remained incomplete in many cases. The authors address this gap for sp₄ by transforming the system of inequalities governing the indices in the Verma basis vectors into the combinatorial conditions defining KN tableaux, which were developed by Kashiwara and Nakashima to label elements of symplectic crystal bases.

The main result demonstrates two facts: first, there exists a weight-preserving bijection between the Verma vector system and the set of KN tableaux of sp₄ with the appropriate shape determined by the highest weight; second, the Verma vector system forms a basis of the irreducible module. The proof of linear independence is carried out directly.

This work is significant because it bridges an algebraic construction (Verma bases) with a combinatorial framework (KN tableaux), providing new structural insight into representations of type C Lie algebras. The authors indicate that this approach extends to Lie superalgebras, having already obtained Verma bases for spo(4|1).
original_abstract: We construct a one-to-one correspondence between the Verma basis vectors of a finite dimensional irreducible representation $L(λ)$ of the symplectic Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ and the Kashiwara-Nakashima tableaux of $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ with shape $λ$ naturally. We also give a proof of the linear independence of the Verma vector system directly.

title: On Fourier decay and the distance set problem
generated_summary:
This paper advances the Falconer distance set problem by establishing significantly improved dimensional thresholds under mild Fourier analytic assumptions, leveraging the recently introduced Fourier spectrum framework. The classical conjecture posits that a Borel set in ℝᵈ with Hausdorff dimension exceeding d/2 must have a distance set of full dimension. The authors show that for Salem sets (sets with optimal Fourier decay), the distance set has full Hausdorff dimension whenever the set's dimension exceeds d/4 + 1, dramatically improving Mattila's classical result and beating the d/2 threshold for dimensions d ≥ 5.

The methodology centers on exploiting the Fourier spectrum, which interpolates between Fourier dimension and Hausdorff dimension by capturing Lᵖ decay of the Fourier transform for intermediate values of p. The authors derive general estimates that combine information from both small and large values of the spectrum parameter, yielding flexible conditions applicable to sets with varied Fourier analytic properties—including sets with Fourier dimension zero.

Key results include concrete, checkable conditions on the Fourier spectrum guaranteeing full-dimensional distance sets or positive Lebesgue measure of pinned distance sets for almost all pins. The paper also addresses the two-set distance problem and provides near-sharpness results through explicit constructions.

The significance lies in demonstrating that arithmetic rigidity, rather than mere dimensionality, is the true obstruction in the distance set problem, and that even weak Fourier regularity conditions substantially lower the dimensional threshold required.
original_abstract: We study the Falconer distance set problem in Euclidean space and obtain improved dimensional estimates under natural Fourier analytic assumptions cast in terms of the Fourier dimension and spectrum. Interestingly, under reasonably mild assumptions, we are able to beat the $d/2$ dimension threshold in dimensions $d \geq 5$. For example, we show that (in any ambient spatial dimension $d$) a Borel set with Fourier dimension at least $2$ has a distance set of full Hausdorff dimension. We also show that (in any ambient spatial dimension $d$) a Borel set with Fourier spectrum at least $d/4+1$ at $θ=1/2$ has a distance set of full Hausdorff dimension. In particular, this can hold for sets with Fourier dimension zero (provided $d \geq 4$). We also consider pinned variants of these problems and construct examples that demonstrate the sharpness (or near sharpness) of our results.

title: Maximum Solow--Polasky Diversity Subset Selection Is NP-hard Even in the Euclidean Plane
generated_summary:
