The proof proceeds via a reduction from geometric unit-disk independent set, a problem known to be NP-hard. The key methodological challenge is that the Solow–Polasky objective depends nonlinearly on the distance structure through a matrix inverse, preventing direct adaptation of the earlier general-metric argument. The authors introduce two main technical ingredients: a bounded-box comparison lemma establishing that the Solow–Polasky objective is monotone in each off-diagonal similarity entry when all such entries are uniformly small, and a geometric margin observation showing that finite point sets in the plane naturally provide a positive separation between similarities of independent pairs versus adjacent pairs in unit-disk graphs. Together, these replace the exact two-distance construction with a robust geometric comparison argument.

The result holds for every fixed positive value of the exponential decay parameter in the similarity function. The significance lies in demonstrating that NP-hardness of maximum Solow–Polasky diversity subset selection persists even under severe geometric restrictions, establishing fundamental computational limits for diversity optimization in low-dimensional Euclidean settings relevant to conservation biology, engineering design, and multi-objective optimization.
original_abstract: We prove that, for every fixed $θ_0>0$, selecting a subset of prescribed cardinality that maximizes the Solow--Polasky diversity indicator is NP-hard for finite point sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the Euclidean metric, and therefore also for finite point sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every fixed dimension $d \ge 2$. This strictly strengthens our earlier NP-hardness result for general metric spaces by showing that hardness persists under the severe geometric restriction to the Euclidean plane. At the same time, the Euclidean proof technique is different from the conceptually easier earlier argument for arbitrary metric spaces, and that general metric-space construction does not directly translate to the Euclidean setting. In the earlier proof one can use an exact construction tailored to arbitrary metrics, essentially exploiting a two-distance structure. In contrast, such an exact realization is unavailable in fixed-dimensional Euclidean space, so the present reduction requires a genuinely geometric argument. Our Euclidean proof is based on two distance thresholds, which allow us to separate yes-instances from no-instances by robust inequalities rather than by the exact construction used in the general metric setting. The main technical ingredient is a bounded-box comparison lemma for the nonlinear objective $\mathbf{1}^{\top}Z^{-1}\mathbf{1}$, where $Z_{ij}=e^{-θ_0 d(x_i,x_j)}$. This lemma controls the effect of perturbations in the pairwise distances well enough to transfer the gap created by the reduction. The reduction is from \emph{Geometric Unit-Disk Independent Set}. We present the main argument in geometric form for finite subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$, with an appendix supplying the bit-complexity details needed for polynomial-time reducibility.

title: Algebraic Distance Optimization in Polyhedral Norms
generated_summary:
This paper investigates Voronoi diagrams and distance optimization for algebraic varieties equipped with polyhedral norms, extending previous work on Euclidean distance optimization to non-smooth metric settings. The central question is: given a point on an algebraic variety, which data points in ambient space have their distance to the variety minimized at that point?

The authors develop a framework combining polyhedral geometry, algebraic geometry, and differential topology. For a smooth point on a variety, they show that its Voronoi cell is contained within a union of polyhedral cones—termed the Voronoi cone—determined by the relative position of the variety's normal space with respect to the inner normal fan of the unit ball. Equivalently, this structure can be characterized through the intersection of the dual unit ball with the normal space. For varieties of pure codimension one, the authors construct a stratification based on the dimension of Voronoi cones, providing a concrete recipe for computing this stratification using transversality conditions from differential topology via the preimage theorem.

The paper also analyzes the medial axis—the locus of points equidistant to multiple closest points on the variety—decomposing it into components associated with pairs of faces of the unit ball and establishing degree bounds for the algebraic closure of these components in extreme cases involving vertex-vertex, facet-facet, and vertex-facet pairings.

This work is motivated by applications in optimal transport, where Wasserstein distances induce polyhedral norms via Lipschitz polytopes, and contributes to the broader algebraic study of non-Euclidean distance optimization.
original_abstract: We consider the distance minimization problem to a real algebraic variety $X \subseteq \RR^n$ when the metric is induced by a polyhedral norm. Each point in the variety has a Voronoi cell whose geometry depends on the normal space at the point and the inner normal fan of the polyhedral ball. For codimension-one varieties, we decompose $X$ into sets of points whose Voronoi cones have the same dimension, which is the expected dimension of their Voronoi cell. We prove that this decomposition is a stratification of $X$ and that each strata is a semialgebraic set. We conclude by giving an algebraic description of the medial axis, which is the locus of points whose minimal distance to $X$ is achieved at more than one point on $X$.

title: The eigenvector centrality of hypergraphs
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a novel eigenvector centrality measure for non-uniform hypergraphs (HEC) that extends existing eigenvector centrality definitions, which were previously limited to ordinary graphs and uniform hypergraphs. The key contribution is a unified tensor representation that accommodates hyperedges of varying sizes by leveraging the least common multiple of the hypergraph's cardinality set to construct an adjacency tensor. A vertex's centrality is determined by the sum of geometric means of scores of all vertices sharing the same hyperedge, transforming the centrality computation into a tensor eigenvalue problem. The authors prove that for connected hypergraphs, the constructed tensor is weakly irreducible, guaranteeing the existence and uniqueness of a positive eigenvector solution.

Experiments on six real-world hypergraphs from diverse domains—including email networks, co-authorship networks, and recommendation systems—demonstrate that HEC captures complementary structural information beyond classical centrality measures such as degree, hyperdegree, clique-expansion, and vector centralities. HEC shows moderate correlations with existing measures but identifies substantially different sets of critical vertices, particularly among top-ranked nodes. Robustness analysis reveals that HEC effectively identifies structurally important vertices while prioritizing overall network resilience. Notably, HEC assigns higher scores to vertices in smaller hyperedges, reflecting stronger interactions within compact groups.

This work provides a principled mathematical framework for assessing vertex importance in non-uniform hypergraphs, offering a fresh perspective that jointly considers hyperedge heterogeneity, local influence, and global iterative dependence.
original_abstract: A hypergraph is called uniform when every hyperedge contains the same number of vertices, otherwise, it is called non-uniform. In the real world, many systems give rise to non-uniform hypergraphs, such as email networks and co-authorship networks. A uniform hypergraph has a natural one-to-one correspondence with its adjacency tensor. In 2019, Benson proposed the eigenvector centrality of uniform hypergraphs via its adjacency tensor. In this paper, we define an adjacency tensor for hypergraphs and propose the eigenvector centrality for hypergraphs. When the hypergraph is uniform, our proposed eigenvector centrality reduces to Benson's. When each edge of the uniform hypergraph contains exactly two vertices, our proposed centrality reduces to the eigenvector centrality of graphs. We conducted experiments on several real-world hypergraph datasets. The results show that, compared to traditional centrality measures, the proposed centrality measure provides a unique perspective for identifying important vertices and can also effectively identify them.

title: Solving Convex-Concave Problems with $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-4/(3p+1)})$ $p$th-Order Oracle Complexity

This paper advances the theory of higher-order methods for smooth convex-concave minimax optimization, breaking the previously conjectured optimal complexity barrier of Õ(ε⁻²ᐟ⁽ᵖ⁺¹⁾) pth-order oracle calls that all existing methods achieved. The authors establish a new upper complexity bound of Õ(ε⁻⁴ᐟ⁽³ᵖ⁺¹⁾), which is strictly better for all orders p ≥ 1.

The methodology centers on applying a high-order momentum acceleration technique to both primal and dual variables, reducing the original minimax problem to solving a sequence of Õ(ε⁻⁴ᐟ⁽³ᵖ⁺¹⁾) proximal minimax subproblems. Each subproblem is regularized to have a constant condition number for pth-order methods, enabling efficient solution by any existing convergent pth-order algorithm. The framework, called Minimax-AIPE, employs a three-level nested loop structure: an outer loop handling the primal variable, a middle loop for the dual variable, and an inner loop solving the regularized subproblems via tensor steps.

The authors complement their upper bound with the first non-trivial lower complexity bound of Ω(ε⁻⁴ᐟ⁽³ᵖ⁺³⁾) for higher-order minimax optimization under general conditions. When p = 1, the upper and lower bounds match, recovering the known optimal first-order complexity. For p ≥ 2, a gap remains between the bounds.

This work is significant as it demonstrates that higher-order information provides greater acceleration than previously believed for minimax problems, opening new directions for closing the remaining gap between upper and lower bounds.
original_abstract: When the objective has Lipschitz continuous $p$th-order derivatives, it is known that convex-concave minimax problems can be solved with $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2/(p+1)})$ $p$th-order oracle calls. This complexity upper bound was speculated to be optimal as it is achieved by a natural generalization of the optimal first-order method. In this work, we show an improved upper bound of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-4/(3p+1)})$ by applying the Monteiro-Svaiter acceleration. We also establish a lower complexity bound of $Ω(ε^{-2/(3p-1)})$, suggesting a gap still exists for $p \ge 2$.

title: Local Depth-Based Corrections to Maxmin Landmark Selection for Lazy Witness Persistence
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a family of local depth-based corrections to maxmin landmark selection for constructing lazy witness complexes in persistent homology computations. The core idea leverages halfspace depth and centerpoint theory from discrete geometry: after selecting initial maxmin landmarks, each landmark is replaced by a deeper representative of its local Voronoi cell, pushing landmarks away from outliers and toward geometrically robust positions. Among the variants studied, support-weighted partial recentering emerges as the preferred method, moving landmarks only partway toward the local depth maximum with step sizes modulated by cell support.

On the mathematical side, we prove local geometric guarantees for these corrections: a convex-core robustness lemma derived from halfspace depth, a $2r$ cover bound for subset recentering, and projected cover bounds for the implemented partial-recentering rules. On the algorithmic side, we identify a practically effective variant through a layered empirical study consisting of planar synthetic benchmarks, a parameter-sensitivity study, and an MPEG-7 silhouette benchmark, together with a modest three-dimensional torus extension. The main planar experiments show that support-weighted partial recentering gives a consistent geometric improvement over maxmin while preserving the thresholded $H_1$ summary used in the study. In this work, we propose a novel framework that integrates a simplified reference dynamics model with a data-driven surrogate measurement model. This fusion process leverages the strengths of both models to estimate complex dynamical behaviors under conditions of partial observability. title: From Finite-Node Conifold Geometry to BPS Structures I: Algebraic State Data

original_abstract: Let $π:X\to Δ$ be a one-parameter degeneration whose central fiber $X_0$ is a complex threefold with finitely many ordinary double points $Σ=\{p_1,\dots,p_r\}\subset X_0$. title: The high order spectral extrema of $2K_r$-free graphs

original_abstract: In this paper, we determine the graphs with maximum value of the sum number from $k$-clique spectral radius to $(2r-1)$-clique spectral radius among all $2K_{r}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices for $ r\le k$ and large $n$. We also determine the graphs with maximum $3$-clique spectral radius among all $2K_{3}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices. Our results are spectral versions of some results on generalized Turán numbers.

title: Powers of Edge Ideals of Prime Ideal Graphs: Generators, Primary Decomposition, and Linear Powers

The authors establish that these graphs are complete split graphs whose parameters are canonically determined by the prime ideal structure, specifically by the sizes of P\{0} and R\P.

They then characterize the minimal monomial generators of every power I(Γ_P(R))^n, providing precise conditions on exponent vectors. Additionally, a closed-form counting formula for the number of minimal generators of each power is derived in terms of the ring parameters.

The results are illustrated through explicit computations for ℤ_6, ℤ_8, and the general family ℤ_{p^m}. original_abstract: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with multiplicative identity. Let $P$ be a proper prime ideal of $R$. The prime ideal graph $Γ_P(R)$ has a vertex set of $R\setminus\{0\}$, and two different vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent to each other if and only if $xy\in P$. We show that $Γ_P(R)\cong K_{|P|-1}\vee \overline{K}_{\,|R|-|P|}$, so prime ideal graphs form a ring-induced family of complete split graphs determined by the two parameters $a=|P|-1$ and $b=|R|-|P|$. Using this decomposition, we determine the minimal vertex covers of $Γ_P(R)$, obtain an explicit irredundant primary decomposition of the edge ideal $I(Γ_P(R))$, and characterize the minimal monomial generators of every power $I(Γ_P(R))^n$. More precisely, $x^αy^β\in G(I(Γ_P(R))^n)$ if and only if $|α|+|β|=2n, \ |β|\leq n$, and $0\leq α_i\leq n$ for all $i$. As a consequence, we derive a closed formula for $μ(I(Γ_P(R))^n)$ and prove that every power $I(Γ_P(R))^n$ is polymatroidal. Hence, each power has linear quotients and a $2n-$linear minimal free resolution; equivalently, $I(Γ_P(R))$ has linear powers. Examples over $\mathbb{Z}_6$ and $\mathbb{Z}_8$ are included.

title: Small scale creation in 2D gravity-capillary water waves with vorticity

original_abstract: In this paper, we consider 2D incompressible Euler equations in an unbounded domain with a free surface and a fixed bottom at finite depth. The fluid motion is under the influence of gravity and surface tension. We construct initial data with a flat free surface and small velocity, such that the $L^\infty$ norm of the vorticity gradient has at least a double-exponential growth rate within the lifespan of the corresponding solution. This work generalizes the result of Zlatos to the free-surface setting and Hu--Luo--Yao to the case of an unbounded domain.

title: On $\boldsymbolΣ^1_3$- and $Σ^1_4$-uniformization

title: Asymptotic e-processes
generated_summary:

original_abstract: We introduce the concept of an asymptotic e-process, which is a doubly indexed stochastic process $(E_{m,n})_{m,n\in\mathbb{N}}$ that approximates an e-process with monitoring time $n$ in terms of a suitable limiting behavior for an approximation parameter $m\to \infty$. This theory is motivated by practical applications in sequential hypothesis testing, in which e-variables can only be constructed approximately from observations due to model misspecification or estimation errors. We derive an asymptotic version of Ville's inequality, which bounds excursion probabilities of $(E_{m,n})_{m,n\in\mathbb{N}}$ over some threshold uniformly over $n$ up to a time horizon $r_m$ that is determined by the quality of process approximation over $m$. title: FedSEA: Achieving Benefit of Parallelization in Federated Online Learning

original_abstract: Online federated learning (OFL) has emerged as a popular framework for decentralized decision-making over continuous data streams without compromising client privacy. However, the adversary model assumed in standard OFL typically precludes any potential benefits of parallelization. Further, it fails to adequately capture the different sources of statistical variation in OFL problems. In this paper, we extend the OFL paradigm by integrating a stochastically extended adversary (SEA). Under this framework, the loss function remains fixed across clients over time. However, the adversary dynamically and independently selects the data distribution for each client at each time. We propose the \algoOFL{} algorithm to solve this problem, which utilizes online stochastic gradient descent at the clients, along with periodic global aggregation via the server. We establish bounds on the global network regret over a time horizon \(T\) for two classes of functions: (1) for smooth and convex losses, we prove an \(\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T})\) bound, and (2) for smooth and strongly convex losses, we prove an \(\mathcal{O}(\log T)\) bound. Through careful analysis, we quantify the individual impact of both spatial (across clients) and temporal (over time) data heterogeneity on the regret bounds. Consequently, we identify a regime of mild temporal variation (relative to stochastic gradient variance), where the network regret improves with parallelization. Hence, in the SEA setting, our results improve the existing pessimistic worst-case results in online federated learning.

title: Stable laws for heavy-tailed observables on polynomially mixing billiards

The methodology centers on decomposing the observable into two components that isolate each effect separately. The authors induce on a subset away from the cusps, where the return map has exponential mixing but the return time function has polynomial tails. One component captures the heavy-tailed behavior and is analyzed using point process techniques for exponentially mixing systems, while the other captures the slow mixing contribution and is handled using results for Hölder observables on polynomial towers. A key technical contribution is a "vanishing small values" condition verified for exponentially mixing Young towers, along with new abstract lifting tools for transferring induced stable laws to the original system.

The main result establishes a transition: the stable law index is determined by the heavy-tailed observable when α < 1/β (Noah effect dominates) and by the slow mixing mechanism when α > 1/β (Joseph effect dominates). The authors also extend previous results for intermittent maps to the full parameter range, answering open questions from prior work. These findings provide a unified understanding of competing mechanisms for anomalous behavior in physically relevant dynamical systems.
original_abstract: We investigate the competition between two distinct mechanisms generating stable laws in deterministic dynamical systems: slow mixing of the system and heavy-tailed observables. For heavy-tailed observables on polynomially mixing billiards with cusps we show these two mechanisms interact and there is a transition, depending on the mixing exponent and the index of the heavy-tailed observable, such that the limit law is determined by either the observable or the dynamics. We prove stable limit laws for heavy-tailed observables of the form $φ(x)= d(x,x_0)^{-\frac{2}α}, 0< α< 2$, where $x_{0} \in \partial Q$ is a generic point on the dynamical system given by the collision map of a polynomially mixing billiard $(T, Q, μ)$ with cusps. The observable $φ$ has a tail of stable index $α$, i.e. $μ(|φ|>t) \sim t^{-α}$. The billiard systems we consider have a slow mixing rate so that suitably scaled Hölder observables on the billiard satisfy a stable law of index $1/γ$, with $γ$ a function of the flatness of the cusps. We establish stable limit laws satisfied by Birkhoff sums of $φ$ for the parameter range $γ\in (1/2,1)$, $α\in (0,2)$ ($α\not =1$) as a function of $γ$ and $α$. As an application, in the setting of intermittent maps, we extend the results of~\cite{CNT2025} to cover all parameter values of the map and the observable $φ(x)= d(x,x_0)^{-\frac{1}α}$ (which has stable index $α$ if $x_0\not =0$) in the regime $0< α< 2$, $0<γ<1$. We show if $x_0=0$, the indifferent fixed point, then the stable law has index $(\frac{1}α+γ)^{-1}$.

title: Framelet-Based Blind Image Restoration with Minimax Concave Regularization

The blind deblurring problem is solved within a coarse-to-fine framework, alternating between latent image estimation and blur kernel estimation through an efficient numerical algorithm.

original_abstract: Recovering corrupted images is one of the most challenging problems in image processing. Among various restoration tasks, blind image deblurring has been extensively studied due to its practical importance and inherent difficulty. In this problem, both the point spread function (PSF) and the underlying latent sharp image must be estimated simultaneously. This problem cannot be solved directly due to its ill-posed nature. One powerful tool for solving such problems is total variation (TV) regularization. The $\ell_0$-norm regularization within the TV framework has been widely adopted to promote sparsity in image gradients or transform domains, leading to improved preservation of edges and fine structures. However, the use of the $\ell_0$-norm results in a highly nonconvex and computationally intractable optimization problem, which limits its practical applicability. To overcome these difficulties, we employ the minimax concave penalty (MCP), which promotes enhanced sparsity and provides a closer approximation to the $\ell_0$-norm. In addition, a reweighted $\ell_1$-norm regularization is incorporated to further reduce estimation bias and improve the preservation of fine image details and textures. After introducing the proposed model, a numerical algorithm is developed to solve the resulting optimization problem. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is then demonstrated through experimental evaluations on several test images.

title: On McKean-Vlasov SDEs with polynomial drifts for SIS epidemic models

The authors establish existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the McKean-Vlasov SDE, along with quantitative moment estimates, by combining pathwise uniqueness arguments with comparison principles. They investigate three fundamental asymptotic regimes: exponential extinction, persistence above a threshold, and persistence around an equilibrium, providing sufficient conditions for each. These results recover and extend known conditions from classical stochastic SIS models to the mean-field setting.

For numerical simulation, the authors develop an extended Euler-Maruyama scheme based on interacting particle systems that handles the superlinear polynomial growth of the drift coefficient. They prove strong L^p-convergence and derive explicit error bounds, recovering the classical convergence rate of one-half under standard regularity conditions.

This work represents a significant contribution by bridging compartmental epidemic modeling with McKean-Vlasov SDE theory, offering a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing disease dynamics in structured populations with inter-population transmission mechanisms.
original_abstract: We present a tractable class of one-dimensional McKean-Vlasov equations that allow for unique strong solutions and extend the dynamics of various SIS epidemic models that are well-established in the literature. While the distribution-dependent drift coefficients are of polynomial type, the diffusion coefficients may involve sums of power functions. Our analysis includes various scenarios of extinction and persistence of the disease and an effective Euler-Maruyama scheme, for which we derive an explicit strong error estimate in $p$th moment for $p\geq 2$.

title: Mapping-based Hard-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Networks for unbounded wave problems

original_abstract: The aim of this paper is to introduce a Mapping-based Hard-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (MH-PINN) for efficiently and accurately solving unbounded wave problems. First, we propose a coordinate mapping technique that compactifies the infinite physical domain into a finite computational space. This effectively resolves the sampling difficulties inherent to standard PINNs in unbounded regions. Additionally, it avoids the artificial truncation errors introduced by traditional methods such as perfectly matched layers. Second, we design a physics-based hard-constrained network structure that automatically satisfies both the inner boundary conditions and the far-field radiation conditions. This structure eliminates boundary loss terms, yielding high computational efficiency and fast convergence, which effectively addresses the challenges of high-frequency problems. Third, we introduce an inverse factor correction for boundary coefficients to address the influence of asymptotic factors,which makes the method highly geometrically adaptable. Finally, we present numerical examples covering various acoustic radiation and scattering scenarios as well as elastic dynamics scenarios to demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of our algorithm.It highlights its potential for broader applications in the field of computational wave dynamics.

title: Orlov-Schulman symmetries of the self-dual conformal structure equations

original_abstract: We construct Orlov-Schulman symmetries for the self-dual conformal structure (SDCS) hierarchy. We provide an explicit proof of compatibility of additional symmetries with the basic Lax-Sato flows of the hierarchy, and consider several simple examples, including Galilean transformations and scalings. We also present a picture of the Orlov-Schulman symmetries in terms of a dressing scheme based on the Riemann-Hilbert problem.

title: Symplectic Error of Implicit Symplectic Integrators: A Qualitative Structural Analysis

original_abstract: We study how inexact nonlinear solvers lead to a loss of exact symplecticity in the Symplectic Euler (SE) and Stormer-Verlet (SV) schemes when applied to general nonseparable Hamiltonian systems. These schemes are implicit and require nonlinear solvers in practice. Here, we consider a fixed number $M$ of fixed-point iterations (FPI). While SE is exactly symplectic under exact solves, a finite $M$ gives only pseudo-symplecticity. Compared to previous results, we provide a more qualitative, block-wise characterization of the induced pseudo-symplecticity by analyzing the resulting perturbations to the matrix of symplectic structure $J$. We prove that the perturbed matrix $\tilde{J}$ is skew-symmetric, that one diagonal block vanishes identically (depending on the SE variant), and that the remaining blocks are $O(h^{M+1})$ perturbations of their counterparts in $J$, with time step $h$. A quadratic Hamiltonian example shows these bounds are sharp. Extending to compositions, we quantify how SV inherits distinct decay orders across different blocks of the symplectic defect. As a corollary, we show that the perturbation of volume preservation in phase space arises solely from the off-diagonal blocks of $\tilde{J}$, and we bound the induced energy error along trajectories. Numerical experiments on a tokamak magnetic-field Hamiltonian, where q-implicit SE is fully nonlinear (requiring FPI) but p-implicit SE is linearly implicit, confirm the sharpness of the theory and highlight the gap to the exactly symplectic counterpart.

title: Comparison of model order reduction techniques with one-shot procedure for topology optimization for thermal applications

Notably, the authors combine MOR with the one-shot method, which performs only a single multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradient iteration per optimization step, using these inaccurate solutions to build the reduced bases.

Numerical experiments on 2D and 3D heat sink design problems demonstrate that the alternative stopping criterion eliminates a significant discrepancy in MOR utilization between forward and adjoint equations. For the 3D problem with eight million elements, MOR combined with accurate solvers achieves up to 3.5× speedup with designs within 4% of reference performance. original_abstract: Density-based topology optimization has become a powerful method for automatically generating optimized designs in a wide variety of applications. However, it comes with a large computational cost when solving the physical model requires large-scale simulations. Here, we investigate the use of model order reduction (MOR) techniques to accelerate the simulations in the context of thermal design applications. We project the governing and the adjoint equations onto a low-dimensional subspace by constructing two distinct reduced bases -- one for the forward state and one for the adjoint system -- using solution snapshots from previous design iterations. These snapshots are generated using either the high-fidelity solver or inaccurate fast solvers, such as the one-shot method \citep{amir2024one}. Additionally, we demonstrate that properly selecting the stopping criterion for the iterative linear solver is crucial for the effective use of reduced models. In our 3D example, the proposed framework reduces the overall total simulation time relative to the high-fidelity workflow by a factor up to $3$ when combined with high-fidelity solves and a factor up to $16$ when combined with the one-shot method. Moreover, we find that the reduced order model approach is able to achieve a speed up of $1.54$ with respect to the one-shot method.

title: The reciprocal complement of a surface

The authors completely resolve the dimension problem for quadrics in affine 3-space, determining the dimension of Ρ(K[X,Y,Z]/(f)) when f has degree 2. original_abstract: We study the reciprocal complement $\mathcal{R}(D)$ of a two-dimensional finitely generated $K$-algebra $D$ by linking it with the properties of a surface with coordinate ring $D$. We give several sufficient criteria to have $\dim\mathcal{R}(D)=2$, and we use them to show several explicit examples; in particular, we determine the dimension of $\mathcal{R}(D)$ when $D$ is the quotient of $K[X,Y,Z]$ by an irreducible polynomial of degree $2$. title: On the reciprocity law in $\mathbb{F}_{q}[t]$

By computing the product of all group elements under each representation—one yielding expressions involving the dth power residue symbols and the other involving degree-related terms—and equating the two results, the authors obtain the reciprocity law relating the dth power residue symbols of P and Q.

The significance of this work lies in providing a conceptually transparent proof that highlights the reciprocity law as a fundamental consequence of the Chinese remainder theorem, complementing the historically more direct development of higher reciprocity laws in the function field setting compared to number fields.
original_abstract: In 1991, Rousseau gave a new proof of Gauss's quadratic reciprocity by comparing two distinct coset representations of the group $(\mathbb{Z}_{p}^{*} \times \mathbb{Z}_{q}^{*}) / U$ using the Chinese Remainder Theorem, without Gauss's Lemma. In this paper, we extend Rousseau's approach to $\mathbb{F}_{q}[t]$, providing a new, elementary proof of the reciprocity law for the $d$th power residue symbol, where $d$ is any divisor of $q-1$.

title: Preconditioners for the Onsager-Stefan-Maxwell equations for multicomponent diffusion

The augmentation renders the Schur complement well-approximated by a block diagonal mass matrix, enabling complete decoupling across all fields and chemical species. Key results demonstrate discretization-robust or mildly growing GMRES iteration counts across a diverse set of problems: cross-diffusion in human airways, thermally driven gas separation, nonideal benzene-cyclohexane mixing, and electrolytic transport in a Hull cell. This work enables scalable simulation of multicomponent diffusion problems that were previously limited by the cost of solving large coupled linear systems, with broad applicability across chemical engineering, electrochemistry, and biological transport.
original_abstract: The Onsager-Stefan-Maxwell (OSM) equations are an important model of mass transport in multicomponent flows with multiple chemical species. They describe the coupling of diffusive fluxes between species, accounting for their interactions through frictional and thermodynamic driving forces. In this work we propose an augmented Lagrangian preconditioner and prove its discretization-robustness for a Picard linearization of the stationary OSM equations in the isobaric, isothermal, ideal gaseous setting. For the Newton linearization we employ the augmented Lagrangian preconditioner as a block diagonal smoother inside a monolithic geometric multigrid iteration and combine with vertex star Schwarz methods. This strategy is shown to be applicable in a wide variety of settings which incorporate cross-diffusion, nonideal mixing, thermal, pressure, convective, and electrochemical effects. We demonstrate robustness or mild dependence with respect to mesh refinement and polynomial degree of the proposed monolithic preconditioning strategy for different types of multicomponent flows in several applications: cross-diffusion in the human airways, separation of gases under a temperature gradient, nonideal mixing of benzene and cyclohexane, and electrolytic transport in a Hull cell undergoing electroplating.

title: Exact Quadratic Penalty Function for Symplectic Eigenvalue Problem

The authors develop SympEigPen, a non-monotonic gradient method employing Barzilai-Borwein step sizes with enhancements including a restarting strategy with symplectic Rayleigh-Ritz steps and randomized step sizes to maintain iterate full-rankness. original_abstract: The symplectic eigenvalue problem for symmetric positive-definite (spd) matrices plays a crucial role in various scientific fields, including quantum mechanics and control theory. This paper introduces a trace-penalty minimization method, which transforms the symplectic eigenvalue problem into the unconstrained minimization of the trace-penalty function. We prove the equivalence between the penalty problem and the original constrained optimization problem under mild conditions, in the sense that the second-order stationary points of the trace-penalty function correspond to the solutions of the symplectic eigenvalue problem. Moreover, we develop an algorithm to minimize the trace-penalty function efficiently, which follows the scheme of gradient methods, together with the Barzilai-Borwein (BB) adaptive step-size rule and non-monotone line-search technique. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms a wide range of existing methods, such as Riemannian gradient-based methods, in terms of computational efficiency and convergence rate for dense, sparse, and sparse-add-low-rank matrices. These numerical results further demonstrate the great potential of our proposed algorithm, especially in solving large-scale symplectic eigenvalue problems.

title: SignatureTensors.jl: A Package for Signature Tensors in Julia

original_abstract: We introduce SignatureTensors.jl, a new package for computing signature tensors of paths in julia. We present its core functionality and demonstrate its use through illustrative examples. The package is compatible with the computer algebra system OSCAR, enabling both exact and numerical computations with signatures.

title: On Ricci forms of canonical metrics over noncompact complex manifolds

original_abstract: In this paper, we study several types of geometric problems related to the Ricci curvature on noncompact complex manifolds, such as the existence of Kähler-Einstein metrics on complete Kähler manifolds with negative Ricci curvature, which can be seen as an improvement of the main theorem in Cheng-Yau [4]; the existence of canonical Hermitian metrics with prescribed Ricci curvature on complete Hermitian manifolds, which can be regarded as noncompact versions of the Gauduchon conjecture on certain complete complex surfaces. Our method can also be used to construct Hesse-Einstein metrics in affine differential geometry.

title: A Durrmeyer-type variant of Grünwald Interpolation Operators

original_abstract: In this paper, we construct a Durrmeyer-type variant of Grünwald interpolation operators on the space $L^p[0,π]$. We prove their fundamental properties, including boundedness and convergence in the $L^p$-norm. We establish the convergence results using a Korovkin-type theorem in the setting of Banach function spaces. Furthermore, we obtain quantitative estimates for the convergence by means of the modulus of continuity and an appropriate $K$-functional.

title: Growing random planar network with oriented branching and fusion

The authors prove an L² law of large numbers for the empirical measure of rectangles, demonstrating convergence at rate 1/t to an explicit limiting measure. original_abstract: We consider a growing planar network where a tip grows at constant speed, branches at constant rate and inactivates when it meets a branch already created. We only consider here orthogonal branching occurring always in the same direction. This yields a spatial branching property to the growing network. The connected components of the network then form a branching process of rectangles with double immigration. Using a spine approach for a typical rectangle and coupling arguments, the study is boiled down to a one dimensional stick breaking model with aging. We can then prove long time convergence of empirical measure of the family of rectangles after polynomial rescaling. The limiting distribution and speed of convergence can be explicitly described. The proofs also rely on the description of common ancestor of rectangles in the branching structure with double immigration.

title: Deep Image Prior for photoacoustic tomography can mitigate limited-view artifacts

Including explicit TV regularization within the DIP loss function widens the window for obtaining good reconstructions, reducing sensitivity to stopping criteria.

original_abstract: We study the deep image prior (DIP) framework applied to photoacoustic tomography (PAT) as an unsupervised reconstruction approach to mitigate limited-view artifacts and noise commonly encountered in experimental settings. Efficient implementation is achieved by employing recently published fast forward and adjoint algorithms for circular measurement geometries. Initialization via a fast inverse and total variation (TV) regularization are applied to further suppress noise and mitigate overfitting. For comparison, we compute a classical TV reconstruction. Our experiments comprise simulated PAT measurements under limited-view geometries and varying levels of added noise as well as experimental measurements together with using a digital twin for quality assessment. Our findings suggest that DIP framework provides an effective unsupervised strategy for robust PAT reconstruction even in the challenging case of a limited view geometry providing improvement in several quantitative measures over total variation reconstructions.

title: On minimal non-sofic and $ω$-non-sofic groups

The authors observe that any non-sofic group, if one exists, must either contain a minimal non-sofic subgroup or be ω-non-sofic, providing a dichotomy that structures the investigation of the longstanding open question of whether all groups are sofic.

The methodology combines classical group-theoretic techniques—including Zorn's lemma arguments, properties of finitely generated groups, and closure properties of sofic groups—with systematic analysis of these two classes. A central theorem demonstrates that if a minimal non-sofic group has a maximal normal subgroup that is both residually finite and finitely generated, then that subgroup must be central, making the group a perfect central extension of a finitely generated non-amenable simple group. Additional results address periodic non-sofic groups, showing that the existence of periodic non-sofic groups without involutions implies the existence of divisible periodic non-sofic groups.

The significance lies in establishing structural constraints that any counterexample to soficity must satisfy, potentially narrowing the search space or leading to contradictions that would resolve the soficity question.
original_abstract: We investigate structural properties of non-sofic groups, assuming that such groups exist. We introduce and study two classes: minimal non-sofic groups and $ω$-non-sofic groups. For minimal non-sofic groups, we establish strong structural restrictions. In particular, we show that if $G$ is a minimal non-sofic group and $M$ is a finitely generated residually finite maximal normal subgroup of $G$, then $M$ is central and $G$ is a perfect central extension of a finitely generated non-amenable simple group. On the other hand, we show that locally graded non-sofic groups are necessarily $ω$-non-sofic. More precisely, such groups contain finitely generated non-sofic subgroups admitting strictly decreasing chains of finitely generated normal subgroups whose intersection is nontrivial and lies in the profinite residual. Finally, using results on existentially closed groups, we prove that the existence of a non-sofic group implies the existence of a countable existentially closed non-sofic group whose centralizers form a densely ordered chain of non-sofic subgroups of order type $(\mathbb{Q},\leq)$. In particular, we show that if a non-sofic group exists, then the class of $ω$-non-sofic groups is non-empty. Moreover, we prove that the existence of a non-sofic group implies the existence of a non-sofic group of unbounded exponent.

title: Analytical Extraction of Conditional Sobol' Indices via Basis Decomposition of Polynomial Chaos Expansions

The methodology treats spatial coordinates or conditioning parameters alongside stochastic variables as a joint augmented input vector within a single PCE surrogate. Through basis factorization, the authors derive analytical lemmas showing that the influence of conditioning variables can be encapsulated within parametric coefficient fields, which are closed-form functions of the conditioning variables. These coefficient fields enable direct computation of spatially varying conditional moments and Sobol' indices through pure algebraic manipulation of the global expansion coefficients.

Key results demonstrate that the proposed method produces smooth, physically consistent sensitivity fields that inherit the analytical continuity of the underlying basis functions, providing a natural "global filtering" effect. In contrast, traditional Monte Carlo and point-wise PCE approaches yield noisy, uncorrelated sensitivity fields. The method achieves high quantitative accuracy while requiring construction of only a single unified surrogate model.

The significance of this work lies in its substantial computational savings, elimination of thousands of independent local models, and guaranteed physical coherence across the conditioning domain, making it particularly valuable for spatially distributed uncertainty quantification problems such as those arising in stochastic computational fluid dynamics.
original_abstract: In uncertainty quantification, evaluating sensitivity measures under specific conditions (i.e., conditional Sobol' indices) is essential for systems with parameterized responses, such as spatial fields or varying operating conditions. Traditional approaches often rely on point-wise modeling, which is computationally expensive and may lack consistency across the parameter space. This paper demonstrates that for a pre-trained global Polynomial Chaos Expansion (PCE) model, the analytical conditional Sobol' indices are inherently embedded within its basis functions. By leveraging the tensor-product property of PCE bases, we reformulate the global expansion into a set of analytical coefficient fields that depend on the conditioning variables. Based on the preservation of orthogonality under conditional probability measures, we derive closed-form expressions for conditional variances and Sobol' indices. This framework bypasses the need for repetitive modeling or additional sampling, transforming conditional sensitivity analysis into a purely algebraic post-processing step. Numerical benchmarks indicate that the proposed method ensures physical coherence and offers superior numerical robustness and computational efficiency compared to conventional point-wise approaches.

title: Hyperbolicity of Multiple Ascending HNN Extensions of Free Groups

The main contribution is establishing sufficient conditions under which ascending HNN extensions associated with several endomorphisms of a free group are word-hyperbolic.

The author proves two main theorems. The first states that if multiple hyperbolic, non-surjective endomorphisms of a free group are "essentially disjoint" (meaning the images of sufficiently high powers have trivial pairwise intersection up to conjugacy), then the associated multiple ascending HNN extension is word-hyperbolic for sufficiently large powers. The second theorem replaces essential disjointness with "independence," a condition requiring distinct attracting laminations, and shows this also guarantees hyperbolicity. The key methodological insight is demonstrating that these endomorphisms satisfy an appropriate version of the "3-out-of-4 stretch condition," originally introduced by Bestvina, Feighn, and Handel. The proof that independence implies essential disjointness uses train track representatives and weak convergence of iterated images to attracting laminations, building on work by Reynolds and Mutanguha on train track theory for non-surjective endomorphisms.

These results generalize the known hyperbolicity criteria from automorphisms to non-surjective endomorphisms in the multiple-generator setting, contributing to the broader understanding of when groups constructed via HNN extensions exhibit negative curvature properties analogous to those in geometric topology.
original_abstract: Bestvina-Feighn-Handel show that for finitely many generic and independent hyperbolic automorphisms $φ_1, \cdots, φ_r$ of $F_n$, the resulting extension $F_n \rtimes F_r$ is hyperbolic. This paper generalizes the above statement to the case where $φ_1, \cdots, φ_r$ are hyperbolic non-surjective endomorphisms of $F_n$. In our case the output is a multiple HNN extension associated to a graph with one vertex and $r$ edges. All edge and vertex groups are isomorphic to $F_n$.

title: The General Formulation of Loss-Based Priors for Parameter Spaces

The key methodological innovation is replacing point exclusion with neighbourhood exclusion around each parameter value, which restores a non-trivial notion of inferential loss in continuous settings. The resulting class of prior distributions is indexed by a positive definite matrix governing the geometry of the exclusion region.

We then showcase an application of the reduced parameters to establishing non-transducibility results. title: Arc search in graphs via Szegedy walks

First, we investigate how the symmetry of a graph is reflected in its time evolution matrix, and provide a sufficient condition under which the success probability of the search is independent of the marked arc. In particular, we prove that if a graph is arc-transitive, the success probability is independent of the choice of the marked arc. Next, we analyze path and cycle graphs and show that the quantum search is ineffective for these graphs, whereas it performs well for complete bipartite graphs $K_{n,n}$. These results provide a theoretical foundation for studying arc and edge searches on various graphs, while also suggesting new problems concerning the eigenvalue analysis of edge-signed graphs in spectral graph theory.

title: Global well-posedness and temporal decay estimates for the viscous $β$-plane equations

original_abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem of the viscous $β$-plane equations. We first establish the global well-posedness of the system for the initial data sufficiently small compared to the Rossby parameter. The smoothing effect of the flow is then proved, and it is shown that the obtained global solution satisfies the equation in the classical sense. We also reveal that under some additional assumptions, the solution decays as fast as the corresponding linear solution and asymptotically behaves like a constant multiple of the integral kernel of the linearized equation. title: Counterexamples to the Corsten-Frankl conjecture on diameter-Ramsey simplices

original_abstract: Corsten and Frankl conjectured that a simplex is diameter-Ramsey if and only if its circumcenter lies in its convex hull. We disprove this conjecture in every dimension $d\ge 3$. The main tool is a sufficient criterion based on a higher-order deficit decomposition: if the squared deficits $D^2-\|p_i-p_j\|^2$ admit a nonnegative decomposition over subsets of the vertex set, with total mass at most $D^2$, then the simplex is diameter-Ramsey. The pairwise deficit criterion of Frankl--Pach--Reiher--Rödl is recovered as a special case. As an application, for every $d\ge 3$ we construct a diameter-Ramsey $d$-simplex whose circumcenter lies outside its convex hull. A particularly simple family has squared edge lengths $\|p_1-p_2\|^2=\|p_1-p_j\|^2=7~ (4\le j\le d+1)$, $\|p_1-p_3\|^2=4$, and $\|p_i-p_j\|^2=4 ~ (2\le i<j\le d+1)$.

title: The interplay between network transitivity and community structure

original_abstract: Recent empirical observations suggest that network transitivity is highly correlated with community structure in many real-world networks. For a GBM with balanced communities, the limits of the global and average clustering coefficients are identical, whereas these limits differ for unbalanced communities. In general, the clustering coefficients do not exhibit a monotonic relationship with community structure strength. original_abstract: We establish finite-time last-iterate guarantees for vanilla stochastic gradient descent in co-coercive games under noisy feedback. This is a broad class of games that is more general than strongly monotone games, allows for multiple Nash equilibria, and includes examples such as quadratic games with negative semidefinite interaction matrices and potential games with smooth concave potentials. Prior work in this setting has relied on relative noise models, where the noise vanishes as iterates approach equilibrium, an assumption that is often unrealistic in practice. We work instead under a substantially more general noise model in which the second moment of the noise is allowed to scale affinely with the squared norm of the iterates, an assumption natural in learning with unbounded action spaces. Under this model, we prove a last-iterate bound of order $O(\log(t)/t^{1/3})$, the first such bound for co-coercive games under non-vanishing noise. title: Geometric quantification for nonlinear deformation in knitted fabrics

original_abstract: Knitted fabrics exemplify a broad class of architected materials capable of large deformations, enabling shape morphing, mechanical biocompatibility, and embedded multifunctionality without material damage. Although geometric nonlinearity has been intuitively utilized in their design, a quantitative description of stitch-resolved deformation and its temporal evolution remains lacking. Applied to representative knitted structures, this framework resolves how global deformation is distributed among stitch reorientation, loop bending, surface bending, and dilation. Moreover, it reveals how regions of large geometric variation emerge, persist, and redistribute over time. Rather than directly measuring stress, these geometric descriptors define a unified geometric state space for comparing knitted structures and identifying candidate regions of mechanical localization. The framework provides a quantitative language for nonlinear deformation in knits and establishes a geometry-based representation that can be coupled to constitutive models, experimental measurements, and graph-based inverse-design workflows.

title: The mean curvature type hypersurfaces with prescribed gradient image

original_abstract: In this paper, we consider the existence of mean curvature type hypersurfaces with prescribed gradient image. Let $Ω$ and $\tildeΩ$ be uniformly convex bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with smooth boundary. original_abstract: Inference-time LLM alignment methods, particularly activation steering, offer an alternative to fine-tuning by directly modifying activations during generation. Exploiting this property, we model LLM inference as a linear time-varying dynamical system and adapt the classical linear quadratic regulator to compute feedback controllers using layer-wise Jacobians, steering activations toward desired semantic setpoints in closed-loop with minimal computational overhead and no offline training. We also derive theoretical bounds on setpoint tracking error, enabling formal guarantees on steering performance. Using a novel adaptive semantic feature setpoint signal, our method yields robust, fine-grained behavior control across models, scales, and tasks, including state-of-the-art modulation of toxicity, truthfulness, refusal, and arbitrary concepts, surpassing baseline steering methods. title: A Data-embedded Solution Paradigm for Nonconvex Probable Event Constrained Optimization

original_abstract: This paper introduces a new modeling framework for optimization under uncertainty, called Probable Event Constrained Optimization (PECO). Unlike conventional chance-constrained formulations, which only limit the probability of constraint violation, PECO also explicitly requires feasibility for all events whose probability exceeds a prescribed threshold. This guarantees that solutions remain valid across all high-probability realizations of uncertainty. To solve PECO, we proposed a data-embedded program (DEP) which directly incorporates historical measurements of the uncertain parameters to obtain a deterministic approximation for PECO. While existing solution methods for optimization problems under uncertainty rely heavily on convexity or linearity assumptions, the proposed data-embedded solution paradigm provides a unique opportunity for solving nonlinear and nonconvex PECOs. The effectiveness of this approach depends on properly estimating the number of elements in the family of solution-determining data sets. As we enter the era of big data, this information can be properly estimated by leveraging the power of machine learning.

title: Handling some Diophantine equation via Euclidean algorithm and its application to purely exponential equations
generated_summary:
This paper advances the study of purely exponential Diophantine equations of the form $a^x + b^y = c^z$ and the related Pillai-type equation $a^x - b^y = c$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are fixed coprime positive integers. The work contributes to the Scott-Styer conjecture, which predicts that such equations typically have at most one solution.

The authors introduce a novel method applying the Euclidean algorithm for polynomials to derive nontrivial congruence relations among solutions of these equations. This technique, combined with p-adic analysis, effective irrationality measures, and classical tools from Diophantine approximation, enables them to obtain sharp and effective bounds on the number of solutions for specific families of parameters.

The key results include three theorems. The first establishes that for any fixed prime $c$ of the form $2^r \cdot 3 + 1$, the equation $a^x + b^y = c^z$ has at most one solution except for finitely many effectively determinable cases. The second theorem completely resolves the Scott-Styer conjecture for $c \in \{7, 13, 97\}$, completing the verification for all $c < 100$. The third theorem proves that the Pillai-type equation has at most one solution when $a$ is a prime of the specified form with $r \leq 3912$, identifying $(13, 3, 10)$ as the sole exception with exactly two solutions.

These results represent significant progress toward Pillai's conjecture and provide effective methods applicable to broader classes of exponential Diophantine equations.
original_abstract: In this paper, we use a variety of classical and new research methods for ternary exponential Diophantine equations and extensive use of computer calculations to study the conjecture of R. Scott and R. Styer which asserts that for any fixed relatively prime positive integers $a,b$ and $c$ all greater than 1 there is at most one solution to the equation $a^x+b^y=c^z$ in positive integers $x,y$ and $z$, except for listed specific cases. Precisely, we confirm that for any fixed prime $c$ of the form $2^r \cdot 3 +1$ with some positive integer $r$ the conjecture holds true, except for finitely many cases all of which can be effectively determined. Most importantly we prove the conjecture to be true whenever $c = 7, 13$, or $97$, giving another proof of the result of T. Miyazaki and I. Pink for $c=13$. We also contribute to the estimation of the number of positive integer solutions $(x,y)$ to the equation $a^x-b^y=c$ for any fixed positive integers $a,b$ and $c$ with both $a$ and $b$ greater than 1. Further, based on a key idea in the proofs of the above results, we present a new application of the Euclidean algorithm for polynomials to the polynomial-exponential Diophantine equation \[ X^m - X^n = q^{y_1} - q^{y_2} \] in positive integers $X, y_1$ and $y_2$, where $m$ and $n$ are given positive integers with $m>n$, and $q$ is a given prime.

title: The Pentagon Graph Operator
generated_summary:
This paper introduces the pentagon graph operator, which maps a graph to the edge-intersection graph of its induced 5-cycles, extending the induced-cycle edge-intersection framework previously developed for 4-cycles (the quadrangle graph operator) to 5-cycles. The work represents a natural progression in the study of graph operators that transform graphs while preserving isomorphism.

The main contribution is the establishment of a complete trichotomy theorem for the pentagon graph operator. The theorem proves that every graph falls into exactly one of three mutually exclusive categories under repeated application of the operator: pentagon-vanishing (the sequence eventually reaches the empty graph), pentagon-periodic (the sequence eventually cycles through isomorphic graphs), or pentagon-expanding (the vertex count grows without bound). The proof proceeds by exhaustive case analysis: if no iterate is empty and vertex orders remain bounded, the pigeonhole principle guarantees that two iterates must be isomorphic, yielding periodicity.

The paper also develops explicit constructions witnessing all three behaviors. Notably, the pentagon case introduces distinctive geometric phenomena not present in the quadrangle setting, rooted in the relationship between the dodecahedron and icosahedron. Specifically, the pentagon graph of the dodecahedron is shown to be the icosahedron, and the icosahedron is a fixed point of the operator.

The significance of this work lies in demonstrating that the vanishing-periodic-expanding trichotomy, while consistent with the general theory of graph operators, manifests unique structural features in the pentagon case connected to classical polyhedral geometry.
original_abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\mathscr{C}_5(G)$ denote the graph whose vertices are the induced $5$-cycles of $G$, where two vertices are adjacent whenever the corresponding cycles share an edge. We investigate the iterative behavior of the pentagon graph operator $\mathscr{C}_5(G)$ , positioning it as the natural continuation of the quadrangle graph operator and the broader induced-cycle graph operator program. We construct explicit pentagon-vanishing, pentagon-periodic, and pentagon-expanding graphs. In particular, the dodecahedron and the icosahedron provide natural periodic examples, while an icosahedral tadpole-hat construction yields expanding families. Our main result proves that every graph is exactly one of three types with respect to $\mathscr{C}_5(G)$: vanishing, periodic, or expanding. The paper suggests a broader theory for the operators $C_k$ generated by induced cycles of fixed length $k$.

title: The Steklov spectrum of convex polygonal domains II: investigating spectral determination
generated_summary:
This paper investigates inverse Steklov spectral problems for convex polygonal domains, examining the extent to which the Steklov eigenvalue spectrum determines the geometry of convex polygons. The primary tool is the characteristic polynomial, a trigonometric polynomial depending on edge lengths and interior angles that is a Steklov spectral invariant. Since many important classes of polygons (isosceles triangles, rectangles, kites, regular polygons) fail previously established genericity conditions, the authors combine the characteristic polynomial with Euclidean geometric constraints to obtain new results.

For triangles, the authors show that any Steklov isospectral set is finite, almost all triangles are uniquely determined by their Steklov spectra among triangles, and each non-obtuse triangle is uniquely determined within that class. For quadrilaterals, rectangles are uniquely determined among all convex quadrilaterals and triangles, while parallelograms and kites yield partial uniqueness results. Regular n-gons are shown to be uniquely determined within their class. A notable contribution addresses whether the Steklov spectrum distinguishes convex polygons from smoothly bounded domains: the authors prove that triangles and quadrilaterals cannot be Steklov isospectral to any simply-connected domain with smooth boundary.

These results significantly advance understanding of Steklov spectral determination for polygonal domains, complementing known results for the Dirichlet Laplacian and addressing cases where previous genericity assumptions fail, while highlighting that the existence of Steklov isospectral non-isometric planar domains remains open.
original_abstract: The extent to which the geometry of an object is determined by some associated spectral data is a longstanding problem. We investigate this problem in the context of the Steklov spectrum, focusing on convex polygons. We prove that almost all triangles are uniquely determined by their Steklov spectra within the class of all triangles; further results depending on the types of angles in the triangles are given. We examine three special classes of convex quadrilaterals--rectangles, parallelograms, and kites--and obtain results ranging from unique spectral determination to determination up to three possibilities. For regular $n$-gons, we are again able to prove spectral determination within certain classes of polygons. More generally, we investigate the extent to which the Steklov spectrum distinguishes convex polygons from simply-connected domains with smooth boundary; that is, does the Steklov spectrum detect corners? We prove that triangles and quadrilaterals are spectrally distinguished from such smoothly bounded domains; moreover, we show that having the same Steklov spectrum as such a domain imposes substantial restrictions on the edge lengths of higher-order $n$-gons. Throughout, our main tool is the characteristic polynomial developed in works by Stanislav Krymski, Michael Levitin, Leonid Parnovski, Iosif Polterovich, and David A. Sher.

title: Beyond Bellman: High-Order Generator Regression for Continuous-Time Policy Evaluation
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the first-order discretization bottleneck in continuous-time policy evaluation from discrete logged trajectories. The main contribution is replacing the standard Bellman baseline—a one-step backward recursion that is first-order in grid width—with high-order generator regression that achieves order-*i* accuracy using multistep moment matching on the same trajectory information.

The methodology constructs multistep coefficients that cancel lower-order truncation terms in the space-time generator expansion, yielding second-order (Gen2) and third-order (Gen3) surrogates. The authors provide an end-to-end recursion theorem decomposing error into five named components: generator misspecification, projection error, pooling bias, finite-sample fluctuation, and start-up error, with explicit constants tracking how local gains propagate through the backward recursion.

Empirically, controlled calibration experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates on log-log plots. Across benchmark families spanning dimensions 2 to 24, Gen2 reduces integrated RMSE by 13–48% relative to the Bellman baseline, with the largest gains on medium and larger systems where first-order error accumulates most. The paper also maps the operating region, showing that gains require sufficiently rich feature classes and degrade under large behavior mismatch or severe nonstationarity, with Gen2 identified as the reliably stable default.

The significance lies in demonstrating that higher-order discretization improvements are practically achievable within existing logged-trajectory protocols, providing both theoretical guarantees and a concrete decision-frequency regime map for practitioners in continuous-time reinforcement learning.
original_abstract: We study finite-horizon continuous-time policy evaluation from discrete closed-loop trajectories under time-inhomogeneous dynamics. The target value surface solves a backward parabolic equation, but the Bellman baseline obtained from one-step recursion is only first-order in the grid width. We estimate the time-dependent generator from multi-step transitions using moment-matching coefficients that cancel lower-order truncation terms, and combine the resulting surrogate with backward regression. The main theory gives an end-to-end decomposition into generator misspecification, projection error, pooling bias, finite-sample error, and start-up error, together with a decision-frequency regime map explaining when higher-order gains should be visible. Across calibration studies, four-scale benchmarks, feature and start-up ablations, and gain-mismatch stress tests, the second-order estimator consistently improves on the Bellman baseline and remains stable in the regime where the theory predicts visible gains. These results position high-order generator regression as an interpretable continuous-time policy-evaluation method with a clear operating region.

title: Classification of Rational Functions of Degree Three over Finite Fields
generated_summary:
This paper provides a complete classification of degree three rational functions over finite fields of odd characteristic up to PGL-equivalence, complementing prior work that addressed the even characteristic case. The classification determines explicit representatives for all equivalence classes under the natural action of the projective linear group PGL(2, 𝔽_q) on rational functions.

The authors divide degree three rational functions into three classes based on the preimage structure of points under the function viewed as a map on the projective line. Class I (fully ramified functions) was previously classified, and Class II functions are reduced to canonical forms shown to be pairwise nonequivalent. The most challenging case, Class III, is handled by constructing invariants derived from ramification point types to distinguish equivalence classes. For characteristic at least 5, the difficulty arises because degree three rational functions can have up to four ramification points in odd characteristic, compared to at most two in even characteristic. The authors employ the Hasse-Weil bound on rational points of algebraic curves to verify that their constructed set of representatives achieves the correct cardinality, with modifications provided for characteristic 3.

The results confirm the explicit formula N(q,3) = (q² + 23q + 12)/24 for odd q not divisible by 3 and provide analogous formulas for other cases. Concrete examples over 𝔽₂₇ and 𝔽₂₅ illustrate the classification. This work has implications for constructing irreducible polynomials, studying permutation rational functions, and understanding function field extensions over finite fields.
original_abstract: We study rational functions over finite fields under PGL-equivalence. We say that $f, g \in \Bbb F_q(X)$ are \emph{equivalent} if there exist $ψ, φ\in \Bbb F_q(X)$ of degree one such that $g = ψ\circ f \circ φ$. Most properties of rational functions over finite fields as they appear in theory and applications are preserved under this equivalence. In a recent work, Mattarei and Pizzato classified rational functions of degree three over finite fields in even characteristic. In the present paper, we classify all rational functions of degree three over finite fields in odd characteristic. Our approach is based on careful analyses of the value frequencies and the ramification points of the degree three rational functions. The completion of our classification also relies on an explicit formula for the number of equivalence classes of degree three rational functions over finite fields recently obtained by the first author.

title: Asymptotic Stability of Hartree--Fock Homogenous Equilibria in $\mathbb{R}^d$
generated_summary:
This paper establishes the asymptotic stability and scattering theory for the Hartree-Fock equation near homogeneous equilibria in dimensions d ≥ 3, providing the first such result in the physically relevant three-dimensional case. The work addresses the dynamics of a one-particle density matrix describing weakly interacting fermions, incorporating both classical meanfield interactions and quantum exchange effects.

The authors work in Fourier space, analyzing the perturbative dynamics around translation-invariant equilibria of the form f(|k|²). The methodology centers on understanding phase mixing mechanisms driven by a modified Schrödinger dispersion relation that arises from the exchange term. Key technical challenges include inverting the Penrose dielectric function for the linear response, handling momentum-dependent quantum echo resonances that cause derivative losses, and managing the non-local nature of the exchange operator. The authors develop a nonlinear iterative scheme in weighted L∞ Fourier norms that propagates phase mixing estimates while controlling these complex resonances.

The main result demonstrates that for sufficiently small initial perturbations and small exchange potentials, solutions exist globally in time, the configuration space density decays at rate t^(-d+ε), and solutions scatter to a linear dynamics governed by a limiting Hamiltonian in the Hilbert-Schmidt operator topology. The significance lies in extending nonlinear Landau damping results to the quantum Hartree-Fock setting and treating momentum-dependent echo resonances, which also arise as central obstructions in the classical Vlasov theory near spatially inhomogeneous equilibria.
original_abstract: In this paper, we establish nonlinear Landau damping and asymptotic stability of a large class of translation-invariant steady solutions to the time-dependent Hartree--Fock equations in the presence of an {\em off-diagonal exchange operator}, which arises naturally in the meanfield theory of a large fermionic system, in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge 3$. Despite being a sub-order operator, the inclusion of the exchange term disturbs the classical Schrödinger dispersion and causes a complex linear response from the background electrons to the space density whose dispersion relation is no longer a Fourier multiplier as in the classical Vlasov and Hartree theory. In addition, the group velocity of each elementary waves involves a mixture of all other Fourier modes, leading to delicate {\em momentum-dependent echo resonances}. To overcome the issues, we develop a nonlinear iterative scheme that relies on a detailed resolvent analysis, makes use of a transport type dispersion in Fourier spaces, and propagates phase mixing and Landau damping in weighted $L^\infty_{k,p}$ norms.

title: Lions and Contamination: Trees and General Graphs
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the lions and contamination problem—a pursuit-evasion model on graphs where lions clear vertices while contamination spreads along unguarded edges—through its connection to pathwidth, a fundamental graph width parameter. The authors establish a comprehensive pathwidth-based framework for understanding the minimum number of lions needed to clear graphs.

The methodology combines structural graph theory techniques with careful analysis of clearing strategies. The authors introduce "remote operations" as analytical tools to rigorously track contamination dynamics and prove key monotonicity lemmas relating different clearing paths. They leverage properties of isometric subgraphs and path decompositions to establish their bounds.

The key results are fourfold. First, for trees, the lion number satisfies pw(T) ≤ L(T) ≤ pw(T) + 1, providing the tightest possible pathwidth-based characterization. Second, a counterexample demonstrates that the lion number is not monotone under general subgraph inclusion, resolving an open question from prior work. Third, the universal upper bound L(G) ≤ pw(G) + 1 holds for all connected graphs, though pathwidth cannot provide a general lower bound. Fourth, the monotone lion number L^m(G) is shown to be equivalent to pathwidth up to a constant factor, which completely resolves an open question by Bertschinger et al. regarding whether ordinary and monotone lion numbers can diverge arbitrarily.

These results fundamentally distinguish the lions and contamination model from classical graph searching paradigms and establish pathwidth as the natural parameter governing monotone clearing complexity.
original_abstract: This paper investigates a special variant of a pursuit-evasion game called lions and contamination. In a graph where all vertices are initially contaminated, a set of lions traverses the graph, clearing the contamination from every vertex they visit. However, the contamination simultaneously spreads to any adjacent vertex not occupied by a lion. We analyze the relationships among the lion number $\mathcal{L}(G)$, monotone lion number $\mathcal{L}^m(G)$, and the graph's pathwidth $\operatorname{pw}(G)$. Our main results are as follows: (a) We prove a monotonicity property: for any graph $G$ and its isometric subgraph $H$, $\mathcal{L}(H)\le \mathcal{L}(G)$. (b) For trees $T$, we show that the lion number is tightly characterized by pathwidth, satisfying $\operatorname{pw}(T)\le \mathcal{L}(T)\le \operatorname{pw}(T)+1$. (c) We provide a counterexample showing that the monotonicity property fails for arbitrary subgraphs. (d) We show that, in contrast to the tree case, pathwidth does not yield a general lower bound on $\mathcal{L}(G)$ for arbitrary graphs. (e) For any connected graph $G$, we prove the general upper bound $\mathcal{L}(G)\le \operatorname{pw}(G)+1$. (f) For the monotone variant, we establish the general lower bound $\operatorname{pw}(G)\le \mathcal{L}^m(G)$. (g) Conversely, we show that $\mathcal{L}^m(G)\le 2\operatorname{pw}(G)+2$ holds for all connected graphs, which is best possible up to a small additive constant.

title: Relaxed Generalized Scalar Auxiliary Variable Exponential Integrator for A Modified Landau-de Gennes Theory for Smectic Liquid Crystals
generated_summary:
This paper presents a novel numerical scheme for simulating the gradient-flow dynamics of Smectic-A liquid crystals within the modified Landau-de Gennes (mLdG) framework, which couples a Q-tensor field describing orientational order with a scalar density variation field characterizing smectic layering. The main contribution is the development of a relaxed generalized Scalar Auxiliary Variable Exponential Integrator (EOP-GSAV-EI) scheme that addresses the severe computational challenges posed by the stiff, multi-scale, and highly nonlinear coupled system involving second-order and fourth-order parabolic PDEs.

The methodology combines Exponential Time Differencing to exactly resolve stiff linear operators with a generalized SAV approach to handle nonlinear coupling terms. This yields a scheme that is linear and decoupled at each time step, requiring only constant-coefficient linear systems solvable via Fast Fourier Transform. The authors rigorously prove unconditional energy stability of the scheme with respect to a modified discrete energy.

Numerical experiments in both two and three dimensions confirm first-order temporal convergence, preservation of the maximum bound principle, and strict energy dissipation. The scheme accurately captures complex physical phenomena including phase front propagation, X-shaped grain boundary formation, topological defect recombination, and steady-state target patterns. Comparisons with standard ETD methods without SAV demonstrate that the proposed scheme eliminates severe numerical oscillations and enables robust simulations with significantly larger time steps, representing an important advance for computational liquid crystal modeling.
original_abstract: The Smectic-A (SmA) phase is modeled by a modified Landau-de Gennes (mLdG) model proposed by Xia et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett., 126 (2021), 177801], in which a tensor order parameter Q for the orientational order is coupled with a real scalar $u$ characterizing the positional order. In this paper, we propose and analyze a novel, highly efficient, and unconditionally energy-stable numerical scheme for this coupled system by combining the generalized scalar auxiliary variable-exponential integrator (GSAV-EI) approach with a relaxed correction strategy. In particular, we reformulate the exponential time differencing time discretization into an equivalent quasi-implicit backward Euler-type structure, a pivotal step that eliminates the restrictive CFL mesh-ratio conditions of the original GSAV-EI method and enables a rigorous fully discrete error analysis. Theoretically, we rigorously establish the unconditional energy stability with respect to a modified discrete energy and the uniform boundedness of the numerical solutions Q, along with optimal error estimates in both time and space. Comprehensive numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, and structural preservation of the algorithm, as well as its capability in capturing complex topological defect dynamics.

title: Rigidity, Fluctuations, and Multifractal Structure of Axiom A Systems: SRB Measures, Livshits Rigidity, and Fluctuation Theorems
