original_abstract: We introduce cut-free nested sequent systems for a broad class of quantified modal logics (QMLs). The QMLs we consider are semantically defined using relational models that assign both an inner and outer domain to each world. This rich model structure enables the specification of various QMLs by enforcing different frame conditions, including increasing, decreasing, constant, and empty domains, as well as general path conditions and seriality. We extend the usual notion of nested sequent to include signatures, i.e., multisets of terms, which let us naturally define rules capturing the aforementioned domain conditions. A distinctive feature of our nested sequent systems is the use of reachability rules--inference rules parameterized by formal grammars (viz., semi-Thue systems). These rules operate by propagating or consuming formulae or terms along certain paths within a nested sequent, where paths are encoded as strings generated by a parameterizing grammar. This paper is the first to provide sound and complete nested systems for QMLs semantically characterized by models using both inner and outer domains. We analyze the proof-theoretic properties of these systems, identify a number of admissible structural rules, establish the invertibility of all rules, and prove a non-trivial syntactic cut-elimination theorem. We also observe that the standard universal quantifier rule used in nested systems subsumes the Extended Barcan Rule, which forces nested systems to capture QMLs with constant outer domains.

title: Adaptive Kernel Selection for Kernelized Diffusion Maps
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the kernel selection problem in Kernelized Diffusion Maps (KDM), a spectral method that recovers eigenfunctions of diffusion-type operators from data. The authors propose two complementary adaptive kernel selection strategies: a variational multiple-kernel learning (VMKL) framework that differentiates through the KDM generalized eigenproblem to optimize convex kernel mixtures, and a cross-validation pipeline combined with random Fourier features (CV+RFF) that searches over multiple kernel families and bandwidths using a held-out eigenvalue-sum score.

Theoretical contributions include proofs of well-posedness for convex kernel mixtures, Lipschitz stability of KDM operators with respect to kernel weights, spectral projector continuity, and exponential consistency of the CV selector. The authors also identify and analyze structural failure modes of unconstrained gradient-based bandwidth optimization, showing that Rayleigh-based objectives inherently suffer from bandwidth collapse or trivialization.

Experiments on Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, double-well potentials, and geometric manifolds demonstrate that CV+RFF achieves near-perfect eigenfunction recovery (SubR² > 0.96) on OU problems by automatically selecting non-Gaussian kernels like Matérn-3/2, yielding up to 2× error reduction over uniform Gaussian baselines. A hybrid approach—using CV for coarse kernel family selection followed by bounded variational refinement—further improves results, demonstrating genuine complementarity between the two strategies. These findings establish practical guidelines for kernel adaptation in spectral methods for manifold learning and dynamical systems analysis.
original_abstract: Selecting an appropriate kernel is a central challenge in kernel-based spectral methods. In \emph{Kernelized Diffusion Maps} (KDM), the kernel determines the accuracy of the RKHS estimator of a diffusion-type operator and hence the quality and stability of the recovered eigenfunctions. We introduce two complementary approaches to adaptive kernel selection for KDM. First, we develop a variational outer loop that learns continuous kernel parameters, including bandwidths and mixture weights, by differentiating through the Cholesky-reduced KDM eigenproblem with an objective combining eigenvalue maximization, subspace orthonormality, and RKHS regularization. Second, we propose an unsupervised cross-validation pipeline that selects kernel families and bandwidths using an eigenvalue-sum criterion together with random Fourier features for scalability. Both methods share a common theoretical foundation: we prove Lipschitz dependence of KDM operators on kernel weights, continuity of spectral projectors under a gap condition, a residual-control theorem certifying proximity to the target eigenspace, and exponential consistency of the cross-validation selector over a finite kernel dictionary.

title: The Gomory-Hu inequality and trees
generated_summary:
This paper investigates ultrametric spaces generated by connected graphs with non-negative vertex labelings, extending previous work on labeled trees to arbitrary connected labeled graphs. The central focus is the Gomory-Hu inequality, which states that for a finite ultrametric space (X, d), the cardinality of the distance set satisfies |D(X)| ≤ |X|, with spaces achieving equality termed GH-spaces.

The authors employ tools from metric space theory and graph theory, defining a mapping on vertices of connected labeled graphs that generalizes the shortest path metric to an ultrametric analogue. They examine when this construction yields pseudoultrametrics or ultrametrics and characterize when the resulting spaces belong to the GH class.

The key results include three main theorems. First, every connected labeled graph generates a pseudoultrametric on its vertex set, which becomes a genuine ultrametric when the graph is locally finite. Second, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for ultrametric spaces generated by finite labeled trees to be GH-spaces. Third, a partial generalization extends these conditions to arbitrary finite connected labeled graphs. Additionally, the authors prove that every finite connected graph admits some vertex labeling that generates a GH-space, and they explicitly describe such labelings for complete finite graphs.

The significance of this work lies in deepening the structural understanding of finite ultrametric spaces through graph-theoretic methods, connecting the Gomory-Hu inequality to properties of labeled graphs and trees, with applications relevant to network flow theory, computer science, and related fields.
original_abstract: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$, and let $U(G)$ be the set of all ultrametric spaces $(V,d_l)$ generated by vertex labelings $l\colon V \to \mathbb R^+$. We prove that the inequality $$ |D(V)| \le |E| + 1 $$ holds for all $(V,d_l) \in U(G)$, where $D(V)$ is the distance set of $(V,d_l)$. The necessary and sufficient conditions under which the above inequality turns to an equality are found. Moreover, we prove that each connected graph with non-negative vertex labeling generates a pseudoultrametric space and find some sufficient conditions under which this space is ultrametric.

title: Simple modules over truncated current Lie algebras of the Witt algebra
generated_summary:
This paper initiates the study of modular representations of truncated current Lie algebras associated with the Witt algebra over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic p > 3. The truncated current Witt algebra is defined as the tensor product of the Witt algebra W with a truncated polynomial ring in an auxiliary variable t, inheriting both a Lie bracket and a restricted Lie algebra structure.

The authors classify simple modules over these algebras by organizing them according to the height of their p-characters, following the classical approach used for the Witt algebra itself. The methodology centers on constructing χ-reduced Verma modules through parabolic induction, leveraging the natural grading and filtration inherited from the Witt algebra. A key structural observation is that when the p-character has height at most one, every simple module arises as a homomorphic image of such a reduced Verma module, established via Frobenius reciprocity.

The principal results provide a complete classification of isomorphism classes of simple modules for p-characters of height at most one, organized across three theorems corresponding to heights −1, 0, and 1. For p-characters of height greater than one, the authors show that the reduced enveloping algebra admits only one simple module up to isomorphism, and they explicitly construct this module and determine its dimension.

This work is significant as it extends the representation theory of truncated current Lie algebras beyond the reductive setting to Cartan-type Lie algebras, potentially providing a framework for studying truncated current algebras associated with other restricted Lie algebras of Cartan type.
original_abstract: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>3$, and let $W$ denote the $p$-dimensional Witt algebra, the first example of a non-classical simple Lie algebra. For a non-negative integer $\ell$, consider the associated truncated current Lie algebra $W_\ell=W \otimes \Bbbk[t]/(t^{\ell+1})$. In this paper, we first study simple $W_\ell$-modules having $p$-character $χ$ of height at most one, and provide a complete classification of such modules up to isomorphism. We then investigate a family of simple $W_\ell$-modules whose $p$-characters have height greater than one.

title: Hausdorff Dimension of Anosov Subgroups' Limit Sets with Special Self-Affine Complexity
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the Hausdorff dimension of limit sets of projective Anosov subgroups in the projective general linear group PGL(d,ℝ), addressing fundamental questions at the intersection of higher-rank geometry and fractal analysis. The central challenge is that, unlike rank-one settings, Anosov subgroup actions on their limit sets lack conformality, making dimension computation difficult.

The authors employ Patterson-Sullivan theory combined with geometric constructions exploiting "special self-affine complexity" at integer dimensions to resolve two open questions posed by Li-Pan-Xu. The methodology leverages the affinity exponent—a concept originating from self-affine set theory—and introduces a "non-folding property" as a conformal assumption that prevents pathological multi-scale behavior of limit sets within Euclidean balls.

The key results are threefold. First, if a projective Anosov subgroup has a limit set with Hausdorff dimension equal to d−1, then d must equal 2 and the group is a cocompact lattice in PGL(2,ℝ). Second, for irreducible projective Anosov representations of closed surface groups, the affinity exponent equals 1 if and only if the representation is Hitchin. Third, for non-folding Anosov subgroups, the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set equals the critical exponent of the associated Poincaré series, establishing a clean generalization of classical Patterson-Sullivan results.

These findings advance understanding of higher Teichmüller theory and the fractal geometry of higher-rank discrete group actions, partially answering questions about θ-positive representations raised by Yao.
original_abstract: Let $Γ\subset \mathsf{PGL}(d,\mathbb{R})$ be an irreducible projective Anosov subgroup and let $Λ^1(Γ)$ be its projective limit set. Viewing $Λ^1(Γ)$ as an analogue of a self-affine set, we investigate the Hausdorff dimension of $Λ^1(Γ)$ under specific assumptions regarding its affine complexity: 1. If $Λ^1(Γ)$ is of full Hausdorff dimension, then $d= 2$ and $Γ$ is a cocompact lattice. 2. If $d = 3$ and $Γ$ is the image of a closed surface group under an irreducible Anosov representation, then $Λ^1(Γ)$ never has Hausdorff dimension $1$ unless the representation is Hitchin. 3. If the limit set $Λ^1(Γ)$ exhibits a partial quasi-self-similarity (in the sense of Falconer~\cite{falconerselfsimilar1}) -- which can be implied by the ``regular distortion property'' of $Γ$ -- then the Hausdorff dimension of $Λ^1(Γ)$ equals the critical exponent of the first simple root. An application of this result is the computation of the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set for arbitrary $Θ$-positive representations of convex cocompact Fuchsian groups.

title: On Nests and Large Components of Random Real Algebraic Curves
generated_summary:
This paper advances the understanding of the topology of Kostlan random real algebraic plane curves by developing variants of the barrier method to establish new lower bounds on large connected components, deep nests of ovals, and separation probabilities.

The authors introduce a modified barrier method that controls the sup-norm only on region boundaries rather than the full C¹-norm, leveraging Z₂-homology invariants that remain stable under such weaker control. For constructing reference polynomials with nested ovals, they employ Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind to achieve favorable L² and sup-norm properties, overcoming difficulties that arise from naive constructions. A "global barrier method" based on Shiffman-Zelditch sup-norm bounds is also developed for handling simultaneous perturbations at distant points.

The key results establish that for any ε > 0: the expected number of connected components with length at least d^(ε-1) grows as d^(1-ε); the expected number of nests with depth at least d^ε grows as d^(1-ε); and for finitely many points in RP² with pairwise Fubini-Study distances exceeding d^(ε-1/2), the probability they lie in different complementary components is at least d^(-δ(m)). An upper bound of √d/2 on the expected depth at any point is also proven.

These results significantly improve previous bounds where component lengths and nest depths were limited to fixed constants, demonstrating that topologically complex features with growing complexity appear abundantly in random algebraic curves.
original_abstract: We develop a variant of the barrier method in order to address questions about topology of Kostlan random real algebraic plane curves. In particular we prove that the expected number of connected components of the curve of length at least $\displaystyle{O\left(\sqrt{d^{-1}\log \log d}\right)}$ grows to infinity with $d$, and likewise, the expected number of nests of the curve of depth at least $\displaystyle{O\left(\log\log d\right)}$ grows to infinity with $d$. In another direction, we adapt an $L^{\infty}$-norm bound result of Shifmann and Zelditch to subspaces and employ it to obtain a lower bound for the probability that a finite number of points remain all in different components of the complement of a large degree random curve.

title: Saturation of Markov Polynomials
generated_summary:
This paper provides a constructive proof of the Saturation conjecture for Markov polynomials, which are Laurent polynomial solutions to the generalized Markov equation in three variables. Markov polynomials, indexed by rational numbers in [0,1], can be expressed in a specific form where the numerator is a homogeneous polynomial whose terms correspond to integer lattice points. The Newton polygon of each Markov polynomial defines a region in the lattice plane bounded by specific inequalities. The Saturation conjecture, previously posed by the authors, asserts that every integer lattice point within this Newton polygon corresponds to a monomial with a non-zero coefficient in the Markov polynomial — meaning no "gaps" exist in the support of the polynomial.

The proof leverages the known correspondence between Markov polynomials and perfect matchings of snake graphs, a combinatorial framework developed in the context of cluster algebras. The authors construct an explicit walk along the Newton polygon, demonstrating that for each lattice point, a corresponding perfect matching of the associated snake graph can be produced through local operations on matchings. This constructive approach systematically traverses diagonals and boundary points of the Newton polygon, ensuring complete coverage.

The key result confirms that the terms appearing in Markov polynomial numerators are precisely characterized by the lattice points of their Newton polygons. This resolution strengthens the structural understanding of Markov polynomials and opens avenues for investigating the specific coefficient values using similar combinatorial techniques applied to snake graph matchings.
original_abstract: Solutions to the Markov equation appear in many mathematical contexts. We aim to build on the understanding of them by proving a recent conjecture about Markov polynomials; solutions to a generalised version of the Markov equation. The proof we provide is a constructive argument based on the Markov snake graph, a combinatorial object related to Markov numbers, deepening the connection between the Markov equation and combinatorics.

title: An Adaptive Smoothing Algorithm for Non-Lipschitz Optimization on Manifolds with Complexity Guarantees
generated_summary:
This paper presents an Adaptive Smoothing Riemannian Gradient Algorithm (ASRGA) for solving optimization problems on compact embedded submanifolds where the objective function may exhibit non-Lipschitz singularities, arising from regularization terms involving ℓ_p quasi-norms with p ∈ (0, 1]. Such problems appear in sparse principal component analysis, dual principal component pursuit, sparse dictionary learning, and other applications where non-Lipschitz regularizers promote sparsity more effectively than their Lipschitz counterparts.

The methodology couples a carefully scheduled decay of a smoothing parameter—which approximates the non-Lipschitz objective with smooth surrogates—with Riemannian gradient descent steps. To avoid the computational burden of line search and the need to estimate problem-dependent parameters, ASRGA employs a smoothing-aware adaptive stepsize policy inspired by AdaGrad, where gradient accumulation and effective stepsizes are scaled according to the current smoothing level to compensate for the blow-up of Lipschitz constants.

The authors establish global convergence to stationary points and prove that ASRGA finds an ε-approximate stationary point within O(ε^(p−4)) iterations. This represents the first complexity bound for non-Lipschitz Riemannian optimization. When p = 1, the bound reduces to O(ε^(−3)), matching known results for Lipschitz problems on manifolds. Numerical experiments demonstrate that ASRGA consistently outperforms existing methods, including for the Lipschitz case, confirming both the theoretical soundness and practical effectiveness of the approach.
original_abstract: We study a class of optimization problems on Riemannian manifolds, where the objective function consists of a smooth term and quasi-norm type penalties with exponent $p \in (0, 1]$. The essential difficulty lies in the fact that the objective function may not be locally Lipschitz continuous, which places this type of problems beyond the reach of existing Riemannian techniques. To overcome this obstacle, this paper constructs a general smoothing framework and establishes fundamental properties for developing efficient algorithms. In particular, we propose a smoothing Riemannian gradient algorithm equipped with a smoothing-aware AdaGrad-type stepsize rule. Its global convergence is demonstrated together with an iteration complexity of $O (ε^{p - 4})$, which includes the best available iteration complexity of $O (ε^{- 3})$ for Lipschitz problems with $p = 1$ as a special case. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first complexity result for non-Lipschitz optimization on Riemannian manifolds. Preliminary numerical experiments corroborate the practical efficiency of the proposed approach in real-world applications arsing from machine learning and data science.

title: Accuracy Certificates for Convex Optimization at Accelerated Rates via Primal-Dual Averaging
generated_summary:
This paper investigates primal-dual algorithmic correspondences in regularized convex smooth composite optimization, with a focus on computing provably convergent optimality certificates. The authors systematically characterize three classes of methods distinguished by their number of averaging operations.

For one-average methods, the authors establish that modified dual averaging (MDA) in the primal space is equivalent to the generalized conditional gradient (GCG) method in the dual space, with both yielding computable primal-dual optimality certificates at O(1/ε) complexity. For two-average methods, they show that aggregated GCG (AggGCG) is self-dual but lacks straightforward certificate guarantees. Motivated by this gap, the authors propose a novel three-average acceleration (TAA) method that restores computable certificates while achieving an accelerated O(1/√ε) complexity. A key finding is that TAA's dual counterpart is the well-known gradient extrapolation method (GEM), which consequently also admits computable optimality certificates at the same accelerated rate—a novel result for GEM in this setting.

The optimality certificates are based on aggregated cutting-plane models that provide verifiable upper bounds on the primal-dual gap. The authors provide geometric intuition through zero-sum matrix game and Fisher market interpretations. These results enhance the practical utility of GEM as a subsidiary solver by establishing computable termination conditions, and they unify recent literature on proximal bundle methods with classical accuracy certificates in convex optimization.
original_abstract: Many works in convex optimization provide rates for achieving a small primal gap. However, this quantity is typically unavailable in practice. In this work, we show that solving a regularized surrogate with algorithms based on simple primal-dual averaging provides non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for a \textit{computable} optimality certificate. We first analyze primal and dual methods based on one average, namely modified dual averaging and generalized conditional gradient, and establish $\tilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ certificate complexities. Motivated by asymmetries in the one-average case, we analyze a self-dual, two-average method that preserves symmetry while losing certificate guarantees. To recover certificate convergence, we propose a three-average method that achieves an accelerated $\tilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-1/2})$ certificate complexity. Furthermore, we prove primal-dual algorithm correspondences for the one, two, and three-average cases. In particular, the primal three-average accelerated method mirrors the well-known gradient extrapolation method in the dual. By interpreting our results through the lens of zero-sum matrix games and Fisher markets, we further connect primal-dual averaging methods to game theory and market dynamics.

title: Tabu Search for Tactical Wireless Network Design in Challenging Environments
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the design of tactical wireless networks for scenarios where conventional telecommunications infrastructure is unavailable, such as during natural disasters. The main contribution is a Tabu Search-based optimization algorithm for maximizing the bottleneck throughput—the worst-case data transmission rate—across a network modeled as a directed, rooted tree connecting 10 to 50 nodes equipped with multi-beam antennas supporting multiple channels and frequencies.

The authors decompose the complex, highly nonlinear network design problem into manageable sub-tasks: master hub selection, partitioning of neighboring nodes, channel and frequency assignment, and antenna configuration. A key innovation is the use of geometric functions to partition the master hub's successors, drastically reducing the exponential number of candidate configurations and enabling more efficient neighborhood exploration. Two algorithm variants, TABU1 and TABU2, are proposed, each incorporating different lower bound evaluation procedures to assess topology quality during the search process.

Experimental comparisons using synthetic data demonstrate that the proposed algorithms, particularly TABU2, outperform existing methods by achieving broader and deeper exploration of the solution space within the same computational budget, yielding higher-quality network configurations across instances of varying sizes.

The significance of this work lies in its practical applicability to real-world tactical communication scenarios, accounting for realistic physical characteristics such as terrain-induced signal loss and interference rather than relying on simplifying assumptions common in prior literature. Future directions include integrating machine learning techniques, particularly graph neural networks, to further accelerate the optimization process.
original_abstract: Tactical wireless networks play a vital role in ensuring reliable connectivity in scenarios where conventional telecommunications infrastructure is unavailable or damaged, such as areas impacted by natural disasters. These networks are designed to operate efficiently in difficult and unpredictable environments by adapting to the unique characteristics of the terrain. This research addresses a real-world challenge from the communications industry: designing tactical wireless networks that meet the specific constraints defined by our industrial partner, with the goal of optimizing signal strength and coverage while minimizing interference. To this end, we propose two tabu search algorithms that incorporate several heuristic subroutines, enabling the efficient generation of high-quality network designs. Results from synthetic tests demonstrate that our approach produces networks rapidly and effectively, offering significant improvements over existing methods.

title: Lagrangian Mean Curvature Equations on exterior domains
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior at infinity and the exterior Dirichlet problem for Lagrangian mean curvature equations on exterior domains, extending classical results for special Lagrangian equations to the perturbed setting where the phase function takes the form Θ + f(x) with f(x) decaying at infinity.

The main contributions are twofold. First, the authors establish precise asymptotic expansions for solutions near infinity in both two and higher dimensions. In dimension two, they develop a novel extended exterior (K, K')-quasiconformal mapping method to determine the decay rate of the Hessian, bypassing the barrier function techniques used in prior work. This approach requires only uniform ellipticity rather than concavity of the operator, representing a meaningful methodological advance. For dimensions n ≥ 3, they employ a contradiction argument combining Evans-Krylov estimates with weak Harnack inequalities to establish Hessian convergence. Second, the authors solve the exterior Dirichlet problem for Lagrangian mean curvature equations with prescribed asymptotic behavior, extending previous results from the special Lagrangian case (f ≡ 0) to the perturbed case and from supercritical/critical phases to include subcritical phases when f ≡ 0.

Key results include optimal decay rate conditions (β > 2 is shown to be sharp) and the construction of generalized symmetric sub- and supersolutions enabling Perron's method for existence. These findings generalize the foundational work of Li-Li-Yuan and provide a comprehensive framework for understanding Lagrangian mean curvature equations on exterior domains.
original_abstract: We introduce an extended exterior $(K,K^{\prime},α_0)$--quasiconformal mapping method to study the asymptotic behavior at infinity of solutions to the supercritical phase Lagrangian mean curvature equation \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n} \arctan λ_i(D^2u) = θ+ f(x) \] on exterior domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where the constant $|θ|\in((n-2)π/2,nπ/2)$, $n\geq 2$, and $f=O(|x|^{-β})$ is a perturbation term with the sharp decay condition $β>2$ at infinity. Our work generalizes the classical exterior Bernstein-type theorem for the special Lagrangian equation ($f\equiv0$) established by Li--Li--Yuan [Adv. Math. (2020)]. Via Perron's method, we solve the corresponding Dirichlet problem outside a bounded, uniformly convex domain, prescribing asymptotic behavior at infinity. For $n \geq 3$, we establish existence and uniqueness of viscosity solutions in both the supercritical phase case with $f \not\equiv 0$ and the subcritical phase case with $f \equiv 0$. This extends earlier work by Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (2019)] on the exterior Dirichlet problem for the special Lagrangian equation ($f \equiv 0$) under weaker regularity assumptions on the interior boundary and boundary data.

title: Dual formulations of geometric curvature flows and their discretizations
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a novel family of "dual formulations" for geometric curvature flows—including mean curvature flow, surface diffusion, and solid-state dewetting—by incorporating an auxiliary dual multiplier variable at the continuous level. While these reformulations are mathematically equivalent to the classical models, they are specifically designed to enable parametric finite element discretizations that are simultaneously linearly implicit, energy stable, and mesh-quality preserving.

The key methodological insight is that the dual multiplier makes the energy-dissipation structure explicit in a form that transfers naturally to fully discrete schemes. The authors combine this framework with the minimal-deformation-rate (MDR) tangential motion, which optimally redistributes mesh points by selecting the velocity that minimizes the deformation-rate energy subject to the normal-velocity constraint. The resulting "dual-MDR" schemes overcome a fundamental tension in existing methods: the Barrett-Garcke-Nürnberg (BGN) approach provides energy stability but can lose mesh quality at small time steps, while the direct MDR discretization maintains mesh quality but lacks energy stability and is less robust near singularities.

Numerical experiments demonstrate that the dual-MDR schemes maintain high mesh quality across a wide range of time-step sizes, preserve discrete energy dissipation, accurately resolve pinch-off singularities, and handle challenging scenarios such as solid-state dewetting with incompatible initial conditions. The framework extends beyond MDR to accommodate other artificial tangential motions, offering a general and flexible approach for structure-preserving computation of curvature-driven surface evolution.
original_abstract: We propose new formulations of geometric curvature flows -- referred to as \emph{dual formulations} -- that are equivalent to the original formulations but provide a novel framework for constructing linearly implicit and energy-stable schemes for curvature-driven surface evolution, including mean curvature flow, surface diffusion, and solid-state dewetting on a substrate with a moving contact line. The dual formulations are derived by introducing, at the continuous level, an additional unknown in the form of a dual multiplier. This augmentation does not alter the continuous dynamics but makes the underlying energy-dissipation structure explicit and, in turn, enables a systematic design of linearly implicit discretizations that inherit energy stability. A key feature of this framework is that it accommodates a broad class of artificial tangential motions which can be used to maintain good mesh quality of the computed surfaces. As an illustration, we combine the framework with the minimal-deformation-rate (MDR) tangential motion, leading to what we call the \emph{dual-MDR} scheme. The resulting method is linearly implicit and energy-stable, while retaining the MDR tangential motion to maintain good mesh quality. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the convergence of the proposed schemes, their structure-preserving properties, and advantages on representative benchmark problems.

title: On quantum functionals for higher-order tensors
generated_summary:
This paper investigates quantum functionals for higher-order tensors, focusing on whether non-singleton-supported distributions can yield universal spectral points in Strassen's asymptotic spectrum theory. Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam previously showed that upper and lower quantum functionals agree for singleton-supported distributions, making them universal spectral points. This work examines whether this extends to laminarly-supported distributions involving genuine multipartite bipartitions.

The authors employ tools from geometric invariant theory, particularly the Kempf-Ness theorem, which provides rigidity results for states with maximal entropy across marginals. They develop a novel determinant-based upper bound on the lower quantum functional that captures tension between maximizing entropy on individual subsystems versus across non-singleton bipartitions.

The key results establish three main findings. First, for every laminarly-supported distribution that is not singleton-supported, there exist tensors where the upper and lower quantum functionals disagree, proving these are not universal spectral points. Second, the authors identify a strict sub-semiring of "laminar-quantum-robust" tensors where agreement holds, which includes embedded lower-order tensors, graph tensors, and the quantum-information-theoretic W₄ tensor. Third, by Strassen's extension theorem, each laminar quantum functional on this sub-semiring extends to some universal spectral point that has not been previously identified.

These results delineate the boundary of the quantum functional approach, reveal new structural features of the asymptotic restriction ordering for higher-order tensors, and establish the existence of unknown universal spectral points with potential implications for algebraic complexity and quantum entanglement theory.
original_abstract: Upper and lower quantum functionals, introduced by Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam (STOC 2018, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2023), are families of monotone functions of tensors indexed by a weighting on the set of subsets of the tensor legs. Inspired by quantum information theory, they were crafted as obstructions to asymptotic tensor transformations, relevant in algebraic complexity theory. For tensors of order three, and more generally for weightings on singletons for higher-order tensors, the upper and lower quantum functionals coincide and are spectral points in Strassen's asymptotic spectrum. Moreover, the singleton quantum functionals characterize the asymptotic slice rank, whereas general weightings provide upper bounds on asymptotic partition rank. It has been an open question whether the upper and lower quantum functionals also coincide for other cases, or more generally, how to construct further spectral points, especially for higher-order tensors. In this work, we show that upper and lower quantum functionals generally do not coincide, but that they anchor new spectral points. With this we mean that there exist new spectral points, which equal the quantum functionals on the set of tensors on which upper and lower coincide. The set is shown to include embedded three-tensors and W-like states and concerns all laminar weightings, significantly extending the singleton case.

title: DeepRitzSplit Neural Operator for Phase-Field Models via Energy Splitting
generated_summary:
This paper introduces DeepRitzSplit, a physics-informed neural operator framework for solving phase-field models by combining the Deep Ritz energy minimization method with a semi-implicit convex-concave energy splitting technique. The key innovation is formulating the training loss as an energy minimization problem derived from the splitting scheme, which guarantees unconditional energy dissipation regardless of the chosen timestep—a property not generally ensured by conventional finite difference, finite element, or other physics-informed neural operator approaches.

The authors also design a Reaction-Diffusion Neural Operator (RDNO) architecture that mirrors the structure of semi-implicit numerical schemes, improving interpretability and training efficiency compared to standard architectures like Fourier Neural Operators and U-Nets. The framework is demonstrated on two problems: the Allen-Cahn equation for phase separation and a more complex anisotropic dendritic growth model coupling phase evolution with heat transfer.

Key results show that DeepRitzSplit achieves better generalization on unseen datasets compared to data-driven neural operators for the Allen-Cahn equation. For dendritic growth, the method accurately captures physical quantities such as solid phase fraction and tip velocity while being faster than conventional spectral schemes. Notably, neural operators trained on configurations with only one to three grains generalize well to multi-grain scenarios. The authors further demonstrate that DeepRitzSplit can serve as an effective preconditioner for subsequent residual-based training to improve geometric accuracy. This work establishes a physically consistent and efficient neural surrogate framework for large-scale phase-field simulations.
original_abstract: The multi-scale and non-linear nature of phase-field models of solidification requires fine spatial and temporal discretization, leading to long computation times. This could be overcome with artificial-intelligence approaches. Surrogate models based on neural operators could have a lower computational cost than conventional numerical discretization methods. We propose a new neural operator approach that bridges classical convex-concave splitting schemes with physics-informed learning to accelerate the simulation of phase-field models. It consists of a Deep Ritz method, where a neural operator is trained to approximate a variational formulation of the phase-field model. By training the neural operator with an energy-splitting variational formulation, we enforce the energy dissipation property of the underlying models. We further introduce a custom Reaction-Diffusion Neural Operator (RDNO) architecture, adapted to the operators of the model equations. We successfully apply the deep learning approach to the isotropic Allen-Cahn equation and to anisotropic dendritic growth simulation. We demonstrate that our physically-informed training provides better generalization in out-of-distribution evaluations than data-driven training, while achieving faster inference than traditional Fourier spectral methods.

title: Gamma-Based Expansion for the First-Passage Time Distribution of Stochastic Logistic Models with Harvesting

Numerical experiments, validated against Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrate that the method performs well in regimes of moderate dispersion (coefficient of variation below one), where the cumulant structure approximates that of a Gamma distribution. original_abstract: The first passage time problem is considered for stochastic logistic growth model with constant harvesting and multiplicative environmental noise. Explicit expressions for the moments and cumulants of both upcrossing and downcrossing FPTs in the presence of constant thresholds are obtained through a power-series expansion of the Laplace transform. Then a closed-form representation of the FPT density is recovered via an orthogonal Laguerre--Gamma expansion . This representation is used to numerically evaluate FPT densities, with the truncation order controlling the trade-off between accuracy and stability. Numerical experiments based on Monte Carlo simulations confirm the high accuracy of the method in regimes of moderate dispersion and highlight its limitations when higher-order moments grow rapidly. Application to fisheries management models shows that the method remains effective even for large-scale population. title: Horospherical Depth and Busemann Median on Hadamard Manifolds

original_abstract: \We introduce the horospherical depth, an intrinsic notion of statistical depth on Hadamard manifolds, and define the Busemann median as the set of its maximizers. The construction exploits the fact that the linear functionals appearing in Tukey's half-space depth are themselves limits of renormalized distance functions; on a Hadamard manifold the same limiting procedure produces Busemann functions, whose sublevel sets are horoballs, the intrinsic replacements for halfspaces. The resulting depth is parametrized by the visual boundary, is isometry-equivariant, and requires neither tangent-space linearization nor a chosen base point.For arbitrary Hadamard manifolds, we prove that the depth regions are nested and geodesically convex, that a centerpoint of depth at least $1/(d+1)$ exists, and hence that the Busemann median exists for every Borel probability measure. Under strictly negative sectional curvature and mild regularity assumptions, the depth is strictly quasi-concave and the median is unique. We also establish robustness: the depth is stable under total-variation perturbations, and under contamination escaping to infinity the limiting median depends on the escape direction but not on how far the contaminating mass has moved along the geodesic ray, in contrast with the Fréchet mean. Finally, we establish uniform consistency of the sample depth and convergence of sample depth regions and sample Busemann medians; on symmetric spaces of noncompact type, the argument proceeds through a VC analysis of upper horospherical halfspaces, while on general Hadamard manifolds it follows from a compactness argument under a mild non-atomicity assumption.

title: On the packing dimension of projected measures
generated_summary:

The methodology builds on the packing dimension profiles framework of Falconer and Howroyd. The authors establish Lipschitz continuity of certain dimension profile functions and develop careful integral estimates involving the Assouad dimension of the measure's support. Key technical tools include Hölder's inequality arguments, covering number estimates, and potential-theoretic characterizations of packing dimension.

The central results provide two complementary theorems. First, when D(μ) ≥ m, the packing dimension of the projected measure equals m for almost every m-dimensional subspace, recovering a Hausdorff-type projection formula. Second, when D(μ) < m, the authors establish a lower bound for the packing dimension profile involving the Assouad dimension of the support, showing that if the Assouad dimension does not exceed m, then the classical projection formula for packing dimension holds. These results extend naturally to images of measures under fractional Brownian motion via Xiao's framework.

The significance lies in providing a complete characterization of when packing dimension projection formulas hold, identifying the Assouad dimension of the support as the key geometric quantity controlling the stability of packing dimension under projections, thereby unifying and extending previous partial results.
original_abstract: We study the packing dimension of Borel measures under orthogonal projections. We give a necessary and sufficient condition such that typical projections of Borel probability measures have full packing dimension and derive general lower bounds in the complementary case. Our approach shows that the Assouad dimension of the support influences the behavior of projected measures. The same method yields corresponding results for images under fractional Brownian motion.

title: Weak solutions and weak-strong uniqueness for a Cahn-Hilliard type model with chemotaxis
generated_summary:

The authors establish three main results: global existence of weak solutions, local existence of strong solutions, and weak-strong uniqueness. The analysis employs a singular Flory-Huggins potential, which confines the phase parameter to the physical interval [-1,1] and ensures coercivity of the free energy functional. A central methodological contribution involves a renormalized formulation of the nutrient equation, obtained by dividing by the nutrient concentration and applying chain-rule arguments. This exploits a reinforced minimum principle showing strict positivity of the nutrient variable. Combined with uniform integrability arguments, this yields strong convergence needed to identify the supercritical cross-diffusion term in the limit. The weak solution concept is complemented by an integrated entropy inequality, which proves essential for the weak-strong uniqueness argument via a relative energy method.

The significance of this work lies in resolving the open problem of global solution existence in three dimensions without requiring logistic degradation terms or subcritical sensitivity assumptions. original_abstract: We prove existence of weak solutions and weak-strong uniqueness for a mathematical model which couples the evolution of a phase-parameter $\varphi$ satisfying a Cahn-Hilliard type relation with the one of an additional variable $σ$ influencing the phase separation process. The main application of the model refers to cancer growth processes, where $σ$ may represent the concentration of a chemical substance affecting the evolution of the tumor, and is governed by a nonlinear parabolic equation characterized by a cross-diffusion term alike that occurring in the Keller-Segel model for chemotaxis. This term is also responsible for the most relevant difficulties in the mathematical analysis of the system. Complementing previous results on the model, we prove here global in time existence for a very weak notion of solution to which a suitable energy imbalance and a logarithmic inequality for the nutrient are added. Noting that the system also admits local in time "strong" solutions, we can also exhibit a weak-strong uniqueness result whose proof exploits in an essential way the entropy-type inequality satisfied by weak solutions.

title: Towards Symmetry-sensitive Pose Estimation: A Rotation Representation for Symmetric Object Classes
generated_summary:

The methodology involves formally classifying objects from the T-LESS and ITODD benchmark datasets into symmetry classes based on their rotational symmetries per axis, then defining class-specific SARR representations with frequencies corresponding to the degree of symmetry. The representation operates directly on annotations, making it compatible with any pose estimation network architecture. The authors train CenterNet-based networks using depth images and compare SARR against five standard rotation representations (Euler angles, rotation matrices, 6D representation, quaternions, and trigonometric identities) across multiple training scopes.

Key results demonstrate that SARR consistently outperforms all other representations, achieving approximately 3-5% absolute improvement over the second-best representation across both datasets. Under the symmetry-sensitive ARC metric, SARR-trained networks outperform all existing methods on T-LESS, including those using RGB-D inputs and 3D models.

This work highlights the importance of encoding symmetry awareness directly into rotation representations rather than relying solely on symmetry-invariant evaluation metrics, offering a principled and generalizable approach applicable to various symmetric object classes.
original_abstract: Symmetric objects are common in daily life and industry, yet their inherent orientation ambiguities that impede the training of deep learning networks for pose estimation are rarely discussed in the literature. To cope with these ambiguities, existing solutions typically require the design of specific loss functions and network architectures or resort to symmetry-invariant evaluation metrics. In contrast, we focus on the numeric representation of the rotation itself, modifying trigonometric identities with the degrees of symmetry derived from the objects' shapes. We use our representation, SARR, to obtain canonic (symmetry-resolved) poses for the symmetric objects in two popular 6D pose estimation datasets, T-LESS and ITODD, where SARR is unique and continuous w.r.t. the visual appearance. This allows us to use a standard CNN for 3D orientation estimation whose performance is evaluated with the symmetry-sensitive cosine distance $\text{AR}_{\text{C}}$. Our networks outperform the state of the art using $\text{AR}_{\text{C}}$ and achieve satisfactory performance when using conventional symmetry-invariant measures. Our method does not require any 3D models but only depth, or, as part of an additional experiment, texture-less RGB/grayscale images as input. We also show that networks trained on SARR outperform the same networks trained on rotation matrices, Euler angles, quaternions, standard trigonometrics or the recently popular 6d representation -- even in inference scenarios where no prior knowledge of the objects' symmetry properties is available. Code and a visualization toolkit are available at https://github.com/akriegler/SARR .

title: Centre manifold theorem for maps along manifolds of fixed points

A second result applies this theorem via a surgery argument to gradient descent dynamics for deep neural networks, producing local centre manifolds near points where the stability threshold is violated.

The significance lies in enabling rigorous dimension reduction for studying the surprising convergence phenomena observed in deep learning when using large step sizes that violate classical stability conditions, paving the way for a general theory of non-convex optimization in this regime.
original_abstract: We prove a centre manifold theorem for a map along a manifold-with-boundary of fixed points, and provide an application to the study of gradient descent with large step size on two-layer matrix factorisation problems.

title: On the Calabi estimate of geometric flows of Hermitian metrics
generated_summary:

The main theorem states that if a smooth curve of Hermitian metrics satisfies a uniform equivalence condition and certain bounds on curvature, torsion, and related geometric quantities, then a uniform first-order bound holds. original_abstract: We establish a general result ensuring a $C^1$ a priori bound for smooth curves of Hermitian metrics. As a main application, we obtain a new regularity result for Hermitian curvature flows, and in particular for the second Chern-Ricci flow.

title: Local Convergence Results for Sequential Quadratic Programming with Complementarity Constraints
generated_summary:

Numerical examples demonstrate qualitative advantages over classical SQP applied to NLP reformulations, including cases where SQPCC converges to S-stationary points while SQP converges to inferior non-S-stationary points.

The results are particularly relevant for dynamic optimization and model predictive control applications, where SQPCC iterates maintain a direct connection to sensitivity analysis of parametric MPCCs that classical SQP approaches lose.
original_abstract: Mathematical programs with complementarity constraints (MPCCs) are a challenging class of nonlinear optimization problems, because their nonlinear programming reformulations violate standard constraint qualifications at every feasible point. This paper analyzes sequential quadratic programming with complementarity constraints (SQPCC). In this method, the complementarity constraints are retained in the subproblems, yielding quadratic programs with complementarity constraints (QPCCs). The main contribution of the paper is a new local convergence result for the SQPCC method to S-stationary points. We show that there exists at least one sequence of QPCC S-stationary points converging to a reference S-stationary point of the MPCC, and we characterize conditions under which each such sequence converges and under which such a sequence is locally unique. In contrast to previous results, the analysis is established under weaker second-order sufficient conditions and requires no upper-level strict complementarity. Our result builds upon local convergence results for the classical SQP method. We present local convergence results for SQP within the kappa-omega setting, which also cover linearly convergent variants. These assumptions, which are widely used in the analysis of Newton-type methods, provide a natural framework for quantifying subproblem approximation errors, their effect on the convergence speed, and the effect of nonlinearity on the size of the local convergence region. Furthermore, we establish an active-set stabilization result for SQPCC, identifying conditions under which the optimal complementarity and inequality active sets are identified after finitely many iterations, and conditions under which such identification occurs only asymptotically. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical findings and highlight some advantages of SQPCC over classical SQP applied to MPCCs.

title: Spectral approximation for the separable covariance mixture model
generated_summary:
This paper introduces the **separable covariance mixture model**, where a data matrix is expressed as a sum of terms, each involving left and right covariance matrices applied to independent copies of a random matrix with independent entries. This model generalizes several important frameworks in high-dimensional statistics, including separable covariance models and finite-order moving average processes, without requiring the restrictive assumption that covariance matrices within each family are simultaneously diagonalizable.

The main contribution is establishing a non-asymptotic deterministic equivalent for the resolvent of the sample covariance matrix. Specifically, the authors prove that the resolvent is well-approximated by a deterministic matrix defined through a dual system of matrix-valued equations, with approximation error of order 1/n holding with high probability. The methodology relies on three key tools: a quantitative uniqueness argument for near-solutions of the dual equations, a specialized application of Stein's lemma for the Gaussian case combined with concentration bounds, and a universality argument extending results to general entry distributions satisfying moment conditions.

As asymptotic consequences, the authors derive weak convergence of empirical matrix-valued spectral measures and a generalized Marchenko-Pastur law for the limiting eigenvalue distribution. Numerical simulations on three examples—covariance mixtures, moving average processes, and random permutation mixtures—validate the theoretical predictions. This work significantly broadens the applicability of spectral analysis tools to high-dimensional data with complex, non-simultaneously-diagonalizable dependence structures.
original_abstract: This paper introduces the separable covariance mixture model, which assumes a data-matrix $Y$ to be of the form $$ \sum\limits_{r=1}^R A_r X B_r $$ for one random $(d \times n)$-matrix $X$ with independent centered variance-one entries, and for two families of deterministic matrices $A_1,\dots,A_R \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ and $B_1,\dots,B_R \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$. Under certain assumptions, it is shown that the resolvents $(\frac{1}{n} Y Y^* - z \operatorname{Id}_d)^{-1}$ and $(\frac{1}{n} Y^* Y - z \operatorname{Id}_n)^{-1}$ respectively approximate the deterministic matrices $$ -\frac{1}{z}\Big( \operatorname{Id}_d + \sum\limits_{r,s=1}^R δ^{(B)}_{r,s}(z) A_{r} A_{s}^* \Big)^{-1} \ \ \text{ and } \ \ -\frac{1}{z}\Big( \operatorname{Id}_n + \sum\limits_{r,s=1}^R δ^{(A)}_{r,s}(z) B_{s}^*B_{r} \Big)^{-1} \ , $$ where $δ^{(A)}, δ^{(B)} \in \mathbb{C}^{R \times R}$ are uniquely defined solutions to a certain dual system of equations. The results are non-asymptotic and do not require simultaneous diagonalizability of the families $(A_r)_{r \leq R}$ or $(B_r)_{r \leq R}$, as was required in previous works such as [Hazarika and Paul (2025)] or [Mei et al. (2023)]. An asymptotic application, which describes the limiting spectral distribution of the sample covariance matrix analogues $\frac{1}{n} Y Y^*$ or $\frac{1}{n} Y^* Y$, is included.

title: The complex of discrete Morse matchings of the $n$-simplex: homotopy types and structural results
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the homotopy types of complexes of discrete Morse matchings for the *n*-simplex and its boundary, advancing understanding of these parameter spaces that encode gradient vector fields in discrete Morse theory. The main contributions include complete determination of homotopy types for *n* = 3 and structural results applicable to all dimensions.

The authors employ a combination of direct homology computations, the framework of Bravo and Camarena, exhaustive parallel enumeration, and combinatorial techniques including contiguity arguments and explicit bijections between facets. For *n* = 3, they determine the homotopy types of the complex of discrete Morse matchings for both the 3-simplex and its boundary, showing that the associated pure complexes share a common homotopy type.

Key structural results valid for all *n* include: an explicit bijection between top-dimensional facets of the simplex and boundary complexes, implying equal numbers of optimal matchings; a layer-count lemma reducing optimal matching enumeration to the (*n*−2)-skeleton with uniform fiber size *n*+1; and a null-homotopy result showing that the inclusion of the matching complex of any finite simplicial complex into that of its cone is null-homotopic. For *n* = 4, computational evidence confirms predictions of the restriction theorem, while the positive reduced Euler characteristic rules out homotopy equivalence with a wedge of odd-dimensional spheres.

These results significantly advance understanding of discrete Morse matching spaces, with implications for computational topology and the flexibility of discrete Morse reductions used in topological data analysis.
original_abstract: The complex of discrete Morse matchings $\M(K)$, introduced by Chari and Joswig, is a simplicial complex whose simplices are the acyclic matchings on the Hasse diagram of $K$. Its homotopy type is known in only a handful of cases. In this paper, we compute the homotopy types of $\M(Δ^3)$ and $\M(\partialΔ^3)$, the corresponding pure complexes $\M_{P}(Δ^3) \simeq \M_{P}(\partialΔ^3)$, and the generalized complex of discrete Morse matchings $\GM(Δ^3) \simeq \GM(\partialΔ^3)$. For general $n$ we prove the identity $f(n) = (n+1) \cdot |\text{top-dimensional facets of } \M(Δ^n_{(n-2)})|$, reducing the enumeration of optimal matchings on $Δ^n$ to an enumeration on its $(n-2)$-skeleton, and we show that the inclusion $\M(K) \hookrightarrow \M(CK)$ is null-homotopic for any cone. We also compute the $f$-vector of $\M(Δ^4)$, whose top entry $f(4) = 380{,}125$ is the number of optimal discrete Morse matchings on $Δ^4$. We conclude with two conjectures extending the $\M_{P}$ and $\GM$ equivalences to all $n$.

title: Operators on injective tensor products of L1-preduals

Key results include the preservation of various operator properties (weak compactness, the Dunford-Pettis property, Pełczyński's property (V), and others) when passing from C(K,E)-spaces to X ⊗̌ε E spaces. The paper also treats the special case where B_{X*} is scattered.

The significance lies in unifying and generalizing a substantial body of work on C(K,E)-spaces, demonstrating that many classical results extend naturally to the setting of L₁-preduals through the injective tensor product framework.
original_abstract: Let X be an L1-predual and E,F be Banach spaces. We use the fact that an unconditionally converging operator T from the injective tensor product of X and E to F is strongly bounded and extend T to an operator S on continuous F-valued functions on the dual unit ball of X with the preservation of properties of T. This procedure provides a unified approach for proving properties of the tensor product of X and E based on the properties of E.

title: Informativity of Data-Knowledge Pairs for Lyapunov Equations

They derive an algebraic condition equivalent to joint informativity under mild assumptions, characterized by the existence of a solution to a system of Lyapunov equations determined by both the dataset and prior knowledge. Based on this characterization, they also develop a data-driven method for computing Lyapunov equation solutions.

original_abstract: In the past few years, data informativity with prior knowledge has attracted increasing attention. This line of research aims to characterize a dataset on a dynamical system that enables system analysis or design only by the dataset and given prior knowledge on the system. In this paper, we investigate such a characterization for the data-driven problem of computing a unique solution to Lyapunov equations. First, we introduce a notion of joint informativity for data-knowledge pairs as an extension of the standard informativity concept. Second, we derive an algebraic equivalent condition for the joint informativity. Finally, we provide further insights into the joint informativity by considering a special case of prior knowledge. The characterization presented in this paper is developed for a wide class of prior knowledge, enabling the incorporation of various forms of system information.

title: The Magnitude of Dominated Sets: A Pareto Compliant Indicator Grounded in Metric Geometry

They prove an all-dimensional projection formula and establish strict set monotonicity for finite unions of anchored boxes, which directly yields Pareto compliance for magnitude as a set indicator. In three-dimensional simplex examples, magnitude-optimal configurations naturally align with complete Das–Dennis grids for suitable population sizes, while hypervolume favors more interior-filling layouts.

The significance of this work lies in establishing magnitude as a mathematically principled alternative to hypervolume, grounded in geometric measure theory, with computational complexity in the same asymptotic regime. This opens new connections between indicator theory, dominated-set geometry, and reference-direction methods in multiobjective optimization.
original_abstract: We investigate \emph{magnitude} as a new unary and strictly Pareto-compliant quality indicator for finite approximation sets to the Pareto front in multiobjective optimization. Magnitude originates in enriched category theory and metric geometry, where it is a notion of size or point content for compact metric spaces and a generalization of cardinality. For dominated regions in the \(\ell_1\) box setting, magnitude is close to hypervolume but not identical: it contains the top-dimensional hypervolume term together with positive lower-dimensional projection and boundary contributions. This paper gives a first theoretical study of magnitude as an indicator. We consider multiobjective maximization with a common anchor point. For dominated sets generated by finite approximation sets, we derive an all-dimensional projection formula, prove weak and strict set monotonicity on finite unions of anchored boxes, and thereby obtain weak and strict Pareto compliance. Unlike hypervolume, magnitude assigns positive value to boundary points sharing one or more coordinates with the anchor point, even when their top-dimensional hypervolume contribution vanishes. We then formulate projected set-gradient methods and compare hypervolume and magnitude on biobjective and three-dimensional simplex examples. Numerically, magnitude favors boundary-including populations and, for suitable cardinalities, complete Das--Dennis grids, whereas hypervolume prefers more interior-filling configurations. Computationally, magnitude reduces to hypervolume on coordinate projections; for fixed dimension this yields the same asymptotic complexity up to a factor \(2^d-1\), and in dimensions two and three \(Θ(n\log n)\) time. These results identify magnitude as a mathematically natural and computationally viable alternative to hypervolume for finite Pareto front approximations.

title: Asymptotic stability and diffusion-driven pattern formation in a predator-prey system with two chemicals

Specifically, prey release chemical attractants that guide predator movement toward prey concentrations, while predators emit repellent chemicals that drive prey dispersal away from predator regions. This four-component system couples two population densities with two chemical signal concentrations, providing a biologically grounded mechanism for cross-diffusion observed in systems such as bacteria-bacteriophage and algae-zooplankton interactions.

The authors employ rigorous mathematical analysis to establish global existence and uniform boundedness of classical solutions using energy estimates and Sobolev embedding techniques. title: Morita equivalence for quantum graphs

The authors introduce a quantized notion of pullback between quantum graphs via unital *-homomorphisms satisfying specific Kraus representation conditions, and construct the "skeleton" of an irreducibly acting quantum graph as a noncommutative analogue of the classical true-twin reduction. The skeleton construction identifies multiplicities in the multiplier algebra decomposition and factors the operator system accordingly.

The central result (Theorem A) establishes that for irreducibly acting quantum graphs, TRO-equivalence, Δ-equivalence, and being full pullbacks of isomorphic quantum graphs are all equivalent characterizations of Morita equivalence. A stronger notion (Theorem B) simultaneously requires TRO-equivalence of both the operator systems and their associated algebras, which for classical graphs reduces to graph isomorphism. For noncommutative graphs specifically, the two notions coincide and admit concrete characterization through completely positive maps (Theorem C). The authors further prove that key quantum graph parameters—including the quantum independence number, quantum Lovász theta function, and projective packing number—are invariant under TRO-equivalence of noncommutative graphs (Theorem D), while chromatic and clique numbers are not.

original_abstract: We introduce an operator-algebraic framework for Morita equivalence of quantum graphs based on $Δ$-equivalence of operator systems introduced by Eleftherakis, Kakariadis and Todorov. Adopting the perspective of Weaver, we view quantum graphs as quantum relations, that is, operator systems endowed with a bimodule structure over the commutant of a von Neumann algebra. Within this framework, we show that two irreducibly acting quantum graphs are Morita equivalent if and only if they are both full pullbacks of a common quantum graph. This extends a result of Eleftherakis, Kakariadis and Todorov for graph operator systems to the quantum graph setting. In passing we construct a true-twin reduction analogue for an irreducibly acting quantum graph. We further characterise the case where we have simultaneous TRO-equivalence of the quantum graphs and their associated algebras, thus giving a second, stronger notion of Morita equivalence. In the special case of noncommutative graphs, corresponding to the zero-error quantum communication setting, the two notions coincide and we obtain a characterisation in terms of strong co-homomorphisms of noncommutative graphs. title: Spherical singularities in compactified Ruijsenaars--Schneider systems

Depending on the value of a parameter $0<y< π$, they arise in two drastically different forms: in type (i) these are toric systems, while in the type (ii) cases they possess globally continuous action variables that generate a Hamiltonian torus action (only) on a dense open subset of the phase space. title: An Exact Algorithm for Public Transport Line Planning Considering Passenger and Operational Costs and Lost Demand

original_abstract: Line planning in public transport is the strategic problem of selecting lines and their operating frequencies. This problem is important as it defines the passenger service, based on available connections and expected travel times, and drives operational cost in terms of the number of vehicles required. This paper presents a line planning model that minimizes the weighted sum of passenger travel time, including in-vehicle time and frequency-dependent waiting and transfer times, and operating costs for the public transport agency. Unlike traditional approaches that assume demand to be fixed, our approach requires a minimum service level for demand to be captured, ensuring that services are provided only when they are attractive to users and cost-efficient to operate. The introduced capacity constraints ensure sufficient capacity on the lines and help guide the trade-off between expected demand on selected lines and their frequencies. The resulting mixed-integer program presents a challenging combinatorial problem as the number of passenger paths grows rapidly in relation to the number of lines and frequencies considered. To address this, we propose an iterative exact algorithm that utilizes a reduced problem representation and dynamically expands it with additional frequencies and paths. Evaluated on four networks with varying complexity and cost trade-offs, our method achieves significant speed-ups and tighter bounds compared to solving the complete model directly by CPLEX, particularly when operator and passenger costs are more evenly balanced in the objective. Furthermore, we demonstrate how accounting for lost demand leads to more efficient resource use from an overall perspective.

title: Multi-stream Quickest Change Detection: Foundations and Recent Advances

original_abstract: This paper provides an overview of recent developments in quickest change detection (QCD) for high-dimensional multi-sensor systems, with an emphasis on settings involving structural constraints and limited sensing resources. Additionally, we discuss sampling constraints, where observations must be selected or acquired sequentially under resource limitations. Multi-stream applications can require making multiple detections, for example when detecting changes separately in different streams. The underlying assumptions on probability models, the types of changes taking place, commonly used decision-making criteria, performance indices, and error types are described. We also briefly discuss the application of machine learning in cases where the underlying probability models are not known or there is a need to select which sensors should monitor the phenomena because of the large scale of the system.

original_abstract: We investigate the homological behaviour of compactly generated triangulated categories under separable extensions. We also establish a relation between singularity categories in this setting, proving that the singularity category of a separable extension is equivalent, up to retracts, to a separable extension of the singularity category. original_abstract: We study second-order stochastic parabolic equations in a cylindrical domain with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. Under a natural compatibility condition on the gradient noise, we establish global Schauder estimates in stochastic Hölder spaces for the Dirichlet problem. The coefficients and free terms are assumed to be Hölder continuous in the spatial variables, while only their boundary traces are required to be Hölder continuous in time. As a consequence, we obtain existence and uniqueness of quasi-classical solutions in stochastic Hölder spaces, and further derive pathwise classical solvability in Hölder classes.

title: Complex normalizing flows can be information Kähler-Ricci flows

original_abstract: We develop interconnections between the complex normalizing flow for data drawn from Borel probability measures on the twofold realification of the complex manifold and the Kähler-Ricci flow. title: Adaptive finite element methods with optimally preconditioned GMRES guarantee optimal complexity

original_abstract: We analyze optimal complexity of adaptive finite element methods (AFEMs) for general second-order linear elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs) in the Lax-Milgram setting. To this end, we formulate an adaptive algorithm which steers the local mesh-refinement as well as the termination of a generalized minimal residual solver (GMRES) with optimal preconditioner to solve the arising non-symmetric finite element systems. Algorithmic interplay of mesh-refinement and iterative solver is shown to be optimal: A natural and fully computable quasi-error monitoring discretization error and algebraic solver error guarantees unconditional convergence for any choice of adaptivity parameters, i.e., the algorithm cannot fail to converge. This is ensured algorithmically via a novel adaptive feedback-control for the solver-termination parameter that monitors and ensures full R-linear convergence.
