For the total weighted completion time objective, they show that a priority-based policy achieves a parametrized approximation ratio. These results extend to a broader family of practically motivated distributions, where a policy called WLEL achieves a 2-approximation for weighted completion time.

The significance of this work lies in establishing a structural connection between reentrant flow shops and parallel machines, providing a general framework that can facilitate future research on stochastic scheduling in reentrant manufacturing environments. The authors note that extending results beyond unit processing times remains an important open direction.
original_abstract: We study flow shop scheduling with stochastic reentry, where jobs must complete multiple passes through the entire shop, and the number of passes that a job requires for completion is drawn from a discrete probability distribution. The goal is to find policies that minimize performance measures in expectation. Our main contribution is a reduction to a classical parallel machine scheduling problem augmented with machine arrivals. This reduction preserves expected objective values and enables transferring structural results and performance guarantees from the auxiliary problems to the reentrant flow shop setting. We demonstrate the usefulness of this reduction by proving the optimality of simple priority policies for minimizing the makespan and the total completion time in expectation under geometric and, more generally, monotone hazard rate distributions. For minimizing the total weighted completion time, we derive an approximation guarantee that depends only on the squared coefficient of variation of the underlying distributions for a simple priority policy. Our results constitute the first optimality and approximation guarantees for flow shops with stochastic reentry and demonstrate that established scheduling policies naturally extend to this setting through the proposed reduction.

title: A 2-adjunction between representations and preorder morphisms
generated_summary:
This paper establishes a formal 2-adjunction between two categorical structures: representations and preorder morphisms. Representations, a recently introduced model defined by a preorder on a set of states and a relation from a set of meanings to states satisfying certain axioms, had previously lacked strong connections to established mathematical frameworks. The main contribution is demonstrating that representations stand in a tight, non-trivial relationship with preorder morphisms—maps between preordered sets that preserve the ordering structure—through a 2-categorical adjunction.

The methodology relies heavily on relation algebra, employing tools such as relational composition, residuals, and converse operations to formulate and prove the key results. The author defines the category of preorder morphisms (proms) with appropriate morphisms between them, and constructs an order-enriched category (2-category) of representations where morphisms carry a natural ordering via 2-cells. The adjunction is then constructed between these two categorical structures using explicit functorial mappings.

The key result is the existence of this 2-adjunction, which provides a principled bridge between the two frameworks. This has dual significance: it offers a retrospective justification for the definition of representations by grounding them in relation to classical, well-understood constructs from order theory, and it opens a pathway for transferring known results about order-preserving maps to the setting of representations, potentially yielding new insights about their structure and properties.
original_abstract: The recently introduced model of representations has been defined and motivated somewhat ex-nihilo. In this document, I will show that representations are related to a more ''classical'' model through a 2-adjunction. The target model is that of preorder morphisms, i.e. maps between sets equipped with reflexive and transitive relation that satisfy some natural preservation property. The aim of this is two-fold: first, this provides in my opinion a further justification of representations, as an object in non-trivial yet tight connection to some natural constructs; and secondly it suggests some classical results about order preserving maps could have interesting consequences for representations. This work has been presented (but not published or peer-reviewed) at RAMiCS 2026.

title: Wasserstein barycenters on metric graphs
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the regularity of Wasserstein barycenters over metric graphs, which are spaces formed by vertices connected by edges viewed as paths homeomorphic to compact intervals. The main contribution is proving that Wasserstein barycenters on metric graphs are "quasi-regular": while they may not be fully absolutely continuous with respect to the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, their singular part can only consist of Dirac masses concentrated at vertices of the graph. This result is optimal, as demonstrated by a known counterexample on a tripod where the barycenter of three absolutely continuous measures supported on distinct branches is a Dirac mass at the central vertex.

The methodology proceeds in two main steps. First, the authors establish a restriction property for barycenters, showing that restricting a Wasserstein barycenter to subsets of the graph preserves the barycenter property. This allows reduction to a "mesoscopic" scale where the barycenter is supported on a single edge. Second, they construct a branched covering map that transfers the Wasserstein barycenter problem from the graph to the real line, where powerful tools—including the isometric embedding of the Wasserstein space into a Hilbert space via quantile functions—yield absolute continuity results.

The key finding is that the interior of every edge carries only absolutely continuous mass from any Wasserstein barycenter. This result is significant because metric graphs lack the synthetic lower curvature bounds that underpin regularity results in Riemannian manifolds and Aleksandrov spaces, requiring fundamentally new techniques adapted to branching geometries.
original_abstract: In this paper we provide conditions for a Wasserstein barycenter to be absolutely continuous with respect to its Hausdorff measure away from the vertices of the graph.

title: Optimal Linear Interpolation under Differential Information: application to the prediction of perfect flows
generated_summary:
This paper extends the classical Kriging (best linear unbiased prediction) framework to incorporate pointwise linear differential equation information for predicting fields governed by PDEs. Two complementary methods are proposed. The first, collocated co-Kriging, treats discretized differential equations at collocation points as secondary observations within an extended design space that includes derivative indices as additional dimensions. The second, Lagrangian Kriging, enforces differential constraints directly at prediction points via Lagrange multipliers in the optimization formulation. Both methods operate without assuming Gaussian process priors, using leave-one-out cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning instead of maximum likelihood estimation.

The authors derive closed-form expressions for optimal weights and prediction variances for both approaches and provide detailed analytical comparisons. Key findings reveal a fundamental accuracy-versus-cost tradeoff: co-Kriging achieves superior prediction accuracy by leveraging cross-covariances among constraint equations but incurs significantly higher computational costs (scaling as O((n+p)³)), while Lagrangian Kriging offers 100-1000× speedups but sacrifices interpolation properties and cannot incorporate constraints that do not explicitly involve the predicted quantity.

The methods are demonstrated on synthetic ODE/PDE problems and applied to predicting potential flows around cylinders and NACA airfoils, producing satisfactory flow reconstructions with meaningful uncertainty quantification. This work provides a distribution-free, computationally tractable framework for physics-informed spatial prediction with natural extensibility to nonlinear PDEs.
original_abstract: Approximation of functions satisfying partial differential equations (PDEs) is paramount for simulation of physical fluid flows and other problems in physics. Recently, physics-informed machine learning approaches have proven useful as a data-driven complement to numerical models for partial differential equations, bringing faster responses and allowing us to capitalize on past observations. However, their efficiency and convergence depend on the availability of vast training datasets. For sparse observations, Gaussian process regression or Kriging has emerged as a powerful interpolation model, offering principled estimates and uncertainty quantification. Several attempts have been made to condition Gaussian processes on linear PDEs via artificial or collocation observations and kernel design.These methods suffer from scalability issues in higher dimensions and limited generalizability. The aim of this study is to explore the extension of the Kriging predictor in the presence of linear PDE information at a finite number of collocation points. Two approaches are proposed: 1) A collocated co-Kriging with primary observations of the physical field and auxiliary differential observations; 2) A constrained Kriging optimization problem strongly satisfying linear PDE constraints at the points of prediction through a Lagrangian formulation. Numerical experiments are given for ordinary differential equations, 2D harmonic PDEs and an application to perfect flows around a cylinder. This work highlights a trade-off between the computational efficiency of the Lagrange multipliers approach and the strict interpolation of observations.

title: A Kantorovich-type variant of Grünwald Interpolation Operators
generated_summary:
This paper introduces Grünwald-Kantorovich operators, a new sequence of integral-type operators that extend the classical Grünwald interpolation operators from continuous function spaces to Lebesgue spaces and broader Banach function spaces. The key motivation arises from the observation that the original Grünwald operators, which average consecutive Lagrange interpolation operators on Chebyshev nodes, are not bounded in the L¹ norm and thus cannot be directly extended to Lᵖ spaces. By replacing pointwise evaluations with local integral averages—analogous to the classical Kantorovich modification of Bernstein operators—the authors construct operators that overcome this limitation.

The methodology involves first establishing uniform boundedness of the new operators in both C[0,π] and L¹[0,π], then extending boundedness to Lᵖ[0,π] for 1 < p < ∞ via the Riesz-Thorin interpolation theorem. Convergence results are proved alongside quantitative estimates using the modulus of continuity for continuous functions and K-functionals for Lᵖ functions. A crucial result demonstrates that the operators are pointwise bounded by the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, which enables extension of convergence results to various Banach function spaces through a non-positive Korovkin-type theorem.

The significance of this work lies in its broad applicability: convergence is established in weighted Lebesgue spaces, Grand Lebesgue spaces, Orlicz spaces, variable exponent Lebesgue spaces, and Morrey spaces. The authors note that extending convergence to entire Banach function spaces, rather than nontrivial subspaces, remains an open problem.
original_abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new sequence of operators based on the Grünwald interpolation operators on Chebyshev nodes on the space $L^p[0,π]$. The operators we consider are integral variants of the Grünwald interpolation operators, inspired from the classical Kantorovich operators. Unlike the original Grünwald interpolation operators, our construction enables the derivation of convergence results not only on $C[0,π]$ but also in the space $L^p[0,π]$. First, we establish the uniform boundedness of this sequence on these spaces and subsequently prove the convergence of the operators. We obtain quantitative estimates using modulus of continuity and a suitable K-functional. Furthermore, we derive a point-wise estimate via the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. By invoking a Korovkin-type theorem, we extend the convergence results to several Banach function spaces on a nontrivial subspace. In particular, we establish these results for weighted Lebesgue spaces, Grand Lebesgue spaces, Morrey spaces, Orlicz spaces etc.

title: Dirac's theorem and the switch geometry of perfect matchings
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the structure of the reconfiguration graph of perfect matchings in graphs as a function of minimum degree, establishing phase transitions analogous to those in random discrete systems. The authors define the *k*-switch graph *H_k(G)*, where perfect matchings are connected when their Hamming distance is at most 2*k*, and systematically determine minimum degree thresholds guaranteeing various structural properties including connectivity, existence of giant components, absence of isolated vertices, and polynomial mixing time.

The key results reveal a rich phase diagram. For 2-switches, the connectivity threshold lies near 2*n*/3, while for *k*-switches with *k* ≥ 3, connectivity is guaranteed just above the classical Dirac threshold of *n*/2. Below these thresholds, the reconfiguration graph can shatter into exponentially many components with linearly many frozen edges. Remarkably, the threshold for isolated vertices in *H_k(G)* connects to the famous Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture on directed cycle lengths in oriented graphs. The authors also prove that at the connectivity thresholds, the switch Markov chains achieve polynomial mixing time, enabling efficient approximate sampling of perfect matchings.

The methodology combines structural graph theory arguments, symmetric difference analysis of matchings, the canonical paths method for bounding mixing times, and explicit constructions for lower bounds. Results extend to balanced bipartite graphs, partial matchings, and Ore-type degree conditions.

This work initiates a systematic "emergent combinatorics" framework for understanding the geometry of matching spaces, connecting reconfiguration combinatorics, extremal graph theory, and algorithmic sampling.
original_abstract: Let $G$ be a graph on an even number $n$ of vertices and let ${\cal M}_G$ be the collection of perfect matchings in $G$. Dirac's theorem says that if the minimum degree $δ(G)$ of $G$ is at least $n/2$, then ${\cal M}_G$ is guaranteed to be non-empty, while this is not necessarily the case if $δ(G) \le n/2-1$. Given an integer $k\ge 2$, let $\mathcal H_k(G)$ be the reconfiguration graph formed on ${\cal M}_G$ by connecting two distinct $M_1,M_2\in {\cal M}_G$ by an edge in $\mathcal H_k(G)$ if $M_1$ can be obtained from $M_2$ by switching at most $k$ edges. Besides non-emptiness, as per Dirac's theorem, what other natural properties of $\mathcal H_k(G)$ are guaranteed based on the minimum degree $δ(G)$ of $G$? We show that if $δ(G) \ge \lfloor2n/3\rfloor+1$, then $\mathcal H_2(G)$ must be connected and an expander, while for each $δ\le \lfloor(2n-2)/3\rfloor$ there are $n$-vertex graphs $G$ with minimum degree $δ$ such that $\mathcal H_2(G)$ is disconnected. We also show that, if $δ(G) \ge n/2+2$, then $\mathcal H_3(G)$ must be connected and an expander, while for each $δ\le n/2-C_k$ there are $n$-vertex graphs $G$ with minimum degree $δ$ such that $\mathcal H_k(G)$ is disconnected, for some $C_k$ depending on $k\ge 3$. Furthermore, for every $\varepsilon >0$, there exists a $c>1$ such that for every $k\ge 2$ and every large enough $n$, there are $n$-vertex graphs $G$ with $δ(G) \ge \frac{n}2-\varepsilon kn$ such that $\mathcal H_k(G)$ has at least $c^n$ components. With respect to guaranteeing that $\mathcal H_k(G)$ has positive minimum degree (or, equivalently, no isolated vertices) we show that if $δ(G) \ge n/2+1$, then $\mathcal H_2(G)$ must have positive minimum degree. For $k\ge 3$, we show how this threshold for $δ(G)$ is related to the notorious Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture.

title: On Spielman's Laplacian Eigenratio Conjecture and Related Problems
generated_summary:
This paper investigates Spielman's conjecture on the Laplacian eigenratio λ₂(G)/λₙ(G), which proposes a lower bound analogous to the Alon-Boppana bound but formulated for general graphs in terms of average degree. The authors reveal a surprisingly nuanced picture: the conjecture fails for infinitely many average degrees d > 2, holds for all d ≤ 2, and remains valid for all d-regular graphs.

The methodology combines several approaches. Counterexamples for d > 2 are constructed using bipartite Ramanujan graphs from the Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava framework. For regular graphs, the authors develop a test-vector technique comparing λ₂ and λₙ through carefully chosen vectors supported near pairs of distant edges, yielding Laplacian eigenratio analogues of Nilli's Alon-Boppana refinements. This approach extends to higher-multiplicity statements comparing multiple Laplacian eigenvalues simultaneously.

Key results include an unconditional theorem showing that Ramanujan graphs possess linearly many adjacency eigenvalues below −2√(d−1) + ε, without requiring assumptions on odd girth or bipartiteness. The paper also resolves two additional conjectures: the You-Liu conjecture that stars maximize the Laplacian eigenratio among trees, and Gu's conjecture that graphs with sufficiently large Laplacian eigenratio contain Hamilton cycles, the latter proved by connecting eigenratios to expansion properties and applying recent breakthroughs on Hamiltonicity of expanders.

These results establish the Laplacian eigenratio as a fundamental graph parameter with deep connections to spectral theory, expansion, and structural graph properties.
original_abstract: Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with Laplacian eigenvalues $0=λ_1(G)\le λ_2(G)\le\cdots\le λ_n(G)$. Motivated by the Alon-Boppana bound and the Ramanujan phenomenon for regular graphs, Spielman conjectured that, for every graph $G$ with fixed average degree $d\ge 1$, its Laplacian eigenratio satisfies $$ \frac{λ_2(G)}{λ_n(G)} \le \frac{d-2\sqrt{d-1}}{d+2\sqrt{d-1}}+o_n(1), $$ where $o_n(1)\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$. The main purpose of this paper is to investigate this conjecture. We show that the situation is mixed. On the negative side, the conjecture fails for infinitely many average degrees $d>2$, via constructions based on bipartite Ramanujan graphs. On the positive side, it holds in two important settings: we verify it for all average degrees $d\le 2$, and we prove it for all regular graphs. In fact, for regular graphs we obtain stronger bounds comparing higher Laplacian eigenvalues. As a consequence, we show that for every fixed $d\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large $d$-regular Ramanujan graph has linearly many adjacency eigenvalues below $-2\sqrt{d-1}+\varepsilon$, thereby strengthening earlier results of Li and Cioabă by giving an unconditional result of this form. We also settle two related conjectures: one of You and Liu concerning the maximum Laplacian eigenratio of trees, and one of Gu concerning the Hamiltonicity of graphs with large Laplacian eigenratio.

title: Automorphism groups of hyperelliptic curves of $2$-rank zero
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the automorphism groups of hyperelliptic curves of 2-rank zero over algebraically closed fields of characteristic 2, motivated by Oort's conjecture concerning automorphism groups of generic supersingular principally polarized abelian varieties.

The authors study Artin-Schreier curves of the form Y² − Y = f(X), where f(X) is a polynomial with only odd-degree terms, which characterize all hyperelliptic curves of 2-rank zero in characteristic 2. They analyze automorphisms arising from specific coordinate transformations and establish the group extension structure of the full automorphism group through two key homomorphisms. The computational approach employs Gröbner basis calculations using the computer algebra system Magma to determine explicit group structures for small genera.

The main results reveal that for genus n = 1 through 6, the reduced automorphism group RA(C) and the full automorphism group Aut(C) are completely classified in terms of direct and semidirect products of cyclic groups. For odd n ≥ 3, the kernel of a key homomorphism is trivial, simplifying the group structure. The authors also compute automorphism groups of supersingular Scholten-Zhu type curves for genera up to 9.

These findings lead to two refined conjectures: that generic hyperelliptic curves of 2-rank zero in characteristic 2 have trivial reduced automorphism group for genus greater than 2, and that generic supersingular hyperelliptic curves have trivial reduced automorphism group when the genus is not a power of 2. The genus-2 case provides a known counterexample to the original Oort conjecture.
original_abstract: In this paper, we determine the reduced automorphism groups of hyperelliptic curves of a small genus in characteristic $2$, when they are of $2$-rank $0$. Such a curve is an Artin-Schreier curve defined in the form $y^2-y=f(x)$ for a polynomial $f(x)$. After we clarify semidirect-product structures of the automorphism groups for an arbitrary genus, we derive the detailed group structures for the reduced automorphism groups of the curves of a small genus, through computations using the computational algebra system Magma. With these experiments, we formulate two conjectures, which are analogues for our curves of the Oort conjecture on automorphism groups of generic principally polarized supersingular abelian varieties.

title: Sophie Germain Primes and the Totient of Fibonacci Numbers
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the relationship between Sophie Germain primes and the divisibility of Euler's totient function applied to Fibonacci numbers. The main contribution is establishing conditions under which an odd prime q divides the totient φ(F_m) for all integers m in certain residue classes modulo the Pisano period π(q), captured by the set S(q).

The methodology combines classical properties of Fibonacci arithmetic—including ranks of apparition z(p), Pisano periods π(q), and Legendre symbol evaluations of 5 modulo primes—with multiplicative number theory. The authors leverage the factorization structure of the Fibonacci characteristic polynomial over finite fields and known divisibility relations from Carmichael, Wall, and Lucas.

Key results include a sufficient criterion showing that if a prime p ≡ 1 (mod q) has z(p) dividing π(q), then multiples of z(p) modulo π(q) belong to S(q). For Sophie Germain primes q where z(2q+1) divides π(q), the set S(q) is nonempty and forms an arithmetic progression with an odd number of elements. A striking congruence constraint demonstrates that such primes must satisfy q ≡ 8 (mod 15). The authors prove that the uniqueness of the witnessing prime forces k = 2 for k ≤ 31 and conjecture this holds generally. A converse conjecture, verified computationally for q ≤ 50,000, posits that S(q) being nonempty implies the existence of such a witnessing prime.

The significance lies in connecting the infinitude of Sophie Germain primes to structural properties of Fibonacci totients, offering a novel reformulation of a longstanding open problem in prime number theory.
original_abstract: We study the set $S(q)$ of residue classes $r$ modulo the Pisano period $π(q)$ for which $q \mid \varphi(F_m)$ for every $m \equiv r \pmod{π(q)}$. We prove that if $q$ is a Sophie Germain prime and $z(2q+1) \mid π(q)$, then $S(q)$ is a nonempty arithmetic progression, and for $q > 5$ its cardinality is odd and $q \equiv 8 \pmod{15}$. Conversely, we show that if a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod{q}$ has $z(p) \mid π(q)$, then necessarily $p = 2q+1$, so $q$ is Sophie Germain. We conjecture that $S(q) \neq \emptyset$ forces the existence of such a prime $p$; this is verified for all $q \leq 50000$. Assuming that $z(2q+1) \mid π(q)$ holds for infinitely many Sophie Germain primes (verified computationally for approximately 23.9% of them), the Sophie Germain conjecture implies the existence of infinitely many primes $q \equiv 8 \pmod{15}$ with $(2q+1) \mid F_{π(q)}$ -- a purely Fibonacci-theoretic condition. These results generalize to arbitrary Lucas sequences $U_n(P,Q)$ with non-square discriminant.

title: Duality Between Prime Factors and The Prime Number Theorem For Arithmetic Progressions -- Higher Order Dualities
generated_summary:
This paper extends a series of results connecting prime factor sequences to the Prime Number Theorem for Arithmetic Progressions (PNTAP) through higher-order duality identities originally discovered by the first author (Alladi) in 1977. The main contribution is the generalization of previously known first-order and second-order duality results to all orders k ≥ 3, establishing that for arbitrary positive integers k and arithmetic progressions j (mod ℓ) with (j, ℓ) = 1, specific weighted sums involving the Möbius function and the k-th largest prime factor converge to prescribed values.

The methodology builds on Alladi's higher-order duality identities, which connect the k-th largest and smallest prime factors of integers through the Möbius function. The authors first prove in quantitative form that a key summation involving products of prime factors equals zero for k ≥ 2. They then establish that the sequence of k-th largest prime factors P_k(n) is uniformly distributed across reduced residue classes modulo any positive integer. Combining this uniform distribution result with the duality identities yields the main theorems.

The key results are presented with explicit error terms, and the paper provides complete proofs for k = 3 before outlining the analogous arguments for k ≥ 4, where asymptotics become increasingly complex. The significance extends beyond analytic number theory, as the authors discuss algebraic generalizations to number fields and function fields, connecting to work by Dawsey, Sweeting-Woo, and others, thereby opening several directions for future research in algebraic settings.
original_abstract: In 1977, the first author observed a duality between the largest and smallest prime factors of integers, and established as a consequence some new results on the Möbius function $μ(n)$ using the Prime Number Theorem for Arithmetic Progressions. In that 1977 paper, higher order dualities were observed involving the $k$-th largest and $k$-th smallest prime factors, facilitated by the Möbius function and $ω(n)^{k-1}$, where $ω(n)$ is the number of distinct prime factors on $n$. In 2024, the first author and Jason Johnson proved new results involving $μ(n)$ and $ω(n)$, by exploiting the second order duality identity of Alladi (1977). We establish here extensions to all higher orders $k$, the results of Alladi (1977) and of Alladi-Johnson (2024), by utilizing the $k$-th order duality in Alladi's 1977 paper. First, we show that for each $k\geq 2$, $$ \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{μ(n)ω(n)^{k}}{n} =0, $$ where $μ(n)$ is the Möbius Function and $ω(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$. Further, using the General Duality Identity and the Prime Number Theorem of Arithmetic Progressions, we prove that for integers $j,\ell$ satisfying $1 \leq j \leq \ell$ and $(j,\ell)=1$ $$ \sum_{\substack{n=2 \\ p_1(n) \equiv j\;(mod\;\ell)}}^{\infty} \frac{μ(n)ω(n)^{k-1}}{n}=0, \nonumber $$ for every $k \geq 3$; this result for $k=1$ is due to Alladi (1977) and for $k=2$ due to Alladi-Johnson (2024). We also recast this result in the following manner as a density-type theorem: for integers $j,\ell$ satisfying $1 \leq j \leq \ell$ and $(j,\ell)=1$ $$ (-1)^k\sum_{\substack{n=2 \\ p_1(n) \equiv j\;(mod\;\ell)}}^{\infty} \frac{μ(n){ω(n)-1 \choose k-1}}{n}=\frac{1}{\varphi(\ell)}, \nonumber $$ for every $k \geq 3$. All results are established here in quantitative form.

title: Some New Results on Energy of Graphs with Self Loops
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the energy of graphs with self-loops, extending prior work on the relationship between the energy of a simple graph G and its self-looped counterpart. Graph energy, introduced by Gutman in 1978, is defined as the sum of absolute values of eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix. The concept was recently extended to graphs with self-loops by Gutman et al., who conjectured that the energy always increases when self-loops are added—a conjecture later disproved by counterexamples.

The main contribution of this work is the identification of graph families where the energy of a graph with self-loops equals the energy of the corresponding simple graph, even when the number of self-loops is strictly between zero and the total number of vertices. The authors construct such families using the union of copies of a simple graph G and its fully looped version G^l. Specifically, they prove that for the graph H_n = G ∪ G^l, the energy is preserved (E(H_n) = E(H_{qn})) under certain eigenvalue conditions on G. This result is generalized to arbitrary combinations pG ∪ qG^l for non-negative integers p and q. The methodology relies on analyzing the characteristic polynomial and eigenvalues of the combined adjacency matrix. A concrete example using the complete graph K_3 illustrates that E(K_3 ∪ K_3) = E(K_3 ∪ K_3^l). These findings contribute to the broader understanding of how self-loops affect spectral properties of graphs, a topic relevant to mathematical chemistry and spectral graph theory.
original_abstract: The graph $G_σ$ is obtained from graph $G$ by attaching self loops on $σ$ vertices. The energy $ E(G_σ)$ of the graph $G_σ$ with order $n$ and eigenvalues $λ_1,λ_2,\dots,λ_n$ is defined as $ E(G_σ)= \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n\left|λ_i-\dfracσ{n}\right| $. It has been proved that if $σ=0\; or\; n$ then $ E(G)=E(G_σ) $. The obvious question arise: Are there any graph such that $E(G)=E(G_σ)$ and 0$<σ<n$? We have found an affirmative answer of this question and contributed a graph family which satisfies this property.

title: Kill-Probability-Maximization Guidance: Breaking from the Miss-Distance-Minimization Paradigm
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a kill-probability-maximization (KPM) guidance strategy that fundamentally shifts interceptor guidance design from the traditional miss-distance-minimization paradigm to directly maximizing the single shot kill probability (SSKP). The key insight is that conventional approaches, which use cookie-cutter damage functions with hard miss-distance thresholds, lack robustness when facing nonnominal targets and cannot guarantee adequate kill probability in stochastic scenarios.

The methodology rests on two pillars. First, the authors propose a soft, probabilistic lethality model that assigns a continuous kill probability as a function of miss distance, more realistically capturing gradual performance degradation. Second, they incorporate this lethality model into a Bayesian decision-theoretic framework compliant with the generalized separation theorem, which exploits game space decomposition from differential game guidance laws (DGL1 and DGLCC). An interacting multiple model particle filter approximates the full posterior probability density function of the game state, enabling optimal decisions that weight particles near the warhead's effective lethal radius disproportionately rather than penalizing all miss distances equally.

Extensive Monte Carlo simulations against both nominal and nonnominal ("smart") targets with four warhead types demonstrate that KPM variants consistently improve SSKP over both standard and estimation-aware guidance law variants. Crucially, the proposed approach modifies only the guidance law, enabling deployment as a software update to existing interceptors without hardware changes, thereby extending operational effectiveness against evolving threats.
original_abstract: Classical guidance laws aim at minimizing the miss distance, thus implicitly determining the minimum warhead lethality radius required against nominal targets. However, nonnominal targets or scenarios might render the designed warhead insufficient, causing a significant degradation in the single-shot kill probability (SSKP). We propose a guidance methodology that shifts the interceptor's objective from minimizing the miss distance to directly maximizing the SSKP, while taking into account the warhead's probabilistic lethality model. Complying with the generalized separation theorem, the new paradigm is based on modifying deterministic differential-game-based guidance laws using Bayesian decision theory. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate consistent SSKP improvement over the standard and recently introduced estimation-aware guidance laws, when tested against nominal and nonnominal evasively maneuvering targets.

title: Commuting Toeplitz operators with biharmonic symbols
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the commutativity problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit disk when the symbols are biharmonic functions of a specific form. The main contribution extends previous work on commuting Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols to the broader class of biharmonic symbols, which naturally generalizes the harmonic case since every harmonic function is biharmonic but not conversely.

The authors consider biharmonic functions constructed using the Almansi representation, where the analytic components are polynomials in the complex variable. The methodology relies primarily on the Mellin transform as an analytical tool for handling the functional identities that arise from the commutativity condition. This approach represents a departure from techniques used in prior work on harmonic symbols, which cannot be directly adapted to the biharmonic setting due to its substantially greater complexity.

The main result provides a complete characterization: two Toeplitz operators with biharmonic symbols of the specified polynomial form commute if and only if one symbol is a linear combination of the other and a constant. This mirrors the classical result for harmonic symbols, showing that commutativity imposes a strong linear dependence condition on the symbols even in this more general setting.

The significance of this work lies in advancing the largely open general commutativity problem for Toeplitz operators by extending known results to a wider function class while introducing the Mellin transform as an effective new tool for this type of analysis.
original_abstract: We investigate the commutant problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit disk whose symbols belong to a subclass of biharmonic functions. We obtain a complete characterization of when two such Toeplitz operators commute. As a consequence, we derive a full description of normal Toeplitz operators with symbols in this class.

title: A generalization of the Takagi function for beta-expansions
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the regularity properties of a generalized Takagi function G_β defined in the context of beta-expansions with base 1 < β ≤ 2. The classical Takagi function, a well-known example of a continuous but nowhere differentiable function, corresponds to the special case β = 2. The generalized function G_β arises naturally in the multifractal analysis of digit frequency functions for beta-expansions.

The main contributions are two complementary regularity results. First, the authors establish that G_β is pointwise α-Hölder continuous for any α ∈ (0,1) at Lebesgue-almost every point in the unit interval. The proof relies on a key oscillation formula for G_β that captures fluctuations in the sum of digits, combined with the first Borel-Cantelli lemma. This approach yields Hölder coefficients bounded by a positive constant related to the orbit of the point under the corresponding beta-map. Second, the authors prove that G_β fails to be pointwise Lipschitz continuous at Lebesgue-almost every point, demonstrating an essential irregularity. This result is established by constructing sequences converging to almost every point with controlled oscillation ratios, using the central limit theorem for piecewise C² expanding maps applied to the beta-map dynamics. The ergodic properties of the beta-map with respect to its unique absolutely continuous invariant measure play a central role throughout.

title: The Cactus Criterion: When Nonlinear Hodge Theory Reduces to Linear on Graphs

original_abstract: Let $G$ be a finite connected simple graph with a chosen orientation of its edges. For the edge potential $ψ(t)=\cosh t-1,$ we minimize $\sum_{e\in E^\to}ψ(z_e)$ over each affine class $ω+dC^0(G)\subset C^1(G)$. The minimizer is the unique representative satisfying the nonlinear coclosed equation $δ\sinh z=0,$ and hence defines a nonlinear selector $\Picc:C^1(G)\to C^1(G).$ We show that $\Picc$ is real analytic, identify its image as $\imop \Picc=\Mcc=\operatorname{arsinh}(\kerδ),$ and compute its differential as a weighted Hodge projector. In particular, $\Picc$ agrees with the ordinary Hodge projector $\PiH$ to first order at the origin, and the first nonlinear correction is cubic. Our main global theorem is a graph-theoretic criterion: for every admissible edge potential -- even, $C^2$, strictly convex, and non-quadratic -- the associated nonlinear selector coincides with $\PiH$ on all of $C^1(G)$ if and only if $G$ is a cactus graph. title: A Deep Ritz Method for High-Dimensional Steady States of the Cahn--Hilliard Equation

original_abstract: The Cahn--Hilliard equation is a fundamental model for describing phase separation phenomena in binary mixtures. Traditional numerical methods, such as finite difference and finite element methods, often incur substantial computational cost, particularly when computing steady-state solutions in high-dimensional settings. To address this challenge, we propose a deep learning-based framework, namely the Deep Ritz method, for computing steady states of the Cahn--Hilliard equation under periodic boundary conditions. An enhanced augmented Lagrangian formulation is incorporated to strictly enforce the mass conservation constraint, while separable Fourier feature mappings are employed to naturally encode periodicity and enhance the representation of nontrivial solution structures. The proposed method exhibits a notable dual capability: it not only achieves fast convergence to steady states but also effectively identifies multiple nontrivial solutions corresponding to different local minimizers of the energy functional. Extensive numerical experiments in one-, two-, and three-dimensional cases demonstrate that the method can successfully capture a rich variety of phase separation patterns, including droplet-type, lamellar, and tubular structures, highlighting its effectiveness and robustness in exploring complex high-dimensional energy landscapes.

original_abstract: Based on the Hilb-type formula and van der Corput-type lemmas, we present optimal asymptotic estimates for the decay of the Laguerre and Hermite coefficients for functions with algebraic and logarithmic singularities, which in turn yield the convergence rates of the corresponding spectral orthogonal projections. Numerous examples are provided to verify the optimality of these asymptotic results.

title: A Numerical Analysis for Pursuit-Evasion Games under the Stackelberg Eqilibrium

original_abstract: This study presents a numerical analysis framework for pursuit--evasion differential games under the Stackelberg equilibrium. The Semi-DCNLP method is introduced as an optimization solver for flight path optimization problems formulated under the Stackelberg equilibrium. In a spacecraft pursuit-evasion differential game, the Semi-DCNLP method produces trajectories that closely match those obtained with a shooting method. This agreement supports the validity of the proposed approach.

title: The Algebraic Degree of Network Games via Tropical Geometry: A Geometric Perspective on Datta's Formula

original_abstract: The algebraic degree of a network game measures the complexity of its totally mixed Nash equilibria. For sparse multilinear network games, Datta's formula expresses this degree combinatorially in terms of a permanent, but the geometric origin of this formula has remained unclear. In this paper, we provide a tropical-geometric derivation of Datta's formula by identifying totally mixed equilibria with stable intersection points of tropical hypersurfaces associated with the indifference equations. We show that the mixed cells arising from the multilinear Newton polytope structure induce the cycle-cover combinatorics of the polynomial graph, so that the permanent appears as a tropical intersection count. This interpretation yields several structural consequences. We prove that the algebraic degree is multiplicative over strongly connected components, and we establish a sharp contrast between two basic multilayer coupling mechanisms: Cartesian-type couplings remain bounded through a transfer-matrix trace formula, whereas tensor-type couplings exhibit exponential growth governed by the permanent of a local gadget. These results show that algebraic degree provides a structural complexity invariant for network architecture. We further illustrate the theory on coupled cyclic games and networked energy-market models, and we support the theoretical predictions with numerical experiments based on homotopy continuation.

title: Exact Simulation from Tempered Stable Distributions with Infinite Variation ($α\ge1$)

For the case α ∈ [1, 2), the authors derive upper bounds on the ratio of the target density to a proposal density, establishing the theoretical foundation for rejection sampling. A simulation study with 10 million proposal samples demonstrates the method's effectiveness, achieving acceptance probabilities ranging from approximately 1/2.33 to 1/8.66 across various parameter configurations. original_abstract: We develop the first exact and computationally tractable method for simulating from tempered stable distributions in the infinite variation case, which corresponds to $α\in[1,2)$. A small simulation study shows that the approach works well.

title: Quantitative Stability of the Shadow for Wasserstein Projections and Sample Complexity
generated_summary:

Their proof strategy combines two key ingredients: a contraction property of L^p projections onto convex sets of probability measures, and state-of-the-art Hölder continuity results for optimal transport maps. This extension enables them to derive sample complexity bounds for the empirical shadow, establishing convergence rates that depend on the Wasserstein dimension of the underlying measures rather than ambient dimension.

original_abstract: In this paper, we study the stability of the shadow, a projection of a measure onto the set of couplings with respect to the Wasserstein distance. The shadow was introduced by \citet{Eckstein_Nutz_2022} to analyze the stability of the Sinkhorn algorithm, and was recently revisited by \citet{kim2026extensioncouplingprojectionoptimal} for statistical applications. Under mild conditions, we establish the bi-Hölder continuity of the shadow. As a consequence, we also derive the sample complexity of the shadow by combining smoothing techniques with recent results on the rate of convergence of empirical measures in Wasserstein distance. The key idea of the proof is twofold: first, a contraction property of the $L^p$ projection, recently used independently by \citet{kim2025stabilitywassersteinprojectionsconvex} and \citet{alfonsi2025wassersteinprojectionsconvexorder} to study the stability of projections onto the convex order cone in Wasserstein space; and second, the Hölder continuity of optimal transport maps established by \citet{Quantitative_stability_duke2023}, together with its recent extension by \citet{mischler2025quantitativestabilityoptimaltransport}.

title: Asymptotic behavior of the variance of the BLUE for the mean of stationary processes

original_abstract: In this paper, we survey results on the asymptotic behavior of the variance of the best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) for the mean of stationary processes. This behavior is influenced by the regularity and memory structures of the observed models. The results show that the asymptotic behavior of the variance of the BLUE is determined solely by the behavior of the spectrum near the origin. For nondeterministic models, the variance of the BLUE exhibits hyperbolic behavior, similar to the power function, while for purely deterministic models, the variance decreases at an exponential rate. Specifically, a necessary condition for the variance of the BLUE to approach zero exponentially is that the spectral density of the model vanishes on a set of positive Lebesgue measure in any neighborhood of zero. We also present results on the asymptotic efficiency of various unbiased linear estimators in comparison to the BLUE.

title: Classification and deontic explosion for contrary-to-duty obligations

original_abstract: Carmo and Jones have presented a sequence of candidate axiom systems for conditional obligation between 1997 and 2022. For their most recent system we demonstrate a limited form of deontic explosion: given that a student does not get the highest possible grade on a test, any other passing grade is acceptable. In addition to that negative result, we give a positive one: revisiting the strongest version of Carmo and Jones' 1997 system, we provide a surprising classification of all satisfying models in terms of a single forbidden possible world.

title: Steady-state Based Approach to Online Non-stochastic Control

The work provides a more interpretable benchmark for general convex costs while maintaining strong theoretical guarantees, bridging ideas from online feedback optimization and online learning.
original_abstract: We study the problem of online non-stochastic control (ONC), which is the control of a linear system under adversarial disturbances and adversarial cost functions, with the aim of minimizing the total cost incurred. A recent line of literature in ONC develops algorithms that enjoy sublinear regret with respect to a benchmark based on the set of steady-states that are attainable by a constant input. In this work, we extend this research direction by giving an algorithm that enjoys $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret with respect to a richer benchmark set, namely the set of steady-states attainable under an \emph{affine controller}. Since this benchmark substantially broadens the comparison class, it provides significantly stronger performance guarantees. Our proposed algorithm combines a Follow-The-Perturbed-Leader-style online non-convex optimization approach with a batching method that maintains stability despite changing policies. Although our proposed algorithm requires solving non-convex subproblems, we show that an approximate solution to this subproblem is sufficient to ensure $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret. Furthermore, numerical experiments show that our algorithm enjoys lower total cost and similar computation to existing methods in certain settings.

title: Long time smooth solutions of 3D cubic quasilinear wave systems with small weakly decaying initial data

original_abstract: For the 3D cubic quasilinear wave system $\square_{c_i} u^i=G^i(u,\partial u,\partial^2u)=\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{0\le|α|,|β|,|γ|\le1 \\ 1\le j,k,l \le m}}g_{αβγ}^{ijkl}\partial^αu^j\partial^βu^k\partial^γu^l$, it is well known that global solution $u$ exists when the small smooth initial data $(u,\partial_tu)|_{t=0}$ $=(u_0(x), u_1(x))$ are compactly supported or decay rapidly at spatial infinity. Our main ingredients consist in establishing a series of new weighted $L^\infty-L^2$ estimates and Strichartz estimates based on the strong Huygens' principle for 3D linear wave equations.

title: Subsample-based Estimation under Dynamic Contamination
generated_summary:

They show that for pure autoregressive models, residual contamination has finite memory, while models with moving average components exhibit potentially infinite (though geometrically decaying) propagation. To address this, they propose a "patch removal operator" that excludes not only contaminated observations but also subsequent indices affected by residual propagation, governed by a model-implied trimming parameter.

Monte Carlo simulations across VAR, VMA, and VARMA specifications confirm that standard oracle subsampling produces substantial bias that worsens with outlier magnitude, while the proposed correction restores estimation accuracy with only modest efficiency loss under clean data. The framework establishes formal asymptotic invariance and consistency results.

These findings have important implications for empirical practice: robust inference in dynamic models requires propagation-compatible corrections rather than simple observation removal, ensuring that estimated models reflect the underlying data generating mechanism rather than contamination artifacts.
original_abstract: Subsample-based estimation is a standard tool for achieving robustness to outliers in econometric models. This paper shows that, in dynamic time series settings, such procedures are fundamentally invalid under contamination, even under oracle knowledge of contamination locations. The key issue is that contamination propagates through the model's residual filter and distorts the estimation criterion itself. As a result, removing contaminated observations does not, in general, restore the uncontaminated objective or ensure consistency. We characterise this failure as a structural incompatibility between pointwise subsampling and residual propagation. To address it, we propose a propagation-compatible transformation of index sets, formalised through a patch removal operator that removes the residual footprint of contamination. Under suitable conditions, the proposed operator leaves the estimator asymptotically unchanged under the uncontaminated model, while restoring consistency for the clean-data parameter under contamination. The results apply to a broad class of residual-based estimators and show that valid subsample-based estimation in dynamic models requires explicit control of residual propagation.

title: Rigidity and Cohomology of Seaweed Lie Algebras

For the indecomposable case, the authors establish a vanishing theorem for the reductive-part-invariant cohomology of the nilradical using a homotopy operator combined with a Casimir identity. For the decomposable case, the same spectral sequence reduction isolates the contribution from the center, and a theorem of Coll and Gerstenhaber on cohomology of Lie semidirect products yields an explicit decomposition.

The key results show that indecomposable seaweed algebras have vanishing adjoint cohomology in all degrees, making them absolutely rigid. Decomposable seaweeds, by contrast, have nontrivial cohomology described canonically in terms of the center and the quotient by the center. The structural bridge is that a seaweed is indecomposable precisely when its center vanishes.

These findings extend the rigidity theory of parabolic subalgebras—known to be rigid by Tolpygo's theorem—to the broader seaweed class. The paper also demonstrates that seaweed algebras are not generally closed under formal deformation, suggesting they should be studied within larger algebraic families such as proset algebras.
original_abstract: Seaweed (biparabolic) subalgebras form a large and structurally rich class of subalgebras of simple Lie algebras. We determine their adjoint cohomology. If $\mathfrak{s}$ is an indecomposable seaweed subalgebra of a complex simple Lie algebra, then \[ H^\ast(\mathfrak{s},\mathfrak{s})=0, \] and hence $\mathfrak{s}$ is absolutely rigid. If $\mathfrak{s}$ is decomposable, then the Coll--Gerstenhaber decomposition for Lie semidirect products gives, for each $n\ge 0$, a canonical description of $H^n(\mathfrak{s},\mathfrak{s})$ in terms of exterior powers of $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{s})^\ast$ and the zero-weight cohomology of $\mathfrak{s}/\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{s})$. In particular, the center is the unique source of nontrivial adjoint cohomology. These results identify indecomposability as the precise condition for cohomological rigidity and give a uniform description of adjoint cohomology for seaweed Lie algebras.

title: The Jordan multiplication semigroup of matrix algebras is the full endomorphism semigroup

The proof proceeds in stages. They then demonstrate that these Jordan-theoretic transvections generate all elementary transvections relative to a standard basis, first handling the 2×2 case explicitly and propagating to arbitrary n×n matrices through corner embeddings and commutator arguments. This establishes that the semigroup contains the special linear group SL(V). The passage to the full endomorphism semigroup uses a determinant-surjectivity argument showing all invertible operators belong to the semigroup, combined with exhibiting a singular element of corank one to generate all singular endomorphisms.

This result has no associative analogue, since left multiplication operators in associative algebras merely reproduce the algebra itself. The theorem reveals a striking rigidity phenomenon: the noncommutativity encoded in Jordan multiplication generates maximal linear complexity. The characteristic-2 exclusion is shown to be essential, as the Jordan product then annihilates the identity matrix.
original_abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $M_n(\mathbb{K})$ be the algebra of all $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{K}$. We consider the corresponding special Jordan algebra $\mathcal{A}:=M_n(\mathbb{K})^+$ with symmetrized product $A\circ B:=(AB+BA)/2$, and write $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm v}:=M_n(\mathbb{K})$ for the underlying $\mathbb{K}$-vector space of $\mathcal{A}$. For $A\in\mathcal{A}$, let $\mathrm{L}_A(X):=A\circ X$ be the multiplication operator. We consider the Jordan multiplication semigroup generated by all multiplication operators, \[ \mathrm{JMS}(\mathcal{A}):=\langle \mathrm{L}_A:A\in\mathcal{A}\rangle\subseteq \mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm v}). \] We prove that $\mathrm{JMS}(\mathcal{A})=\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm v})$. Equivalently, every $\mathbb{K}$-linear endomorphism of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm v}$ is a composition of multiplication operators. The proof is primarily linear-algebraic. The main step is to show that $\mathrm{SL}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm v})\subseteq \mathrm{JMS}(\mathcal{A})$ by constructing elementary transvections inside the semigroup. We then prove determinant surjectivity on the unit group of $\mathrm{JMS}(\mathcal{A})$ and combine it with the existence of a singular element of rank $n^2-1$ to obtain the full endomorphism semigroup. In the finite-field case, the determinant-surjectivity step is established via Jacobi-sum estimates.

title: Maximum Cuts and Fractional Cut Covers: A Computational Study of a Randomized Semidefinite Programming Approach

The methodology involves three key steps: solving an SDP relaxation, sampling cuts from the (potentially perturbed) optimal SDP solution, and optimizing over the sampled cuts via linear programming. A critical algorithmic ingredient is perturbation of the SDP solution before sampling, which addresses the challenge of covering "thin" edges with small relative weight.

Key findings demonstrate that sample sizes of 128m (where m is the number of edges)—far smaller than theoretical bounds—suffice to achieve approximation ratios consistently exceeding the theoretical guarantee of approximately 0.878. original_abstract: We present experimental work on a primal-dual framework simultaneously approximating maximum cut and weighted fractional cut-covering instances. In this primal-dual framework, we solve a semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation to either the maximum cut problem or to the weighted fractional cut-covering problem, and then independently sample a collection of cuts via the random-hyperplane technique. We then simultaneously certify the approximate optimality of a cut and a fractional cut cover. We present several implementations which reliably achieve the celebrated Goemans and Williamson approximation ratio of $α_{\mathrm{GW}} \approx 0.878$ for both optimization problems simultaneously, after $\lceil 128 \ln m \rceil$ samples, a number significantly smaller than the best theoretical bounds. This is the first experimental work approximating the weighted fractional cut-covering problem, and we deliver robust and repeatable results despite the use of randomized algorithms and floating-point arithmetic. Careful pre-processing of instances and post-processing of numeric results allow for good empirical outcomes with both first-order and second-order SDP solvers. Nearly optimal SDP solutions are suitably perturbed to ensure better probabilistic and numerical behavior. Our experiments deviate from theory by using a linear programming (LP) solver to compute fractional cut covers. For most instances studied, LP solving produces certifiably better results than the theoretical algorithm after $\lceil 128 \ln m \rceil$ samples. All our experiments strictly follow a unified pipeline which explicitly documents all parameters used in each run.

title: On The Mathematics of the Natural Physics of Optimization
generated_summary:

The methodology centers on the Transversality Mapping Principle, which guarantees the existence of an optimal control problem whose terminal transversality conditions map to the first-order necessary conditions (KKT conditions) of a given constrained optimization problem. The extremal state trajectories of this control problem serve as continuous-time convergent "algorithms" for the original optimization problem. Rather than discretizing these differential equations directly, the authors develop an inverse optimality framework combined with proximal aiming, where algorithms are generated through controlled jumps that decrement a stability Lyapunov function (SLF), satisfying an instantaneous Hamilton-Jacobi inequality.

Key results include the demonstration that many known optimization algorithms, including Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and SQP methods, naturally emerge from this unified framework through specific choices of SLFs and control spaces. Notably, convergence is inherently guaranteed by construction rather than requiring separate proofs.

The significance lies in providing a universal mathematical physics foundation for optimization algorithms, potentially unifying disparate methods under a single theoretical umbrella. The authors also suggest a possible extension to quantum computing through connections between Hamilton-Jacobi and Schrödinger equations, with implications for large-scale machine learning applications.
original_abstract: A number of optimization algorithms have been inspired by the physics of Newtonian motion. Here, we ask the question: do algorithms themselves obey some ``natural laws of motion,'' and can they be derived by an application of these laws? We explore this question by positing the theory that optimization algorithms may be considered as some manifestation of hidden algorithm primitives that obey certain universal non-Newtonian dynamics. This natural physics of optimization is developed by equating the terminal transversality conditions of an optimal control problem to the generalized Karush/John-Kuhn-Tucker conditions of an optimization problem. Through this equivalence formulation, the data functions of a given constrained optimization problem generate a natural vector field that permeates an entire hidden space with information on the optimality conditions. An ``action-at-a-distance'' operation via a Pontryagin-type minimum principle produces a local action to deliver a globalized result by way of a Hamilton-Jacobi inequality. An inverse-optimal algorithm is generated by performing control jumps that dissipate quantized ``energy'' defined by a search Lyapunov function. Illustrative applications of the proposed theory show that a large number of algorithms can be generated and explained in terms of the new mathematical physics of optimization.

title: Forbidden subgraphs in divisor graphs and an Erdős divisibility problem
generated_summary:

The main contribution is a general theorem showing that for any family of admissible sets satisfying three axioms—being downward closed, decomposing over coprime components, and being preserved by integer dilation—the maximum size of an admissible subset of {1, …, n} equals c·n + o(n) for an effectively computable constant c, and the number of such subsets has an exponential growth rate with a computable base. The methodology relies on a theorem of McNew concerning local statistics of divisor graphs, which expresses relevant divisor-graph statistics as explicit convergent series.

Applied to the Erdős two-fork problem (forbidding any element from dividing two others), the authors improve known bounds, establishing 0.6729 ≤ c₂ ≤ 0.6736, narrowing the gap to approximately 0.0007. The counting rate satisfies 1.729 ≤ α₂ ≤ 1.874. The framework extends uniformly to r-forks, in-forks, k-chains, and even infinite families of forbidden patterns such as cycle-freeness. This unifying approach provides computable density and counting estimates for a broad class of extremal divisibility problems, while Erdős's question about the irrationality of c₂ remains open.
original_abstract: Erdős asked for the largest size $f(n)$ of a subset of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with no element dividing two others. We show that $f(n)=c_2\,n+o(n)$ for an effectively computable constant $c_2$, and moreover that the number $q(n)$ of such subsets satisfies $q(n)=β_2^{n+o(n)}$ for a computable constant $β_2$. To prove this, we recast the divisibility constraint as forbidding a certain directed subgraph in the divisor graph on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and prove a more general result: for any finite family of connected forbidden subgraphs of the divisor graph, both the extremal density and counting rate are effectively computable. The proof uses a theorem of McNew on local statistics of divisor graphs.

title: Uniform Hyperbolicity and Symbolic Dynamics: Markov Partitions, Shadowing, and the Coding of Axiom A Systems
generated_summary:

The work proves five main theorems with full quantitative control. The Spectral Decomposition Theorem partitions the nonwandering set into basic sets with quantitative mixing rates. original_abstract: This paper establishes the geometric theory of uniformly hyperbolic sets with explicit quantitative bounds throughout, and contains five main theorems. The Stable Manifold Theorem is proved via the backward graph transform, with a complete fiber-contraction argument yielding $C^r$ regularity and Hölder dependence of the local stable and unstable manifolds on the base point, with explicit manifold-size estimate in terms of the contraction rate $λ$ and the second-derivative bound of the diffeomorphism. The Spectral Decomposition Theorem gives the unique decomposition of the nonwandering set into basic sets, with explicit mixing rates for the topologically mixing factors. The Shadowing Lemma provides explicit error bounds controlling how far a pseudo-orbit deviates from a tracking true orbit. The existence of Markov partitions of arbitrarily small diameter is established constructively, with explicit diameter bounds expressed in terms of the shadowing constants. Finally, the coding map from the subshift of finite type to the hyperbolic set is constructed and shown to be Hölder continuous with quantitative control on the exceptional set where it fails to be injective. Along the way we establish canonical coordinates through the bracket map with quantitative bounds. All constants are expressed in terms of the contraction rate, the Hölder exponent of the derivative, the manifold dimension, and the injectivity radius, providing the quantitative infrastructure required to transfer the symbolic spectral theory of Part I and the variational theory of Part II to the smooth setting. This paper constitutes Part III of a six-part series on the thermodynamic formalism for hyperbolic dynamical systems.

title: Fully discrete scheme for the fifth-order KdV-Burgers-Fisher equation using Strang splitting and Fourier collocation methods
generated_summary:
This paper presents a fully discrete numerical scheme for solving the fifth-order Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers-Fisher (KBF) equation, which models systems combining dispersive, dissipative, and reactive effects. The main contribution lies in constructing and rigorously analyzing the convergence of a scheme that combines Strang splitting for time integration with Fourier collocation for spatial discretization.

The methodology decomposes the KBF equation into simpler subproblems that can be solved individually: one handled via exact integration in Fourier space and the other approximated using the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. The convergence analysis proceeds in two stages. First, the authors establish second-order convergence of the Strang splitting in the Sobolev space H^s using Lie commutator bounds and numerical quadrature estimates under suitable regularity assumptions on the exact solution. Second, they extend the analysis to the fully discrete setting by combining the global time discretization error with Fourier interpolation error estimates, proving convergence of the complete scheme.

Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical predictions, demonstrating second-order temporal convergence when applied to a test problem with periodic boundary conditions using 256 collocation points. The error measurements in the discrete L² norm align with the analytically derived convergence rates.

The significance of this work lies in providing a rigorous mathematical framework for a practical and efficient numerical method applicable to a broad class of fifth-order nonlinear evolution equations encompassing KdV, Kawahara, Burgers, and Fisher-type models as special cases.
original_abstract: Operator splitting is an effective technique for the numerical solution of nonlinear partial differential equations by decomposing a complex problem into simpler subproblems. In this study, we present and analyze a fully discrete scheme for the fifth-order Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers-Fisher equation (KBF) by combining Strang splitting for time discretization with the Fourier collocation method for spatial discretization. In particular, the Fourier collocation method is an essential component of the proposed fully discrete scheme and yields spectral accuracy in space under suitable regularity assumptions. The KBF equation describes the interaction of reaction, dissipative, and dispersive mechanisms by incorporating the Fisher reaction term together with Burgers-type diffusion and higher-order KdV dispersion. The equation is split into a linear operator and a nonlinear operator, and the resulting subproblems are solved within the Strang splitting framework. Convergence is analyzed in the Sobolev space $H^s$. The local error is derived using operator-theoretic arguments in Banach spaces together with Lie commutator estimates, while the global error is obtained using the Lady Windermere's fan argument. The analysis yields second-order convergence in time and spectral convergence in space. Numerical results confirm the theoretical error estimates and demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed fully discrete scheme.

title: Decentralized Stability-Constrained Optimal Power Flow for Inverter-Based Power Systems
generated_summary:
This paper presents the first decentralized stability-constrained optimal power flow (OPF) framework for inverter-based power systems, enabling systematic integration of small-signal stability requirements into operational decision-making. The approach addresses the growing need for stability-aware dispatch as power systems transition from synchronous-machine-dominated to inverter-based architectures.

The methodology leverages decentralized algebraic stability conditions that depend only on local voltage differences between neighboring buses, derived through passivity-based arguments and Gershgorin's Circle Theorem. These sufficient conditions for small-signal stability can be directly embedded as constraints in standard OPF formulations without requiring global system models, eigenvalue computation, or time-domain simulations. The authors introduce the concept of Nodal Stability Shadow Prices (NSSPs), which quantify the marginal economic impact of stability requirements at each device.

Key theoretical results reveal that in lossless networks with active-power-only costs, binding stability constraints can exhibit zero shadow prices—a degeneracy between stability and objective structure. However, incorporating realistic reactive power costs, reflecting the opportunity cost of limited inverter capacity, yields positive shadow prices with meaningful economic interpretations. Numerical experiments on two-bus and IEEE 39-bus systems demonstrate that the reactive power droop parameter plays a critical role in stability margins and highlight practical stability-economics trade-offs.

The framework's significance lies in its scalability, interpretability, and ability to provide device-level economic attribution of stability contributions, making it practical for future low-inertia power system operations.
original_abstract: Future inverter-dominated power systems feature higher variability and more stressed operating conditions, which motivates the consideration of stability in operational settings. Existing approaches to stability-constrained OPF often rely on eigenvalue calculation, global model information, or dynamic evaluation inside optimization formulation, which are computationally intensive and difficult to scale. This paper proposes the first decentralized stability-constrained OPF framework for inverter-based power systems. The key novelty lies in the incorporation of a class of algebraic decentralized small-signal stability criteria that admits tractable representations in steady-state variables and is therefore suitable for optimization. The decentralized stability condition is based on local voltage differences and enables clear theoretical and practical economic interpretation of the stability contribution from each inverter. We define a Nodal Stability Shadow Price (NSSP) for each inverter, and characterize the role of these stability constraints through their associated shadow prices, enabling a nodal interpretation of their economic impacts. It is proved that under active-power-only objectives in lossless networks, binding stability constraints may occur but will admit zero shadow prices if all other operational constraints are inactive. Most importantly, we reveal the importance of considering the opportunity cost of reactive power for inverter-based resources (IBRs) that have limited capacity. When reactive power costs are considered, stability constraints can carry strictly positive shadow prices and admit meaningful economic impacts.

title: Geometric Stability of the Schoen-Yau Zero Mass Theorem
generated_summary:
This paper surveys the geometric stability of the Schoen-Yau Zero Mass Rigidity Theorem, which states that an asymptotically flat three-dimensional Riemannian manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and zero ADM mass must be isometric to Euclidean space. The central question is whether sequences of such manifolds with mass approaching zero converge geometrically to Euclidean space, and under which notion of convergence this holds.

The authors systematically examine numerous examples of sequences with mass converging to zero—including Riemannian Schwarzschild spaces, geometrostatic manifolds, constructions with Schoen-Yau tunnels, bubbling, wells, and sewing techniques—to evaluate different notions of geometric convergence. They demonstrate that Gromov-Hausdorff convergence fails for certain examples (such as those with wells of increasing depth), while volume preserving intrinsic flat convergence appears to be the appropriate framework.

The paper formulates a precise conjecture: that isoperimetric regions in sequences of manifolds from Bray's class (excluding closed interior minimal surfaces) with uniformly bounded diameter and ADM mass approaching zero converge in the volume preserving intrinsic flat sense to Euclidean balls. This conjecture has been proven in the spherically symmetric setting by Lee-Sormani. The restriction to Bray's class is justified through examples showing that tunnels and bubbles with interior minimal surfaces produce non-Euclidean limits, but cutting along these minimal surfaces restores convergence to Euclidean space. The survey identifies scrunching without tunnels as the key open question that could potentially provide counterexamples.
original_abstract: In 1979, Schoen and Yau proved their famous Positive Mass Theorem which is a combination of a comparison theorem: {\em a three dimensional asymptotically flat Riemannian manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature has nonnegative ADM mass}, and a rigidity theorem: {\em if such a manifold has zero ADM mass then it is isometric to Euclidean space}. Here we review results and open questions on the geometric stability of their zero mass rigidity theorem: {\em if such a manifold has almost zero mass, how close is its geometry to that of Euclidean space}? We review the geometry of these spaces, examples of sequences of such spaces with mass approaching zero, and a variety of geometric notions of convergence. Although there has been much progress, it is still an open question (even in dimension three): exactly which geometric notion of convergence works best to capture the geometric stability of this famous rigidity theorem.

title: Fundamental cycles in grid graphs
generated_summary:
This paper resolves a problem posed by McCarty regarding the sparsity of fundamental cycles in grid graphs, with implications for sparse representations of binary matroids and integer programming. The central question asks whether, for any spanning tree of an n×n grid graph, the average length of fundamental cycles must grow with n.

The authors answer this question affirmatively by establishing tight asymptotic bounds. They prove that the average length of a fundamental cycle with respect to any spanning tree of the n×n grid is at least Ω(log n), demonstrating that n(k) = 2^Θ(k) suffices to guarantee an average fundamental cycle length of at least k. Complementing this lower bound, they construct an explicit spanning tree achieving an average fundamental cycle length of at most 40 log₂ n, showing the logarithmic bound is asymptotically tight.

The methodology combines combinatorial arguments about grid graph structure with careful constructions of spanning trees. The upper bound construction is presented through recursive or tiling-based approaches using subgrids, while the lower bound arguments leverage properties of grid embeddings and the unavoidable complexity of spanning tree paths in planar grid structures.

These results are significant because they connect to the broader study of sparse matroid representations, which underpin recent advances in combinatorial optimization, particularly efficient algorithms for structured integer programs. The findings confirm that graphic matroids of grid graphs inherently lack sparse echelon-form representations, providing foundational insight into the limits of sparsification techniques.
original_abstract: We show that the average length of a fundamental cycle with respect to any fixed spanning tree of the $n\times n$ square grid is at least $Ω(\log n)$; the bound is asymptotically tight. This result answers in the affirmative a question posed by McCarty in relation to sparse representations of binary matroids.

title: Pointwise character bounds for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
generated_summary:

The main result provides a uniform constant C such that the absolute value of any irreducible character, evaluated at any group element, is bounded by C times the dimension of the representation divided by a product involving inner products of the shifted highest weight with positive roots and the spatial parameter. This represents the first full pointwise character bound for spherical functions on a higher-rank compact symmetric space.

The methodology relies on the Weyl character formula and a "descent formula" that decomposes irreducible characters into sums of lower-rank (SU(2)) characters near singular sets. The proof exploits Weyl group symmetry to reduce the problem to three representative configurations of spectral and spatial parameters. A key technical insight is that appropriate grouping of terms in the descent formula, indexed by cosets of parabolic subgroups of the Weyl group, produces crucial cancellations needed to obtain the desired bounds.

As applications, the author derives new L^p bounds for irreducible characters of SU(3) that improve upon previously known estimates, particularly in the "singular regime" of spectral parameters. The pointwise bound also yields improved estimates for character values at non-central elements, strengthening results relevant to the singularity theory of central measures on compact Lie groups. The author conjectures that the bound extends to spherical functions on general irreducible compact symmetric spaces and indicates the framework should generalize to other compact Lie groups.
original_abstract: We present a basic pointwise bound for the irreducible characters of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ and, as an application, derive new $L^p$ bounds for these characters. Our approach is based on the descent of characters to singular sets and the cancellation in this formula.

title: A framework for the study of the qualitative dynamics of general Iterated Function Systems
generated_summary:
This paper extends a framework previously developed for semiflows to study the qualitative dynamics of general Iterated Function Systems (IFSs), where the constituent maps need only be continuous rather than contractive. The authors work on locally compact, separable metric spaces and require IFSs to have "compact dynamics," meaning they possess a non-empty global attractor.

The methodology centers on introducing "streams"—closed, transitive binary relations that capture which points are dynamically downstream from others. Within this framework, "ponds" represent sets of mutually upstream-and-downstream points, generalizing periodic orbits. The qualitative dynamics are encoded in directed acyclic graphs whose nodes are ponds and whose edges represent downstream relationships. The chain stream, based on an adaptation of Conley's ε-chains to IFSs, serves as the most important stream.

Key results include: the chain stream of an IFS with compact dynamics coincides with that of its restriction to the global attractor; chain-recurrent sets are compact and Hutchinson-invariant; conditions ensuring graph connectivity are established; the Hutchinson map itself has compact dynamics if and only if the original IFS does; and relationships between the chain graphs of an IFS and its Hutchinson map are characterized.
